usually with the features whose edges it rounds (mitcad#105):

```json
{"type": "rectangular_pattern",
 "objects": {"type": "features", "features": ["F4", "F5", "F6"]},
 "direction1": {"axis": "x", "quantity": 3, "distance": 20}, "distance_type": "spacing"}
```

- It leaves no tool body, so it is not copied but applied again at each
  element, on the copies of its edges, with its own sizes (parameters)
  and options. The features go in timeline order then: a fillet after
  the copies of the features before it, whatever the order of `features`.
- The copies' edges are found by their names: in an edge name, a face
  that a copied feature made becomes that face's copy at the element
  (`<pattern>:inst<element>(…)`, inner instances of a pattern of patterns
  inside), a face of another feature stays. A chamfer between a copied
  boss `F4` and the plate `F2` it stands on, `E{F2:end(r{…})|F4:side(c1)}`,
  is repeated on `E{F2:end(r{…})|F7:inst1(F4:side(c1))}`.
- An edge whose copy no body has by that name (none of its faces copied,
  as for a fillet patterned alone over holes an earlier pattern made, or
  its other face is another face at the copy's place) is found by its
  place: the edge whose middle (within 1e-4 mm), direction and length are
  those of the original edge, on the body before the fillet, moved by the
  element's transform. An edge found neither way (a copy that reaches no
  body) is left out with the warning `<fillet> is not repeated where the
  copies lack its edges (elements …)`; faces (`faces` sets) are found by
  name only.
- The copies' new faces are the pattern's: `<pattern>:fillet(<the copy's
  edge>)`, `<pattern>:chamfer(…)`, `<pattern>:corner(…)` (e.g.
  `F7:chamfer(E{F7:inst1(F4:end(r{c1}))|F7:inst1(F4:side(c1))})`). A fillet
  among the objects that rounds a copied chamfer's edges is repeated on the
  copy of that chamfer's face the same way.
- A two-distance or distance-angle chamfer or an asymmetric fillet without
  a reference face measures its first distance on the first face of each
  edge's name; where the copy's name puts the other face first, the copy
  takes it with `flip` swapped, so that the distances stay on the faces the
  original measured them on (also with a mirror). Sets by `faces`, and
  edges found by their place, keep the sorted order of the copies' names.
- The copies go on the body that has their edges (the fillet's own body
  first), all elements in one operation; when that fails, one element after
  another. When that fails too, the pattern starts again with the features
  of one element after another (each element's copies of all the objects,
  then the next element's): where copies overlap (pockets around a hub),
  the rounding of one copy otherwise ends at the edges of the next. A
  fillet whose copies fail even so fails the pattern (`Fillet1 at
  element 2: …`), as does one whose copies find no edge at all (`no copy
  of the edges of Fillet1 is on a body`) and one that failed itself.
  `scale` with fillets or chamfers is unsupported.
- A `thread` among the features (mitcad#719: a tapped hole's thread on
  its wall) is repeated alike on the copies of the faces it threads. Its
  faces' copies are found by name; where none was copied (a pattern of
  the thread alone, mitcad#733), on the cylindrical faces at their places:
  the same radius, the moved axis and ends (within 1e-4 mm). A modelled
  copy is turned as the original moved there (its helix where the moved
  helix lies, not the original's `angle` about the copy's own axis), and a
  mirror's modelled image is left-handed. A cosmetic copy keeps the
  designation, also in a mirror (a tapped size; mitcad#733).

#### Optimized: copying the faces

With `"compute": "optimized"` a pattern or mirror of features that has
fillets or chamfers among them does not work them out on each copy (above):
it copies the faces the features made, as the `.f3d` option of the same
name does. Without a fillet or chamfer the features' tools are the faces
they made, and `optimized` is `identical`.

- What the features did to a body is what lies between the body before
  the first of them and the body after the last: the material they added
  (a boss with the roundings at its foot and on its top) and the material
  they removed (a pocket with its chamfer), each a closed solid bounded by
  the faces the features made (`Kernel::feature_changes`). The solids are
  moved to every element, as a feature's tool is, the removed ones are cut
  from the body and the added ones joined to it, each in one operation:
  no fillet or chamfer is evaluated at an element, so one that the
  geometry kernel fails on at some copy (the roundings of a thousand pins
  on a large body) does not fail the pattern.
- The features are taken in runs of consecutive features of the timeline
  (no other body-changing feature between them), one pair of bodies per
  body a run changes. Features that make or remove bodies, or that do not
  stand at the same places (a pattern of patterns that copies only some of
  them), are repeated as the other options do.
- A copy of added material stands on the faces under its seam (the planar
  faces of the solid that lay on the body, such as the disc a boss's foot
  rounding ends on): the material over the part of a seam face that no
  planar face of the body lies under (coplanar, facing it) is cut off
  along the seam's normal, a copy with nothing under its seam is left out
  (`Kernel::supported_copies`). A seam on a curved face is not clipped.
- The copies' faces are named `<pattern>:inst<element>(<original face>)`
  (the chamfers' and fillets' faces too, not `<pattern>:fillet(…)`). A
  failure of the kernel is the pattern's: the roundings are not tried
  copy by copy. `original_bodies` and the features' own participants do
  not apply: the copies act on the bodies the features changed.

### pattern_at_points

```json
{"type":"pattern_at_points",
 "objects":{"type":"features","features":["F3","F4"]},
 "targets":[{"point":{"sketch":"F5","point":"p1"}},
            {"point":"F6","occurrence":"O1/O2"}],
 "context":"", "compute":"adjust"}
```

Repeats bodies (`objects.type:"bodies", bodies:[BodyUid]`), features
(`features:[FeatureUid]`), or shared component occurrences
(`objects.type:"components", occurrences:["O1/O2",…]`). Body and feature
sources belong to the feature's component; component sources may be elsewhere
in the assembly, provided the new occurrence does not create a component cycle.
Originals remain. Each target adds one translated copy of the entire source
group, preserving relative positions and orientation. Features replay their
tools and operations, including grouped fillets/chamfers, rather than duplicating
the resulting cut body. An unreachable feature copy fails with its target number.

The anchor is automatic unless `anchor:{point:GeomRef, occurrence?:"O1"}` is
given. Remove `anchor` to restore Automatic. The deterministic policies are:

- Components: centre of the axis-aligned bounds of the selected occurrence
  origins; one component uses its local origin at its current placement.
- Feature groups containing holes: centre of the bounds of all selected holes'
  placement/start points. Other selected features, including fillets and chamfers,
  do not move this anchor. Hole depth never substitutes a tool midpoint.
- Feature groups of threads only (mitcad#733): centre of the bounds of the
  middles of the faces they thread (`thread_faces`); the copies go on the faces
  at those faces' places moved to each target, as a pattern or mirror of a
  thread alone does.
- Other bodies/features: centre of the union of source body/tool bounds. A group
  consisting only of finishing features uses the bodies those features changed.

`point` is the normal geometry reference: a sketch point, construction point,
vertex, origin, fixed point, or a resolvable edge centre/midpoint. Keep references
to retain associativity. `occurrence` names the point's frame by an absolute path
from the root; an explicit empty path means the root. If omitted, coordinates
belong to the feature's component. `context` identifies the feature component's
displayed occurrence; if omitted, its first occurrence is used. Invalid explicit
paths never fall back to the origin. Point and source edits recompute placements;
missing or unavailable references produce a failed feature without stale copies.

Duplicate references are rejected. Distinct references resolving to the same
position, or to the source anchor, fail explicitly (distance below 1e-7 mm).
Other geometric overlap follows normal pattern semantics: separate body or
component instances remain separate; feature tools use their normal booleans.
One to 10000 targets are supported. Reordering component targets preserves each
instance's UID; removing a target removes its occurrence. Suppression, rollback
and failure make generated occurrences unavailable, including to downstream moves
and joints. Undo and design files preserve ownership and shared definitions.

Preview adds `anchor:{point:[x,y,z],world:[x,y,z],mode,policy}` and the normal
pattern `elements` (identity first). `mode` is `automatic` or `selected`; `policy`
is `component_origins`, `hole_placements`, `thread_faces`, `source_bounds` or `selected_point`.
`instances:[{body,occurrence,transform,visible}]` lists added occurrence/body pairs
with 4×4 world-transform rows. `removed_instances:[{body,occurrence}]` removes
existing pairs during an edit preview; unchanged shared body IDs stay in `bodies`.

### mirror

```json
{"type": "mirror", "objects": {"type": "bodies", "bodies": ["F2.b0"]},
 "plane": "yz", "combine": false, "compute": "adjust"}
```

A pattern of one copy, element 1 (`<mirror>:inst1(<face>)`). Mirrored
bodies are new bodies; `combine` joins each to its original when they
touch. Mirrored features reflect their finished tool (never a rebuilt
one); `original_bodies`, and fillets and chamfers among the features, as
for patterns. `scale` and `scale_groups` (mitcad#539) as for patterns
with two elements: the image scaled by the factor about its own centre
(FreeCAD's Scaled transformation after a mirror).

The mirror image of a nearly symmetric body lies on the body almost
everywhere, nearly but not exactly, and a boolean of the whole shapes
intersects every such pair of faces (minutes for free-form faces, often
with a wrong result). `combine` therefore joins an image that differs
from its body in at most half of the faces of each only where they
differ by more than 0.1 mm (`Kernel::join_near_copy`, mitcad#88):
material of the image within 0.1 mm of the body's faces is left out, and
an image that differs nowhere by more gives the body unchanged. Any other
image is joined whole. `MITCAD_NO_NEAR_COPIES=1` joins every image whole
(for comparisons).

### combine

```json
{"type": "combine", "target": "F2.b0", "tools": ["F4.b0"], "operation": "join",
 "keep_tools": false, "new_component": false}
```

`join` gives the target one body of the union (several solids when they
do not touch); `cut` removes the tools' union, the first piece in
geometric order keeping the target's id and the others becoming bodies of
the combine (a piece with less than a millionth of the volume of the
largest stays in that piece's body as a lump, as with an extrusion's cut;
after an upstream edit the pieces keep their ids:
[Body ids of a split's pieces](#body-ids-of-a-splits-pieces));
`intersect` keeps the common volume as the target (fails
when empty). Tools are removed unless kept; faces keep their names
through the boolean. With `new_component` the target goes into a new
component.

The target is a body of the combine's component; a tool may be a body of
another component where an occurrence shows it (mitcad#104, mitcad#544):
a tool entry `{"body": …, "occurrence": …}` instead of an id:

```json
{"type": "combine", "target": "F7.b0", "operation": "cut", "keep_tools": true,
 "tools": [{"body": "F2.b0", "occurrence": "O1", "context": "O2"},
           {"body": "F2.b0", "occurrence": "O3", "context": "O2"}]}
```

`occurrence` is the occurrence path to the tool's component, `context`
the one to the combine's (default: its first path); the model keeps them
as an `OccurrenceLink` ([Geometry of other
components](#geometry-of-other-components)), `source` and `target`. The
tool is read there and moved into the combine's coordinates by the
occurrences' placements at the combine's point of the timeline, so the
combine follows when either occurrence moves. A body is a tool once per
occurrence: two occurrences of one component (two screws of one part)
are two tools, each cutting (joining, intersecting) where it is and each
following its own occurrence; the occurrences not listed do nothing. The
same body in the same occurrence twice is refused (`body F2.b0 in O1 is
listed more than once`). A consumed tool (without `keep_tools`) leaves
its own component, once however many occurrences it was a tool in. The
target stays a body of the combine's component: a cut changes that
component's definition, so every occurrence of it shows the cut.

A plain id is a body of the combine's own component, or, as files of
earlier versions and imports write it, a body of another component whose
link `tool_links` holds (saved and read as it was written):

```json
{"type": "combine", "target": "F7.b0", "tools": ["F2.b0"], "operation": "cut",
 "keep_tools": true, "tool_links": {"F2.b0": {"source": "O1", "target": "O2"}}}
```

A `tool_links` entry for a body that is not a plain-id tool is refused
(`linked but not a tool`); a tool of another component without an
occurrence or a link fails the combine (`body F2.b0 (from Extrude1)
belongs to A; …`). Paste New, moves into components and occurrences
moved into others carry both forms' links. Tests:
`core/model-tests/links/src/link_tests.rs` (`a_combine_cuts_with_a_body_in_two_occurrences_each_where_it_is`,
`a_combine_joins_a_body_in_two_occurrences`,
`a_combine_of_an_earlier_version_with_tool_links_loads_and_recomputes_as_before`,
`paste_new_keeps_a_combines_tools_in_occurrences`).

### move, align, scale

```json
{"type": "move", "bodies": ["F2.b0"], "copy": false,
 "transform": {"type": "translate_xyz", "x": 10, "y": 5, "z": 0}}
```

`transform`: `{"type": "free", "matrix": [[r00, r01, r02, tx], [r10, …],
[r20, …]]}` (a rotation and a translation), `translate_xyz` (`x`, `y`,
`z`), `translate_along` (`axis`, `distance`), `rotate` (`axis`, `angle`,
right-handed), `point_to_point` (`from`, `to`), `point_to_position`
(`point`, `x`, `y`, `z`). A moved body keeps its id and face names; with
`copy` the moved copies are new bodies `<move>.b<j>` with faces
`<move>:inst1(<face>)` (a copy that does not move is a copy and paste).
A rotation and a translation (a `move` or an `align`) place the body as
a location on its own shape (mitcad#838, `Kernel::move_shape`): its faces
keep their geometry and the display meshes they have, so the view meshes
nothing again; the body before the move is not changed. A mirror or a
scale makes a transformed copy.

A point or an axis may be geometry of another component, picked where an
occurrence shows it (mitcad#699): `from_occurrence`, `to_occurrence`,
`point_occurrence` or `axis_occurrence` beside the reference is that
occurrence's absolute path from the root (`"O1/O4"`; `""` the root), as
`pattern_at_points` gives its points' occurrences. `move`,
`move_occurrence` and `move_face` take them alike:

```json
{"type": "move_occurrence", "occurrences": ["O2"],
 "transform": {"type": "point_to_point",
   "from": {"body": "F2.b0", "vertex": "V{…}"}, "from_occurrence": "O2",
   "to": {"body": "F2.b0", "vertex": "V{…}"}, "to_occurrence": "O1"}}
```

The reference is resolved in the component the path ends in (a vertex
of its body, a sketch point or construction point of it), placed where
the occurrence puts it at the feature's point of the timeline, and taken
into the coordinates of the feature's component (its first occurrence).
So two copies of one component are told apart, and the move follows when
either occurrence moves later. A point on an occurrence the feature
itself moves is where it was before this motion. Sketches and
construction geometry must be in the component the path ends in
(`Sketch1 is in B, not in Root`); a path that leads nowhere fails the
feature. Without an occurrence a reference is in the feature's
component's coordinates, as in earlier versions (and a body of another
component fails the feature: `body F2.b0 (from Extrude1) belongs to
Part; …`); definitions are written back without the fields they did not
have. Moving an occurrence a path runs through to another parent is
refused. Tests: `core/model-tests/assembly/src/component_tests.rs`
(`a_move_of_an_occurrence_takes_points_where_their_occurrences_place_them`,
`a_move_of_an_occurrence_tells_the_copies_of_a_component_apart`,
`a_move_takes_a_sketch_point_of_another_component_by_its_occurrence`,
`a_move_without_occurrences_takes_its_points_in_its_component_as_before`).

```json
{"type": "align", "bodies": ["F2.b0"],
 "from": {"type": "plane", "plane": {"body": "F2.b0", "face": "F2:start(…)"}},
 "to": {"type": "plane", "plane": "xy"}, "flip": false, "angle": 0}
```

`from` and `to` are `{"type": "point", "point": …}`, `{"type": "axis",
"axis": …}` or `{"type": "plane", "plane": …}`: a point goes onto a
point, line or plane; an axis onto an axis (direction and line; circle
centres meet); a plane onto a plane with the normals opposite (faces
against each other) and origins together (a face's middle). `flip` turns
the moved geometry over; `angle` turns about the target axis or normal.

```json
{"type": "scale", "bodies": ["F2.b0"], "point": "origin",
 "scale": {"type": "uniform", "factor": 2}}
```

`scale`: `{"type": "uniform", "factor"}` or `{"type": "non_uniform", "x",
"y", "z"}` along the model axes; factors greater than zero. A non-uniform
scale turns faces into B-splines (names stay).

### box, cylinder, sphere, torus

```json
{"type": "box", "plane": "xy", "corner": [0, 0],
 "length": 30, "width": 20, "height": 10, "symmetric": false, "operation": "new_body", "participants": []}
{"type": "cylinder", "plane": …, "center": [u, v], "diameter": 20, "height": 30, "symmetric": false, "operation": …}
{"type": "sphere", "plane": …, "center": [u, v], "diameter": 30, "operation": …}
{"type": "torus", "plane": …, "center": [u, v], "diameter": 40, "section_diameter": 10,
 "position": "on_center" | "inside" | "outside", "operation": …}
```

Placed on the plane at plane coordinates (the frame a sketch on the plane
has), height or axis along the plane's normal (negative height: against
it). Each coordinate of `corner` and `center` is a number or, like the
sizes, a value (mitcad#689): an expression or a parameter, such as
`"corner": ["-L/2", "-W/2"]`, which becomes a dimension of the feature
(slots `corner.x`, `corner.y`, `center.x`, `center.y`) and moves the
primitive when the parameters it uses change. A plain number stays a
number, without a parameter, as documents and imports have always
written it, so stored documents load unchanged; the `feature` query
gives a value's parameter name. `operation` and `participants` as for
extrude. Faces:
`<feature>:bottom`, `top`, `side0`..`side3` for a box (side0 at the
corner's y, side1 at x + length, counter-clockwise) and `side0` for
curved faces.

### bounding_solid

```json
{"type": "bounding_solid", "bodies": ["F2.b0", "F4.b0"], "margin": 5}
{"type": "bounding_solid", "margin": 0}
```

A new body (`BoundingSolid<n>`, mitcad#460): the box around the bodies,
grown by `margin` on every side (a negative margin shrinks it; one that
leaves no box fails the feature). `bodies` empty or left out: every body
of the feature's component at its point of the timeline (an earlier
bounding solid too). The box is aligned with the component's axes and
holds the bodies' exact geometry (`Kernel::bounding_box`, the tight box
of their faces, not of a display mesh); it is built with the box
primitive (`Kernel::primitive`), so its faces are named as a box's:
`<feature>:bottom` at the lowest z, `top` at the highest, `side0` at the
lowest y, `side1` at the highest x, `side2` at the highest y and `side3`
at the lowest x. The bodies are only read: the box is built again from
them on every recompute and follows their edits and the margin's. A body
is listed once and must be of the feature's component; no bodies at all
fails the feature. Patterns and mirrors cannot repeat it as a feature (it
has no tool); its body is patterned, mirrored or moved like any other.

Tests: `core.model` (`features::bounding_solid`, mock kernel),
`cli.bounding_solid` (OCCT) and the `.solidcraft` import's
`bounding-solid` test design.

### construction_plane, construction_axis, construction_point

```json
{"type": "construction_plane", "definition": {"type": "offset", "plane": "xy", "distance": 10}}
```

Named `Plane1`, `Axis1`, `Point1`; they make no bodies. Their result is a
datum, which follows parameter edits and is cached like a body.

A construction plane may take the faces, edges and vertices its
definition names from bodies of other components (mitcad#196): `"links":
{"F2.b0": {"source": "O1", "target": ""}}` (an `OccurrenceLink` per body,
as an extrusion's `object_links`, [Geometry of other
components](#geometry-of-other-components)) reads the body in its
component and moves it into the plane's coordinates by the occurrences'
placements at the plane's point of the timeline, so that a midplane
between faces of two components lies where the design places them and
follows when they move. Without a link another component's body is
out of reach and the plane fails.

| Feature | `definition.type` | Fields | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| plane | `offset` | `plane`, `distance` | the plane moved along its normal |
| plane | `angle` | `line`, `angle`, `plane` | through the line, the plane turned about the line (right-handed) |
| plane | `tangent` | `face` (cylinder or cone), `angle`, `plane` | touching the face where the plane's normal, turned about the axis, leaves it |
| plane | `midplane` | `plane1`, `plane2` | halfway (parallel: the first's normal) or the bisector with normal n1 - n2 |
| plane | `two_edges` | `line1`, `line2` | lines in one plane; normal d1 × d2 |
| plane | `three_points` | `point1`, `point2`, `point3` | normal (p2 - p1) × (p3 - p1), x along p2 - p1 |
| plane | `edge_and_point` | `line`, `point` | normal d × (p - o) |
| plane | `tangent_at_point` | `face`, `point` | tangent where the face is nearest to the point |
| plane | `along_path` | `path`, `distance`, `physical` | normal to the path at a fraction (slot `definition.fraction`, unitless) or with `physical` at a length in mm (slot `definition.distance`); a path is edges, a sketch curve, a fixed line or `{"sketch": "F1", "curves": ["c1", "c2"]}`, two or more lines and arcs of a sketch joined end to end, running from the free end of the first listed curve (the first curve's own direction round a closed chain); a corner takes the tangent of the curve before it |
| plane | `normal_at_point` | `path`, `point` | normal to the path where it is nearest to the point |
| plane | `fixed` | `origin`, `x_axis`, `y_axis` (numbers) | a non-parametric plane (`setByPlane` in .f3d designs, the importer's fallback) |
| plane | `offset_through_point` | `plane`, `point` | parallel to the plane through the point (the plane's frame moved along its normal) |
| axis | `circular_face` | `face` (cylinder, cone, torus) | its axis (along its largest component) |
| axis | `perpendicular_at_point` | `face`, `point` | the face normal at the face point nearest to the point |
| axis | `normal_to_face_at_point` | `face` (a face, or a plane: an origin plane, a construction plane or a fixed plane, which stands for a planar face), `point` | through the point, along that normal |
| axis | `two_planes` | `plane1`, `plane2` | their intersection, along n1 × n2 |
| axis | `two_points` | `point1`, `point2` | from the first to the second |
| axis | `edge` | `edge` (a line) | along the edge |
| axis | `fixed` | `origin`, `direction` | a non-parametric axis |
| point | `point` | `point` | a vertex or another point |
| point | `two_edges` | `line1`, `line2` | where the lines (extended) meet |
| point | `three_planes` | `plane1`, `plane2`, `plane3` | their common point |
| point | `center` | `entity` (circle edge, sphere or torus face) | its centre |
| point | `edge_and_plane` | `line`, `plane` | where the line meets the plane |
| point | `along_path` | `path`, `distance`, `physical` | as the plane along a path |
| point | `fixed` | `point` | a non-parametric point |

Fractions and lengths beyond a path's ends continue straight along the
end tangent. A plane's frame (`x_axis`, `y_axis`) is what a sketch on it
uses: offsets and angles move the reference frame; other planes take the
model X axis projected onto them (Y when X is along the normal). Inputs
that do not fit (parallel lines, collinear points, lines that pass each
other) fail the feature with a message. The `preview` of a construction
feature adds its `datum`.

### base

```json
{"type": "base", "source": "bracket.step",
 "bodies": [{"name": "Bracket", "color": [0.8, 0.8, 0.8],
             "brep": {"format": "occt", "compression": "zlib", "size": 6146, "data": "eJy1V..."}},
            {"name": "Scan", "mesh": true, "brep": {…}}],
 "operation": "new_body", "participants": []}
```

Bodies without history: imported files, the bodies of .f3d files and the
.f3d importer's fallback (`features/base.rs`). Normally created with
`import_file` or the [shape API](#base-features-from-shapes), not written
by hand.

- `bodies`: B-rep data (OCCT's binary format, zlib-compressed, base64;
  `compression` may be `"none"`) with an optional `name` and `color`
  (sRGB, 0..1); `mesh` marks a mesh body (triangles only, from STL or
  OBJ). In a project the data is a reference into the project's store
  (`sha256` instead of `data`, see [Design files](#design-files)).
- `operation`: `new_body` (default; body i is `<feature>.b<i>`, named
  after its `name`, made unique with ` (2)`, …), or `join`, `cut`,
  `intersect` with `participants` (all bodies when empty), with the same
  results as an extrusion's. Mesh bodies can only be new bodies; placed
  by a moved or turned occurrence they are measured and reported where
  the design shows them, like other bodies.
- `replaces`: `["F2.b0", …]` (new bodies only): body i takes the id and
  display name of the i-th listed body, so later features that use that
  body continue on the new one; listed bodies beyond the new ones are
  removed. The importers' fallbacks use it.
- Faces are `<feature>:import(<j>)`, j counting the faces of all bodies in
  order (body 0's first) in the kernel's face order, so the names stay as
  long as the data does. Edges and vertices follow:
  `E{F4:import(0)|F4:import(3)}`.

### Component features

```json
{"type": "component_from_bodies", "bodies": ["F2.b0"]}
{"type": "move_occurrence", "occurrences": ["O2"],
 "transform": {"type": "translate_xyz", "x": 0, "y": 0, "z": 30}}
{"type": "capture_position", "positions": [{"occurrence": "O2",
 "transform": [[1, 0, 0, 0], [0, 1, 0, -50], [0, 0, 1, 0]]}]}
```

`move_occurrence` takes the motions of `move` (rigid ones only) and is
named `Move<n>` like moves of bodies; its points and axes may be on
other components with the occurrence they were picked in
(`from_occurrence` …, [move, align, scale](#move-align-scale),
mitcad#699), a point on a moved occurrence where it was before the
move; `capture_position` is
`Position<n>`. See [Components and occurrences](#components-and-occurrences).

### Mesh bodies in surface operations

A mesh body (triangles without surfaces: STL and OBJ files, the face sets
of IFC files and the meshes of other imported models; `kind` `mesh` in the
`bodies` query) has no surfaces for the operations that intersect, offset
or round faces (mitcad#399; OCCT's boolean read a face's null surface and
crashed on Windows, mitcad#392). The features refuse one before the
geometry kernel gets it (`features/surface_bodies.rs`), with an error
naming the body:
`body F5.b0 (from Base1) is a mesh body (triangles without surfaces), which Combine cannot use; it works on solid and surface bodies`.

- Refused where a feature names it: `combine`'s target and tools; the
  `participants` of `extrude`, `revolve`, `sweep`, `loft`, `pipe`, `coil`,
  `helix`, `rib`, `web`, `hole`, `emboss` (its face's body too), `base` and the patterns' features; an
  extent up to its face or the body; the body of `fillet`, `chamfer`, the
  face features (`shell`, `draft`, `offset_face`, `delete_face`,
  `replace_face`, `split_face`), `split_body` and `thread`; a face of it as
  a hole's face, a loft section, a sweep's guide surface, a draft's fixed
  plane, a replace target or a splitting tool; a pattern of its faces; and
  a `mirror` or pattern of bodies with `combine`.
- Left out where an operation takes all bodies (Join, Cut or Intersect
  without `participants`, a cut's `cut_scope` targets, Extrude's automatic
  operation): mesh bodies are not cut or joined, the others are.
- Taken as they are: moves, copies, patterns and mirrors of bodies without
  `combine`, scales, `remove_body`, components, appearances, measurements,
  physical properties, interference (which skips them), Section Analysis
  (which cuts their triangles, mitcad#392) and export.

The geometry facade refuses faces without surfaces too
(`detail::require_surfaces`: booleans, unions, fillets, chamfers, face
operations, splits, removed material and joins of near copies, for every
other caller such as the importers): `join: a mesh body (faces without
surfaces) cannot be used; the operation works on solid and surface
bodies`. A tool's contacts take a mesh body as apart, a mesh face's
`face_geometry` is `mesh` (not planar), and a sketch's section of a mesh
face is an error.

### Body ids of a split's pieces

A feature that leaves a body in several pieces (a Cut or Intersect of
`extrude`, `revolve` and the other profile features, of `box` and the
other primitives and of the copies of patterns and mirrors; a `combine`
cut; `split_body`; a cut's `cut_scope`) gives the body's id to one piece
and new ids of the feature (`F4.b0`, `F4.b1`, …) to the others. The first
time, the pieces come in geometric order (along a planar splitting tool's
normal for `split_body`) and the first keeps the body. The feature then
remembers each piece's volume and centre of mass, and later evaluations
give the ids by matching the new pieces with the remembered ones
(mitcad#408, `core/model/src/features/pieces.rs`), so an upstream edit
that changes the order or the number of the pieces does not hand a later
feature's body (a `remove_body`'s, a fillet's, a combine's) to another
piece:

- A piece matches a remembered one when its volume is within a factor of
  two of it and its centre moved less than a quarter of the size of the
  pieces (the diagonal of their bounding box). The closest pairs are taken
  first (volume change and shift, each 1 at the limit, added); ties go to
  the remembered piece listed first, then to the piece first in geometric
  order.
- The body that was split keeps its id for the piece that matches it.
  Without one it takes the piece left that comes closest to it, and every
  later feature that names the body warns (timeline status `warning`):
  `body F2.b0 is now another piece of what Extrude2 split it into (volume
  40000 → 8000 mm³, centre moved 0 mm)`. The warning lasts while that
  result stands (until the split is evaluated again). When every piece
  matches another remembered piece, the body is gone.
- A remembered piece that no piece matches is no longer made: its id goes
  to no other piece, and new pieces get new ids. `remove_body` passes
  such a body by with a warning (`body F4.b1 is a piece Extrude2 no longer
  makes (its pieces changed): nothing to remove`); any other feature that
  names it fails with the same words. A piece like it that comes back gets
  the id again.
- A body left whole that never was in pieces is not remembered: when a
  later edit splits it, its pieces come in geometric order as the first
  time. Pieces the geometry kernel cannot measure (no volume) also come in
  geometric order.

What a feature remembers is saved with it in the design file, so a design
opens with the ids it was saved with:

```json
{"uid": "F4", "name": "Extrude2", "type": "extrude", …,
 "split_pieces": [{"body": "F2.b0", "size": 70.71,
   "pieces": [{"body": "F2.b0", "volume": 40000, "centre": [25, 20, 10]},
              {"body": "F4.b0", "volume": 20, "centre": [54.5, 0.5, 10], "gone": true}]}]}
```

`body` is the body split (`pass` numbers the splits of one body when the
feature splits it more than once, as a pattern's copies do), `size` the
diagonal of the pieces' bounding box (mm), each piece's `volume` (mm³) and
`centre` (mm, in its component's coordinates), and `gone` for a piece the
last evaluation did not make. A file without `split_pieces` (saved before
mitcad#408) opens in geometric order and takes it on its first recompute.
The document takes what each evaluation remembers without an undo step;
it is an input of the feature's evaluation like a parameter, and a result
fits both what it was evaluated with and what it leaves, so the recompute
cache and the result store reuse results as before. Sheet-metal cuts
(`sheet_cut`) keep the geometric order. Tests: `core.model`
(`piece_ids_tests.rs`, `features::pieces`).

A `remove_body` of every piece below a volume (`{"smaller_than": …}`) is
not offered: a definition's values are lengths, angles or unitless
numbers, and a size filter over a component's bodies would take small
bodies that are no fragments as well; with the ids kept, the named pieces
stay right.

### The extended tool of a split or trim (mitcad#712)

A preview of `split_body`, `split_face` or `trim_surface` with `extend`
(the default) and a plane or face tool shows the tool as the feature
extends it: the preview reports `"tool": true` and `preview_tool_shape()`
returns it (with `tool_instances`), so that a display can show where the
cut runs. It is the faces the operation itself cuts with (a plane as a
face across the box, a face grown along its surface: the same
construction, `Kernel::extended_tool`, the OCCT kernel's
`geometry::extended_tool`), clipped to the box of the bodies split (of
every body of a `split_body` together) grown on every side by 5 % of its
diagonal, at least 1 mm. A `split_body` with further tools (`more_tools`)
shows every plane or face tool, in one compound. Without `extend`, with a
body or sketch curves as the tool, or where the kernel cannot make it (a
tool that does not reach the box), there is none; the split itself is not
affected.

Only a preview makes it (`Evaluate::preview_tool`, for the feature
`Cache::preview` names while `Document::preview_state` computes): it is
made again for every preview of the feature, also when the split's result
comes from the cache, and is kept in the preview's result
(`Recomputed::preview_tool`), never in the feature's output, the cache or
the result store. Recomputes, commits (which reuse the preview's result)
and imports do not make it. Tests: `core.model` (`f2_tests.rs`,
`surface_modelling_tests.rs`), `geometry` (`test_split.cpp`).

## Commands

`command` takes one command object (`{"cmd": "<name>", …}`) or an array
of them. An array runs in order, each command its own undo step, and
stops at the first failure (`commands[2]: …`); the result is the array of
results.

Every result has `"recomputed"`: the number of features the command
evaluated (results from the cache, including a preview's, are not
counted), and `"error"`: the first failed feature (`"Fillet1: …"`) or
null. A command that took results from the [result store](#result-store)
has `"restored"`, their number. A failed feature does not reject the
command: it is skipped, and the `timeline` query shows its error. When
any feature fails, the result also has `"failed_features"`: each one and
whether this command added or edited it ([Failed features in command
results](#failed-features-in-command-results)).

### Timeline and parameters

| Command | Fields | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `add_feature` | `def`, `name` (optional), `component` (optional: a component's uid or name; the active component when left out), `after` or `index` (optional: where in the timeline, see [Adding a feature in the middle of the timeline](#adding-a-feature-in-the-middle-of-the-timeline)) | `uid`, `name`, `parameters` (created); for a new-component operation placed beside a component that takes no components `placed_in`, `instead_of`, `placement_warning` ([Design policy](#design-policy)) |
| `edit_feature` | `uid`, `def` (same type) | `parameters` (created); when the edit makes a new component placed beside a component that takes no components `placed_in`, `instead_of`, `placement_warning` ([Design policy](#design-policy)) |
| `delete_feature` | `uid`, `dependents` (default false) | `deleted`: uids in timeline order |
| `suppress_feature` | `uid`, `suppressed` (default true), or `expression` (a condition the suppression follows; [Bindings](#bindings-values-from-expressions)) | |
| `reorder_feature` | `uid`, `index` (new timeline index) | |
| `rename_feature` | `uid`, `name` | |
| `rename_body` | `uid` (body), `name` | |
| `set_marker` | `position`: the number of features before the marker; `temporary` (default false) | |
| `add_parameter` | `name`, `value` (number in mm, or an expression) or `expression`, `unit` (optional), `comment`, `min`, `max`, `step`, `strict` ([Parameter limits](#parameter-limits)) | |
| `set_parameter` | `name`, and any of: `value` (number in mm or rad, written in the parameter's unit, or an expression) or `expression`, `unit`, `comment`, `favorite`, `min`, `max`, `step`, `strict` ([Parameter limits](#parameter-limits)) | `changed`: parameters whose values changed, the text parameters whose texts changed among them, whether `value` or `expression` was given |
| `rename_parameter` | `name`, `new_name` | |
| `delete_parameter` | `name` (only when no feature and no other parameter uses it) | |
| `set_units` | `length`: the document's length unit (`mm`, `cm`, `m`, `in`, `ft`, …) | `changed` |
| `group_features` | `features` (uids of a run of features next to each other in the timeline, in any order, none in a group yet), `name` (default the next free `Group<n>`) | `name` |
| `ungroup` | `name` | the features stay |
| `rename_group` | `name`, `new_name` | |
| `recompute` | | |
| `sketch.*` | see [Sketch commands](#sketch-commands) | |

- New features go in at the timeline marker, which moves after them
  (with `after` or `index`, at that place before the marker).
- `add_parameter` and `set_parameter` reject commands containing both
  `value` and `expression`. `set_parameter` also accepts only `unit`,
  `comment` or `favorite`; a unit-only edit keeps the existing expression.
- Parameters copied from another document retain that document's default
  units for implicit units inside expressions. The `parameters` query and
  saved parameter record expose them as `expression_units` (`length`,
  `angle`). Editing the expression or applying a configuration keeps these
  defaults; the parameter's own `unit` still takes precedence for its
  dimensions. Changing the destination document's units does not reinterpret
  these copied expressions. Their parameter references remain editable.
- `delete_feature` refuses while other features refer to the feature
  (`Extrude1 is used by Fillet1; …`); with `"dependents": true` they go
  too (the `dependents` query lists them).
- `reorder_feature` refuses a position where a feature would come before
  something it refers to (the `can_reorder` query asks first).
- Features after the marker are rolled back (not evaluated); suppressed
  features are skipped.
- `set_marker` with `"temporary": true` evaluates a command editor's
  rollback without adding an undo step, dropping redo or changing the
  revision. The editor must restore the original marker with the same flag
  before committing an edit or saving. Cancellation leaves the marker,
  history, revision and displayed results unchanged. Ordinary marker moves
  keep their existing undo behavior.
- After a command, new bodies get display names (`Body1`, `Body2`, … the
  next free number), which are saved.
- A timeline group stays a run: deleted features leave it, a feature
  added or moved between its members joins it, a member moved away
  leaves it (the only member takes the group along), an empty group goes.
  Saved as `"groups": [{"name", "features"}]`; a favourite parameter as
  `"favorite": true`.

### Undo, revisions and the saved state

| Command | Fields | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `undo`, `redo` | | `label` of the step, or null |
| `begin_command` | | `token`: an opaque string identifying a checkpoint of the current definition, revision, saved state and both history stacks |
| `restore_command` | `token` | restores that checkpoint after its scene recomputes successfully; keeps the token for retries |
| `discard_command` | `token` | releases the checkpoint without changing the current definition or history |
| `merge_undo` | `depth`: the undo depth before the action, `label` | merges the undo steps after `depth` into one step named `label` (clears redo); `undo_depth`. Refuses a `depth` past the last step |
| `mark_saved` | | `revision`; the definition state is the design file's (saved or opened). No undo step, nothing recomputed |

- Undo and redo restore the whole definition (parameters, timeline,
  marker, body names). Cached results make them fast.
- An asynchronous frontend begins one command checkpoint before temporary
  marker moves or applied sketch previews. Cancel restores and then discards
  it; accept discards it. Restore recovers the exact preexisting redo stack,
  even when a command completed before cancellation reached the worker.
  A failed or cancelled restore changes nothing and retains the token for
  retry. Only one checkpoint may be active per document; stale tokens are
  rejected. Tokens and newly allocated revision numbers are never reused.
  Checkpoints are session state, absent from saved designs; finish the
  command before marking a saved file or replacing the document.
- One user action is often several commands (a rectangle snapped to the
  origin is `sketch.add_point`, `sketch.rectangle` and a `coincident`
  constraint; a drag a `sketch.drag` per mouse move). The caller reads
  `undo_depth` (`document` query) before the action, runs its commands
  and merges them, or undoes back to that depth to take the action back.
- Every accepted command gives the state a new revision, also one that
  recomputes nothing (a rename, a named view); a rejected command, a
  command that changes nothing, a recompute and a preview keep it. Undo
  and redo take back the revision of the state they restore, so undoing
  to the saved state is unmodified again; `merge_undo` keeps the current
  revision. A new command after undo gets a new revision even when it
  makes the same definition. `update_links` gives a new revision when it
  takes new bodies (no undo step).
- A new document is not `modified`. A design file read
  (`Document::from_json`, the bridge's `load_document`) is modified until
  `mark_saved`, since it need not be the file it will be saved to (an
  imported design, recovered work). Saving (`to_json`) does not mark it
  saved by itself.
- `Document::to_json_with_marker(marker)` (bridge `to_json_with_marker`)
  writes the design file with another marker without changing the
  document (autosave while an edit has rolled the timeline back).

### Visibility and display

| Command | Fields | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `set_feature_visible` | `uid` (a sketch or a construction plane, axis or point), `visible` | undo step `Show Sketch1` / `Hide Plane1` unless nothing changes; nothing recomputed |
| `set_body_visible` | `uid`, `visible`, or `expression` (a condition; [Bindings](#bindings-values-from-expressions)) | |
| `set_body_material` | `uid`, `material` (a built-in id below or one of the design's [materials](#materials), or null: its component's default, steel when none is set), `appearance` (`replace`: the material's appearance becomes the body's; `keep`: the body keeps its own; left out: replace unless the body's appearance was set by hand, see [Materials](#materials)), or `expression` (a text naming the material; [Bindings](#bindings-values-from-expressions)) | undo step `Set Material of Body1` (material and appearance together); nothing recomputed |
| `set_body_appearance` | `uid`, `appearance` (an id of the library or the document, see [Appearances](#appearances), or null for the default look), or `expression` (a text naming the appearance; [Bindings](#bindings-values-from-expressions)) | |
| `set_origin_visible` | `visible` | the root's Origin folder shown; undo step `Show Origin` / `Hide Origin` unless nothing changes; nothing recomputed |
| `set_isolation` | `items`: `{"body": "F3.b0", "occurrence": "O1"}` (a body, in the occurrence that places it, none for the root's) or `{"occurrence": "O1/O4"}` (an occurrence by its path); none: unisolate | undo step `Isolate 2 item(s)` / `Unisolate`; an occurrence that is not there is refused |

- Body commands are undo steps (`Hide Body1`, `Show Body1`, `Set Material
  of Body1`, …) unless nothing changes; the body must exist at the
  marker. The `bodies` query and the design file list `"visible":
  false`, `"material"` and `"appearance"` when set, and `"appearance_set_by_hand":
  true` for an appearance that is not its material's. Built-in materials:
  `steel` (7.85 g/cm³, the default), `stainless_steel`, `cast_iron`,
  `aluminum`, `copper`, `brass`, `titanium`, `abs`, `pla`, `nylon`,
  `polycarbonate`, `glass`, `water` (`core/model-base/src/analysis.rs`,
  `core/model/src/material.rs`); a design's own materials and components'
  default materials are in [Materials](#materials).
- Sketches and construction features: by default a sketch is hidden
  while a feature uses it (a profile, curves or points; suppressed
  features and those after the marker count too) and shown while none
  does; construction geometry is shown. A light bulb set with
  `set_feature_visible` wins; it is kept and saved with the feature
  (`"visible": true` or `false`) only where it differs from the default,
  so showing a hidden sketch that no feature uses forgets it.
- The command that gives a sketch its first consumer or takes its last
  one away forgets the sketch's light bulb in its own undo step: the new
  extrusion's sketch hides, and shows again when that extrusion is
  deleted, even if it was hidden by hand meanwhile. A second consumer
  keeps a light bulb set by hand. Deleting a feature forgets its
  visibility; `paste_new` and copied designs start with the defaults.
  Code: `document/browser.rs`.
- The display state (Origin folder, isolation) is per user: the design
  file keeps it as `"display": {"origin": true, "isolated": [...]}` (left
  out when nothing is set), and a project keeps it outside the design
  file ([Design files](#design-files)). Isolation lists only the items
  there at the marker; none left isolates nothing.
- Occurrences have `set_occurrence_visible` ([Components and
  occurrences](#components-and-occurrences)).

### Named views

| Command | Fields | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `add_named_view` | `name` (the next free `NamedView<n>` when left out), `eye`, `target` (points, mm), `up`, `perspective` (default false), `height` (mm of the model the view shows at the target), `replace` (default false: a name in use is refused) | `name`; undo step `Add Named View Detail` (`Change Named View Detail` when replaced) unless nothing changes |
| `rename_named_view` | `name`, `new_name` | |
| `delete_named_view` | `name` | |

Named views change no geometry and recompute nothing; they are saved in
the design file (`"views"`, left out when there are none). The view
named `Home` is the document's home view.

### Analyses

Section analyses (mitcad#41) and print analyses (mitcad#620) kept in the
document (`core/model/src/document/analyses.rs`): the browser's Analysis
folder.

| Command | Fields | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `add_analysis` | `def`, `name` (the next free `Section<n>`, or `Print<n>` for a print analysis, when left out) | `name`; undo step `Add Section1`. It is shown and the others are hidden |
| `edit_analysis` | `name`, `def`, `visible` (optional: true shows it and hides the others, false hides it; as it was when left out) | undo step `Edit Section1` unless nothing changes |
| `set_analysis_visible` | `name`, `visible` | undo step `Show Section1` / `Hide Section1` unless nothing changes; showing hides the others |
| `rename_analysis` | `name`, `new_name` | undo step `Rename Section1` |
| `delete_analysis` | `name` | undo step `Delete Section1` |

A `def` is `{"type": "section", "plane": <plane reference>, "offset": mm,
"flip": bool}` (`offset` default 0, `flip` default false): the bodies cut
at `plane` moved by `offset` along its normal, the side the normal points
to cut away; `flip` reverses the normal. The plane is a [plane
reference](#references-to-geometry) (origin plane, construction plane,
planar face, fixed plane); `add_analysis` and `edit_analysis` refuse one
that is no plane at the marker, and other fields than these.

An optional `occurrence` is the selected plane's UID path from the design
root, for example `"O1/O3"` (empty for the root). Component-owned faces and
construction planes are transformed through that path into design
coordinates before applying the offset. Flip reverses only the normal,
after offsetting, and leaves the physical plane in place. Without a path,
older analyses infer a component's unique placement; repeated components
require an explicit path. A path that does not own the referenced face or
datum is refused. Fixed planes and origin planes without a path remain in
design coordinates.

`{"query":"section_plane","plane":<reference>,"occurrence":"O1/O3",
"offset":-5,"flip":false}` resolves the same definition without adding an
analysis. It returns design-space `origin`, `normal`, and the resolved
`occurrence`; the optional fields have the same defaults as an analysis.

A section can be turned by an angle about an axis (mitcad#823): `angle`
(radians, default 0, not written when 0), `axis` (a line reference: a
straight edge, a sketch line, a construction axis or an origin axis) and
`axis_occurrence` (the axis' UID path from the design root, as
`occurrence` is the plane's; inferred and checked the same way). The
picked plane is first turned rigidly by `angle` about the axis,
right-handed about the axis' direction, in design coordinates after both
occurrence paths; then it is moved by `offset` along the turned normal;
`flip` then reverses only the normal. An axis with angle 0 leaves the
plane as it is. `add_analysis` and `edit_analysis` refuse a non-zero
`angle` without an `axis`, and an axis along the plane's normal; an
analysis whose axis cannot be found at the marker gets the `analyses`
query's `error` and cuts nothing, as a plane that cannot be found. The
`section_plane` query takes the same three fields and then also returns
`axis` (`{"origin", "direction"}` in design coordinates) and the resolved
`axis_occurrence`. Analyses without an angle are written as before; a
MitCad older than mitcad#823 refuses a design with these fields. Drawing
section views cut by a Section Analysis follow its angle.

The `analyses` query lists them in the order added: `name`, `type`,
`visible`, the `def`'s fields, and `section`: {`origin`, `normal`} (the
plane in design coordinates at the marker, offset and flip applied; the
origin is the plane's origin, see [References to
geometry](#references-to-geometry)), or `error` when the plane cannot be
found there (a face of a body that is gone or rolled back). A face
reference follows the model by its topological name, as features' do.

A `def` of `"type": "print"` is a [print analysis](#print-analysis): its
bodies, bed face and settings, and in the `analyses` query `down` (the
print direction at the marker) or `error` (a body or the bed face is
gone).

- At most one analysis is shown at a time: one section cuts the bodies.
  Showing one hides the others, also in a file read with several shown
  (the first shown stays).
- Analyses change no geometry and recompute nothing. They are saved in
  the design file (`"analyses": [{"name", "visible" (only when false),
  "type", "plane", "occurrence" (when supplied), "offset", "flip"}]`, left out when there are none;
  files without it have none), and the comparison of versions lists them
  by name.

### Appearances

How bodies look (mitcad#46, `core/model-base/src/appearance.rs`,
`core/model/src/document/appearances.rs`): a physically based parameter
set, a subset of OpenPBR's and the Principled BSDF's. MitCad's library is
built in and read-only; a document keeps appearances of its own, saved in
the design file. A body names its appearance by id
(`set_body_appearance`), and single faces can have their own
([Appearances of faces](#appearances-of-faces), mitcad#53).

| Parameter | Range | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `base_color` | sRGB [r, g, b], 0–1 | [0.8, 0.8, 0.8] | a dielectric's diffuse colour, a metal's reflection, the tint of transmitted light |
| `metalness` | 0–1 | 0 | 1 for metals |
| `roughness` | 0–1 | 0.5 | 0 a mirror finish |
| `specular` | 0–1 | 1 | the weight of a dielectric's specular reflection |
| `transmission` | 0–1 | 0 | light going through (glass, clear plastic) |
| `ior` | 1–5 | 1.5 | index of refraction |
| `coat`, `coat_roughness` | 0–1 | 0, 0.03 | a clear coat over the base (lacquer, car paint) |
| `emission`, `emission_color` | 0–1000, sRGB | 0, [1, 1, 1] | emitted light: 1 is the colour's own radiance |
| `opacity` | 0–1 | 1 | a cut-out (glass transmits instead) |
| `texture` | `{"path", "size": [w, h] mm (default 100 x 100), "rotation" rad, "projection": "box" (default) or "planar", "data", "normal", "roughness", "metalness", "occlusion", "source"}` | none | an image for the base colour (PNG or JPEG), with the other maps of its set and where it came from ([Texture map sets](#texture-map-sets)), projected in the body's coordinates: `planar` along Z, `box` from the axis each point of the surface faces most; one repeat of the image is `size`, turned by `rotation` about the projection's axis. `path` is relative to the design file's folder or absolute; `data` (base64 of the image file, at most 32 MB) embeds the image in the design file ([Textures](#textures)). The rendered view draws it, the shaded view shows the base colour |

| Command | Fields | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `create_appearance` | `id` (letters, digits, `_`, `-`; the next free `custom<n>` when left out), `name` (`Appearance<n>` when left out), `based_on` (a library or document appearance whose parameters it starts from; the defaults above without it), any parameters | `id`; undo step `Create Appearance Red` |
| `edit_appearance` | `id`, `name` and any parameters (`"texture": null` removes the texture) | undo step `Edit Appearance Red` unless nothing changes; the library's are refused (copy one with `based_on`) |
| `delete_appearance` | `id` | `bodies`: those that used it, which get the default look, and `faces` (`{"body", "face"}`) that used it, which get their body's, in the same undo step `Delete Appearance Red` |

- Ids are unique among the library's and the document's appearances, and
  names too; parameters out of range and unknown fields are refused.
- The `appearances` query lists the library's appearances in the
  application's order, then the document's: `id`, `name`, the
  parameters, `library` (true for the built-in ones), `display_color`
  (sRGB: the colour of the shaded view and exports; the base colour),
  `bodies` (the uids of bodies that use it, also those not at the marker)
  and `faces` (`{"body", "face"}` of faces that use it).
- Library: `steel_satin`, `aluminum_anodized`, `brass_polished`, `copper`,
  `cast_iron`, `paint_red`, `paint_blue`, `paint_green`, `paint_yellow`,
  `paint_black`, `paint_white`, `plastic_black`, `plastic_orange`,
  `rubber`, `glass`, `wood_oak` (their colours as before mitcad#46),
  `chrome`, `gold_polished`, `steel_polished`, `plastic_red`,
  `plastic_white`, `plastic_blue`, `plastic_clear`, `glass_clear`,
  `glass_frosted`, `wood_walnut`, `wood_maple`, `emissive_white`.
- A body without an appearance, or with an id in neither list (an
  imported one), has the default look. A material carries an appearance
  (mitcad#640): setting a body's material sets the body's appearance to
  the material's, unless the body's appearance was set by hand (one that
  is not its current material's) or `set_body_material` says `keep`; see
  [Materials](#materials).
- The commands change no geometry and recompute nothing. The design file
  keeps the document's appearances as `"appearances": [{"id", "name",
  parameters...}]` (left out when there are none; parameters left out of
  a file are the defaults; files without it have none), and the
  comparison of versions lists them by id.

### Appearances of faces

Faces of a body can have appearances of their own, which override the
body's (mitcad#53, `core/model/src/document/bodies.rs`): a label area, a
painted face, a rubber pad.

| Command | Fields | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `set_face_appearance` | `uid` (body), `faces` (topological names of faces of the body at the marker, `F2:side(c1[c4,c2])`), `appearance` (an id, or null: the faces show the body's again), or `expression` ([Bindings](#bindings-values-from-expressions)) | undo step `Set Appearance of Face of Body1` / `Set Appearance of 2 Faces of Body1` / `Clear Appearance of Face of Body1` unless nothing changes; faces that are not there and names that are no face names are refused |
| `clear_face_appearances` | `uid` | undo step `Clear Face Appearances of Body1` unless the body has none |

- A face appearance names its face as assigned (the canonical text of
  the name) and follows it as features' face references do: a later
  feature that changes the face keeps the name, all pieces of a split
  face (`#k`) keep it. When a change renames the face (a sketch edit after
  which a side face's segment ends on another curve: `F2:side(c1[c4,c2])`
  becomes `F2:side(c1[c4,c5])`), the name finds the face of the same
  feature and role whose key has the most curves in common with it (for a
  side face: the same curve), as a profile's region key does; the name
  kept is still the one assigned. A face that is gone finds nothing and
  its appearance is kept for when it comes back (undo).
- The `bodies` query lists them per body as `face_appearances`: `[{"face"
  (as assigned), "appearance", "faces" (a name of each face it finds at
  the marker; empty when the face is gone)}]`, left out when there are
  none.
- They recompute nothing. The design file keeps them with the body's
  other attributes: `"face_appearances": {"F2:side(c1[c4,c2])":
  "paint_red"}` (left out when there are none; files without them have
  none); copied designs rename the feature ids in the names. The
  comparison of versions lists them with the body.

### Textures

An appearance's texture is an image file or an image embedded in the
design file (mitcad#53).

- `"data"` in a `create_appearance` or `edit_appearance` texture embeds the
  image: base64 of a PNG or JPEG file (checked by its first bytes; at most
  32 MB). `path` then names the file it came from. The `appearances` query
  lists an embedded texture with `"embedded": true` and `"image_sha256"`
  (the digest of the image file) instead of its data; that form sent back
  keeps the embedded image (`"embedded": true` without `data` keeps the
  image the appearance has, or that of `based_on` for a new one; refused
  when there is none), so the application changes a texture's size or
  rotation without sending the image again. A texture without `data` and
  `embedded` reads its file again.
- The `appearance_image` query (`id`) gives an embedded image: `data`
  (base64), `format` (`png`, `jpeg`) and `sha256`.
- The design file keeps the image in the texture's `data`; the
  comparison of versions shows `sha256 <digest>` for it. A file with
  shared images or embedded maps keeps each image once instead
  ([Texture map sets](#texture-map-sets)).

### Texture map sets

A texture can be a full set of physically based maps (mitcad#313,
`core/model-base/src/appearance.rs`), so that a design looks the same on
another computer without the image files: besides the base colour image
(the texture's own `path` and `data`), each of

| Map | Image |
|---|---|
| `normal` | a tangent-space normal map, OpenGL convention (green up) |
| `roughness` | roughness, grey 0 (mirror) to 1 |
| `metalness` | metalness, grey 0 (dielectric) to 1 (metal) |
| `occlusion` | ambient occlusion, grey 0 (occluded) to 1 |

is an optional object of the texture, `{"path", "data"}`, a PNG or JPEG
file as the base colour's: `path` relative to the design file's folder or
absolute, `data` (base64, at most 32 MB per image, each map one image)
embeds it. The maps share the base colour's `size`, `rotation` and
`projection`; a set needs its base colour image. A map left out of an
`edit_appearance` texture is removed (the texture is replaced as a
whole).

```json
{"cmd": "create_appearance", "name": "Oak veneer", "texture": {
  "path": "oak_diff_2k.jpg", "data": "/9j/4AAQ…", "size": [300, 300],
  "normal": {"path": "oak_nor_gl_2k.png", "data": "iVBORw0K…"},
  "roughness": {"path": "oak_rough_2k.png", "data": "iVBORw0K…"},
  "source": {"id": "polyhaven", "asset": "oak_veneer_01", "resolution": "2k",
             "license": "CC0-1.0", "url": "https://polyhaven.com/a/oak_veneer_01"}}}
```

- **Embedding:** the application embeds the images of a set it takes
  from a texture source; a map given by `path` alone stays a file of the
  user's, read when the view renders.
- **Source:** `source` records where the set came from: `id` (the
  texture source: `polyhaven`, `folder`, …; letters, digits, `_`, `-`),
  `asset` (the asset's id in it), and optionally `resolution` (`2k`),
  `license` (an SPDX identifier, `CC0-1.0`) and `url` (the asset's web
  page, http or https). The model keeps and lists it; it never fetches
  anything.
- **Listing:** the `appearances` query lists each embedded map image as
  the base colour's, `{"path", "embedded": true, "image_sha256"}`, and
  `source` as given. That form sent back keeps the images. `"embedded":
  true` with `image_sha256` keeps the image of that digest the design
  embeds, also another appearance's (so a set is reused without sending
  its images again; refused when the design has none of that digest);
  without `image_sha256` it keeps the image of the same map of the
  texture it replaces (or of `based_on`).
- **`appearance_image`** takes `map` (`base_color`, the default, or a map
  above) and gives that image.
- **One copy per image:** an image the design embeds already (the same
  SHA-256) is shared, not copied: in memory, in the states undo keeps,
  and in the design file. The file keeps a texture's embedded image in
  its `data` as before while no map image is embedded and no image is
  embedded twice; otherwise every embedded image is kept once in the
  top-level `"images": [{"sha256", "data"}]` (in the order of first use)
  and the textures and maps refer to it by `"image": "<sha256>"`. Opening
  checks each image (PNG or JPEG, at most 32 MB, its digest, listed once)
  and refuses a reference to an image that is not there. Files without
  `images` and maps open as before, and a design with one embedded
  texture is written as before. Older versions of MitCad do not open a
  file with `images` or maps (an unknown field).
- The comparison of versions shows each map's image as `sha256 <digest>`.

### Render settings

How the rendered view (`docs/rendering.md`) lights and shows the design
(mitcad#47, `core/model-base/src/render_settings.rs`), kept per document so a
design keeps its look. Sections of fields with defaults: the four below
and `output`, the final render's ([Render output](#render-output),
mitcad#48); later sections are added the same way, and files without a
section have its defaults. The user's lights are a list beside them
([Render lights](#render-lights), mitcad#54).

| Field | Values | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `environment.preset` | `studio`, `studio_white`, `studio_dark`, `outdoor`, `image` | `studio` | built-in light setups (procedural, no image files): `studio` soft key, fill and top lights in light grey surroundings; `studio_white` bright white surroundings, very soft light; `studio_dark` dark surroundings, a key and two rim lights; `outdoor` a clear sky and the sun; `image` an HDR image all around |
| `environment.strength` | 0–100 | 1 | a factor on all of the environment's light |
| `environment.rotation` | rad, within two turns | 0 | turns the studio's lights or the image about Z (counter-clockwise from above) |
| `environment.sun_elevation` | 0–pi/2 rad | pi/4 | `outdoor`: the sun's height above the horizon |
| `environment.sun_azimuth` | rad, within two turns | 5/4 pi | `outdoor`: where the sun is, counter-clockwise from X seen from above (5/4 pi: front left) |
| `environment.image` | a path | none | `image`: an equirectangular `.hdr` or `.exr` file, relative to the design file's folder or absolute; kept when another preset is chosen |
| `background.mode` | `view`, `color`, `environment` | `view` | behind the bodies: the view's own background (View > Environment), `background.color`, or the environment itself |
| `background.color` | sRGB [r, g, b], 0–1 | [1, 1, 1] | |
| `ground.shadows` | bool | true | a ground that shows only the bodies' shadows (a shadow catcher); without it there is no ground |
| `ground.reflections` | bool | false | the ground is glossy and catches the bodies' reflections too (with `shadows`) |
| `ground.height` | mm | none | the ground's Z; none: under the lowest body |
| `film.exposure` | -10–10 stops | 0 | each stop doubles the light |
| `film.view_transform` | `standard`, `filmic`, `neutral` | `standard` | from light to screen colours: `standard` sRGB, brighter than white clips; `filmic` a filmic curve (soft highlights, contrast in the darks); `neutral` base colours stay as they are under white light, only highlights are compressed |

| Command | Fields | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `set_render_settings` | per section (`environment`, `background`, `ground`, `film`, `output`) an object of the fields that change; `null` gives a field its default (none for `image` and `height`) | `changed`; undo step `Change Render Settings` unless nothing changes |
| `reset_render_settings` | | `changed`; the defaults, undo step `Reset Render Settings` unless they are already |

- Values out of range, unknown fields and sections are refused with the
  section's name (``ground: unknown field `depth` ``); nothing changes then.
- The commands change no geometry and recompute nothing.
- The `render_settings` query gives every section with every field (`image`
  and `height` only when set), and `lights`.
- The design file keeps them as `"render": {"environment": {...},
  "background": {...}, "ground": {...}, "film": {...}}` when they are not
  the defaults (fields left out of a file are the defaults); the
  comparison of versions lists each changed field as a document change
  (`render.environment.preset studio -> outdoor`).

### Render lights

Lights of the user's own (mitcad#54), besides the environment's: the
render settings' `lights`, a list in the `render_settings` query (`[]`
without any), saved with the other sections (files without it have no
lights) and changed by commands of their own. Lengths in mm, angles in
radians, Z up. Every light keeps every field; those of other kinds are
ignored.

| Field | Values | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | letters, digits, `_`, `-` | `light<n>` | what the commands name it by; cannot change |
| `name` | text | `Light<n>` | |
| `type` | `point`, `spot`, `area`, `sun` | `point` | a point (or small ball) shining all around; a point light in a cone; a glowing rectangle or disc (soft light); parallel light from far away (no position) |
| `enabled` | bool | true | off: kept, lights nothing |
| `space` | `world`, `camera` | `world` | `camera`: `position` and `direction` are relative to the camera (x to the right, y up, z toward the viewer, from the eye): the light follows the view |
| `position` | [x, y, z] mm, within 10⁷ | [0, 0, 200] | where it is (not for `sun`) |
| `direction` | [x, y, z], not zero | [0, 0, -1] | where it shines (spot, area, sun); kept as a unit vector |
| `color` | sRGB [r, g, b], 0–1 | [1, 1, 1] | |
| `power` | 0–10⁶ | 5 (sun 2) | point, spot, area: watts (a 5 W point light 300 mm away gives 4.4 W/m² where it falls straight, about the default studio's key light); sun: its irradiance in W/m² |
| `size` | 0–10⁶ mm | 20 | point, spot: the ball's diameter (0: hard shadows); area: the width, or the disc's diameter |
| `size_y` | 0–10⁶ mm | 20 | area: the rectangle's height |
| `shape` | `rectangle`, `disc` | `rectangle` | area |
| `spot_angle` | more than 0, at most pi | pi/4 | spot: the cone's full angle |
| `spot_blend` | 0–1 | 0.15 | spot: how softly the cone's edge fades |
| `angle` | 0–pi/2 | 0.02 | sun: its disc's angular diameter (0: hard shadows) |

| Command | Fields | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `add_render_light` | the light's fields (`type` sets the default `power`), all optional; `id` when not the next free `light<n>` | `id`; undo step `Add Light <name>` |
| `edit_render_light` | `id`, the fields that change (`null`: the field's default) | `changed`; undo step `Change Light <name>` unless nothing changes |
| `delete_render_light` | `id` | undo step `Delete Light <name>` |

- At most 64 lights; ids are unique. Values out of range, unknown fields
  or kinds and unknown ids are refused with the light's place
  (``lights.light1.power must be between 0 and 1000000, got -1``);
  nothing changes then. `set_render_settings` has no `lights`;
  `reset_render_settings` removes them with the other settings.
- The comparison of versions lists a light added or removed
  (`render.lights.light1 (none) -> Light1 (area)`) and its changed fields
  (`render.lights.light1.power 40 -> 60`).
- The model only keeps the lights; the rendered view and the final
  render light the design with them (`docs/rendering.md`, "Lights").

### Render output

The final render to an image file (mitcad#48; File > Render Image and
`mitcad-cli render`, `docs/rendering.md` "Final render"): the render
settings' fifth section, `output`, with the same rules as the others
(`set_render_settings` with `"output": {...}`, null for a field's
default; saved when not the defaults, so files of mitcad#47 open with
them; compared field by field, `render.output.format png -> exr`).

| Field | Values | Default | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `output.width` | 16–16384 px | 1920 | the image's width |
| `output.height` | 16–16384 px | 1080 | the image's height with `aspect` `fixed` |
| `output.aspect` | `view`, `fixed` | `view` | `view`: as high as the view is in proportion (the command line, without a view, takes width x height); `fixed`: width x height, and the view shows the image's frame |
| `output.samples` | 1–65536 | 128 | samples per pixel (adaptive sampling can stop converged pixels earlier) |
| `output.time_limit` | 0–86400 s | 0 | stop after this long even before the samples are done; 0: no limit |
| `output.denoise` | bool | true | denoise once the samples are done |
| `output.transparent` | bool | false | an alpha channel instead of the background: only the bodies and their shadows (not for JPEG) |
| `output.format` | `png`, `png16`, `jpeg`, `exr` | `png` | PNG (8 or 16 bits) and JPEG as the view shows the render (exposure and view transform, sRGB); OpenEXR (half floats) the render's linear light without exposure and view transform, alpha premultiplied |
| `output.quality` | 1–100 | 90 | JPEG's quality |

- Width, height, samples, time limit and quality out of range are refused
  with the field (``output.samples must be between 1 and 65536, got 0``).
- The model only keeps these settings; the application and `mitcad-cli`
  render with them.

## Queries

`{"query": "<name>", …}`; the result is JSON. Bodies are those at the
timeline marker.

| Query | Fields | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `document` | | `features`, `marker`, `bodies` (count), `undo`, `redo` (labels or null), `undo_depth`, `units` {`length`, `angle`}, `warnings` (what loading the file changed, such as renamed parameters), `revision`, `modified` (not the state last marked saved), `display` {`origin`, `isolated`}; with components `components`, `occurrences` (counts), `active_component` |
| `timeline` | | `marker`, `groups` (when any: `name`, `features` in timeline order) and `features`: `uid`, `name`, `type`, `suppressed`, `status` (`ok`, `warning`, `error`, `suppressed`, `rolled_back`, `pending` before the first recompute), `error` (the error, or the import note and the warnings joined with `; `), `import` (what the importer said about it, when it did: a fallback, a partial item, a placeholder; see [The import's outcomes on the timeline](#the-imports-outcomes-on-the-timeline)), `component` (when not the root), for a sketch before the marker `dof` (0 when fully constrained), for a sketch or construction feature `visible` and `visible_set` (its light bulb was set), for a feature that uses sketches `sketches` (their uids in timeline order: profiles, paths, guides, curves or points it refers to, also while it is suppressed or after the marker; the browser lists the feature under each, mitcad#177) |
| `feature` | `uid` | `uid`, `name`, `type`, `suppressed`, `status`, `error`, `visible`, `visible_set`, `warnings` (when any), `import` (the import note, when any), `def` (parameters by name) |
| `parameters` | | `name`, `expression`, `unit` (`""` for unitless), `value` (mm or rad), `text` (the value in its unit, `"12.5 mm"`), `comment`, `kind` (`user`, `model`, `reference`: a driven dimension's, read-only), `owner` (the feature of a model or reference parameter), `dependencies` (names its expression and its limits use), `favorite`; with limits also `limits`, `unclamped`, `unclamped_text`, `limited`, `limit_message`, `limit_references`, and `intrinsic` for a feature's own limits ([Parameter limits](#parameter-limits)) |
| `evaluate` | `expression`, `kind`: `length` (default), `angle` or `unitless`; `parameter` (optional, [Parameter limits](#parameter-limits)) | `value` (mm or rad), `text` (in the document's unit, `"40 mm"`), `references` (parameter names used), `expression` (with decimal points: `"d1 * 1,5"` gives `"d1 * 1.5"`); with `parameter` also `limited`, `limited_value`, `limited_text` |
| `appearances` | | the library's and the document's appearances with their parameters ([Appearances](#appearances)) |
| `appearance_image` | `id`, `map` (`base_color` default, `normal`, `roughness`, `metalness`, `occlusion`) | an embedded image of an appearance's texture set: `data` (base64), `format`, `sha256` ([Textures](#textures), [Texture map sets](#texture-map-sets)) |
| `render_settings` | | the document's render settings, every section and field ([Render settings](#render-settings)) |
| `bodies` | `properties`, `volumes`, `versions`, `bbox` | `uid`, `name`, `component` (when not the root's), `visible`, `material`, `appearance`, `face_appearances` ([Appearances of faces](#appearances-of-faces)) (when set), `mesh`: true for a mesh body ([Mesh bodies in surface operations](#mesh-bodies-in-surface-operations)); with `"properties": true` also `kind` (`solid`, `sheet`: faces or open shells, `mesh`, `empty`), `volume`, `area`, `center`, `bbox` {`min`, `max`} (in the component's coordinates), `faces`, `edges` (counts); with `"volumes": true` only `volume` (cheaper); with `"versions": true` also `version`, the shape's version as 32 hexadecimal digits, which changes whenever the body's shape does (mitcad#689: MCP's command results list the bodies a command changed); with `"bbox": true` also `bbox` without the other properties (mitcad#714: the boxes in MCP's `changes`) |
| `profiles` | `hashes` | `sketch`, `sketch_name`, `region`, `consumed` (an extrude uses it); with `"hashes": true` also `hash` (16 hex digits of the region's geometry and sketch frame: the same while the profile's face would be the same) |
| `faces` | `body`; `geometry`, filters `surface`, `min_area`, `max_area`, `normal`, `normal_tolerance`, and `offset`, `limit` ([Faces and edges with geometry](#faces-and-edges-with-geometry)) | per face: `names`, `surface` (`plane`, `cylinder`, …), `area`; with `"geometry": true` also its surface's geometry and `bbox`; with a filter, `offset` or `limit` an object: `total`, `offset`, `faces` (each also with `index`) |
| `edges` | `body`; `geometry`, filters `curve`, `min_length`, `max_length`, and `offset`, `limit` ([Faces and edges with geometry](#faces-and-edges-with-geometry)) | per edge: `name`, `curve` (`line`, `circle`, …), `length`; with `"geometry": true` also its curve's geometry and `bbox`; with a filter, `offset` or `limit` an object: `total`, `offset`, `edges` (each also with `index`) |
| `dependents` | `uid` | `dependents`: `uid`, `name` of the features that refer to it, directly or through others, in timeline order (what `delete_feature` with `dependents` deletes too) |
| `can_reorder` | `uid`, `index` | `ok`, and `error` (the reason `reorder_feature` would give) when not |
| `sketch` | `uid` | see [Sketch commands](#sketch-commands) |
| `threads` | `cosmetic` (optional, false: only the cosmetic threads, the ones the view draws; a modelled thread is in the geometry, and measuring its face cost a design with modelled threads 0.3-0.6 s each time the window showed it, mitcad#878) | threads on the bodies (thread features and tapped holes): `feature`, `name`, `body`, `face`, `standard`, `designation`, `class`, `right_handed`, `modeled`, `major_diameter`, `minor_diameter`, `pitch`, a multi-start thread's `starts` and `lead` (mitcad#893), and from the face `internal`, `radius`, `start`, `end` (points on the axis where the thread begins and ends; a cosmetic thread's end chamfers move them to where their cones meet the cylinder). A modelled thread whose crest lies on its face leaves pieces of the face between its grooves, and the face at the marker is measured. A modelled thread feature whose crest lies off its face (a class's diameters, a radial clearance) takes or covers all of the face along its part, leaving nothing of it (over the whole face) or only what lies outside the part, which does not show where the thread runs: it is listed with the face measured on the body before the feature, as long as the faces it made from it are on the body, and its end chamfers move `start` and `end` to where their cones meet the crest (mitcad#433, mitcad#628). A tapped hole's modelled thread whose crest lies off its wall (a radial clearance) is listed on the wall as the hole measured it before cutting the thread, as long as the thread's faces made from it are on the body (mitcad#436, mitcad#628); a result stored before mitcad#628 keeps only the walls left without any piece, and a part's wall in it is measured at the marker |
