| `thread_sizes` | `standard` (`iso_metric`, `unified`, `whitworth`, `npt`, `tyre_valve`, `forming_screw`, `trapezoidal`, `iso_taper` or `custom`; all when left out) | `standards`, ISO metric first, then Unified, Whitworth (bolt sizes, then the pipe sizes `G 1/4`), NPT, tyre valve, forming screw and trapezoidal threads (`Tr8x1.5`, the preferred pitch first), ISO 7-1, and last `custom` (mitcad#893: `"custom": true`, no sizes and no classes; its size is given): `standard`, `title` (the thread type's name), `default` (true for ISO metric), `sizes` (smallest first: `size` as the table names it, `10`, `1/4`, `#10`; `major_diameter` mm; `designations`, the coarse pitch or UNC first, each one `thread` and `hole` accept), `classes_external`, `classes_internal`, `default_class_external` (6g, 2A, Medium, Standard, 7e), `default_class_internal` (6H, 2B, Medium, Standard, 7H); a taper pipe thread's size also `tap_drill` (mm: the minor diameter of the internal thread its effective length into it, NPT's L2 and ISO 7-1's gauge length, mitcad#733) |
| `thread_chamfer` | `designation`, `standard` (`iso_metric` when left out), `internal` (false when left out); for `custom` (mitcad#893) `major` and `pitch` instead of `designation` | the size's default end chamfer ([thread](#thread), mitcad#304): `diameter` (mm, from the size table), `angle` (45, degrees to the axis) |
| `named_views` | | in the order added: `name`, `eye`, `target`, `up`, `perspective` (when true), `height` |
| `recompute_times` | | the features the last recompute evaluated (cache hits left out), in timeline order: `uid`, `name`, `type`, `ms` (wall time of its evaluation); and `ms`, their sum |
| `changes_since_saved` | | `known` (the state last marked saved is on the undo or redo stack, or is this one), `steps`: oldest first, the labels of the undo steps made since (`Change d3`), or `Undo <label>` for those undone since, leaving out those that changed only the display state; empty when nothing else changed or not known (never saved, a step dropped by a new command after undo) |
| `report` | | `timeline` and `bodies` with properties; with components also `components` and `instances` (with properties) |

Other queries: [analysis](#analysis-queries), [components](#component-commands-and-queries),
`dxf_info` ([DXF](#dxf-into-sketches)), `cache` ([Caches](#caches)),
`tangent_chains` ([Tangent chains](#tangent-chains)), `measurements` and
`annotations`
([Measurement objects](#measurement-objects), [Annotations](#annotations)).

- `evaluate` reads the expression as a value slot of that kind does: a
  bare number takes the document's unit of the kind (`"90"` as an angle
  is 90 degrees); a result of the wrong dimensions, a syntax error or an
  unknown name rejects the query with the reason.
- `report` as text is `Document::report(false)` (what `mitcad-cli`
  prints).
- `mitcad-cli info <file> --timings` prints the slowest features after
  opening a design; the ctests `cli.perf_recompute` and
  `cli.perf_join_recompute` do so for generated models
  (`tools/cli/tests/perf_model.json`, `perf_join_pattern.json`: a pattern
  joined near bodies it does not touch). `mitcad-cli run <script>
  --timings` prints how long each step of a script took
  (`Document::run_script_timed`; `cli.perf_sketch_pattern` on
  `perf_sketch_pattern_10.json`, mitcad#670).
- For picking, C++ asks the shape directly: `Shape::name_of_edge`,
  `Shape::names_of_face` and `Shape::find_edges`
  (`geometry/include/mitcad/geometry/shape.hpp`).

### Faces and edges with geometry

The `faces` and `edges` queries tell where each face and edge is
(mitcad#714), in the body's component's coordinates, mm and radians:

```json
{"query": "faces", "body": "F2.b0", "geometry": true, "surface": "cylinder",
 "max_area": 500, "offset": 0, "limit": 50}
{"query": "faces", "body": "F2.b0", "normal": [0, 0, 1], "normal_tolerance": 0.001}
{"query": "edges", "body": "F2.b0", "geometry": true, "curve": "circle", "min_length": 30}
```

- `"geometry": true` adds each item's geometry and its `bbox` {`min`,
  `max`} (the tight axis-aligned box; null for a face without geometry
  or a degenerate edge). A face on a plane has `origin` (the plane's
  point nearest to the model origin) and `normal` (out of the material);
  on a cylinder or a cone `origin` (the axis point nearest to the face's
  centre), `axis` (pointing along its largest component) and `radius` (a
  cone's at `origin`, with `half_angle`); on a sphere `center` and
  `radius`; on a torus `center`, `axis`, `major_radius` and
  `minor_radius`; on other surfaces (B-splines, planar ones too) only the
  box. An edge has `start` and `end`; a circle or an arc also `center`,
  `radius` and `normal` (it runs counter-clockwise about the normal from
  `start` to `end`, the same point for a full circle).
- Filters: faces by `surface` (the type `surface` names), `min_area` and
  `max_area` (mm²), `normal` (planar faces whose outward normal is that
  direction, of any length, within `normal_tolerance` radians, default
  1e-6); edges by `curve`, `min_length` and `max_length` (mm). All given
  filters apply together.
- With a filter, `offset` or `limit` the answer is an object: `total`
  (the number of items that match), `offset`, and `faces` or `edges`, the
  matching items from `offset` on, at most `limit` of them, each with its
  `index` in the body's face or edge order. Without them it is the array
  of every item, as before. A large body (hundreds of faces of holes)
  is read in pages this way.
- `Kernel::face_geometries` and `Kernel::edge_geometries` describe the
  items in one pass; `Kernel::face_bounding_boxes` and
  `Kernel::edge_bounding_boxes` measure the boxes of the page's items
  only. Tests: `api::face_lists_tests`, `cli.face_geometry`
  (`tools/cli/tests/face_geometry.json`, a block with two holes on the
  OCCT kernel).

### Analysis queries

| Query | Fields | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `datums` | `origin` (also the origin datums) | per datum: `uid`, `name`, `type` and its geometry |
| `datum` | `uid` (`F3` or `xy`) | `type` `plane`: `origin`, `normal`, `x_axis`, `y_axis`; `axis`: `origin`, `direction`; `point`: `point` |
| `properties` | `bodies` (default all), `density`, `densities` {uid: g/cm³} | `bodies`: `uid`, `name`, `material`, `density`, `volume`, `area`, `mass`, `center_of_mass`, `inertia` (3 × 3, at the centre of mass), `principal_moments`, `principal_axes`; `total`: `volume`, `area`, `mass`, `center_of_mass`, `inertia` |
| `measure` | `a`, `b` (optional) selections | `a`, `b`: `kind` and `volume`, `area`, `length`, `point`, `circle` {`center`, `axis`, `radius`, `sweep`}, `axis` {`origin`, `direction`} (*Measure with axes*), `plane` {`origin`, `normal`} of a planar face or a datum plane (the middle of the face on its plane, the normal out of the material; mitcad#714) as they apply; with `b` also `between`: `distance`, `on_a`, `on_b`, `inside`, `angle` (null unless both have a normal, a direction or an axis), `offset` (only for two parallel planes, *Measure in the design*), `axis_distance`, `axis_points`, `center_distance` (*Measure with axes*) |
| `interference` | `bodies` (default all), `min_volume` (mm³, default 1e-6) | `bodies` (count), `pairs`: `a`, `b`, `names`, `volume` |
| `section` | `plane`, `bodies` (default all), `world` (default false) | `plane`, per body `edges`, `faces`, `length`, `area`, `clip`, and the totals with `cut`, `kept` and `removed` ([Section Analysis past every body](#section-analysis-past-every-body-mitcad824)) |
| `compare_step` | `file`, `bodies`, `step_body` (name or index), `samples`, `fuzzy`, `max_deviation`, `max_relative` | `step_bodies`, `volume`, `step_volume`, `volume_only_mitcad`, `volume_only_step`, `relative_difference`, `max_deviation`, `mitcad_to_step` and `step_to_mitcad` {`max`, `rms`, `at`, `samples`}, `bounds_difference`; with limits `pass` and `exceeded` |

- Units: mm, mm², mm³, g/cm³, kg, kg mm², radians. Density:
  `densities[uid]`, else the body's material, else `density` for bodies
  without one, else steel.
- A selection is `{"body": "F2.b0"}` with an optional `"face"`, `"edge"`
  or `"vertex"`, `{"datum": "F5"}` (or an origin datum, `"xy"`, `"x"`,
  `"origin"`, in any case), either with an optional
  `"occurrence"` (a path from the root by ids, `"O1/O4"`, or by names,
  `"Arm:1/Pin:2"`; *Measure in the design*), an entity as `ui_state`
  lists the selection (`{"kind": "face", "owner": "F2.b0", "name": …,
  "occurrence": …}`; *Selections by names and as entities*), or text:
  `"Body1"`, `"F2.b0"`, `"Body1/F2:end(r{c5})"`, `"xy"`, `"F5"`. A
  section `plane` is a plane reference.
- Kernels without an analysis answer with an error (`the geometry kernel
  does not support …`).
- `Document::analysis(query, json)` (C++ `analysis`) answers
  `properties`, `measure`, `interference`, `section`, `compare_step` and
  `datums` as text (`mitcad-cli`) or pretty JSON.

`analysis_shape(request)` returns a shape handle for display, null when
there is none:

| `shape` | Fields | Shape |
|---|---|---|
| `datum` | `uid` (`F3`, `xy`), `size` (default 100) | a square face, an edge or a vertex |
| `section` | `plane`, `body`, `occurrence` (optional), `curves` (default false) | the section faces, or curves |
| `clip` | `plane`, `body`, `occurrence` (optional) | the body without the half-space on the plane's normal side; what is left of its faces, edges and vertices keeps the body's names (picks on the clipped view refer to the body), faces on the plane stay whole, and the caps have no names. A body the plane does not reach is not cut (mitcad#438): one behind the plane (touching it at most) is the body's own shape, one wholly on the normal side an empty compound |
| `interference` | `a`, `b` (bodies) | their overlap |

Mesh bodies (triangles without surfaces, from STL, OBJ and the meshes of
imported models) are sectioned and clipped triangle by triangle
(mitcad#392): the `section` edges are one straight edge per triangle the
plane crosses (an edge of triangles lying in the plane counts once), and
it has faces and an area only when the mesh is closed. The `clip` shape
keeps the triangles behind the plane, cut along it, with the section
faces as planar caps when the mesh is closed; when the plane removes
nothing it is the body itself. A body that mixes mesh faces with faces on
surfaces is an error.

By default, `section` queries and the `section`/`clip` shapes operate in
component-local coordinates, preserving the original API. With `world:true`,
the `section` query resolves its plane in design coordinates and measures
each visible occurrence separately; entries also include `occurrence` (UID
path) and `component`. Repeated bodies contribute once per visible occurrence.
Resolve an ambiguous plane reference with `section_plane` first and pass
its fixed `origin`/`normal` to this query.

The `section` and `clip` shape requests accept an optional `occurrence`
UID path for the **body**. When supplied, their input plane is in design
coordinates and is transformed into that occurrence's local coordinates.
The returned shape remains local: display it using the body's original
placement. The path must own the body. This gives every displayed component
the same physical cutting plane without applying placement twice.

### Section Analysis of many bodies (mitcad#438)

`analysis_clips(request)` (C++ `Document::analysis_clips`) clips several
bodies at one plane at once, as the `clip` shape clips each:
`{"plane": <plane>, "bodies": [{"body": "F2.b0", "occurrence": "O1/O2"}, …]}`
(`occurrence` optional, as for `clip`). The result has one entry per body
in the request's order (`count`, `shape(i)`, `error(i)`): the clipped
shape, or null with the error the `clip` request would give that body (an
unknown body, an occurrence that does not own it, a failed boolean); one
body's error does not stop the others. Section Analysis and Hide Above
Sketch clip the bodies shown with it (`MainWindow::modelBodies`).

The bodies' booleans run on all cores (OCCT's thread pool, each body one
operation of `geometry::run_operation`, so a crash inside OCCT is that
body's error), and so do the sections of the `section` query with
`world:true` (`Kernel::clip_all` and `Kernel::section_all`, whose defaults
take one body after another). A body the plane does not reach needs no
boolean: its kept bounding box tells the bridge
(`core/cpp/bridge/analysis.cpp`) that the clip keeps or removes it whole,
or that the plane passes it farther than the body's tolerances, which
gives an empty section.

### Section Analysis off the UI thread (mitcad#438)

`prepare_clips(request)` (C++ `Document::prepare_clips`) takes the same
request as `analysis_clips` and `prepare_query(request)` a `section` query
(`{"query": "section", ...}`, the only query it prepares; another is
refused as an invalid prepared query): each takes from the document what
the work needs (each body's shape with the plane in its coordinates, the
answer's fields, or a body's error) while the document is idle, and its
`run()` works it out later without the document, on any thread, as the
document would have answered when it was prepared: what it holds of the
bodies stays as it was when the document changes. The section worker of
the application runs them (`app/framework/SectionWorker.hpp`). What they
hold is detached from the bodies when they are prepared
(`Kernel::detach_all`, whose default takes the shapes as they are): a
body the plane may cut or touch as a copy that shares no face, edge or
vertex with it, with the same face names, its box and its mesh faces'
triangles; a body the plane passes farther than its tolerances as
itself, its box measured then, which alone tells its clip (kept or
removed whole) and its empty section. So `run()` never reads a sub-shape
the application's view or a model job may write into meanwhile (meshes),
and what it clips can be meshed on its thread. A clipped body is what is
left of its copy (the copy itself when the clip leaves it whole after
all); a body the plane passes and keeps is its own shape, as with
`analysis_clips`. `input(i)` and `detached(i)` tell what the clip of body
`i` reads.
Both stop when the running thread's geometry is told to
(`geometry/cancel.hpp`): the bodies not started by then fail as
cancelled.

### Section Analysis over a feature preview (mitcad#943)

A body of the `analysis_clips` and `prepare_clips` requests takes two
more fields: `"preview": true` clips the body as the previewed command
leaves it (`Document::preview`'s result, as `preview_body_shape` gives
it) instead of the body at the marker, also a body the preview makes,
which is no body at the marker (an error `body … is not in the preview`
when the preview has no such body, or there is no preview); and
`"transform": {"linear": [[…], […], […]], "translation": [x, y, z]}`,
the rigid placement that puts the body in the design where the view
draws it (a preview's moved occurrence, a body the preview makes), takes
the plane into the body's coordinates by its inverse instead of by
`occurrence` (which it replaces; the body's component is not checked).
`{"plane": {"origin": [10, 0, 0], "normal": [1, 0, 0]}, "bodies":
[{"body": "F2.b0", "preview": true, "transform": {"linear": [[1, 0, 0],
[0, 1, 0], [0, 0, 1]], "translation": [0, 0, 0]}}]}`. The application
clips the bodies a feature preview draws with their new shapes or
placements this way while Section Analysis or Hide Above Sketch is on
(`app/framework/SectionPreview.hpp`), prepared while the document holds
the preview and run on the section worker.

### Section Analysis past every body (mitcad#824)

The `section` query's answer also tells what the clip of the view does
with each body: each body's `clip` is `cut`, `kept` (whole: its box lies
behind the plane, touching it at most) or `removed` (whole: its box lies
on the plane's normal side, touching it at most), told from the body's
box as the `clip` shape and `analysis_clips` tell it without a boolean
(`analysis::clip_side`, within `Precision::Confusion`; a body without a
box counts as cut). `cut`, `kept` and `removed` count them; with `world`
they count the visible occurrences the query measures, a body once per
occurrence. A plane that cuts none of the bodies (`cut` 0) leaves the
view empty (all `removed`) or shows the bodies uncut (all `kept`), with a
zero `area` and `length`; a plane on a face of a body behind it keeps the
body (`kept`) while its section is that face. `prepare_query` answers the
same: the boxes are read when it is prepared. The text answer
(`Document::analysis`, `mitcad-cli`) adds `The plane cuts no body: <n>
kept whole, <m> removed whole` then. Section Analysis' panel shows a
warning instead of the zero totals in that case (`app/COMMANDS.md`).

## Preview

`preview` takes an `add_feature` or `edit_feature` command and evaluates
it on a copy of the document without committing it. The result:

```json
{"uid": "F5", "name": "Extrude3", "status": "ok", "error": null, "warnings": [],
 "bodies": [{"uid": "F2.b0", "name": "Body1", "changed": true}], "removed": [], "tool": true}
```

- `bodies`: all bodies at the marker after the command (`changed`: new or
  modified by it); `removed`: the bodies it removes; `warnings`: what a
  feature that succeeded built with caveats (the `status` stays `ok`).
- A pattern adds `elements`: every element's transform as 3 rows of 4 by
  element number, suppressed ones too. A construction feature adds its
  `datum`. A sweep adds `sweep_path`, where its profile lies on its path
  ([sweep](#sweep), mitcad#795).
- A `move` or `move_occurrence` whose motion is a `rotate`,
  `point_to_point` or `point_to_position` adds `motion` (mitcad#838): what
  the motion was worked out from, in the feature's component's
  coordinates: `{"type": "rotate", "origin": [x, y, z], "direction":
  [x, y, z]}` (the axis it turns right-handed about, a unit direction),
  `{"type": "point_to_point", "from": [...], "to": [...]}` or
  `{"type": "point_to_position", "point": [...]}`. The app's drag of the
  angle or the position moves the shown bodies by it without asking the
  model again, about the same axis as the result. Test:
  `f4_tests::move_previews_report_what_their_motion_turns_about`.
  A `move_face` reports it alike, from the same resolution of its
  `transform` (mitcad#854), and so does a preview that failed after its
  motion was worked out (a motion that moves nothing, faces that cannot
  follow it), so that the app's Rotate ring keeps turning about the
  model's axis. Test:
  `f4_tests::move_face_previews_report_the_axis_they_turn_about`.
- A command that places occurrences elsewhere (a joint, a
  `move_occurrence`; mitcad#55) adds `placements`: each occurrence whose
  placement in the design changes, `path` (uids from the root, `O1/O4`;
  an occurrence inside a moved one is listed too) and `transform` (4x4,
  in the design), so a preview can show the bodies where it puts them.
- `instances` (when there are any): the occurrence/body pairs the command
  makes, each `body`, `occurrence` (uids from the root, `O1/O4`; empty in
  the root), `transform` (4x4, in the design) and `visible` (false in a
  hidden occurrence or for a hidden body); a new body has one in each
  occurrence of its component, at that occurrence's placement.
  `removed_instances`: the pairs the command takes away (`body`,
  `occurrence`). Every other body keeps its pairs: a display shows it
  where and when the `instances` query shows it, with
  `preview_body_shape` for a changed one. A body neither shown nor in a
  visible new pair (a hidden body, one in a hidden occurrence, one an
  isolation leaves out) stays hidden, also when the command changes it,
  and no body is drawn without a pair's placement (mitcad#266; the app:
  `app/framework/PreviewBodies.hpp`).
- `preview_body_shape(uid)` returns a body as the command leaves it and
  `preview_tool_shape()` the extrusion before its boolean (a split's or
  trim's extended tool: [The extended tool of a split or
  trim](#the-extended-tool-of-a-split-or-trim-mitcad712)).
- `tool_instances` (with `tool`): where that tool is in the design. The
  tool is in its feature's component's coordinates, so there is one entry
  per occurrence of that component (one with an empty `occurrence` in the
  root): `occurrence` (uids from the root), `transform` (4x4, in the
  design) and `visible` (false in a hidden occurrence). A display draws
  the tool, and the app's provisional drag proxy of it, at these
  placements (mitcad#636).
- An `edit_feature` preview computes the feature in its own component
  (not the active one) under its own uid, and when the marker is before
  the feature (an editor rolls it back) the feature is still computed, the
  later ones staying rolled back (mitcad#309).
- The next command or `clear_preview` drops the preview; committing the
  same command reuses its results.

## Scripts

`run_script` (`mitcad-cli run`) takes an array of steps: commands,
comments (`{"comment": "…"}`) and expectations (`{"expect": {…}}`), which
check the document after the steps before them. Examples:
`tools/cli/tests/*.json`.

| Expectation | Checks |
|---|---|
| `"bodies": n` | bodies at the marker |
| `"body": "Body1"` (name or uid) | `"volume"`, `"area"` (relative `"tolerance"`, default 1e-6), `"faces"`, `"edges"` (counts), `"has_face"`, `"has_edge"`, `"no_edge"` (names), `"min"`, `"max"` (bounding box corners, the same tolerance), `"bbox": {"min", "max"}`, `"center"` (of mass; `"tolerance"` in mm), `"min_face_area"` (every face has at least this area, mm²: no slivers) |
| `"total_volume"` | all bodies |
| `"occurrence"` (a path, or an occurrence placed once) with `"body"` | the body as placed: `volume`, `area`, `center`, `bbox`, `min`, `max` |
| `"instances"`, `"world_volume"` | the visible placed bodies: count, sum of volumes |
| `"feature": "Fillet1"` (name or uid) | `"status"`, `"error_contains"` |
| `"parameter": "d3"` | `"value"` |
| `"sketch": "Sketch1"` (name or uid) | `"regions"` (its region keys in any order), `"dof"` |
| `"query": {…}` | `"result"`: the query's answer contains it (objects: the keys given; arrays: element by element; numbers within the relative `"tolerance"`, default 1e-6), e.g. `{"expect": {"query": {"query": "datum", "uid": "F3"}, "result": {"origin": [0, 0, 30]}}}` |

The first failing step stops the script: `steps[4]: expected Body1 to have
volume 48000, got 47961.37`.

## Sketch commands

Every `sketch.*` command but `sketch.create` names its sketch with
`"sketch": "F1"` and is one undo step (`Add Line to Sketch1`). An edit
works on a copy of the definition: the sketch is solved from the edited
positions with the current parameter values and the solution is stored.
An edit after which the sketch no longer solves is rejected, naming the
constraints in conflict, as is a constraint or driving dimension the
others already imply (add the dimension driven instead).

A point input is `[x, y]` (a new point) or `"p3"` (an existing point,
which joins the new curve to it). Values follow [Values](#values); a new
dimension gets a model parameter owned by the sketch (`Sketch1 fillet
radius`). Tool sizes (`radius`, `width`, `count` …) are plain numbers: a
tool only draws, and dimensions are added separately.

Results of editing commands: `entities` (new points and curves),
`constraints`, `dimensions` (new ids), `parameters` (created), `texts`,
`removed` (when anything was removed), `made` (the main curves the tool
made, in order) and `status` (as the `sketch` query: `dof`,
`fully_constrained`, `redundant`, `conflicts`).

| Command | Fields | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `sketch.create` | `plane` (default `xy`; `xz`, `yz`, a construction plane `"F5"` or `{"face": …, "body": …}`), `frame`, `name` (optional), `occurrence` and `context` (optional: a plane of another component, see [Geometry of other components](#geometry-of-other-components)), `upright` (default false; see [An upright sketch frame](#an-upright-sketch-frame)) | result `uid`, `name` |
| `sketch.add_rectangle` | `corner` [x, y], `width`, `height` (values) | a dimensioned rectangle: fixed first corner, horizontal and vertical constraints, `width` and `height` dimensions; result also `curves`, `region` |
| `sketch.add_circle` | `center` [x, y], `diameter` (value) | fixed centre and a diameter dimension; result also `curves`, `region` |
| `sketch.add_point` | `at`, `fixed` | |
| `sketch.add_line` | `start`, `end` (point inputs), `construction`, `centerline` | |
| `sketch.rectangle` | `mode`: `two_point` (`a`, `b` corners), `three_point` (side `a`–`b`, `c` on the opposite side), `center` (`center`, `corner`); `construction`; `radius` (value, optional: rounded corners, [Rounded rectangles and fillets of several corners](#rounded-rectangles-and-fillets-of-several-corners)) | four joined lines (counter-clockwise), horizontal and vertical (perpendicular for `three_point`), a construction diagonal with the centre at its midpoint for `center`; with `radius` also four arcs (`made`: the lines, then the arcs) |
| `sketch.circle` | `mode`: `center` (`center` point input, `radius`), `two_point` (`a`, `b`: a diameter), `three_point` (`a`, `b`, `c`), `two_tangent` (`lines` [2], `radius`, `near`), `three_tangent` (`lines` [3]); `construction` | tangent constraints for the tangent modes |
| `sketch.arc` | `mode`: `three_point` (`start`, `through`, `end`), `center` (`center`, `start`, `end`: the direction of the end, `clockwise`), `tangent` (`from`: an end point of a curve, `end`); `construction` | `tangent` adds a tangent constraint |
| `sketch.polygon` | `center`, `vertex`, `sides` (3–256), `inscribed` (default true; false: `vertex` is a side's middle), `construction` | joined lines that stay a regular polygon (four degrees of freedom: placement, orientation, size; mitcad#303): inscribed, equal sides with the corners on a construction circle; circumscribed, the sides tangent to a construction circle and the corners on a second construction circle around the same centre point (the first circle is the one through `vertex`). Polygons stored earlier keep their constraints |
| `sketch.slot` | `mode`: `center_to_center` (`a`, `b`), `center_point` (`center`, `end`: an end's centre), `arc` (`center`, `start`, `end`); `width` | two end arcs, two tangent sides, a construction centre line or arc with the arc centres at its ends, equal end arcs |
| `sketch.ellipse` | `center` (point input), `major` (end of the major axis), `minor_radius`, `start` and `end` (point inputs; an elliptical arc), `construction` | |
| `sketch.spline` | `points` (point inputs), `degree` (optional), `closed` (optional, mitcad#783), `construction` | without `degree` a cubic through the points; with it, a B-spline with these control points; `closed` (fit points only, at least three): the cubic runs on from the last point back to the first and is smooth through it |
| `sketch.add_text` | `text`, `at` (or `frame`), `height`, `angle`, `font`, `bold`, `italic`, `align`, `valign`, `spacing`, `frame` (three point ids, or `{"corner": [x, y], "diagonal": [x, y]}`: a new construction rectangle, turned by `angle`), `path`, `flip_x`, `flip_y`, `cap_height`, `wrap`, `line_spacing`, `pen_align`, `ink_top`, `glyphs` (stored outlines, see the sketch definition's `texts`), `font_file` (a font file's path instead of `font`, mitcad#473: the file's family becomes `font`, its outlines of the text are stored; a file that cannot be read or is not a font is refused), `value` (a text parameter's name or a text expression the text follows, [Text parameters](#text-parameters); `text` may then be left out) | the glyphs bound profiles |
| `sketch.edit_text` | `id`, and any of `text`, `at`, `height`, `angle`, `font`, `bold`, `italic`, `align`, `valign`, `spacing`, `path`, `flip_x`, `flip_y`, `cap_height`, `wrap`, `line_spacing`, `pen_align`, `ink_top`, `font_file` (a font file's path; `""` leaves the file for `font`), `value` (a text parameter's name or a text expression the text follows; `""` stops it following one, [Text parameters](#text-parameters)) | a new `text`, `font`, `bold` or `italic` drops the text's stored `glyphs`; for a text in a font file it stores the file's outlines again (refused when the file is not there, or when its path came with the design and no `font_file` is given, mitcad#929), and another `font` leaves the file |
| `sketch.add_constraint` | `constraint`: as in the definition, without `id` | a `coincident` between the end points of two curves merges them into one point (see [Points that become one](#points-that-become-one)): the result has no new constraint, `removed` lists the removed point (and what the merge dropped), and `merged` is `{"kept": "p3", "removed": "p7"}`; a constraint that older geometric constraints imply in part replaces them: `removed` lists them and `implied_removed` is `[{"constraint": "k1", "type": "horizontal"}]` (see [A constraint that replaces one it makes redundant](#a-constraint-that-replaces-one-it-makes-redundant)) |
| `sketch.add_dimension` | `dimension`: as in the definition, without `id`, `value`, `driven`; `value` (default: what it measures now), `driven`, `text` [x, y] | |
| `sketch.set_dimension` | `dimension` (`k3`), `value` | a number or an expression changes the dimension's own parameter; a parameter name makes the dimension use that parameter; `name = expression` renames its parameter and sets it (see [Values](#values)); a driven dimension becomes driving (its reference parameter becomes its parameter, under the same name) |
| `sketch.set_driven` | `dimension`, `driven` (default true) | driving again keeps the measured value; driven, its own parameter becomes its reference parameter |
| `sketch.set_signed` | `dimension` (a `horizontal_distance` or `vertical_distance`), `signed` (default true) | the point stays where it is: a driving value is negated where `b` lies on the negative side (see [Signed point dimensions](#signed-point-dimensions)) |
| `sketch.set_dimension_text` | `dimension` (`k3`), `text` [x, y] | where the value is shown; undo step `Move Dimension in Sketch1` |
| `sketch.set_active` | `items` (constraints and dimensions, `k3`), `active` (default true), `reason` (optional, with `active` false) | inactive ones are kept but left out of the solve; activating is refused when the sketch then does not solve or is over-constrained; `made` lists the items whose state changed; undo step `Activate in Sketch1` / `Deactivate in Sketch1` (see [Inactive constraints and dimensions](#inactive-constraints-and-dimensions)) |
| `sketch.redefine_plane` | `plane` (optional, as `sketch.create`), `occurrence`, `context`, `offset`, `x`, `y`, `angle` (values; left out: kept, a plain zero: none), `flip`, `upright` | the sketch moved to another plane or face and placed there; a plane after the sketch is refused; undo step `Redefine Plane of Sketch1` (see [Redefine Sketch Plane](#redefine-sketch-plane)) |
| `sketch.remove` | `items`: `p3`, `c4`, `t5`, `k6` | a point takes the curves that use it, a curve its points no other curve uses; constraints and dimensions on removed entities go too; a curve or point a derived offset computes (a spline or ellipse chain's) is refused, its source goes with the offset (mitcad#361) |
| `sketch.set_construction` | `curves`, `construction` (default true) | |
| `sketch.set_centerline` | `lines`, `centerline` (default true) | |
| `sketch.set_fixed` | `entities`, `fixed` (default true) | |
| `sketch.drag` | `entity`: a point with `to` [x, y], or a curve with `by` [dx, dy] or `radius`; or `entities` (points and curves) with `by` | pulls as far as the constraints allow; a derived offset's curve or point pulls its source chain by as much; `entities` drags a selection together (see [Dragging a selection](#dragging-a-selection)) |
| `sketch.move` | `entities`, `by` [dx, dy] or `rotate` {`center` (point input), `angle`}, `copy` | a move keeps the constraints (the points are dragged); a copy copies the constraints among the entities; a derived offset's curves move their source chain, their copies are ordinary curves; `made` lists the copies |
| `sketch.trim` | `curve`, `at` [x, y] | removes the piece around `at` between the curves crossing it; a curve nothing crosses is deleted; of a closed spline the rest becomes a spline by control points (mitcad#783); refused for a projected curve (linked or not: `sketch.convert_projected` first, mitcad#357, also for `sketch.extend`, `sketch.fillet` and `sketch.chamfer`) and for a curve a derived offset computes; a trim or an extension that ends on a derived offset's curve ends in a plain point, since its curves take no constraints (mitcad#361) |
| `sketch.extend` | `curve`, `at` | extends the end nearest `at` (a line or an arc) to the next curve; an arc extended all the way round becomes a circle; reaching an existing point joins it (a shared end; a projected or computed point holds the end with a point-to-point `coincident` instead), elsewhere the end lies on the curve; result `joined`: the point reached, when it joined one (see [Points that become one](#points-that-become-one)) |
| `sketch.insert_spline_point` | `curve` (a spline), `at` [x, y] | a point on the spline where it is nearest `at`: a fit point between its neighbours, or a control point by knot insertion that keeps the shape exactly; result `made`: the new point; see [Insert Point on a spline](#insert-point-on-a-spline) (mitcad#836) |
| `sketch.fillet` | `a`, `b` (lines), or `curves` (lines) and/or `points` (corners) for several corners; `radius` (value) | a tangent arc with a radius dimension; the corner stays as a point on both lines, and a length dimension of either line becomes a distance to it, so dimensions keep their meaning; several corners: one arc each, one radius dimension and the others Equal to the first ([Rounded rectangles and fillets of several corners](#rounded-rectangles-and-fillets-of-several-corners)) |
| `sketch.chamfer` | `a`, `b`, `distance`, and `distance2` or `angle` (values) | a line and its distance (and distance or angle) dimensions from the kept corner |
| `sketch.offset` | `curves` (a chain of joined curves, or one closed curve), `distance` (value) | to the right of the chain direction (a closed curve: positive is out); one parameter for the distance; an `offsets` record (derived with ellipses and splines); result `constraints` [the offset's id] and `warnings`; a curve the same as another counts once, see [Projected outlines and their offsets](#projected-outlines-and-their-offsets) |
| `sketch.edit_offset` | `offset` (`k8`), `distance` (value), `flip` | the distance changes, `flip` moves it to the other side; the curves keep their ids |
| `sketch.mirror` | `entities`, `axis` (a line `c4`, or the sketch's own axis `"x"` or `"y"`, made in the same undo step when the sketch has none, see [The sketch's axes and origin as entities](#the-sketchs-axes-and-origin-as-entities); mitcad#876) | copies with symmetric constraints (an ellipse copy also keeps an equal minor radius); points on the axis are shared; the axis line among `entities` is left out (refused only when nothing else is left), and a point whose curve is mirrored too (a circle's centre picked with the circle) gets no symmetry of its own, which would be redundant (mitcad#876) |
| `sketch.circular_pattern` | `entities`, `center` (point input; a new point is fixed), `count` (originals included), `angle` (value, default a full turn) | a `patterns` record; result `constraints` [the pattern's id] |
| `sketch.rectangular_pattern` | `entities`, `direction` (default [1, 0]), `count` [n1, n2], `spacing` [s1, s2] (values, signed: a negative spacing goes against its direction, mitcad#447; not zero), `symmetric` ([bool, bool], default none: per direction the originals are the middle instance, an odd count, and the copies lie on both sides) | as above |
| `sketch.edit_pattern` | `pattern` (`k5`), and any of `count` (n, or [n1, n2]), `angle`, `spacing`, `direction`, `center`, `entities` (the originals) | the copies follow |
| `sketch.project` | `source`: an edge, a face (its boundary) or a vertex of the bodies before the sketch (left out only for a section of a whole `body`, mitcad#736), or a curve or point of an earlier sketch, `{"sketch": "F1", "curve": "c4"}` / `{"point": "p3"}`, or `{"sketch": "F1"}` for all its curves (see [Projecting another sketch's curves and points](#projecting-another-sketchs-curves-and-points), mitcad#904), `body` (optional; none for a sketch's geometry), `linked` (default false), `occurrence` and `context` (optional: geometry of another component, see [Geometry of other components](#geometry-of-other-components)), `section` (default false: a face's or a body's section curves, or an edge's crossing points, instead; see [Section curves in sketches](#section-curves-in-sketches)) | fixed reference entities, a curve or point the same as another of the source once; a planar B-spline seen edge on is the line between its extreme points (mitcad#389), as a conic is; a linked projection follows its source when the model changes, each entity the fresh curve of its kind most like it (`by_geometry` in its record, since 0.4.1); a projection without it (files of earlier versions, imports) follows only a source whose curves come back of the same kinds, in the same order and joined the same way, and otherwise keeps its geometry and warns (mitcad#249); joined to the projected geometry already in the sketch, see [Projected outlines and their offsets](#projected-outlines-and-their-offsets) |
| `sketch.import_dxf` | `path` (.dxf), `unit` (of a drawing that names none: `mm` default, `cm`, `m`, `in`, `ft`), `at` (the sketch point the drawing's origin goes to, default [0, 0]), `layers` (only the entities on these layers; all when left out; a layer with nothing on it is refused) | as other edits, and `curves`, `points` (shared points made), `text_count`, `warnings`; undo step `Insert DXF into Sketch1`; see [DXF](#dxf-into-sketches) |
| `sketch.import_svg` | `path` (.svg), `scale`, `at`, `stroke_outline` (mitcad#473) | see [SVG](#svg-into-sketches) |
| `sketch.add_code` | `text` (the content), `at` (the lower left corner, default [0, 0]), `module` (mm, default 1), `angle`, `kind` (`qr`), `ecc` (`L`, `M` default, `Q`, `H`) (mitcad#473) | a text with `code` (see the sketch definition's `texts`), `texts` [its id]; undo step `Add QR Code to Sketch1`; a content no QR code holds (too long for the level) or a module of no size is refused |
| `sketch.edit_code` | `id` (`t5`), and any of `text`, `at`, `module`, `angle`, `ecc` | undo step `Edit QR Code in Sketch1`; refused as `sketch.add_code` |
| `sketch.clean_up_projections` | `merge` (default true: also lines on or overlapping a collinear one) | as other edits, and `cleaned` (`[{"curve", "kept", "how", "link"}]`; `how`: `same`, `on` or `joined`; `link`: the source the removed curve followed when the kept one does not) and `warnings` (what it removed, links lost, regions later features use that change their names); undo step `Clean Up Projections in Sketch1`; see [Clean Up Projections](#clean-up-projections) |
| `sketch.clean_up_stale_projections` | none | as other edits, and `stale` (`{"removed": [curves], "trimmed": [lines], "unlinked": [sources], "kept": [{"curve", "why"}], "preview": {"removed": [{"curve", "type", "geometry"}], "cut": [{"line", "start", "end"}]}}`; `why`: `region`, `user_curve`, `constrained` or `used`; `preview`: the removed curves as they were, geometry as the `sketch` query gives it, and the pieces trimmed off lines, from the old end to the new one, for a preview to draw) and `warnings` (the same in words, and regions later features use that change their names); undo step `Clean Up Stale Projections in Sketch1`; see [Clean Up Stale Projections](#clean-up-stale-projections) |
| `sketch.convert_projected` | `entities`: curves and points | the projected ones become ordinary free sketch geometry; as other edits, and `converted` (the entities converted), `kept` (their points that stay projected) and `warnings`; undo step `Convert to Sketch Geometry in Sketch1`; see [Convert to Sketch Geometry](#convert-to-sketch-geometry) |

The `sketch` query (`{"query": "sketch", "uid": "F1"}`) returns:

- `uid`, `name`, `plane`, `frame` (`origin`, `x_axis`, `y_axis`, `normal`
  in the coordinates of the sketch's component, moved into the design by
  an occurrence's `world` placement, mitcad#958; or null when the sketch
  did not evaluate),
  `solved`, `error`;
- `warnings`: the sketch evaluation's (as the timeline's), such as linked
  projections that could not follow their sources;
- `warning_entities` (mitcad#264): one list of entity ids per warning, in
  the order of `warnings`, of what the warning is about, so that a client
  need not read the text: a linked projection's warning lists all of its
  entities when it is `kept` or `lost`, else its `stale` curves when it has
  any, else its `unfollowed` entities; the warning about collapsed curves
  (mitcad#365: a line of no length, a circle or arc of no radius, which make
  no region) lists those curves, also as `degenerate` beside `dof` and
  `redundant`; a warning about anything else (a
  font replaced) has an empty list. The `warnings` entries stay strings
  (the `timeline` and `feature` queries' are the same strings), so their
  readers are unchanged;
- `entities`: the definition's (linked projections, and what is
  constrained to them, where the last evaluation put them: their sources'
  current geometry), with solved `at` for points, `geometry`
  for curves (line `start`, `end`; circle `center`, `radius`; arc also
  `start_angle`, `end_angle`, `start`, `end`; ellipse `major_radius`,
  `minor_radius`, `rotation`; splines `degree`, `control`, `weights`,
  `knots`) and `fully_constrained`; entities a derived offset computes
  have `"derived": true`;
- `constraints`, `dimensions` (with parameter names, `measured`, and for
  a driving one its parameter's `expression` and `comment`), `projections` (each also, after an evaluation where it did
  not follow all the way: `unfollowed`, its entities that found nothing
  like them in the source; `unmatched`, how many of the source's curves and
  points none of its entities follows; `lost`: the source is gone; `kept`:
  its curves no longer match the source's, so it kept its last geometry:
  following by geometry would tear an arc from the curves it shares points
  with, or one without `by_geometry` found them changed, mitcad#249;
  `stale`: its curves that match none of the source's current curves,
  all of them for a lost source, mitcad#252);
- `texts`, also `family` (the font used), `fallback` (the bundled font
  instead of the one asked for), `stored_outlines` (true when the
  outlines are the text's stored `glyphs`, its font missing; `family` is
  then the text's font and `fallback` false) and `outline`: `[{"id":
  "t9.g0.c0", "curves": [geometry, …]}]`; a text's stored `glyphs` are
  left out, `has_glyphs` true in their place;
- `patterns` and `offsets`, also `values` and `value`: `parameter`,
  `value`, `expression`;
- `regions`: `key`, `area`, `centroid`, `loops` (segment keys, outer loop
  first); a glyph's region also `text` and `letter` (false for a
  counter);
- `dof`, `fully_constrained` (entity ids), `redundant` (constraint ids
  implied by the others) and `conflicts` (sets of ids that contradict
  each other);
- `unmet_inactive` (only when not empty): the inactive constraints and
  dimensions the geometry does not meet ([Inactive constraints and
  dimensions](#inactive-constraints-and-dimensions)).

The positions, curves and status come from the sketch's last evaluation
while it succeeded and was made from the definition and the parameter
values the document has now (mitcad#679: `Document::evaluated_solve`;
the definition the result cache keeps with the evaluation, and the
values it read). A sketch with projections, one that failed, is rolled
back or suppressed, or whose definition or values changed since is
solved by the query, with the same result. The document also keeps the
last answers (`Document::known_sketch_answer`), each with the sketch's
definition, its evaluation, warnings and the parameters it was made
from: asked again while none of them changed, the query answers at
once. A drag's edit stores the drag's own solve instead of solving its
result again, so one `sketch.drag` solves twice: the drag and the
recompute.

### Clean Up Projections

`sketch.clean_up_projections` (mitcad#232, `sketch/cleanup.rs`) tidies
projected (reference) curves; nothing else does it automatically across
projections, since two projections that coincide now may differ after a
change (the region finder counts coincident curves once, so they make no
slivers):

- a curve the same as another (either way round, its own points or
  shared) goes; the lower id stays, which keeps the regions' names;
- with `merge`, a line on a longer collinear one goes, and two collinear
  lines that overlap and follow no source become one (the lower id, from
  the outer ends);
- constraints, dimensions and other curves that used the removed curve or
  its points use the kept curve and its points there; constraints that
  then say nothing (a curve parallel to itself) go; a curve a pattern, an
  offset or a text uses stays;
- a kept curve follows its own projection's source only (`link` in
  `cleaned`, and a warning): a merged curve is not split again when the
  sources differ;
- a region whose name changes (names are made of curve ids) and that a
  later feature uses is a warning; the whole is one undo step, and it is
  refused when there is nothing to clean up.

### Clean Up Stale Projections

`sketch.clean_up_stale_projections` (mitcad#252, `sketch/stale.rs`) tidies
a sketch whose linked projections stopped following their sources (the
source changed shape since: an imported projection, a face edited
upstream). It works on the curves the last evaluation found stale (the
`sketch` query's `stale` of each projection), so the sketch must have
evaluated:

- a stale curve goes when it matters to nothing: it bounds no region a
  later feature uses (the profiles later features sweep, as they find
  them, and the regions their definitions name) and names no segment of
  one (a curve at a segment's end), no pattern, offset or text uses it, no
  constraint or dimension ties it, or a point that goes with it, to
  geometry that stays, and no curve of the user's ends on it; the others
  stay, listed in `kept` with why;
- a stale line that stays because it bounds a used region, and runs past
  the region, is trimmed to where the region's last segment on it ends
  (the user's line that closes the profile, the new outline's corner);
  only an end that nothing else holds moves (an old corner that only other
  stale lines share gets a point of its own), only when the points
  constrained onto the line stay on what is left and no dimension measures
  it, and only when every used region keeps its name and area;
- a projection that would still not follow (kept, lost, or with stale or
  unfollowed entities left) is unlinked: its entities stay as fixed
  references and the sketch stops warning; one whose entities all go goes
  with them. A projection is never linked again by geometry
  (`by_geometry`): following by geometry moves its entities to the
  nearest curves of the source, which can change the profiles and faces
  later features and other sketches see;
- a region whose name changes and that a later feature uses is a warning;
  the whole is one undo step, and it is refused when there is nothing to
  clean up.

### Points that become one

Curves are joined only through a shared point (Offset's chains, the
chain selection, the free-end markers); two ends held together by a
point-to-point `coincident` are two ends. So (mitcad#259, mitcad#260,
`sketch/points.rs`):

- `sketch.extend`: when the extension's nearest hit lies on an existing
  point (within the tolerance of the full-turn check), the extended end
  becomes that point: a point of the curve reached first, else any other
  (the lower id), never one of the extended curve. A projected point, or
  one a derived offset computes or a pattern makes, is the model's: the
  end is a new point with a point-to-point `coincident` to it. Elsewhere
  the end point stays (mitcad#362): when only the extended curve ends it
  and it is not fixed, projected, computed or a pattern's, it moves onto
  the curve reached and keeps its id, its constraints and its dimensions
  (the extent constraints of the curve, its length, arc length and
  midpoints, go), and a `coincident` holds it on the curve; a dimension on
  it whose parameter is a plain number of its own takes the value it now
  measures, one with an expression or a shared parameter keeps its value
  and holds. Any other end is a new point on the curve reached. A hit in
  the middle of a curve (a T junction) is not a split; collinear lines
  stay two lines.
- `sketch.add_constraint` with a `coincident` between two points that are
  both ends of curves (lines, arcs, elliptical arcs, spline ends) merges
  them: one is kept (a fixed point over a free one, else the one more
  constraints and dimensions name, else the lower id) and everything that
  named the other (curve ends, constraints, dimensions, text frames) names
  the kept one. Constraints and dimensions that then say nothing go (a
  distance between the two points, a point-on-curve on a curve the point
  now ends, the same constraint twice); a point symmetric to itself about
  a line becomes a point on the line. The sketch is solved with the
  coincidence first, where it solves, so the kept point is where the solve
  puts it; a merged sketch that does not solve, or that the merge
  over-constrains, is refused, and nothing changes. It stays a constraint
  when either point is no curve end (a lone point, a centre, a spline's
  inner point), one curve has both points, both are fixed, or either is
  projected, computed by a derived offset or a pattern's. Existing
  constraints are not migrated.

### Convert to Sketch Geometry

`sketch.convert_projected` (mitcad#257, `sketch/convert.rs`) turns the
projected (reference) curves and points among `entities` into ordinary
sketch geometry: not `reference`, not `fixed`, out of their linked
projection's `entities`:

- a curve takes its points with it, except a point a projected curve that
  stays also uses: that point stays projected (fixed, still following), the
  converted curve joined to it, and it is listed in `kept`;
- a projected point given (a projected vertex) converts the same way when
  no projected curve that stays uses it;
- a projection with nothing left goes; the others follow their sources for
  what is left. One without `by_geometry` (an import's, or of a file of an
  earlier version) follows only a source whose curves come back as it
  listed them, so with some of its entities converted it keeps its
  geometry from then on, which `warnings` says;
- constraints and dimensions stay (the sketch may get degrees of freedom);
  region keys do not change; a stale curve converted is no longer stale;
- entities that are not projected are left as they are (`warnings`); the
  command is refused when none of `entities` is projected, or when nothing
  would convert (only points projected curves that stay use).

### A constraint that replaces one it makes redundant

A new constraint the others already imply is refused ("k6 would
over-constrain the sketch: …"). When it is implied only in part, it
replaces the older constraint it makes redundant, as the user's last
intent (mitcad#287, `SketchEdit::drop_implied` in `sketch/edit.rs`): a
rectangle standing on a projected line, its bottom `horizontal` and its
left corner `coincident` with the line's left end; a `coincident` of its
right corner with the line's right end fixes the corner's x, which
nothing else does, and its height, which the left corner and the
`horizontal` already fix. The `horizontal` goes and the `coincident` is
added:

- `sketch.add_constraint` removes older geometric constraints from the
  redundant sets the new constraint makes (the solver's diagnosis), one
  at a time, each only when it lowers the redundant count, until the
  count is back where it was before the command; the new constraint must
  still take at least one degree of freedom away.
- Never removed: a dimension, a fixed entity, an `equal_spacing` and a
  constraint on projected geometry (the links that hold the sketch to the
  model). When only those would do, nothing is removed and the
  constraint is refused as before; a constraint that contradicts the
  others (a dimension of another length) fails the solve and is refused.
- The result lists the removed constraints in `removed` and, with their
  types, in `implied_removed`: `[{"constraint": "k1", "type":
  "horizontal"}]`. The command is one undo step: undo restores them.
- The sketch tools show it as a hint (`Horizontal removed: implied by the
  new Coincident`), also for a constraint a snap makes while drawing.
- The removal tries first the constraints on the new constraint's own
  movable geometry (its points and curves and the points of those
  curves, not fixed ones such as an axis or the origin), then the others,
  each group in id order (mitcad#865): a Symmetry of two circles
  replaces the constraint that held one of the circles, not one further
  along the chain its position follows from.

### Symmetry of circles with fixed radii

A `symmetric` constraint of two circles or two arcs mirrors their
centres and makes their radii equal (an arc: its ends mirrored, start to
end). When the others already make the radii equal (both dimensioned,
or an `equal`), `sketch.add_constraint` leaves the radius equality out
(mitcad#865, `SketchEdit::fit_symmetric` in `sketch/edit.rs`) and stores
the constraint with `"radii": false`: it then mirrors the positions only
(the centres, and an arc's end directions from its centre), so that it
takes what is not fixed yet instead of over-constraining the sketch:

- Implied in part, it replaces the older geometric constraints it makes
  redundant, as in [A constraint that replaces one it makes
  redundant](#a-constraint-that-replaces-one-it-makes-redundant), never a
  dimension: four Ø10 circles in a dimensioned square, the bottom left
  one free along a construction diagonal (1 degree of freedom), and a
  Symmetry of the two left circles about the x axis: the radii are left
  to the dimensions, the bottom left centre's `coincident` with the
  diagonal goes, and the sketch is fully constrained.
- Implied in full, it is refused as before (`k12 would over-constrain
  the sketch: …`).
- Without `radii` (all designs before), or with two radii free, the
  radii are made equal as before.

### An upright sketch frame

`sketch.create` with `"upright": true` (and no `frame`; mitcad#692) gives
the new sketch the own frame (`frame`) that shows the design upright when
the sketch opens: the application looks along the frame's normal with the
sketch's y axis up, so the frame decides what is up on the screen. Create
Sketch in the application asks for it; scripts and other callers get the
plane's frame unless they ask.

- y, the screen's up: the design's +Z projected onto the plane, when the
  plane's normal is not along Z (the XZ and YZ planes, vertical and
  slanted faces); the design's +Y when it is (the XY plane, top and
  bottom faces).
- The normal stays the plane's, the side the sketch is drawn on, so the
  sketch is not mirrored; x = y × normal. The screen's horizontal stays
  the sketch's x, so Horizontal and Vertical constraints, the grid and
  the dimensions stay horizontal and vertical on the screen.
- Results: XY keeps its frame (x = +X, y = +Y). XZ gets x = -X, y = +Z
  (the plane's own frame has y = -Z). YZ gets x = +Y, y = +Z (the plane's
  own x = -Z). A face facing ±X or ±Y gets y = +Z whichever way it faces;
  a top face y = +Y, x = +X, a bottom face y = +Y, x = -X.
- The design's axes are taken where the sketch is shown: in the
  coordinates of its component through the occurrence `context` or
  `occurrence` names (else the component's first occurrence).
- The frame is stored only when it differs from the plane's: a sketch on
  XY or a top face has none. The sketch keeps it as any own frame, also
  when its plane moves later; existing and imported sketches keep theirs.
  The command stays one undo step (`Add Sketch2`).

### Projected outlines and their offsets

An edge projected again, or a face projected after one of its edges,
used to add a second curve on the edge with points of its own, so the
outline was no chain for `sketch.offset` (mitcad#741). Now:

- `sketch.project` joins the new entities to the projected geometry
  already in the sketch (`sketch/project.rs`, `join_existing`): a curve
  the same as one there is not added again (the result's `warnings`
  name it), and ends and loose points where an end or a loose point is
  are that point. A linked projection joins only the entities of linked
  projections of the same body and link, an unlinked one only projected
  entities in no projection, so a static curve never ends on a point
  that follows a source. Points of arcs are never shared between linked
  projections (a line takes either place when two sources part, an arc
  would no longer fit its centre); an arc the same as one there is left
  out only when no other new curve ends on it. A join that would make
  three non-construction curves end at one point is not made: a face
  projected beside one it shares an edge with keeps its own line on that
  edge, so that each outline stays a chain (Chain Selection stops where
  three curves meet). A projection that adds nothing gets no record. Within one projection, ends closer than half
  of 1e-7 of its size share a point (a model's edges meet within its
  tolerance), as following allows.
- `sketch.offset` counts curves that are the same (within 1e-7 of the
  sketch's size, a line or a spline either way round) once: of such a
  pair, picked or not, it takes the one that shares its ends with more of
  the other listed curves, the listed one when that is as good, and
  `warnings` says so ("c3 lies on c9 (the same curve twice): c9 is
  offset"). Curves that are no chain are refused with the reason: where
  they branch, or the curve that does not join and how far its nearest
  end is from theirs (two ends within 0.01 mm that are two points: a
  Coincident constraint joins them). An open chain whose free end lies
  within 0.01 mm of another curve's end on a point of its own (of the
  same construction kind) warns. The exact offset's refusal at a corner
  names the two curves.
- A sweep's or a pipe's sketch path (`path.rs`) takes a curve the same as
  an earlier one once, chained or listed.
- Chain Selection in the application (Offset) starts from the curve a
  picked one lies on when the picked one joins nothing and that one
  does.

### Insert Point on a spline

`sketch.insert_spline_point` (mitcad#836, `sketch/spline_points.rs`):
`sketch`, `curve` (a `spline` or a `fitted_spline`), `at` [x, y] (a place
on or near the curve). One undo step, `Insert Spline Point in <sketch>`;
result `made`: the new point.

- **Fitted spline:** a new fit point where the curve is nearest to `at`,
  listed between its two neighbours in the curve's order (in a closed
  spline after the last point when the place is on the stretch back to
  the first). The curve still passes through every fit point; between the
  new point's neighbours it may change shape a little, as the cubic now
  interpolates one more point. Refused on an existing fit point.
- **Spline by control points:** a knot inserted once at the parameter
  nearest to `at` (Boehm's algorithm; rational splines too): one more
  control point and the same curve, exactly, at every parameter. The
  `knots` (and `weights`) are written out in full. The control points
  next to the new one move to keep the shape (`degree - 1` of them, fewer
  where the knot is there already); they keep their ids. Refused at the
  ends of the curve (a closed spline: where it closes), where the knot is
  there `degree` times already (the curve passes through a control point
  there), and when a point that would move is listed twice in `control`.
- Closed splines work alike: a closed fitted spline, and a spline by
  control points whose ends are one point (or whose knots are unclamped).
- Every existing point keeps its id, its constraints and its dimensions;
  a constraint on a control point that moved may then pull the curve when
  the sketch solves. Refused for a projected curve and for a curve a
  derived offset computes, as Trim is.

### Dragging a selection

`sketch.drag` with `entities` (points and curves, mitcad#837) and `by`
[dx, dy] drags them together, as sketch mode does when the press is on
one of several selected curves or points:

```json
{"cmd": "sketch.drag", "sketch": "F1", "entities": ["c1", "c4", "p3"], "by": [5, 3]}
```

- Every point of the entities (a curve's ends, centre and control
  points) is pulled by the offset from where it is now, as far as the
  constraints allow; a point that several of them share, such as a
  selected end of a selected curve, is pulled once. All of it is one
  solve, as a single drag's, and one undo step `Drag in Sketch1`.
- Constraints and dimensions hold: those among the entities keep the set
  rigid, fixed geometry holds and geometry constrained to something
  outside the set pulls back as the solver decides, and geometry outside
  the set follows its constraints and shared points.
- A derived offset's curve or point pulls its source chain, as in a
  single drag.
- `entities` takes `by` only, and not together with `entity`; an empty
  list is refused.

### Scaling a sketch

`sketch.scale` (mitcad#860, `sketch/scale.rs`): `sketch`, `factor` (a
number greater than zero), `center` (a point id or [x, y]; the sketch
origin when left out). It scales the whole sketch about `center`, one
undo step `Scale <sketch>`:

```json
{"cmd": "sketch.scale", "sketch": "F1", "factor": 2.5}
```

- Every point of the sketch's own geometry moves away from or towards
  `center` by the factor; circles' radii and ellipses' minor radii, the
  texts' places, heights and line spacings (a QR code's module size) and
  the places of the dimensions' values scale with it. The sketch's origin
  point and axes stay where they are.
- The values of its driving length dimensions (every kind but `angle`),
  of its offsets' distances and of its rectangular patterns' spacings are
  multiplied by the factor, so that the sketch keeps its shape and its
  constraints. Angles stay.
- Refused for a sketch with projected, intersected or linked geometry
  (it follows its source), and when one of those length values is
  another parameter or an expression of one (change that instead).

**The first dimension scales the sketch.** `sketch.add_dimension` with
`"scale_sketch": true` (default false; the application sends it while the
preference *Scale the sketch to its first dimension* is on, its default)
applies the first-dimension rule to a driving dimension: when the sketch
was drawn out of proportion, its geometry is first scaled uniformly about
the sketch origin by the dimension's value over what it measures now, as
`sketch.scale` does, so that the dimension holds; then the dimension is
added as usual. Both are one undo step, `Add Dimension to <sketch>`.

- Only a length, distance, radius or diameter (every kind but `angle`),
  and only when the sketch has no other dimension, offset or rectangular
  pattern, no projected, intersected or linked geometry, and no fixed
  entity other than its origin point and axes (`sketch.axis`). Otherwise,
  and for a driven dimension, nothing is scaled, as without the flag.
- The constraints are kept; text heights scale too. The dimension's
  `text` place, given on the sketch as drawn, scales with it.
- Result: as other edits, and `scaled` (the factor) when the sketch was
  scaled. A value equal to what the geometry measures scales nothing; so
  a drawing tool's typed value, which draws its shape at that size,
  scales the sketch only where the shape was drawn at another size.

## Components and occurrences

The design is a root component (`C0`, named `Root` until renamed); other
components (`C1`, …) are placed in it, or in each other, by occurrences
(`O1`, …, named `<component>:<n>`, e.g. `Plate:2`). Code:
`core/model/src/assembly.rs`, commands in `document/components.rs`.
Examples: `tools/cli/tests/f6_*.json`.

- **One timeline.** Every feature belongs to a component: the active one
  when it is added (or `component` of `add_feature`). A feature works on
  the bodies of its own component, in that component's coordinates: a
  body of another component fails the feature (`body F3.b0 (from
  Extrude2) belongs to Component1; …`), and a sketch or construction
  geometry of another component is refused when the feature is added.
  Sketch planes and projections, and a combine's tools, may name another
  component's geometry with where it was picked ([Geometry of other
  components](#geometry-of-other-components)).
- **Shared definitions.** A component's bodies are built once, in its own
  coordinates; every occurrence shows them placed by its transform, and a
  component placed in another is placed again with every occurrence of
  that one. The `bodies` query lists the definitions, the `instances`
  query the bodies as placed in the design. For display, draw each
  instance's `body_shape` moved by its `transform`.
- **New components.** `create_component` makes an empty one placed in the
  active component. The operation `new_component` of extrude, revolve,
  the primitives and base features, and combine's `new_component`, make a
  component placed in the feature's component (identity; beside it when
  its design policy takes no components, [Design policy](#design-policy)), named
  `Component<n>`, holding the bodies the feature creates (a combine: its
  target); editing the operation away removes it (refused while something
  was added to it), and deleting the feature deletes it unless something
  else is in it. `components_from_bodies` adds, per body, a
  `component_from_bodies` feature in the body's component: the body moves
  into a new component named after it, where it is, keeping its id and
  name; later features on it belong to that component. The features
  that made a body can move into a component with it instead
  ([Moving features into components](#moving-features-into-components)).
- **Placements.** An occurrence's transform is rigid (rows of a rotation
  and a translation, `[[r00, r01, r02, tx], …]`, in its parent's
  coordinates). Timeline features place occurrences of their own
  component: `move_occurrence` moves them, `capture_position` puts them
  at captured placements. `set_occurrence_transform` sets an occurrence's
  own placement while no feature before the marker places it, or with
  `"capture": true` adds a `capture_position` feature. A grounded
  occurrence does not move: the command is refused and a feature that
  would move it fails (`Plate:2 is grounded`).
- **Copies.** `copy_occurrence` places the same component again (one
  definition). `paste_new` makes a new component, a copy of the
  definition with its history: its features (new ids and default names;
  references among them follow), their own parameters (copied with their
  expressions; other parameters are shared), the components placed in it
  and, for a component a new-component operation made, that feature. A
  component made from bodies, or linked, is copied as its bodies (a base
  feature), retaining body material, visibility and appearance assignments;
  face overrides follow the snapshot's new face names. Both go into the
  active component, which must not be in the copied one.
- **External components.** `insert_component` places another design
  file in the active component: linked (default) as a read-only
  component whose bodies are a base feature holding the file's visible
  bodies as that design places them (its link: `path`, a digest of the
  text and the feature), or with `"link": false` as a copy of the file's
  design with its history (its root becomes the new component; its user
  parameters come along, renamed `name_1` when the name is taken). Linked
  components cannot be activated or edited. `update_links` (with the
  design file's directory as `base` for relative paths) reads the linked
  files again and takes the bodies of those that changed; a missing file
  keeps the saved bodies. Callers run it when they open a design (no
  undo step; what changed is a load warning). Only files in the design's
  project are followed (mitcad#929; for a design in no project, its
  folder and the folders in it): a link whose path is absolute outside it,
  or whose `..` leads out of it, is not read at all, and its component
  keeps the saved bodies with the message "<component>: the link outside
  the project is not followed (<path>); it keeps the bodies saved with
  the project". Without `base` no link is followed. So that links stay
  followed, `insert_component` records a file in the project by its path
  relative to `base` (`../parts/plate.mitcad`, with `/`), whatever form
  `path` had; a file outside the project keeps `path` as given, and its
  link is not followed when the design opens again.
- **Deleting.** `delete_occurrence` deletes an occurrence; the last one
  of a component deletes the component with its features, the feature
  that made it and what depends on them, and the components only it
  contained (a component made from bodies gives them back to its parent).

### Component commands and queries

| Command | Fields | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `create_component` | `name` (optional), `transform` (optional), `activate` (default true), `policy` (optional: a preset name or settings, [Design policy](#design-policy)) | `component`, `occurrence`, `name`; `placed_in`, `instead_of`, `placement_warning` when it went beside an active component that takes no components ([Design policy](#design-policy)) |
| `components_from_bodies` | `bodies` | `components`: `feature`, `component`, `name` |
| `activate_component` | `component` (uid or name; `C0` the root), `opening` (default false: one undo step; true: as the document opens, mitcad#426, with no undo step and no new revision, so the document stays as modified as it was and nothing is recomputed; the application activates the root of every design it opens) | `component`; with `opening` also `previous`, the component that was active |
| `rename_component` | `component`, `name` (unique) | `renamed_body`: `uid`, `name` of the body renamed with it, or null |
| `ground_occurrence` | `occurrence`, `grounded` (default true) | |
| `set_occurrence_visible` | `occurrence`, `visible`, or `expression` (a condition; [Bindings](#bindings-values-from-expressions)) | |
| `set_occurrence_transform` | `occurrence`, `transform`, `capture` (default false) | `feature`: the capture, or null |
| `copy_occurrence` | `occurrence`, `transform` (optional) | `occurrence`, `name` |
| `paste_new` | `occurrence`, `transform` (optional) | `component`, `occurrence`, `name` |
| `delete_occurrence` | `occurrence` | `deleted`: features |
| `insert_component` | `path` or `library` ([Component libraries](#library-parts)), `link` (default true), `transform`, `name`, `base` (directory of relative paths), `mount` (placed by a mount frame instead of `transform`, [Mount frames](#mount-frames)), `parameters` (linked with options, [Options of inserted components](#options-of-inserted-components)) | `component`, `occurrence`, `name`, `bodies` (the new component's), `frames` (its mount frames: `name`, `kind`, `joint`, `pitch`, `cells`, `footprint`, `feature` (the joint origin), `occurrence`), `joint` and `joint_name` (a mount placement's, else null), `mount` (what the placement did, as `mount_preview` answers); with `parameters` also `moves` and `refused` |
| `update_links` | `base` (optional) | `messages` |
| `reparent_occurrence` | `occurrence` (path from the root), `parent` (path; empty: the root) | see [Moving an occurrence to another parent](#moving-an-occurrence-to-another-parent) |

| Query | Fields | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `components` | | `active`; `components` (the root first): `uid`, `name`, `created_by`, `link` (path), `library` (a library part's record, or null), `features`, `bodies`, `occurrences` (count), `policy` ([Design policy](#design-policy)); `occurrences`: the tree from the root, each `uid`, `name`, `path`, `component`, `transform` (rows, in the parent, at the marker), `world` (4x4 into the design), `grounded`, `visible`, `children` |
| `instances` | `properties`, `hidden` (default false) | the bodies as placed: `path` (occurrence uids), `occurrence` (path name, empty for the root's), `component`, `component_name`, `body`, `name`, `visible`, `transform` (4x4); with `properties` the placed body's `volume`, `area`, `center`, `bbox` |

- An occurrence is given by its uid (`O3`), its name (`Plate:2`) or its
  path from the root (`Arm:1/Pin:2` or `O1/O4`: the last one).
- A `transform` is 3 or 4 rows of 4 numbers (a 4x4 matrix ends with `[0,
  0, 0, 1]`), or `{"translation": [x, y, z], "rotation": {"axis": [x, y,
  z], "angle": a}}` (both optional; the rotation about the origin comes
  first).
- Each command is an undo step (`New Component Plate`, `Ground Plate:1`,
  `Hide Plate:1`, `Paste Plate:2`, `Paste New Plate (1)`, `Insert
  part.mitcad`, …); hiding, renaming and activating recompute nothing.
- **Renaming a component renames its body** (mitcad#291): a component
  (not the root) with exactly one body at the marker whose name is still
  a default one (the generated `Body<n>`) gives the body its new name too,
  in the same undo step, unless another body already has that name. A
  body the user named is never renamed; once renamed with its component
  the body's name is no longer a default one, so later renames leave it.
  The reply's `renamed_body` names it (null when no body was renamed), so
  the application refreshes the browser and the timeline without asking
  again.
- The text report (`mitcad-cli info`) lists the components and the placed
  bodies.
- Design file (version 2 and later), when there are components:
  `root_component` (the root's name when renamed), `components` (`uid`,
  `name`, `created_by`, `link`), `occurrences` (`uid`, `component`,
  `parent`, `number`, `transform` rows unless the identity, `grounded`,
  `"visible": false`), `active_component`, and a feature's `component`
  when it is not the root. Files without them load with every feature in
  the root component.

## Joints

Joints connect occurrences and say how they may move against each other
(mitcad#55). They are timeline features of the component they are added
in (the active one, or `component`), recomputed in order like
`move_occurrence` and `capture_position`, and edited, suppressed,
reordered and deleted like other features (`edit_feature` takes the `def`
the `feature` query gives). Code: `core/model/src/joints.rs` (kinds,
frames, what recompute does), `features/joint.rs` (definitions),
`document/joints.rs` and `api/joints.rs`, the joint solver
`core/solver/src/rigid.rs` ([README](../../solver/README.md#joints-rigid-bodies));
tests `joint_tests.rs`, `joint_solver_tests.rs`, `core/solver/tests/rigid.rs`,
`tools/cli/tests/joints.json`.

Joints are stored, checked, reported and solved (below), the
application's ASSEMBLE group adds, edits, drives, drags and animates them
([app/COMMANDS.md](../../../app/COMMANDS.md), "Joints"), and the
`.f3d` import brings the file's joints in as these features
([.f3d import with the timeline](#f3d-import-with-the-timeline), *From
the dump IR*).

### Kinds and frames

A joint joins origin `a` to origin `b`. Each origin resolves to a frame
(an origin and x, y, z axes) on geometry of an occurrence's component,
moved into the joint's component by the occurrences' placements. The joint
holds when

`frame_a = frame_b · motion(values) · Rz(angle) · Tz(offset) · flip`

`motion` is the kind's free motions at some values, along and about frame
`b`'s axes, composed in the order listed; `flip` turns frame `a` over
(half a turn about its x axis). Without `flip` the two z axes point the
same way: to put a face on a face (both outward normals), flip.

| Kind | Free motions | Values |
|---|---|---|
| `rigid` | none | |
| `revolute` | turns about z | `rz` |
| `slider` | slides along `slide_axis` (`x`, `y` or `z`, default `z`) | `tx`, `ty` or `tz` |
| `cylindrical` | slides along z, turns about it | `tz`, `rz` |
| `pin_slot` | slides along x, turns about z | `tx`, `rz` |
| `planar` | slides along x and y, turns about z | `tx`, `ty`, `rz` |
| `ball` | turns about z, y and x | `rz`, `ry`, `rx` |

Slides are millimetres, turns radians (right-handed).

**Origins.** `{"occurrence": "O1/O4", "geometry": <reference>,
"frame_override": {...}}`. `occurrence` is a path of occurrences from the
joint's component (uids in definitions; `add_joint` also takes names,
`Arm:1/Pin:2`), empty or left out for the component's own geometry (which
never moves). `geometry` is a [reference](#references-to-geometry) to
geometry of the component the path ends in, resolved there:

| Geometry | Origin | z axis |
|---|---|---|
| planar face | its middle (`Kernel::face_plane`) | the outward normal |
| cylindrical or conical face | the axis point nearest to the face's middle | the axis (along its largest component) |
| toroidal face | the centre | the axis |
| spherical face | the centre | the component's z |
| circular edge | the centre | the axis (along its largest component) |
| straight edge | the middle | along the edge |
| vertex, sketch point, construction point, the origin, a fixed point | the point | the component's z |
| sketch circle or arc | the centre | the sketch's normal |
| sketch line, construction or origin axis, fixed axis | the start or the axis's origin | along it |
| origin plane, construction plane, joint origin, fixed plane | its origin | its normal (its x axis kept) |

Other x axes are the model X projected across z (Y when z is along X).
`frame_override` replaces parts of the frame, in the component's
coordinates: `origin` [x, y, z], `z_axis`, `x_axis` (projected across z);
`shift` [x, y, z] then moves the origin along the frame's own axes as they
are after the override, so that it follows geometry that moves (BUILD's
corners on a profile's end, mitcad#417).
A body is no origin. A sketch or construction geometry of another
component than the path's is refused when the joint is added
(``a: Sketch1 is in Plate, not in Pin``); a body of another component
fails the joint at recompute (`body F2.b0 is not in Pin at this point of
the timeline`).

### Feature definitions

```json
{"type": "joint", "kind": "revolute",
 "a": {"occurrence": "O2", "geometry": {"body": "F4.b0", "face": "F4:start(r{…})"}},
 "b": {"occurrence": "O1", "geometry": {"body": "F2.b0", "face": "F2:end(r{…})"}},
 "offset": 0, "angle": 0, "flip": true,
 "limits": {"rz": {"min": "-90 deg", "max": "90 deg", "rest": "30 deg"}},
 "position": {"rz": "45 deg"}}
{"type": "as_built_joint", "kind": "revolute", "a": "O2", "b": "O1",
 "origin": {"occurrence": "O2", "geometry": "F9"},
 "relative": [[1, 0, 0, 100], [0, 1, 0, 0], [0, 0, 1, 0]], "limits": {}}
{"type": "joint_origin", "geometry": {"body": "F2.b0", "face": "F2:end(r{…})"},
 "frame_override": {"origin": [5, 5, 10]}, "offset": 0, "angle": 0, "flip": false}
{"type": "rigid_group", "occurrences": ["O2", "O3"]}
```

- `joint` (named `Joint<n>`): `kind`, `slide_axis` (sliders only), `a`,
  `b`, `offset` (along z, a length), `angle` (about z), `flip`, `limits`,
