  `position`; `offset`, `angle` and `flip` default to 0 and false. The
  two origins must be on different occurrences, and at most one may be
  the component's own geometry.
- `limits`: per free motion of the kind, `{"min", "max", "rest"}`, each
  optional and a [value](#values) (parameters and expressions: a turn's
  slots are angles, `limits.rz.min_angle`, a slide's lengths,
  `limits.tz.min`). min ≤ rest ≤ max is checked when the joint is added or
  edited, and a parameter change that breaks it fails the joint.
- `position`: per free motion of the kind, the value it is driven to (a
  [value](#values): `position.rz.position_angle`, `position.tz.position`),
  within its limits (checked like `rest`). `drive_joint` and
  `drag_occurrence` set it.
- A free motion is **driven** (held at a value) by its `position`, else
  by its `rest` value; without either it is **free**: it moves as the
  joints need, stays within its limits, and otherwise stays where it is.
  Driven values say where a motion is, not whether it can move: degrees
  of freedom leave them out.
- `as_built_joint` (`AsBuiltJoint<n>`): two occurrence paths `a` and `b`
  joined where they are: `relative` is `a`'s placement in `b`'s
  coordinates when it was made (rows of a rotation and a translation;
  `add_as_built_joint` records it; without it the joint takes the
  placements as they are at its point of the timeline). `origin` (optional,
  an origin as above) is the frame of the free motions, `b`'s coordinates
  without it; an origin on `a`'s side is taken where the recorded
  relation puts it. The joint holds when `a`'s displacement from where
  the recorded relation puts it is the kind's motions in that frame
  (values 0 at the recorded relation). Same kinds, limits and position.
- `joint_origin` (`JointOrigin<n>`): construction geometry of its
  component, a frame on `geometry` (as an origin's) with `frame_override`,
  then moved by `angle` about and `offset` along its z axis and turned
  over by `flip`. Its datum is a plane with that frame (the `datums`
  query; a sketch can be placed on it); joints use it as `"F9"`. It has a
  light bulb like construction geometry. With `mount` it is a mount frame
  of the part (mitcad#525, [Mount frames](#mount-frames)).
- `rigid_group` (`RigidGroup<n>`): two or more occurrences placed in the
  feature's component that move as one from its point of the timeline:
  the joints after it move them together, and a `move_occurrence` of one
  member moves the others by the same motion (`capture_position` sets
  each occurrence it lists). A group with a grounded member stays where
  it is: a move of a member fails (`Base:1 is grounded`).
- Joint features recompute nothing of the bodies and are never written
  to the result store.

### What recompute does

A **unit** is a top-level occurrence of the joint's component (the one
its path starts with) with those its rigid groups join to it; it moves
as one rigid body. A unit is fixed when a member is grounded; the
component's own geometry (an empty path) is fixed too.

At its point of the timeline, a joint resolves its frames (in the
components its paths end in, with that point's bodies, sketches and
construction geometry) and the joint solver solves it together with the
joints in effect before it in the same component that share moving units
with it, directly or through each other, from where the occurrences are
at that point:

- What needs no iteration is placed first, in timeline order: a joint
  between a side that is fixed (or joined to something fixed by the
  joints before it) and one that is not moves the free side, with every
  unit joined to it so far, so that the joint holds at its driven values
  and, for free motions, at the values nearest to where it is; between
  two free sides side `a` moves onto side `b`. An open chain needs
  nothing else.
- Joints that close a loop are iterated: the units move as little as
  possible (turns weighed by the size of the joints' layout) until every
  joint holds, driven motions at their values and free motions within
  their limits.
- The units that moved get placement changes of the joint feature (each
  occurrence's placement set), applied as `move_occurrence`'s are; the
  occurrences' own placements stay the starting ones (`state` `placed`,
  `moved`; `satisfied` when nothing had to move). Placements set by
  joints are not cached: grounding, ungrounding and moving an occurrence
  recompute them.
- Joints whose sides cannot move (both fixed, or both in one unit) only
  hold or fail: `both sides are fixed (Pin:1 and Plate:1) and the joint
  does not hold`, `both sides move with Pin:1, Pin:2 and the joint does not hold`, or `… is not
  at its position`.
- Joints that contradict each other fail the joint feature, which moves
  nothing: `over-constrained: Joint1 (at its rz position), Joint2 and
  Joint4 cannot all hold` (the rank analysis of the joints' equations,
  newest last; `at its … position` names driven values in the
  contradiction). A loop that cannot close from where the occurrences are
  (lengths or limits keep it apart) fails with `the joints cannot all
  hold (Joint1, Joint2, Joint3 and Joint4) from where the occurrences
  are: …`. The joints after it are solved without it.
- A path below a top-level occurrence only locates geometry: the joint
  moves the top-level occurrence (the whole sub-assembly), never an
  occurrence inside it; joints inside a sub-assembly are the
  sub-component's own features, solved in its coordinates.
- At the marker each joint reports its frames and values where the
  occurrences are; a later feature that moved a side (a
  `move_occurrence`) leaves `values` null and `solved` false.

A joint whose origins cannot be resolved (an occurrence that is gone, a
face that is no longer there, a body of another component) fails like any
feature and moves nothing.

### Commands and queries

| Command | Fields | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `add_joint` | `kind`, `slide_axis`, `a`, `b` (origins; `occurrence` by uids or names from the component), `offset`, `angle`, `flip`, `limits`, `position`, `name`, `component` (the active one when left out) | `uid`, `name`, `parameters` (created), `state`, `solved` |
| `add_as_built_joint` | `kind`, `slide_axis`, `a`, `b` (occurrence paths), `origin`, `limits`, `position`, `name`, `component` | the same; `relative` recorded from the placements at the marker |
| `add_rigid_group` | `occurrences` (two or more, placed in the component), `name`, `component` | `uid`, `name` |
| `drive_joint` | `joint` (uid or name), `values` (per motion a [value](#values), or null to take the position away) | `uid`, `parameters` (created), `state`, `values`; one undo step `Drive Joint1` |
| `drag_occurrence` | `occurrence` (uid, name or path), `point` (in the parent component's coordinates, moving with the occurrence; its origin when left out), `target` | as `joint_drag`; one undo step `Drag Pin:1` |

```json
{"cmd": "drive_joint", "joint": "Joint1", "values": {"rz": "crank_angle", "tz": null}}
{"cmd": "drag_occurrence", "occurrence": "Rocker:1", "point": [130, 0, 0], "target": [140, -10, 0]}
```

- `drive_joint` edits the joint's `position`: a parameter (`crank_angle`)
  makes the mechanism follow the parameter. With contact sets,
  `drive_joint`, `drag_occurrence` and `joint_drag` stop where bodies of
  a set touch ([Motion studies and contact
  sets](#motion-studies-and-contact-sets)).
- `drag_occurrence` keeps where `joint_drag` puts the occurrences: their
  own placements become the dragged ones (refused for an occurrence a
  `move_occurrence` or `capture_position` before the marker places:
  `capture the position instead`), and every driven motion that moved is
  driven to its new value (its `position` becomes the number). The
  joints before the marker then reproduce the dragged placements.

| Query | Fields | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `joints` | | `joints`: every joint and as-built joint in timeline order: `uid`, `name`, `type`, `kind`, `slide_axis` (sliders), `component`, `a` and `b` {`occurrence` (path name), `path` (uids)}, `motions`, `limits` (per motion `min`, `max`, `rest` as values), `position` (per driven motion its value), `status` and `error` (the feature's), `state` (`placed`, `satisfied`, or the status: `failed`, `suppressed`, `rolled_back`), `solved` (it holds at the marker), `message` (why not), `moved` (occurrences placed), `values` (per free motion, at the marker; null when the joint does not hold there), `within_limits`, `beyond_limits`, `frames` {`a`, `b`: `origin`, `x_axis`, `y_axis`, `z_axis` in the joint's component, at the marker; an as-built joint's motion frame as each side carries it}; `rigid_groups`: `uid`, `name`, `component`, `occurrences`, `names`, `active`, `status`, `error`; `dof`: per component with joint features, `component`, `total`, `overconstrained`, `redundant` and `conflicting` (joint uids), `units` (`occurrences` moving as one, `names`, `grounded`, `dof`, `mobile`, `joints`) |
| `joint_dof` | `occurrence` (uid, name or path) | in its parent component: `occurrence`, `name`, `component`, `grounded`, `group` (the occurrences moving with it), `dof`, `mobile`, `motions` (none when grounded, all six without joints, its joint's with one, null with more), `joints` (`uid`, `name`, `kind`, `other`, `motions`) |
| `joint_drag` | `occurrence`, `point`, `target` (as `drag_occurrence`) | `placements` (the occurrences that would move: `occurrence`, `name`, `transform` rows in the parent component), `values` (per joint uid of the parent component, its motions' values); changes nothing |
| `joint_frame` | `occurrence` (a path from `component`, uids or names; empty: its own geometry), `geometry`, `frame_override`, `component` (the root when left out) | the frame the origin gives at the marker, placed by the path into `component`'s coordinates: `origin`, `x_axis`, `y_axis`, `z_axis`; `component` (the one the path ends in) and `local` (the frame in its coordinates); refused for geometry of another component than the path's |

- Degrees of freedom are exact: the rank of the joints' equations where
  the occurrences are (the joint solver's analysis; driven values left
  out). `total` is what all units can do together (6 per unit that is not
  grounded less the rank); a unit's `dof` is what it can do with the
  other units held where they are, 0 when grounded. A four-bar linkage
  has `total` 1 while each link alone has 0. A unit is `mobile` when it
  moves in some motion of all units together (the others free too): each
  link of the four-bar linkage is; a unit rigidly joined to the
  component's own geometry or to a grounded one is not (nor is a grounded
  one), and a drag of it moves nothing. `redundant` lists joints
  whose equations repeat earlier ones (they hold: two hinges on one axis,
  the closing joint of a planar loop), `conflicting` those that
  contradict earlier ones where the occurrences are; `overconstrained`
  when either is not empty. Only joints that recomputed count.
- `joint_drag` pulls `point` toward `target` while every joint in effect
  at the marker in the occurrence's parent component holds (driven
  motions follow like free ones, limits hold), moving the other units as
  little as possible: as near as the joints let it. A grounded
  occurrence does not drag (`Crank:1 is grounded`). For a UI's drag
  preview: call it per pointer position, then `drag_occurrence` on
  release.
- `delete_occurrence` deletes the joints, as-built joints and rigid groups
  that name an occurrence that is gone, with what depends on them; they
  are in its `deleted`. Copies of components (`paste_new`, an inserted
  copy) take their joints along, naming the copies' occurrences.
- Joint features are saved as features (design file round trip); files
  without them have none.

### What each side is on

The `joints` query says what each side of a joint is built on
(mitcad#523), so that the application can highlight it (app/COMMANDS.md,
"Joints", *Joint highlight*) without reading the definitions:

- A `joint`'s `a` and `b`, and each constraint row's `a`, `b` (and `a2`,
  `b2` when given), have besides `occurrence` and `path`: `geometry`, the
  reference as the definition stores it (`{"body", "face"}`, `"F9"`,
  `"xy"`, `{"point": [x, y, z]}`, `{"mount": "F7:mount(end_a)"}`, …);
  `on`, what it is: `face`, `edge`, `vertex`, `body`, `sketch_curve`,
  `sketch_point`, `origin` (an origin plane, axis or the origin),
  `construction` (a construction plane, axis or point), `joint_origin`,
  `fixed` (a fixed plane, axis or point: in no geometry) or `mount` (a
  derived part's mount frame, BUILD); `frame_override` when the side has
  one, as the definition has it; and `component`, the component the path
  ends in (the feature's own for an empty path; left out when the path
  leads nowhere).
- An `as_built_joint`'s `a` and `b` have `on` `occurrence` and their
  `component`; its motion origin, when it has one, is `origin`, a side as
  above.

```json
{"name": "Joint1", "kind": "revolute", "component": "C0",
 "a": {"occurrence": "Pin:1", "path": ["O2"], "component": "C2", "on": "face",
       "geometry": {"body": "F4.b0", "face": "F4:start(r{…})"}},
 "b": {"occurrence": "Plate:1", "path": ["O1"], "component": "C1", "on": "face",
       "geometry": {"body": "F2.b0", "face": "F2:end(r{…})"},
       "frame_override": {"origin": [5, 5, 10]}},
 "frames": {"a": {"origin": [20, 20, 10], …}, "b": {…}}}
```

Model test: `joint_tests.rs`, `the_joints_query_says_what_each_side_is_on`.

## Assembly constraints

Assembly constraints (mitcad#148) hold geometry of one occurrence against
geometry of another, each taking away only some motions, and are solved
together with the joints. A `constraint_set` feature holds rows, each one
constraint; one row is a constraint, several are solved together. Code:
`core/model/src/constraints.rs` (what each type holds, references),
`features/constraint_set.rs` (the definition), recompute in `joints.rs`
(`apply`, `solve_new`), the solver's partial equations
`core/solver/src/rigid.rs` ([README](../../solver/README.md#assembly-constraints));
tests `constraint_tests.rs`, `core/solver/tests/rigid_constraints.rs`,
`tools/cli/tests/constraints.json`, `tools/ui-constraint-test.sh`.

```json
{"type": "constraint_set", "rows": [
  {"type": "insert", "offset": -10,
   "a": {"occurrence": "O2", "geometry": {"body": "F4.b0", "edge": "E{F4:bottom|F4:side0}"}},
   "b": {"occurrence": "O1", "geometry": {"body": "F2.b0", "edge": "E{F2:end(r{…})|F3:side0}"}}},
  {"type": "align", "limits": {"min": 0, "max": "10 mm", "rest": 2},
   "a": {"occurrence": "O3", "geometry": {"body": "F6.b0", "face": "F6:start(r{…})"}},
   "b": {"occurrence": "O1", "geometry": {"body": "F2.b0", "face": "F2:end(r{…})"}}}]}
```

- `constraint_set` (named `Constraint<n>`): `rows`, one or more. A row has
  `type`, `a` and `b` (references as [joint origins](#kinds-and-frames):
  an occurrence path from the feature's component and geometry of the
  component it ends in, a `frame_override` allowed), and per type
  `offset` (a length), `angle`, `flip`, `limits` (`min`, `max`, `rest`),
  `lock_rotation`, and for a center `a2` and `b2` (on a's and b's
  occurrence). `a` and `b` must be on different occurrences, at most one
  the component's own geometry. Fields a type does not take are refused
  (`row 1 (align): lock_rotation is for insert rows`).
- **References.** Each resolves to a frame as a joint origin does, and a
  kind: a point (a vertex, sketch or construction point, a sphere's
  centre for an align), a plane (a planar face, a plane; z its outward
  normal), an axis (a straight edge, an axis, a cone or torus), a circle
  (a circular edge, a sketch circle or arc; z the outward normal of a
  planar face the edge bounds, else the axis), a cylinder (its axis and
  radius) or a sphere (centre and radius).

| Type | References | Holds |
|---|---|---|
| `align` | plane (or circle) and plane | a's plane `offset` above b's along b's normal, normals facing; `flip`: the same way |
| `align` | two points | coincident; at a distance with an `offset` |
| `align` | two axes, cylinders or circles | concentric (axes along each other, either way); `offset` apart |
| `align` | a point and a plane, a point and an axis, an axis and a plane | the point on the plane or the axis (`offset` off it), the axis in the plane (`offset` above it) |
| `angle` | planes or axes | the angle between the normals or axes, 0 to 180°; 0 and 180° are parallel; `flip` measures from a's reversed normal |
| `center` | a (and a2); b, or b and b2 | a's point (the middle of a's and a2's) on the plane midway between b and b2 (parallel planar faces); with b alone on b's normal through its middle (a cylinder: on its axis) |
| `tangent` | planes, cylinders, spheres | touching from outside: a plane on a plane facing, a cylinder lying on a plane, cylinders side by side (axes the sum of the radii apart), spheres; `flip`: inside (the other side of the plane, the difference of the radii) |
| `insert` | circle, circle | the centres together, a's plane `offset` along b's normal, the planes facing (a pin's bottom rim into a hole's top rim); `flip`: the same way |
| `insert_axis` | circle, a cylinder (a hole) or circle | a's centre on b's axis, the axes along each other, the depth free |

- **Values.** An align's offset and an angle's angle are values
  (parameters and expressions; `rows.0.offset`, `rows.0.angle`). With
  `limits` (min or max given; an angle row's are angles,
  `rows.0.limits.min_angle`) the value is free between them, held at
  `rest` when given, instead of fixed (offset and angle are then
  refused). Angles are between 0 and 180°; min ≤ rest ≤ max.
- **Lock rotation.** An insert (either) with `lock_rotation` also holds
  the turn about the axis: a's x axis at `angle` about b's z axis from
  b's x axis. The application records the turn where the picks are
  (the `constraint_row` query's `twist`); without `angle` it is 0.
- **Recompute.** At its point of the timeline the rows are solved with
  the joints and constraints in effect before it in the same component
  that share moving units with them, exactly as a joint is ([What
  recompute does](#what-recompute-does)): constraints place their free
  side first by the smallest motion that makes each row hold, join
  nothing, and leave the rest to the iteration; a row whose sides cannot
  move only holds or fails (`row 1 (align): both sides are fixed (Pin:1
  and Plate:1) and the constraint does not hold`). Contradictions name
  rows: `over-constrained: Joint1 and Constraint2 row 1 (align) cannot
  all hold`, a value at its rest `(at its offset)`. Constraint rows count
  in the degrees of freedom, `redundant` and `conflicting` (by the set's
  uid; an align of faces with an axis insert repeats the axes' direction:
  redundant, it holds) and hold while dragging (`joint_drag`,
  `drag_occurrence`: a value between limits moves with the drag and goes
  back to its rest value at the next recompute).
- Like joints, sets are never written to the result store, are deleted
  with an occurrence they name (`delete_occurrence`), follow copies of
  components and are saved as features.

| Command | Fields | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `add_constraint_set` | `rows` (as above; occurrences also by names from the component, `Pin:1`), `name`, `component` (the active one when left out) | `uid`, `name`, `parameters`, `state`, `solved` |

| Query | Fields | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `joints` | | also `constraints`: every constraint set in timeline order: `uid`, `name`, `type`, `component`, `rows` (`row` from 1, `type`, `a` and `b` {`occurrence`, `path`}, `holds` at the marker, `value` of a row with limits), `status`, `error`, `state` (`placed`, `satisfied`, or the status), `moved`, `solved` (every row holds) |
| `constraint_row` | `a`, `b` (references; `occurrence` from `component`, uids or names), `a2`, `b2`, `type` (optional), `component` (the active one when left out) | `kinds` {`a`, `b`: `point`, `plane`, `axis`, `circle`, `cylinder`, `sphere`}, `types` (those the references fit, the likeliest first: two circles an insert, a circle and a cylinder an axis insert, a cylinder or sphere with a plane, or spheres, a tangent, else an align), `type` (the first), `measures` (in the component at the marker: `offset` a's origin above b's plane or a points' distance, `angle` between the z axes, `twist` a's x axis about b's z); with `type`: `fits` and `error` |

The `.f3d` import brings the file's assembly relationships in as
constraint sets (mitcad#155, *Assembly relationships* in the [import
notes](../../import/docs/f3d-components.md#assembly-relationships)).

Not yet: a tangent's contact passing to the second body's other faces
("all faces"), cones and tori in tangents, symmetry and motion
constraints.

## Import and export

### Files

| Command | Fields | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `import_file` | `path` (.step/.stp, .iges/.igs, .brep/.brp, .stl, .obj), `name` (of the feature, optional), `unit_mm` (STL and OBJ: mm per file unit, default 1) | `uid`, `name`, `bodies`: `uid`, `name`, `kind`; `warnings` when empty bodies were left out |
| `export` | `path`, `bodies` (uids or names; all at the marker when left out), `format` (by extension when left out: `step`, `iges`, `stl`, `obj`, `brep`, `3mf`, `usdz`), `schema` (`ap214` default, `ap242`), `unit` (STEP, IGES, STL, OBJ, 3MF: `mm` default, `cm`, `m`, `in`, `ft`; [Mesh files](#mesh-files-in-a-unit-with-a-longest-edge)), `refinement` (STL, OBJ, 3MF, USDZ: `low`, `medium` default, `high` or `{"deviation": mm, "angle": radians, "face_triangles": n, "max_edge": mm}`; see [Mesh refinement](#mesh-refinement)), `ascii` (STL), `colors` (body uid or name: sRGB in [0, 1]), `coordinates` (`design` default, `component`), `occurrence` (a path), `design_folder` (USDZ: the folder relative texture paths are relative to, the design file's), `dialect` (3MF: the slicer whose print settings go with the bodies, [Print profiles](#print-profiles)), `on_bed` (3MF, STL, OBJ: on the print bed faces, [Print bed faces](#print-bed-faces)), `occurrences` and `whole` (3MF: the placements written and the occurrences sent whole, [Export by occurrences](#export-by-occurrences)) | `path`, `format`, `bodies` (uids); 3MF also `meshes`, `skipped`, and with `dialect` `dialect`, `filaments`, `warnings`; USDZ also `materials`, `skipped`, `warnings` |
| `export_sketch` | `sketch` (uid or name), `path` (.dxf), `version` (`r2000` default, `r12`) | `path`, `entities` |

- `import_file` adds one base feature: a body per STEP part or solid,
  IGES solid, BRep compound member or OBJ object, one mesh body for STL.
  Bodies keep the file's names and colours; `source` is the file name.
  One undo step (`Import bracket.step`).
  Empty bodies (a part without geometry) are left out, each with a
  warning that names it (`body 1 (Screw) is empty: left out`, counting
  the file's bodies from 0); a file of only empty bodies is refused
  (`… has only empty bodies (n): nothing to import`). The
  [shape API](#base-features-from-shapes) and the importers' fallbacks
  still refuse an empty body, as their bodies are counted by index.
- `export` writes the bodies with their display names and colours
  (`colors`, else the colours of imported bodies; for STEP, IGES, OBJ,
  3MF; USDZ writes the bodies' appearances, [USDZ](#usdz)). Mesh bodies go
  only to STL, OBJ, BRep, 3MF and USDZ. It changes nothing (no
  undo step, `recomputed` 0).
- `export_sketch` writes the sketch's curves in sketch coordinates and
  millimetres (`$INSUNITS` mm), each curve segment of its profiles once.
  Periodic splines are not written.

### Coordinates and placements of exports

Every format has the bodies where the design shows them:

- A body is placed by the shown occurrences of its component (each a copy
  in the file), by all of them when none is shown; a body of the root
  once, as it is.
- `coordinates: "component"`: each body once, in its own component's
  coordinates.
- `occurrence` (uids `O1/O4` or names `Arm:1/Pin:2`): only the placements
  by this occurrence and the occurrences in it. Listed bodies must be
  placed there (`Pin is not placed in Arm:1`); without `bodies`, the
  bodies it places. A hidden occurrence asked for is written.
- STL and 3MF: the model triangulates each body (`Kernel::triangle_mesh`
  within `refinement`: vertices shared along the faces' edges, triangles
  facing outwards; a mesh body as it is) and places the mesh. An STL file
  is one solid (named after the file) of every placed copy; binary, or
  text with `ascii`.
- The kernel's formats: `Kernel::write_file` gets each body with
  `ExportBody::placements` (each occurrence's transform, named by its
  path; none with `coordinates: component`, and a root body's one
  placement moves nothing). The geometry (`geometry/io`,
  `io::Body::placements`) writes them as locations, never changing a
  body's geometry:
  - **STEP:** when a body moves (a placement that moves it, or several),
    the file is an assembly named after the file: each body a part (its
    name and colour) with an instance per placement, named after the
    occurrence path (`Arm:1/Pin:2`); a root body is an instance that
    does not move. Otherwise the parts alone. MitCad's own import
    flattens the assembly into a body per instance named after the part.
  - **IGES, OBJ, BRep** (and the kernel's STL): a moved copy of the body
    per placement, named after the body with the occurrence path in
    brackets when there are several (`Pin (Arm:1/Pin:2)`). A mesh body is
    moved by its location only (OBJ, BRep).

```json
{"cmd": "export", "path": "assembly.step"}
{"cmd": "export", "path": "local.stl", "bodies": ["Bracket"], "coordinates": "component"}
{"cmd": "export", "path": "pin.igs", "bodies": ["Pin"], "occurrence": "Arm:2"}
```

Tests: `core.model` (`exchange_tests.rs`: occurrences turned, moved and
copied; an occurrence alone, hidden ones, component coordinates, text
STL, errors), `geometry.io` (`test_placements`: STEP assemblies with
instance names, IGES and OBJ copies, BRep and STL, a mesh body moved),
`cli.exchange` (with OCCT: each format read back where the occurrence
places the body), `tools/ui-import-test.sh` (the Export dialog's
Coordinates row), `tools/ui-print-test.sh`.

### 3MF

```json
{"cmd": "export", "path": "part.3mf", "bodies": ["Bracket", "F4.b0"],
 "refinement": "high", "colors": {"Bracket": [0.78, 0.16, 0.16]}}
```

`export` with `format` `3mf` (or a `.3mf` path) writes a 3MF file
(`core/3mf`, the core specification, millimetres) for slicers: one build
item, an object named after the file whose components place one mesh
object per body, so slicers load the bodies as the parts of one object in
their relative positions.

- A mesh object is named after its body; a body with a colour refers to a
  base material of that colour, named after it, in one `basematerials`
  group. A component placed twice gives two components of the one mesh
  object.
- Sheet and empty bodies cannot be printed: listed in `bodies` they are
  an error (`Surface is a sheet body; 3MF takes solids and mesh bodies`);
  when all bodies are written they are left out and listed in `skipped`.
- The result adds `meshes` (per written body, in order: `body`, `name`,
  `triangles`, `volume` of the mesh in mm³, which differs from the body's
  by at most its area times the deviation) and `skipped` (`body`, `name`,
  `reason`).
- Tests: `core.3mf` (writer and reader), `core.model` (`export` with the
  mock kernel), `geometry.io` (`indexed_mesh`: closed meshes facing
  outwards within the deviation's volume), `core.exchange` and
  `cli.export_3mf` (with OCCT).

### USDZ

```json
{"cmd": "export", "path": "assembly.usdz", "refinement": "high",
 "design_folder": "/home/me/designs"}
```

`export` with `format` `usdz` (or a `.usdz` path) writes a Universal
Scene Description package (mitcad#123; `core/usdz`, the
[USDZ specification](https://openusd.org/release/spec_usdz.html)) for AR
viewers, renderers and other programs that read USD: the bodies as shaded
meshes in the design's component hierarchy, with their appearances.

- **Package:** an uncompressed zip whose files start at multiples of 64
  bytes: first the layer `<file name>.usdc`, then the textures' images
  (`textures/<appearance>.png` or `.jpg`). The layer is binary (the
  `.usdc` crate format, version 0.8.0), which AR viewers require of a
  package's layer; `mitcad-usdz` writes it itself (no USD library).
- **Units and axes:** the points stay millimetres (`metersPerUnit`
  0.001). The layer declares `upAxis` "Y", and its root prim (the
  default prim, an `Xform` named after the file, `kind` component) turns
  MitCad's Z-up a quarter about X (`xformOp:rotateX` -90): Z goes to Y,
  Y to -Z: the design's front (-Y) faces +Z, where Y-up viewers look
  from. Viewers that read `upAxis` and
  those that assume Y up show the design upright.
- **Hierarchy:** each placement of a body is a `Mesh` under an `Xform`
  per occurrence on the way to it (`Arm_1/Pin_1/Body1`), each with its
  placement in its parent (`xformOp:transform`); a root body is a mesh of
  the root prim. With `coordinates: component` each body is one mesh of
  the root prim, as its component has it. `occurrence` keeps the
  placements by that occurrence (its parents' `Xform`s around them). A
  component placed twice is written twice. Prim names are the bodies' and
  occurrences' names made valid (ASCII letters, digits and `_`; `Pin (2)`
  becomes `Pin_2`; repeated names get `_2`, `_3`).
- **Hidden bodies:** without `bodies`, hidden bodies, bodies placed only
  by hidden occurrences and the placements of hidden occurrences are left
  out (`skipped`: `hidden`, `in hidden occurrences only`; empty bodies:
  `an empty body`). Listed bodies are written where they are shown, by
  all their occurrences when none is shown, as the other formats. An
  `occurrence` asked for is written even when it is hidden; hidden ones
  inside it are left out.
- **Meshes** (`Kernel::face_meshes` within `refinement`): each face its
  own vertices with the surface's normals (`normals`, vertex
  interpolation), so edges stay sharp and curved faces smooth; triangles
  counter-clockwise seen from outside, `subdivisionScheme` none, an
  `extent`. A mesh body's triangles are faceted; a sheet body is
  `doubleSided`.
- **Materials:** one `Material` per appearance under `<root>/Materials`
  with a `UsdPreviewSurface`: the base colour (linear), metallic,
  roughness, IOR, clear coat and its roughness, emission (its colour times
  its strength), and opacity times 1 - 0.9 x transmission (the preview
  surface has no transmission: clear glass stays faintly visible). A body
  without an appearance gets its colour from `colors` or its import
  (material `color_rrggbb`), else the default look (`default_look`).
  Faces with appearances of their own are a `GeomSubset` each (family
  `materialBind`, `nonOverlapping`) bound to their material. Specular
  weight is not written.
- **Textures:** an appearance's image (embedded, or its file: an absolute
  path, or relative to `design_folder`) goes into the package, read by a
  `UsdUVTexture` (sRGB, repeated) at the mesh's `st` (face-varying
  texture coordinates): the projection the rendered view uses, planar
  from (x, y), box from the axis each triangle faces most, turned back by
  the rotation and divided by the size of one repeat, in the body's own
  coordinates. An image that cannot be read leaves the material in its
  base colour and adds a `warnings` line (`Wood: the texture image
  /path/wood.png cannot be read (...); its base colour is written`).
- The result adds `materials` (their names, in order: appearance ids,
  `color rrggbb`, `default look`), `skipped` (`body`, `name`, `reason`)
  and `warnings`.
- Checked with OpenUSD's validators (`docs/development.md`, *USDZ
  files*): the package rules (stored, aligned, the file types), stage
  metadata, material bindings and subsets, shader inputs.
- Tests: `core.usdz` (the writer, the compression and a reader that
  checks the package and the layer: alignment, the header and sections,
  prims, points, indices, normals, materials and subsets read back),
  `core.model` (`export` with the mock kernel: the hierarchy, hidden
  bodies and occurrences, appearances, face subsets, texture coordinates,
  textures relative to the design's folder), `geometry.io`
  (`face_meshes`: face order, normals out of the body that agree with the
  triangles), `core.exchange` and `cli.export_usdz` (with OCCT),
  `tools/ui-import-test.sh` (File > Export's type).

### DXF into sketches

| Command / query | Fields | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `sketch.import_dxf` | see [Sketch commands](#sketch-commands) | |
| `dxf_info` query | `path` (.dxf) | `unit` (`mm`, `in`, …, or null when the drawing names none), `unit_mm` (null when none), `entities`, `layers` (those with entities, in the layer table's order: `name`, `entities`, `visible` (false when off or frozen), `bounds`), `bounds` {`min`, `max`} of all entities, in drawing units |

`sketch.import_dxf` reads lines, arcs, circles, ellipses and elliptical
arcs, splines (control points with knots and weights, or fit points),
points and text (`mitcad-dxf`: polylines are split into lines and arcs,
block references expanded), converted to millimetres. End points and
centres closer than 1e-6 mm become one sketch point, so joined curves
stay joined; nothing is constrained or dimensioned. `warnings` lists what
the reader approximated and entities left out. A drawing with nothing a
sketch can hold is refused.

Block references are expanded as they are read, never stored per cell
(mitcad#926): an `INSERT` array reads at most 100 000 cells
(`mitcad_dxf::MAX_ARRAY_CELLS`, its first whole rows), and one read places
at most a million entities and block references
(`mitcad_dxf::READ_BUDGET`), counting a block's contents once per
reference to it at every level, as the `.dwg` import counts its
occurrences. A warning names each array cut short and a spent budget;
`dxf_info` and `sketch.import_dxf` read the same way, so both stay
bounded in memory and time.

### SVG into sketches

| Command / query | Fields | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `sketch.import_svg` | `sketch`, `path` (.svg), `scale` (sketch mm per mm of the drawing, default 1), `at` (where the drawing's lower left corner goes, default [0, 0]), `stroke_outline` (default false: stroked paths also as bands of their stroke width) | as other edits, and `curves`, `points` (shared points made), `text_count`, `bands` (strokes made bands), `filled` (the keys of the sketch's regions the drawing paints), `size` ([w, h] mm), `warnings`; undo step `Insert SVG into Sketch1` |
| `svg_info` query | `path` (.svg) | `size` ([w, h] mm at scale 1), `shapes`, `paths`, `filled` and `stroked` (shapes), `texts`, `warnings` |

`sketch.import_svg` (mitcad#473, `sketch/svg.rs`) reads `path`, `rect`
(rounded corners too), `circle`, `ellipse`, `line`, `polyline`, `polygon`,
`text` (with its spans' text: a sketch text at its anchor, `font-size`
high, in its first `font-family`, aligned by `text-anchor`) and `use`
(of an element or a `symbol`), through groups and their `transform`s,
with `fill`, `fill-rule`, `stroke`, `stroke-width`, `display` and
`visibility` from attributes and `style` attributes (style sheets are
not read: a warning). Images and foreign objects are left out with a
warning.

- Geometry, exactly: lines are lines; quadratic and cubic Bézier pieces
  are splines of degree 2 and 3 with the same control points; elliptical
  arcs and circles are arcs and circles of the sketch where the drawing's
  transforms keep them round, and elliptical arcs and ellipses where they
  do not (`preserveAspectRatio="none"`, a non-uniform `scale`). End
  points closer than 1e-6 mm are one sketch point.
- Units: a user unit is a millimetre, unless the root `svg` has a
  `viewBox` and a `width` or `height`: the viewBox then fills that size
  (`mm`, `cm`, `in`, `pt`, `pc`, `px` at 96 per inch; a plain number is
  millimetres), uniformly and centred unless `preserveAspectRatio` is
  `none`. Absolute lengths inside the drawing follow the same scale.
  `scale` multiplies it all. The drawing's y runs down, the sketch's up;
  its viewport's lower left corner (or its content's, without a size)
  goes to `at`.
- `filled`: each region of the sketch after the insert is tested at a
  point inside it against every filled shape by its `fill-rule`
  (`nonzero`, the default, counts the windings of its subpaths;
  `evenodd` their crossings), and with `stroke_outline` against the
  bands, so a logo's letters with their counters or a ring with its hole
  extrude as drawn when Extrude takes the `filled` regions.
- `stroke_outline`: a stroked path also becomes the band of its stroke
  width (the sketch's offset by half the width to both sides, round at
  corners; square ends on an open path); a path that is only stroked
  then leaves its middle line out. Without it a stroked path is its
  middle line. A band whose offset fails (a curve tighter than half the
  width) is left out with a warning.
- A drawing with nothing a sketch can hold is refused.

### Base features from shapes

An importer that builds bodies itself adds them without files:

- Rust: `Document::add_base_feature(BaseInput { name, source, bodies:
  vec![ImportBody { name, color, shape }], operation, participants,
  replaces })` (`core/model/src/exchange.rs`) returns the feature and its
  bodies; `add_base_features(label, …)` adds several as one undo step.
  The shapes are kernel shapes (`SharedPtr<Shape>` with OCCT), stored as
  B-rep data.
- C++: `Document::add_base_feature(const ShapeList&, json)` with
  `{"name", "source", "operation", "participants", "bodies": [{"name",
  "color"}, …]}` (all optional; `bodies` by shape index).
- `Document::import_f3d(path, json)` imports the bodies of an .f3d/.f3z
  file without history, one base feature per body (`{"history": true}`
  also takes the `.smbh` blobs, `{"owners": true}` bodies of which only
  faces are saved, `{"text": true}` returns a summary instead of JSON).
  `mitcad::bridge::f3d_bodies` (`core/cpp/bridge/exchange.hpp`, also
  callable from Rust) builds the bodies of an .f3d file into a
  `ShapeList` with their blob, record and build report.

### .f3d import with the timeline

`{"cmd": "import_f3d", "path": "part.f3d", …}` (C++ `Document::command`,
or `Document::import_f3d_timeline(path, json)` for the report alone)
imports an .f3d design with its timeline replayed as MitCad features
([core/import/README.md](../../import/README.md)): parameters with
their expressions, sketches, construction geometry and features, each
checked against the file's ASM history; an item that cannot be replayed
becomes a base feature holding the file's bodies after it. The design's
components and occurrences come in as MitCad's and every item goes into
its component: the one whose bodies it changes, else the one that owns it
(the design's new-component operations are new bodies there). Occurrences
take the placements the file gives them at the end of its timeline; the
file's joints, as-built joints, joint origins, rigid groups and ground
items come in as [joint features](#joints) where they hold there (else as
as-built joints, with a warning), other assembly relationships are
skipped. The fallbacks, partial items and items suppressed or failed in
the file show on the timeline with the report's notes ([The import's
outcomes on the timeline](#the-imports-outcomes-on-the-timeline)).
One undo step (`Import part.f3d`). The bridge handles the command
(`core/ffi/src/f3d_import.rs`), not the model, because it needs the
file's bodies built with OCCT.

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `design` | the document of an `.f3z` package (its label or the part after `!`); when left out, the root design its `Manifest.json` names, else the one with the longest timeline |
| `dump` | an external dump (JSON, `core/import/SCHEMA.md` §2) replayed instead of the file's own design streams; the file still gives the bodies |
| `no_verify` | do not check the replay against the ASM history (and take only first guesses) |
| `no_fallback` | leave items that cannot be replayed out instead of using the file's bodies |
| `no_compare` | compare the final bodies by volume only, not by surface deviation |
| `geometric_tolerance` | mm, greater than 0 (default 0.01; the application's Preferences, General, *Import tolerance*): how far the replay's geometry may be from the file's where no exact result is (mitcad#224). The decoded edges, faces and vertices are looked for in the replay within 0.001 mm first (a fillet's edge by its middle, ends, or circle centre, radius and plane), then within this tolerance; a match found so keeps the uniqueness rules, counts as `read` where the input was decoded and the match is unique, and the item's report gives its `geometric_deviation`. It is also the distance within which an item's new faces must lie on the file's in the history's geometric check (`core/import/docs/f3d-fallbacks.md`), and the distance a sketch's solved points may lie from the file's where the sketch's regions stay the file's (mitcad#396; else 1e-4 mm); volume and area checks keep their relative tolerances |
| `retry_bodies` | `keep` (default), `replace` or `ask` (mitcad#283): what a retry of an item on the file's stored state before it does with the replayed bodies that match that state (exactly, or within `geometric_tolerance`). `keep`: they stay, parametric, and only the bodies that differ are brought to the state (nothing differs: no retry, and the item takes the file's bodies if it fails); `replace`: the stored bodies replace them too; `ask`: the user is asked through the document's job (`JobControl::question`, `answer`) the first time a retry would replace a body that matches, and the answer holds for the rest of the import, its tries and the documents it refers to (kept without a job). See *Retries on the file's exact state* in `core/import/docs/f3d-fallbacks.md` |
| `time_limit` | seconds; after them the remaining items take the file's bodies without trying definitions |
| `own_start_time_scale` | a factor above 0 (default 1; mitcad#847) on the time an item is first tried from its own start, the state before the operations no item names right before its own (half of the item's 60 s): the checks of a debug build give its slowdown (`mitcad-cli import-f3d --own-start-time-scale`), so that an item that gives its state that way does not hang on the build or the load beside it. It scales a thread's sizing offset's 2 s too (mitcad#874), the other short time of a route tried first. The item's other routes keep their times. Passed on to the documents the design refers to |
| `hang_limit` | seconds without progress after which the import is taken to hang in the geometry kernel (a new document only; the import makes progress between kernel calls, also in its own long loops, so only a kernel call that does not return counts, mitcad#82): the import runs on a thread of its own and is run again with the item it hung on taking the file's bodies (hung comparing the final bodies: by volume only; elsewhere: the stored bodies without the timeline); the report warns. The try given up stops once its kernel call returns (before its next item or definition; a definition's long kernel operations stop inside) and its result is dropped (mitcad#71) |
| `text` | `import_f3d_timeline` returns a readable report |
| `report_path` | also write the JSON report to this file |
| `list` | `import_f3d_timeline` only lists the designs: `{"designs": [{"label", "items"}]}` |
| `memory_limit` | MiB the import may take besides the process's own limits (mitcad#80): low on memory (85 % of the tightest limit, always watched), the import cuts the definition being tried short and tries no more until the memory recovers; those items take the file's bodies, and the report's `low_memory` (`item`, `name`, `memory`, `items`) and a warning say so (`core/import/docs/f3d-performance.md`, *Memory*) |
| `threads` | how many threads the import uses at once (mitcad#95, mitcad#103; default 1, the application gives the logical cores up to 8): workers evaluate the definitions ranked after the one being evaluated, each on its own copy of the document, and the import takes their results in rank order; the file's bodies are read and the history's bodies built ahead of the replay on the same threads. It is the same import as with one thread, only faster (`core/import/docs/f3d-performance.md`, *Definitions evaluated in parallel*, *Work beside the replay*) |
| `learn` | a directory for the learning dump (mitcad#96): one JSON line per modelling item with its raw record, its candidates and the one the history accepted (`core/import/docs/f3d-learning.md`, *Learning the undecoded inputs*); `MITCAD_IMPORT_LEARN` when left out |
| `references` | folders searched for the documents the design refers to (its components of other documents, mitcad#196), besides the reference folder next to it (`<design> vN.refs`): see *Components of other documents* below |
| `reference_files` | files of documents the design refers to, by the documents' URNs (`{"urn:…?version=2": "C:/…/Part v2.f3d"}`; the application's file dialogs); their folders are searched too |
| `skipped_references` | URNs of documents the user chose not to give: reported `skipped` rather than `missing` |
| `no_references` | the components of other documents stay empty (no document is imported) |
| `list_references` | `import_f3d_timeline` only lists the documents the design refers to and where their files are, importing nothing: `{"documents": [{"document", "name", "version", "occurrences", "file", "design", "found", "note", "parent", "depth"}], "folders", "warnings"}`; documents found are followed into their own references (`parent`: the URN of the document that refers to one) |
| `accept_deviations` | which items whose decoded definition builds a result that deviates from the file's stay parametric with it (mitcad#379; see *Deviating results kept at import* below): `true` or `"all"` every one, an array of timeline indices (`[88]`) or `"88,93"` those; left out, `false` or `"none"` (the default): none, they take the file's bodies. Not passed on to the documents the design refers to |

The result: `file`, `design`, `items` (timeline items), `counts` (items
per outcome: `parametric`, `partial`, `fallback`, `skipped`) and
`report`: per design `parameters` (imported, as values, renamed,
skipped, mismatched), `items` (`index`, `name`, `type`, `outcome`,
`features`, `verified`, `note`, `component` when not the root,
`geometric_deviation`: the largest distance in mm beyond 0.001 mm at
which a lookup of its decoded inputs took the replay's geometry for the
file's, when one did; `exact_retry` when it was tried again on the
file's stored state before it: `state`, `bodies` (`keep` or `replace`),
the replayed bodies `kept` and `replaced` and whether it `matched`
there, mitcad#283), `retry_question` (`item`, `answer`: where the
import asked about those bodies, and the answer), `geometric_tolerance`
(the option used),
`history` (`states`, `built`, `matched`, `reached_end`), `bodies` (each
of the file's stored solids with `file_volume`, the replayed body it
matched, `volume_difference`, `max_deviation`, `relative_difference`;
the last is missing when the boolean differences did not finish in
time, were left out because every sample lay within 0.01 mm, or gave
more than the deviations allow),
`extra_bodies`, `warnings`, `components` (`components` made,
`occurrences` placed, `external` occurrences of other documents placed
as occurrences of empty components, `linked` those of them filled from their
documents' files, `placed_inside` the captured positions inside them
that placed copied occurrences, `items` per component), `joints`
(`joints` that came in as joints, their `fixed_sides` and
`inserted_sides` (on components of other documents), joints
`kept_as_built`, `as_built` joints, joint `origins`, `grounded`
occurrences, captured `positions`, `skipped` items), `references` (the
documents the design refers to, below), `appearances` (below), `stopped`
when the import was stopped and `low_memory` when it ran low on memory.

#### Appearances and materials of the file (mitcad#228)

The import gives the replayed bodies the file's appearances and
materials, after the replay (part of its undo step):

- Each appearance a body, face or occurrence uses becomes one document
  appearance ([Appearances](#appearances)), once per asset of the file:
  id `f3d_<name>` (`f3d_paint_enamel_red_glossy`; `_2`, … where taken by
  another), named by the name given to it in the file, else its
  description (`Paint - enamel red glossy`). Its parameters come from the
  asset: the base colour of its shader (sRGB as stored, a linear one
  encoded), roughness, metalness (metals 1), the index of refraction
  (from an opaque surface's reflectance, or a transparent one's own) and
  transmission (transparent and glass ones 1). A document appearance of
  the same id and parameters from an earlier import is used again.
- A body gets its file body's appearance (`set_body_appearance`): the
  stored body the final comparison matched it with. Faces with
  appearances of their own get theirs (`set_face_appearance`): the faces
  of the replayed body through the stored face's point (every piece of a
  face the replay splits).
- An occurrence's appearance override goes to the bodies of its
  component and of the components inside it, where each is placed only
  there (MitCad keeps one appearance per body); the root component's
  override covers the design.
- A body gets MitCad's material (`set_body_material`) where the file's
  is one of MitCad's: the same name (its description up to the first
  comma, or the last part of its classification; also with a grade after
  it, `Aluminum 6061`; ABS written out) and its density within 2 %.
  Every material is listed in the report.

The report's `appearances`: `bodies`, `bodies_set` (the stored design's
solids, and those whose replayed body got the file's appearance),
`faces`, `faces_set`, `materials`, `materials_set`, `overrides`,
`overrides_set`, `not_in_design` (body records of bodies the stored
design does not hold: a snapshot blob's copies of bodies the history
holds, bodies taken by later operations),
`appearances` (each made: `id`, `name`, `asset`, `schema`, `preset`,
`base_color`, `notes` on what MitCad's parameters do not hold —
translucency, emission, bump maps — and `texture`: the image the colour
comes from with its `size` and `offset` in mm and `rotation`, which the
file does not hold, and `maps`: the images of its other maps by
MitCad's map name, `roughness`, `normal`, `bump`, `cutout`, mitcad#313,
which it does not hold either, so no texture set is made from them), `physical_materials` (`asset`, `preset`, `name`,
`category`, `classification`, `density` kg/m³, `mitcad`, `bodies`) and
`gaps` (what did not come in, and why). The readable report gives a line
`appearances: bodies x/y, faces x/y, …`. Left out when the file has none.

#### Components of other documents

A design whose components come from other documents (inserted designs,
fasteners) does not hold those documents. The import imports each document
the design refers to from its own file first, with its history and its own
references (references of references, 16 levels at most; a document that
refers back to one being imported is not; each with the options' time and
hang limits of its own), then replays the design with each such component
an empty component placed by its occurrences, copies the documents into
those components with their histories before its first item, so that every
occurrence shows its document where the file places it, and replays the
items with them in place: the joints, as-built joints, relationships and
grounded occurrences whose sides are inside them (a level of their paths is
an occurrence of the other document) or on their occurrences find their
frames on the copies' faces and edges, and the entities the design's
inputs name in them (bodies, faces and edges of the other document: a
combine's tool, an extrusion's face) are found in the other document's own
history and among the copies' bodies. While the items are replayed the
document's body view (`Document::bodies`) leaves the copies out, since the
replay matches the design's own history, which holds none of their bodies;
the captured positions of occurrences inside them place the copies'
occurrences, as `capture_position` features of those components at the end
of the timeline. MitCad's file links (`ExternalLink`) are to `.mitcad`
designs and keep only bodies, so the copies are of the documents' designs,
parametric where their own import is, one component per document shared by
its occurrences. All of it is the import's one undo step. A document that
is placed in several places is one copy whose own occurrences a captured
position moves in all of them (where two disagree it is left out).

A document's file is the first of: a file given for it
(`reference_files`); the design of the `.f3z` package being imported that
its `DesignDescription.json` names for the URN (else for another version
of the same document, with a note; mitcad#229); the file
`references.json` of the reference folder next to the design, or of a
folder given with `references`, names for its URN (the version the
design uses; else another version of the same document there, with a
note); another design of the same `.f3z` package whose `Manifest.dat`
lists the GUID the design keeps after the URN (the one listing the
fewest GUIDs; never the package's root design or one being imported); a
`.f3d` file of those folders (and of the given files' folders) whose
`Manifest.dat` lists the GUID the design keeps after the document's URN
(a file named `… v<version>.f3d` first). The command line never asks;
the application asks for each document not found (*Files* in
[app/COMMANDS.md](../../../app/COMMANDS.md)).

`report.designs[0].references`: per document `document` (its URN),
`name` (the package description's or the reference folder's, else
the file's name without ` vN`), `version`, `file`, `found` (`chosen`,
`reference folder`, `package`, `by its GUID`), `status` (`linked`, `missing`, `skipped`, `failed`),
`note`, `components` (MitCad's), `occurrences`, `items` (its own
import's items by outcome) and `references` (its own). A warning names
the documents not imported; their components stay empty, as before.
`references.json`:

```json
{"format": "…", "format_version": 1,
 "design": {"name": "Assembly", "versionId": "urn:…?version=1", "version": 1,
            "children": [{"name": "Part", "versionId": "urn:…?version=2", "version": 2,
                          "file": "Part v2.f3d", "children": []}]},
 "files": ["Part v2.f3d"]}
```

(`versionId` is the URN the design names the document by; `file` is
relative to the folder; `format` is the name the folder's writer gives
the format, checked; other keys are left alone.)

Stopping: the import is not undone as a whole, so a job does not cancel
it. Run under a job (`attach_job`, [Progress and
cancellation](#progress-and-cancellation)), the job's cancel is a request
to stop early: the definition being tried is cut short, the modelling
item being replayed and the ones after it take the file's bodies without
trying definitions, as after `time_limit` (note `the import was
stopped`; sketches and construction geometry still come in), the final
bodies are compared by volume only, and the command succeeds with what
was imported. `report.stopped` has `item` (the timeline index of the
first item given up) and its `name`, no `item` when the stop came after
the last one; a warning says so too. The job's test delay slows each
definition tried. `import_f3d` without the timeline is not stopped by a
job.

#### Deviating results kept at import (mitcad#379)

An item whose decoded definition builds a result that is not the file's
(its result does not measure as its history state, or the volume it adds
or removes or its new faces are off the file's, `core/import/docs/f3d-history.md`,
*Matching rules*) takes the file's bodies as before; its report entry
has `deviation`, how far off the result was there:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `volume_change` | mm³ the item adds (negative: removes) |
| `file_volume_change` | mm³ the file's operation adds or removes |
| `volume_difference` | the first minus the second |
| `relative_difference` | that against the file's change (missing when it changes nothing) |
| `largest_distance`, `area_beyond` | the largest distance (mm) of the result's new faces from the file's state after the item, and the share (0–1) of their area farther than the tolerance |
| `file_largest_distance`, `file_area_beyond` | the same of the file's new faces against the result |
| `body_volume`, `stored_body_volume` | mm³ of the bodies the item changed, after it, and of the file's bodies its operation changed |
| `tolerance` | the geometric tolerance (mm) the faces were measured with |
| `reason` | why the result is not the file's |
| `accepted` | whether it was kept |
| `missing_edges` | a rounding or chamfer the geometry kernel fails with all its decoded edges, built with some of them: the edges it leaves out (left out when none) |
| `faces` | `[{"body", "face"}]`: faces of the imported design where it deviates (of the stored geometry standing in for it; of the result where kept), for the application to select |

With `accept_deviations` naming the item, it is parametric instead: its
definition is added again (`outcome` `parametric`, `verified` false, the
note saying so) and the entry has `accepted_deviation` with these numbers
(`accepted` true) instead of `deviation`; its features get the timeline
note *Deviation from the file accepted at import: …*. The items after it
replay on its result; each body it changed counts in the comparisons with
the history with its difference from the file's body taken off, so a
later item is checked by what it changes itself (a later item that does
not give its state there takes the file's bodies, and the file's body
replaces the deviated one from then on, with its own `deviation`), and
the final comparison does not replace those bodies. The text report
lists the deviations not kept (`deviating result (not kept): …`).

#### From the dump IR

How the importer maps IR features (`core/import/SCHEMA.md` §5.3) to the
definitions above. Lengths in the IR are cm (× 10), angles rad; values
bind to parameters by name; B-rep fingerprints are resolved to MitCad
names before the feature. A `Path` is dumped as its `PathEntity` items:
sketch curves (`sketch_entity`, the curve's imported id) →
`{"sketch", "curves"}`, edge fingerprints resolved against the replay →
`{"body", "edges"}` (a path mixing sketches or bodies is unsupported).
"Fallback": the item takes the file's bodies. Where the stream decoder
gives a combine's target and tools, a hole's points or a pattern's or
mirror's objects (mitcad#67), the definitions built from them are tried
first, then those the file's history suggests without them.

| IR `objectType` | MitCad | Fields |
|---|---|---|
| `FilletFeature` | `fillet` | each `edgeSets[]` item a set: `ConstantRadiusFilletEdgeSet` → `constant` (`radius`), `ChordLengthFilletEdgeSet` → `chord_length`, `VariableRadiusFilletEdgeSet` → `variable` (`startRadius`, `endRadius`; `midRadii` with `midPositions` → `mid`), an asymmetric set (`offsetOne`, `offsetTwo`, `isFlipped`) → `asymmetric` (`distance1`, `distance2`, `flip`; which face takes which offset is unknown, so the other way round is a guess the history may pick); `continuity` Curvature (or legacy `isG2`) → `curvature` with `tangencyWeight` → `tangency_weight`; `isTangentChain` → `tangent_chain`; `isRollingBallCorner` → `rolling_ball_corners`; entities that are faces → `faces`, a feature → its faces. G2, asymmetric and mid radius sets and setback corners follow MitCad's own conventions, so they are matched against the history within 0.5 %; what the kernel cannot build falls back |
| `ChamferFeature` | `chamfer` | `EqualDistanceChamferEdgeSet` → `equal_distance`; `TwoDistancesChamferEdgeSet` → `two_distances` with `reference_face` = the face left of each edge (sets split by face), `isFlipped` → `flip`; `DistanceAndAngleChamferEdgeSet` → `distance_angle` with `reference_face` = the face right of the edge, `isFlipped` → `flip`; `cornerType` `ChamferCornerType`, `MiterCornerType`, `BlendCornerType` → `corner` `chamfer`, `miter`, `blend` (miter and blend matched within 0.5 %) |
| `ShellFeature` | `shell` | `inputEntities` faces → `faces`, a body → none; `insideThickness`, `outsideThickness`, `isTangentChain`, `shellType` RoundedOffset → `rounded` |
| `DraftFeature` | | not translated (fallback) |
| `OffsetFacesFeature` (Press Pull) | `offset_face` | `faces` (one feature per body), `distance` |
| `DeleteFaceFeature` | `delete_face` | `deletedFaces` by their names (one feature per body); the faces are found among the replay's by a point on them |
| `ReplaceFaceFeature` | `replace_face` | `targetFaces`: a construction plane → `plane`, one face → `face` (a planar face of a body the replay lacks → a fixed plane), all faces of one body or a body → `body`. Dumps do not record the faces replaced (`sourceFaces` or `inputFaces` are read when a dump has them): the history gives them, the faces of the body the next state changed whose points it no longer has on its faces; listed in full with `tangent_chain` false. Matched against the history within 0.5 %; without a history, or with a target the replay lacks (a curved face of a surface body), fallback |
| `SplitBodyFeature` | `split_body` | `splitBodies` → `bodies`, `splittingTool` → plane / face / body / sketch (a plane the file no longer has comes with the geometry it kept), further tools of the file's selection (`splittingTools`) → `more_tools`, `isSplittingToolExtended` → `extend`; IR body names after the step name the pieces |
| `RemoveFeature` | `remove_body` | `itemToRemove` (a body) → `bodies`; the body leaves the history's states from the replay's on |
| `SplitFaceFeature` | | not translated (fallback) |
| `CombineFeature` | `combine` | `targetBody` → `target`, `toolBodies` → `tools`, `operation` (Join/Cut/IntersectFeatureOperation), `isKeepToolBodies` → `keep_tools` (tools consumed: the history's copies of them are left out from the combine's state on, mitcad#96); `isNewComponent`: the combine goes into the component the import puts the item in |
| `MirrorFeature` | `mirror` | `patternEntityType` + `inputEntities` → `objects` (Faces → faces of one body, Features, Bodies; not Occurrences), `mirrorPlane` (origin `XY`/`XZ`/`YZ` → origin plane; other construction planes → a fixed plane from `geometry`; face fingerprint → face), `isCombine` → `combine` (the stream decoder's, then the other way as a guess; not given: separate copies, then joined), `patternComputeOption` → `compute` |
| `RectangularPatternFeature` | `rectangular_pattern` | `directionOne/TwoEntity` → axes (origin X/Y/Z, edge, fixed from `directionOne/Two` when the entity is null or a sketch line), `quantityOne/Two`, `distanceOne/Two`, `isSymmetricInDirectionOne/Two`, `patternDistanceType` (Extent/Spacing), `patternComputeOption`, `suppressedElementsIds` → `suppressed_elements` matched by `outputs.patternElements[].transform`; without directions (the oldest item version, mitcad#74) the history checks guesses: direction one along an origin axis, two across it at 90°, 60° or 120°, both symmetric or not (`core/import/docs/f3d-history.md`). For this and the circular and path patterns, tapped holes among the features come with their threads, then (inferred) without them: a pattern whose copies the file keeps as plain bores (mitcad#733) |
| `CircularPatternFeature` | `circular_pattern` | `axis` (a sketch circle or arc: the axis through its centre, the line the stream decoder's `_f3d_axis` gives where the sketch faces the other way; an axis entity not found: that line), `quantity`, `totalAngle` → `angle`, `isSymmetric`, `patternComputeOption`, `suppressedElementsIds` |
| `PathPatternFeature` | `path_pattern` | `inputEntities` → `objects`, `path` (one sketch curve → `{"sketch", "curve"}`, lines and arcs of one sketch → `{"sketch", "curves"}`; edges are not translated), `quantity`, `distance`, `patternDistanceType`, `startPoint` → `start`, `isFlipDirection` → `flip`, `isOrientationAlongPath` → `along_path`, `isSymmetric`, `patternComputeOption`, `suppressedElementsIds` (mitcad#468). The stream decoder gives the flip, orientation and symmetry, and instead of `startPoint` the patterned objects' centre → `start_point`; a pattern of features that made no body → `combine` (mitcad#673). Where a flag is not given: the default, then the other way as a guess the history checks ([core/import/docs/f3d-history.md](../../import/docs/f3d-history.md#path-patterns-mitcad468)) |
| `MoveFeature` | `move` | bodies of `inputEntities`; `transform` (rigid, cm) → `free` matrix, or `moveFeatureDefinition` (`TranslateXYZ`, `TranslateAlongEntity`, `Rotate`, `PointToPoint`, `PointToPosition`) to keep it editable; moves of faces are unsupported |
| `CopyPasteBody` | `move` with `copy: true` | `sourceBody` (decoded from the file's item inputs), an identity `free` move; a cut and paste into another component is not translated, and one whose body the file lost keeps the cached result |
| Align (not in the API) | `move` (`free`) or `align` | |
| `ScaleFeature` | `scale` | `inputEntities` (bodies), `point` (origin point → origin, vertex, else fixed), `isUniform`, `scaleFactor`, `xScale`, `yScale`, `zScale` |
| `Box/Cylinder/Sphere/TorusFeature` | `box`, `cylinder`, `sphere`, `torus` | sizes from `parameters.model` by `createdBy` (`DistanceX` the width and `DistanceY` the length of a box); the placement (not in the API) from the stream decoder: `plane` (the plane or face), `frame` and `placement` (4x4 matrices in cm: the point `p` of the primitive's own frame is at `frame * placement * p`; the box's width along its x, its length along y, its height along z; the cylinder's, sphere's and torus' base or centre at the origin, the axis z), `operation`, `participantBodies`, a torus' `torusPosition`; the matrices are expressed in the frame MitCad gives the plane (a box whose edges run along it and whose base lies in it, an axis along its normal), a face the replay has not (the history state lacks it) by the replay's planar face in the same plane |
| `SweepFeature` | `sweep` | `profile` → `profiles` (as for extrude), `path` → `path`, `guideRail` → `guide_rail` with `rail_point` `plane` (mitcad#469), `orientation` (Perpendicular/ParallelOrientationType), `twistAngle` → `twist_angle`, `taperAngle` → `taper_angle`, `profileScaling` (SweepProfileScale/Stretch/NoScalingOption) → `profile_scaling`, `distanceOne`/`distanceTwo` → `extent` `partial` unless both 1, `isDirectionFlipped` → `flip` (with a guide rail the other way first; then the other direction where a partial extent or a rail makes it differ), `operation`, `participantBodies`; `guideSurfaces` → `guide_surfaces` (mitcad#157: each face found by its fingerprint, as other face inputs, with every piece of it the replay splits; a `guideRail` given with them is not used; perpendicular only; faces without geometry → fallback); a path or guide surface on another component's body → `body_links` (mitcad#161), the sweep in its profile's component; a path edge the replay splits → its pieces in order; `extent` FullExtents and `isSolid` false → fallback. From the stream decoder, which gives a profile's sketch only and neither `orientation`, `profileScaling` nor `isDirectionFlipped`, the history picks among the sketch's regions, `distanceTwo` 0 as none or as given, both directions, perpendicular then parallel (scale, then stretch and none with a rail) |
| `LoftFeature` | `loft` | `loftSections[]` by `index`: `entity` a profile → `profile`, a face → `face`, a path of a body's edges (`PathEntity` items of `BRepEdge`s, or one edge; the section of tangent and smooth conditions) → `face`, the face of that body the edges go round (each of them borders it and it has no others), a sketch point, a construction point or a vertex → `point`; first and last `endCondition`: `LoftFreeEndCondition` → none, `LoftPointSharpEndCondition` → `point_sharp`, `LoftDirectionEndCondition` → `direction` (`angle`, `weight`), `LoftTangentEndCondition` → `tangent`, `LoftSmoothEndCondition` → `smooth`, `LoftPointTangentEndCondition` → `point_tangent` (`weight`); `centerLineOrRails` with `isCenterLine` → `centerline`, else `rails`; `isClosed` → `closed`, `isSolid` false → `surface`; `operation`, `participantBodies` (the IR has no ruled loft). A loft with end conditions or rails is kept when it matches the history within 0.5 % (see [loft](#loft)). A profile without its area (the stream decoder gives its sketch only) is each of the sketch's regions in turn, the history picking, at most twelve choices of all sections |
| `PipeFeature` | `pipe` | `path`, `sectionType` (Circular/Square/TriangularPipeSectionType) → `section`, `sectionSize` → `size`, `isHollow` with `sectionThickness` → `thickness`, `distanceOne`/`distanceTwo` → `extent`, `operation`, `participantBodies`. Without `sectionType` and `isHollow` (the stream decoder): a solid circle first, then hollow with `sectionThickness`, square and triangular, the history picking |
| `CoilFeature` | `coil` | the sizes (`parameters.model` by `role`), `coilType` (`PitchAndRevolution`, `RevolutionAndHeight`, `PitchAndHeight`, `SpiralCoilType`) → `helix`, `sectionType` → `section`, `sectionPosition` → `section_position`, `isClockwise` (the default is true: a right-handed helix) → `clockwise` (inverted), `angle` → `angle`, `plane`, `frame` and `placement` as for the primitives (the coil must rise along the plane's normal and start on its x axis), `operation`, `participantBodies` |
| `RibFeature`, `WebFeature` | | not translated (fallback): no inputs are recorded besides thickness and depth |
| `ThreadFeature` | `thread` | `inputCylindricalFaces` (resolved through `point_on_face`) → `faces`; `threadInfo`: `threadType` ISO Metric profile and other metric `M` sizes → `iso_metric`, ANSI Unified → `unified`, BSP Pipe Threads → `whitworth` with `G <size>-<tpi>` → `G <size>`, NPT and ANSI Taper Pipe Threads → `npt`, ISO Taper → `iso_taper` (mitcad#733), others fallback; `threadDesignation` → `designation`, `threadClass` → `class` when MitCad lists it for the face's side (else left out), `isRightHanded` → `right_handed`; `isModeled` true → `modeled` with `diameters` from `majorDiameter`, `minorDiameter` and `pitchDiameter` and the `angle` the next history state shows on each face (one `thread` per face; Whitworth and ISO 7-1 fall back); a taper pipe thread (`isTapered`, the stream decoder's `_f3d_taper`) takes `diameters` where it starts: the pitch diameter at its small end grown by the taper over its length, the height above and below it, tried first without sizing the faces; `isFullLength` false → `length` (`threadLength`), `offset` (`threadOffset`) and `location` (`threadLocation`, swapped where MitCad's cylinder axis runs against the face's `geometry.axis`). First with an `offset_face` of each face to the thread's major (external) or minor (internal) diameter, as the file sizes threaded faces, and one of each chamfer at the face's ends (a cone about its axis from an end circle, narrowing away from a shaft, widening away from a bore) by the radial step times the cosine of its angle to the axis, so that it moves along the radius with the face as in the file (mitcad#335), then with a tube between the two radii (`cylinder`s and `combine`s) cut from or joined to the body, then without |
| `HoleFeature` tapped (`holeTapType` Tapped) | `hole` + `thread` | the hole with its diameter (then `tappedHoleInfo.minorDiameter`), and a `thread` on `hole<i>.wall` with the size of `tappedHoleInfo` (as for `ThreadFeature`; for `thread.isModeled` modelled with its diameters and the angle the thread's state shows on each wall, measured on the hole made alone first, one `thread` per angle, mitcad#733), and for `thread.isFullLength` false `length` and `offset` from the hole's start (`low_end`); a taper pipe thread (cosmetic too) with its `diameters` at the start and `low_end` (the hole's start, mitcad#733); then the hole without the thread. The stream decoder takes a hole's thread from its sub-items, else the thread that names the hole; a modelled or taper pipe thread's operations end the hole's state |
| `HoleFeature` | `hole` | `position` (the stream decoder: every point of `_f3d_positions`) on the planar face named by `holePositionDefinition` or through the point, `holeType` Simple/Counterbore/Countersink with `counterboreDiameter`/`Depth` or `countersinkDiameter`/`Angle`, `holeDiameter`, `tipAngle` (180° → `flat`), `extentDefinition` `DistanceExtentDefinition` → `distance`, `ThroughAllExtentDefinition` or `AllExtentDefinition` → `through_all` (others fall back; with the stream decoder's `_f3d_through_all` through all first, checked by the history), `isDefaultDirection` false → `flip`; one hole whose `holePositionDefinition` (`PlaneAndOffsetsHolePositionDefinition`) gives two edges and their distances → `face_offsets` first, on a cylindrical face one face and a distance from it → `cylinder_offset` first (mitcad#719), unless the hole they give does not lie where the item's state has its hole (points round the inside of its wall in the state's material) while the point's does: then after the point (mitcad#733); a tapped hole's modelled thread is checked against the thread's own state (the hole's last); without a position, the holes the history shows (tried after the decoded definitions) |
| `Joint` | `joint` | in the component its occurrence paths start in (`_f3d.context_component`); `occurrenceOne` → `a`, `occurrenceTwo` → `b` (`_f3d.path` of occurrence objects → occurrence uids, occurrences of components of other documents included: they are occurrences of empty components; a level inside one leaves the joint out); each side's stored frame (`_f3d.frames`, else `geometryOrOrigin*`) on geometry of the side's component that gives it (a joint origin, construction geometry, a circular edge, a planar face or a face of revolution, with a `frame_override` for the rest; on a component of another document its `"origin"`), else a fixed plane; `jointMotion` → `kind` (`slide_axis` by the motion's slot), the values the motions have where the file places the occurrences (from the frames, mitcad#87: a joint that cannot hold there is not added), `rotationLimits` → `rz`'s and `slideLimits` → the slide's `limits` where they hold those values (else left out), the values → `position` where the rest value is another; `_f3d.opposed` → `flip`, `angle` → `angle`, `offset` → `offset` (an offset the file stores rounded takes the placements' value, mitcad#81), `offsetX`/`offsetY` move `b`'s origin. Kept only where every occurrence stays where it was or goes where the file places it after the item or at the end of its timeline (the occurrences' `_f3d.placements`, else its last captured position, else its stored transform); else an `as_built_joint` of the placements with a warning ([core/import/docs/f3d-components.md](../../import/docs/f3d-components.md#joints)) |
| `AsBuiltJoint` | `as_built_joint` | `occurrenceOne`/`Two` → `a`/`b`, `relative` from the placements at its point of the timeline (`_f3d.placements` checked against them, a warning where they differ), `jointMotion` → `kind`, its motion frame `origin` the recorded frame (on geometry of `b`'s component, else of `a`'s, else fixed on `b`), its limits where the recorded placement is the file's and they hold 0 (a rest value other than 0 → `position` 0) |
| `RigidGroup` (an as-built joint of motion type 11) | `rigid_group` | `occurrences` → the occurrences of its component they are or are in (members below the top level and inside components of other documents move with them); with the component's own geometry among them, rigid `as_built_joint`s of each to it |
| `JointOrigin` | `joint_origin` | in the owning component: `geometry` → geometry that gives the frame before `angle` and `offsetZ` (`"origin"` for the component's origin point, a face or edge, else a fixed plane), `angle` → `angle`, `offsetZ` → `offset`; checked against the file's frame, else that frame fixed |
| `GroundOccurrence` | | `occurrence` → the occurrence is grounded |
| `Snapshot` (captured position) | `capture_position` | one per component whose occurrences it places: `positions[]` (`occurrence` paths from the item's component, `transform` there; for a captured position of joints' values, the occurrences whose `_f3d.placements` name it) → each occurrence at its placement in its parent; positions inside components of other documents and of grounded occurrences are left out (`partial`) |
| `GeometricRelationship` | `constraint_set` | in the component its rows' paths start in, a row per decoded constraint (`rows[]`): side two → `a`, side one → `b` (a point or an axis on a plane: it → `a`, the plane → `b`); each frame (`_f3d.frames`) on geometry of the component the path ends in that gives its plane, axis, circle or point (nearest the picked point first), else fixed geometry with the frame; on a component of another document fixed geometry there; two planes, a plane and a circle, a point or an axis on a plane, two axes → `align`, two circles → `insert`, a centring → `center` (`a`, `a2`, `b`, `b2`), an angle → `angle`; `flip` and the sign of `offset` (the parameter, negated where MitCad's normal is the other way) from the references where the file places the occurrences; rows that do not hold there, sides inside components of other documents and circles on components of other documents are left out with the reason ([core/import/docs/f3d-components.md](../../import/docs/f3d-components.md#assembly-relationships)) |
| `TangentRelationship` | `constraint_set` | one `tangent` row between the planar, cylindrical or spherical faces the file's points lie on (`flip` where they touch inside); else left out with the reason |
| Items the stream decoder names by their class only (`ComponentInsert`, `Group`, `FlangeFeature`, ...) | | those without geometry are skipped with what they are, the others are not translated (fallback) with the reason ([core/import/docs/f3d-components.md](../../import/docs/f3d-components.md#items-without-a-translation)) |

### FreeCAD import (.FCStd)

`{"cmd": "import_fcstd", "path": "part.FCStd", …}` (C++
`Document::command`, or `Document::import_fcstd(path, json)` for the
report alone; Rust `mitcad_import_fcstd::import_fcstd(doc, path,
options)`, `import_fcstd_file` with a loader for linked documents)
imports a FreeCAD document's bodies in its structure, with its sketches,
history and parameters (`core/import-fcstd/src/`; the file is read by
`core/freecad`). One undo step (`Import part.FCStd`). How the import
works (stages, checks, readings tried, what falls back):
[core/import-fcstd/docs/freecad.md](../../import-fcstd/docs/freecad.md#freecad-import-fcstd).

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `bodies_only` | the bodies only (FreeCAD's results), without the history, the sketches and the parameters |
| `text` | `import_fcstd` returns a readable report |
| `report_path` | also write the JSON report to this file |
| `reference` | a dump of the document by FreeCAD (`tools/freecad-export/dump.py`) to compare the import with |
| `set_parameters` | `{"Width": "60 mm"}`: parameters changed after the import, before the report measures it (to compare with a dump of FreeCAD's document after the same change) |
