What the document gets:

- Components: `App::Part` and `Assembly::AssemblyObject`, placed by their
  placements (nested ones: subcomponents; hidden ones: hidden
  occurrences). A Body with a placement of its own, and an object a link
  shows, gets a component of its own (its origin the component's) with
  an occurrence at its placement. `App::Link` → an occurrence of the
  linked object's component per array element (`ElementCount`: the
  element objects' placements, else `PlacementList`; `VisibilityList`),
  placed by the link's placement in place of the object's own
  (`LinkTransform` false) or on top of it (true); a link to another
  document reads that file next to the imported one (missing: reported,
  left out); a scaled link → a scaled copy of the body. An assembly's
  grounded joint grounds its part's occurrence; other joints are left
  out.
- Stored bodies: `PartDesign::Body` and the Part workbench's leaf objects
  (with a stored shape that no other shape-bearing object consumes) not
  rebuilt by the history (all of them with `bodies_only`) are one base
  feature per component before the timeline (`FreeCAD bodies`, `FreeCAD
  bodies of <component>`), bodies named after the objects' labels, faces
  `<feature>:import(j)` in the shapes' face order. Hidden objects →
  hidden bodies. Objects without faces are left out with the reason.
- Colours (mitcad#793), of stored bodies and of those the history makes
  alike: each colour of FreeCAD's view (0.21 `ShapeColor`, `Transparency`
  and `DiffuseColor` per face; 1.0 `ShapeAppearance`, one material or one
  per face) is one document appearance, `FreeCAD colour <r> <g> <b>` (with
  its opacity when not opaque), made once however many bodies and faces
  have it (`appearances` in the report). A body gets its object's colour
  (with colours per face the one most faces have), FreeCAD's default grey
  none; a face of another colour gets that colour's appearance
  (`set_face_appearance`): on a stored body the face at FreeCAD's index,
  on a rebuilt one (also one ending in a fallback) the face of the same
  geometry, found as references are; faces not found (merged by FreeCAD's
  `Refine`) are counted in a warning. The report's bodies give
  `appearance` and `face_appearances`. No physical materials.
- The document's `UnitSystem` (1.0 and later) sets the length unit.
- Sketches: a `sketch` feature per `Sketcher::SketchObject`, named after
  its label, in the component of its Body or part, with FreeCAD's
  visibility. Plane: an origin plane it is attached to, a datum plane the
  history made (`"F4"`), a planar face of a body it is attached to
  (`{"face": "F1:import(5)", "body": "F1.b0"}`), else the parallel origin
  plane, else a hidden fixed construction plane; `frame` keeps the stored
  placement. The root point is a fixed point at the origin, the H and V
  axes fixed construction lines when used.
  - Geometry: points, lines, circles, arcs, ellipses and elliptical
    arcs, B-splines (poles as control points; periodic and unclamped
    ones clamped exactly), Bézier curves; arcs of hyperbolas and
    parabolas as exact rational quadratic splines; construction and
    blocked (`fixed`) flags. Internal geometry: a B-spline's control
    point circles are its control points, its end knots its ends; an
    ellipse's axis lines stay construction lines held on it (`midpoint`
    at its centre, the major one ending at its major point, the minor one
    `perpendicular` with an end on the ellipse); foci, interior knots and
    the parts of hyperbolas and parabolas are left out.
  - Constraints: horizontal, vertical (lines, two points), parallel,
    perpendicular (a line and a circle or arc: its centre on the line),
    tangent (two lines: `collinear`), equal, point on object
    (`coincident`; on an axis `horizontal_points`/`vertical_points` with
    the root point), symmetric (about a point: `midpoint` of a
    construction line between the points), block (`fixed`).
  - Dimensions (driven for FreeCAD's reference ones): distance (`length`,
    `arc_length`, `distance`, `point_line_distance`, `line_distance`),
    DistanceX/Y (`horizontal_distance`/`vertical_distance` in the order
    that makes FreeCAD's signed value positive), angle (`angle` in 0..π,
    one line against the H axis, an arc's sweep below 180° between
    construction lines from its centre), radius, diameter.
  - External geometry on a body the import made in the sketch's
    component is a linked projection by its MitCad name; other elements
    are fixed reference geometry; non-defining external geometry is
    construction geometry.
- History: every PartDesign Body and every Part workbench primitive,
  extrusion of a sketch or of another object's faces, revolution of a
  sketch, face of sketches, or operation is rebuilt as
  features in dependency order (ties in document order), each checked
  against FreeCAD's stored shape of it; one that cannot be rebuilt is a
  base feature of the stored shape that `replaces` the Body's body
  (`fallback`), and one whose stored shape is its base's is `skipped`. A
  Body's `Tip` before its last feature: the features after it are
  replayed, then suppressed; a suppressed feature (1.0's `Suppressed`):
  replayed and suppressed (`partial`). Bodies are named after FreeCAD's
  objects, hidden and coloured as there (above). The sketch the import
  makes for a binder of another component's sketch (a feature's profile
  or hole sketch) lies on the bound sketch's own plane with the sketch's
  `plane_link`, and a sketch attached to a face of such a binder on that
  plane with its `plane_link` too (mitcad#963).

| FreeCAD | MitCad | Readings tried |
|---|---|---|
| Pad, Pocket | `extrude` join / cut (the Body's first solid: `new_body`; participants the Body's bodies) on the profile sketch's material regions; Length → `distance`, ThroughAll → `through_all`, UpToFirst / UpToLast → `to_object` body (`through` for the last), UpToFace → `to_object` face or plane, UpToShape (1.0) → `to_object` of its one face or plane, of a whole object's body, or without shapes of the Body's body; `Offset` → `offset`; Midplane / SideType Symmetric → `symmetric` (`full_length`), TwoLengths / SideType Two sides → `two_sides` (1.1's `Type2`); TaperAngle(2) → `taper`; a custom direction (`UseCustomVector`, `ReferenceAxis`: FreeCAD's `Direction`) along the normal; off the normal (mitcad#539) → `extrude` with that `direction` (the lengths along it: FreeCAD's over the cosine with `AlongSketchNormal`; one length, two or symmetric; TaperAngle(2) → `taper`, grown in the profile's plane as FreeCAD grows it) | the regions inside an even number of wires (1.1), else the outer ones with their holes (1.0); the pocket against the normal (`Reversed` turns it), else the other way; the taper's and the offset's signs |
| Revolution, Groove | `revolve` join / cut; the axis: a sketch's H or V axis (its axis line), `Axis<n>` (its n-th construction line), `Edge<n>` (that line), an origin axis, a datum line, a straight edge; 360° → `full`, Midplane → `symmetric` (half each way), TwoAngles → `two_sides`, UpToFace, UpToShape (one face, a plane, a body) and UpToFirst → `to_object`, UpToLast → `to_object` of the Body's body `through` it (mitcad#539; FreeCAD has computed none), a groove's ThroughAll → `full` | the angle's sign; up to an object also about FreeCAD's axis (`Base`, `Axis`) either way; a groove of another type also by its angle (FreeCAD 1.0's grooves read only Angle, Midplane and Reversed) |
| Fillet | `fillet`, constant radius, on the edges and faces (an edge FreeCAD merged: MitCad's pieces along it, by the two faces each lies between where every edge between them is a piece, mitcad#793); `UseAllEdges` → a set of `all_edges` (every edge of the body when the fillet is computed, so edges a sketch edit adds are rounded too) | |
| Chamfer | `chamfer` `equal_distance`, `two_distances` (Size, Size2), `distance_angle` (Size, Angle); edges as for Fillet (`UseAllEdges` → `all_edges`) | `flip` both ways |
| Hole | `hole` at the profile sketch's circles' and arcs' centres (`sketch_points`), Diameter, depth (DrillForDepth taken off) or through all, flat or angled point, counterbore, countersink, counterdrill, Tapered → `taper` (90° less TaperedAngle; FreeCAD's drill point is as high as the straight hole's: the tip angle from the wall's end that gives it); a cosmetic ISO metric, Unified (UNC, UNF, UNEF: `1/4-20 UNC`), Whitworth (BSW, BSF: `1/4-20 BSW`; BSP: `G 1/4`), NPT (`1/4-18 NPT`) or tyre valve (ISOTyre, `5V1`) thread over the hole's depth → a cosmetic `thread` on the walls (the size from the version's list for the thread type, `ThreadSize[ISOMetricProfile]` in `data/enums.json`; the hole keeps FreeCAD's diameter), other threads left out (`partial`); a modelled ISO metric or Unified thread → first as FreeCAD cuts it: per hole a fixed `construction_plane` through the axis, a `sketch` of the groove's section (60° flanks, the root P/8 wide at the major diameter plus the class's clearance; 1.1's quadrilateral, the older hexagon) and a `helix` cutting it from a pitch above the top as deep as FreeCAD's thread runs (through all: two pitches past the body), then the `hole`; then a modelled `thread` (MitCad's basic profile cut from FreeCAD's bore); both stay 1.3e-6 to 2e-6 (the groove) off FreeCAD's thread, so these fall back; Whitworth and NPT ones and those FreeCAD did not model fall back at once, tyre valve ones (FreeCAD rounds their crests) after the thread is tried | `flip` both ways |
| Mirrored, LinearPattern, PolarPattern | `mirror`, `rectangular_pattern` (1.1's second direction too), `circular_pattern` of the originals' MitCad features (`identical`), or of the body (TransformMode whole shape: `combine`, the copies joined to it); planes and axes as above (a sketch's V axis as a mirror plane: the plane through it along the normal); extent or spacing | the distance's or angle's sign |
| MultiTransform | of the originals' features: one transformation as that feature; two LinearPatterns → one `rectangular_pattern` of two directions; two Mirrored → both `mirror`s, a `construction_axis` where their planes meet (`two_planes`) and a `circular_pattern` of 2 about it (the half turn); otherwise (any sequence of Mirrored, LinearPattern and PolarPattern) each transformation a `mirror` or pattern of the one before (patterns of patterns). A Scaled transformation (mitcad#539): first (or alone) → a `scale_pattern` of the originals (Occurrences, Factor), the transformations after it patterns of it; after others → the `scale` (Factor) of the pattern or mirror before it, with `scale_groups` (Occurrences) unless it has as many elements: FreeCAD scales the copies before it in that many runs, each about its own centre; more runs than that one's elements (mitcad#542) → the same scale counted over all the copies before it (`scale_copies`) on that one and on the patterns before it (after two LinearPatterns also one `rectangular_pattern` of two directions with `scale`); several Scaled transformations → their scales on the patterns before each (`scales` where one scales already), the factors multiplying. FreeCAD 1.0 and 1.1 leave out every copy but the original whose factor is 1 once a Scaled transformation follows others (0.21 keeps them; mitcad#542, measured): those readings, first for 1.0 and 1.1, give each pattern the `skipped_copies` of its own such copies (the patterns after it still copy them). Of the whole body (TransformMode whole shape, 1.0 and 1.1; mitcad#539, mitcad#547) → the first transformation a `mirror` or pattern of the body, each next one of the one before (a pattern of patterns of the body: the body as it was at every product of the elements, FreeCAD's product of the transformations), all with `combine`; Scaled ones there as above (`scale_pattern` of the body first; scales, runs and `skipped_copies` of the body's copies), with `scale_center` the Body's origin (FreeCAD's centre in body mode, carried with each copy). Its transformations are no features of their own | the signs of the directions |
| Scaled (alone, not in a MultiTransform) | `scale_pattern` of the originals' features (Occurrences, Factor) | |
| Boolean | `combine` join / cut / intersect of the Body's body with the other Bodies' bodies | |
| Draft | `draft` of the faces about the neutral plane (a pull direction taken as its normal) | `flip`, the angle's sign |
| Thickness | `shell` (Skin; Pipe and RectoVerso as Skin, which FreeCAD's solids give) | inside or outside, rounded |
| AdditiveLoft, SubtractiveLoft | `loft` of the profile and section sketches' regions or planar faces of bodies (`face` sections, mitcad#543), Ruled, Closed | |
| AdditivePipe, SubtractivePipe | `sweep` along the spine sketch's edges, Standard → `perpendicular`, Fixed → `parallel`, Frenet → `frame` `frenet`, Auxiliary → `frame` `auxiliary` along the auxiliary spine sketch's edges (`curvilinear` from AuxilleryCurvelinear, 1.1: AuxiliaryCurvilinear; the spine AuxillerySpine, 1.1: AuxiliarySpine), Binormal → `frame` `constant_binormal`, FreeCAD's `Binormal` turned by the pipe's Placement (mitcad#539); with sections (Transformation Multisection) → `loft` of the profile and the sections with the spine as its `centerline` and the mode's `frame` (mitcad#543), the Fixed mode a `loft` with `orientation` `parallel` (mitcad#547); a profile that is a planar face of a body → the sweep's `profile_face`, a section that is one → a `face` section (mitcad#543) | Frenet also as Standard |
| AdditiveHelix, SubtractiveHelix | `helix` of the profile's regions about the reference axis: the pitch and the turns as the Mode gives them (Height / Pitch, Height / Turns), LeftHanded → `left_handed`, Reversed → `flip`; a cone's angle → `growth` `Pitch * tan(Angle)`, height-turns-growth's Growth → `growth`, both with `"construction": "freecad"`; a subtraction outside the profile (Outside) → `intersect` | the hand and the direction both ways |
| Additive / Subtractive Box, Cylinder, Sphere, Torus, Cone, Prism, Wedge, Ellipsoid | `box`, `cylinder`, `sphere`, `torus` on a fixed plane at the placement; a cone and parts of a turn (Cylinder's and Cone's Angle, Sphere's latitudes and Angle3, Torus's section sector and Angle3): a section in a fixed plane through the axis turned about it (a construction plane, a sketch and a `revolve`); a prism: its polygon `extrude`d from a sketch on a fixed plane; skewed (FirstAngle, SecondAngle; a cylinder too) → `sweep` along the skew, `parallel`; a wedge: a ruled `loft` from its rectangle at Ymin to the one at Ymax (or a point); an ellipsoid: a `sphere` of Radius2 at the origin (a part of one: its section in the XZ plane turned about the z axis, Angle1 to Angle2 and Angle3 round), `scale` non-uniform (Radius3 / Radius2, Radius1 / Radius2), `move` to the placement and `combine` with the Body's body | |
| Plane, Line, Point (datums) | `construction_plane` (`offset` from an origin plane or a planar face when attached flat with only a normal offset; attached flat to an origin plane and turned a quarter or not at all, `offset` from the origin plane parallel to it by the offset's coordinate along its normal; turned about a line in its support's plane through its origin (its x or y axis or between) by a bound angle, `angle` from the support about that line; else `fixed`), `construction_axis`, `construction_point` (`fixed` at the placement); coordinate systems are skipped | |
| Part Box, Cylinder, Sphere, Torus, Cone, Prism, Wedge, Ellipsoid | the primitives as above, new bodies | |
| Part Extrusion of a sketch | `extrude` new body: LengthFwd (else, when LengthRev is zero too, the direction's length), LengthRev → `two_sides` (alone: one side against the direction), Symmetric, Reversed, TaperAngle(Rev); along the normal or a custom direction along it; a custom direction or an edge's (DirMode Custom, Edge: `Dir`) off the normal → `extrude` with that `direction` (mitcad#541: the lengths along it, the tapers too); into faces (Solid off, mitcad#539) → a surface `extrude` (`surface`, `curves`: the sketch's curves that are not construction), off the normal along the `direction`, tapered a surface `extrude` of the regions | the direction, the taper's sign |
| Part Extrusion of another object's faces (mitcad#539, mitcad#541) | per face of the base's bodies (all of them; where another object uses the base too, the copy of its first body and its others) an `extrude` new body with `profile_face`, the lengths and TaperAngle(Rev) as above, along the face's normal, or off it along `Dir` with `direction` (a curved face only so, untapered; Solid on or off: a solid, as FreeCAD makes it), then a base feature without bodies that removes the faces' bodies | the direction, the taper's sign |
| Part Extrusion of an object's edges (mitcad#541) | an object without faces that only Part extrusions use (a Part Circle, RegularPolygon, Polygon or Line, a Draft wire; any type the import has no translation of) is `included`; each extrusion makes a `construction_plane` (`fixed`: the object's placement where its edges lie in it, else the plane through its straight edge and `Dir`) and a `sketch` of the edges as fixed geometry on it, extruded as a sketch is (Solid on: its material regions, any number of loops, mitcad#547; off: a surface extrusion of its curves); edges in no one plane (Solid off, mitcad#547) → per plane they lie in a fixed plane, a sketch and a surface `extrude` of its curves along `Dir` (`direction`); a helix (a Part Helix from its Pitch, Height, Radius, LocalCoord, or one helix edge; Solid off, mitcad#547) → a fixed plane, a sketch of a line from the helix's start along `Dir` and a surface `sweep` of it along a fixed `helix` path, `parallel`; a conical Part Helix, a helix among other edges, a spline in no plane (Solid off, mitcad#548) → the walls of the planar edges as above and per curve in no plane such a sweep along its own fixed `helix` or `fixed_curves` path (the stored curve; a conical Part Helix its stored curves); `partial` (the object's own sizes are not carried over); what FreeCAD fails itself (a curved face, a helix or non-planar edges along the base's normal, tapered, or with Solid on) falls back with that reason | as for a sketch |
| Part Face of sketches (mitcad#539) | `patch` of each sketch's regions inside an even number of wires (FaceMakerClass Bullseye, Cheese, Extrusion; Simple, mitcad#547, where no wire lies in another; of nested wires, mitcad#548, a face filling each wire: a region without holes patched, one with holes patched, its outer opening patched (`boundary`) and the region's patch removed) | |
| Part Revolution of a sketch | `revolve` new body about a fixed axis (Base, Axis); 360° → `full`, Symmetric | the angle's sign |
| Part Sweep of sketches along a sketch (mitcad#543) | new body: one section → `sweep` along the spine's edges, several → `loft` with the spine as its `centerline`; Frenet → `frame` `frenet`; Solid off → `surface` | Frenet also at right angles to the spine |
| Part Sweep along or of other objects (mitcad#547) | a cylindrical Part Helix spine → a fixed `helix` path (Pitch, Height, Radius, LocalCoord, the placement); edges of an object with a body → the body's `edges`; edges of an object without one → one straight edge a fixed line, else a `construction_plane` (`fixed`) and a `sketch` of the edges as fixed geometry, the path its curves; a section of an object's closed planar edges → such a sketch's region, of one vertex → a fixed `point` section; the objects of edges or a vertex only Part extrusions and sweeps use are `included`; `partial` | as for sketches |
| Part Sweep, the remaining inputs (mitcad#548) | a conical Part Helix spine (Angle) → its stored curves as a `fixed_curves` path; edges in no plane of an object without a body → a `fixed_curves` path; one section of an open planar wire → a surface `sweep` of its fixed sketch's `curves`, of a wire in no plane → a surface `sweep` of `fixed_curves` (FreeCAD makes no caps of either); spines and sections of PartDesign features' results → their Body's body's `edges` and faces (the Body replayed for them); the spine and sections make no copy of a body and use none up; several sections of open wires or wires in no plane, and a section of several wires, fall back with that reason | as for sketches |
| Pad, Pocket, Revolution, Groove of several faces (`AllowMultiFace`, mitcad#543) | one `extrude` or `revolve` per face (`profile_face`), the first with the feature's operation, the others joined to it (named " (face 2)", …), as many as there are (mitcad#547) | as for one face |
| Part Cut, Fuse, MultiFuse, Common, MultiCommon | `combine` (the first operand the target) | |
| Part Fillet, Chamfer | `fillet` / `chamfer` of the edge list: a fillet's edges of one radius a `constant` set, each edge of two radii a `variable` set of its own from the first radius at the vertex where FreeCAD's edge starts (`start_vertex`) to the second (mitcad#539); unequal chamfer sizes `two_distances` | `flip` both ways; a fillet edge without a start vertex here (closed) its radii either way |
| Part Mirroring | `mirror` of the source's body (plane Base, Normal or 1.0's MirrorPlane), then a base feature without bodies that removes the source's body | |
| others (binders, Draft objects, plain shapes, …) | a base feature of the stored shape (scripted objects and plain shapes: `fallback_group` `no_counterpart`) | |

- Profiles of Pad, Pocket, Revolution and Groove that are not a whole
  sketch (mitcad#539): a planar face of a body (`Profile` = (object,
  `Face<n>`); FreeCAD takes the first element unless `AllowMultiFace`) →
  the `extrude` or `revolve` of that face (`profile_face`), along its
  outward normal by distances (Length, TwoLengths, Midplane; TaperAngle(2)
  → `taper`, mitcad#541; a custom direction off the normal, mitcad#547,
  → the face's `extrude` with that `direction`, the lengths along it as
  for a sketch's) or by angles; chosen edges of a sketch
  (`Profile` = (sketch, `Edge<n>`, …) with 1.0's `AllowMultiFace`) → the
  sketch's regions inside the areas those edges bound (both readings as
  for a whole sketch); without `AllowMultiFace` FreeCAD takes the whole
  sketch whatever edges the link names, and so does the import. Several
  faces, and faces of lofts and pipes, fall back.
- An operand of the Part workbench that a later object uses too is
  copied (`move` with `copy`) for each earlier use.
- The features of one FreeCAD object are named after its label, those
  that help the main one with a suffix (hidden when they are
  construction planes or sketches): `<label> (plane)` and `<label>
  (section)` of a cone, a prism or a part of a turn, `<label> (bottom
  plane)`, `(bottom)`, `(top plane)`, `(top)` of a wedge, `<label>
  (sphere)`, `(scale)`, `(placement)` of an ellipsoid (a part of one also
  `(plane)` and `(section)`), `<label> (mirror 1)`, `(mirror 2)`,
  `(axis)` of a MultiTransform's mirrors, `<label> (transformation 1)`,
  `(transformation 2)`, … of its chain of patterns and mirrors, `<label>
  (thread)` of a hole, `<label> (source removed)` of a mirroring, `<label>
  plane` of a sketch on an offset or turned construction plane.

Parameters and expressions (`freecad/params.rs`), before the timeline:

- User parameters: spreadsheet cells with an alias (named after it),
  cells an expression names by address (`<sheet>_B3`), VarSets' numeric
  properties (1.0), the history's feature properties that expressions
  refer to (`<label>_<property>`: `Pad_Length`), and sketches' named
  constraints. A name MitCad cannot take, or one several share, gets its
  owner's label in front. Each has FreeCAD's expression translated, else
  FreeCAD's value (a cell without a value that does not translate is
  `skipped`).
- Bound expressions become the expressions of the values the import
  carries over (pads' and pockets' lengths, offsets and tapers,
  revolutions' angles, fillets', chamfers' and holes' sizes, patterns'
  distances, angles and counts, draft angles, thicknesses, primitives'
  sizes, Part extrusions' lengths and tapers, sketches' dimensions), using
  the parameter made of the property where there is one (the feature, or
  the sketch for a named constraint, adopts it). Attachment offsets of
  sketches and datum planes: bound along the normal → a construction
  plane `offset` from the support; a bound turn about the support's x or
  y axis → an `angle` construction plane; turned a quarter (by a value)
  so that a bound side offset moves it along its normal → the parallel
  origin plane `offset` by that expression. A cone's and a partial
  cylinder's radii and height are length dimensions of their section
  sketches. Side offsets that only move a sketch or plane within itself,
  and turns about other axes or with shifts, keep FreeCAD's values.
- Translation: references (`Spreadsheet.Width`, `<<Sheet>>.B3`,
  `.Constraints.width`, `Sketch.Constraints.width`, `VarSet.Depth`,
  `Pad.Length`, `.Height.Value` as a plain number), units (`°` as `deg`,
  `gon` as `grad`, `thou` as `mil`, `"` and `'` as `in` and `ft`, `dm`,
  `nm`, `′`, `″` by their factors), `pi`, `e` as `PI`, `E`, `c ? a : b`
  as `if(c; a; b)`, `log`, `log10` as `ln`, `log`, `mod(a; b)` as `a %
  b`, `hypot`, `cath`, `cbrt`, `trunc`, `sum` and `average` (over ranges
  too) written out, `min` and `max` of several; FreeCAD's signs bind
  tighter than `^` and its `^` is left-associative (`-2^2` = `(-2)^2`). A
  unitless result where FreeCAD has a length or an angle gets FreeCAD's
  unit (`B3 * 1 mm`).
- Every translated expression is compared with FreeCAD's stored value
  (1e-9 relative; an integer property's expression is rounded as FreeCAD
  rounds it, `round(Count / 2)`, when that gives FreeCAD's value); one
  that differs (`mismatched`) or does not translate keeps FreeCAD's
  value, with the reason in the report.

The result: `file`, `design` (the document's label), `items` (objects),
`bodies`, `counts` (objects per outcome: `body`, `component`,
`occurrence`, `parametric`, `partial`, `fallback`, `included`,
`skipped`) and `report`:

- `program_version`, `schema_version`, `units`, `objects_by_type`;
- `items`: per object `index`, `name`, `label`, `type`, `outcome`,
  `note`, `bodies`, `component`, `stale` when its stored shape may be out
  of date;
- `bodies`: each with its `object`, `file` when from another document,
  `uid`, `name`, `component`, `kind`, `volume`, `area`, `center` in its
  component, `color`, `visible`;
- `placed`: where each body, part, link and array element of the
  document shows its geometry: `path`, `bodies`, world `volume`, `area`
  and `center`;
- `components`, `occurrences`, `files` and `missing_files` (linked
  documents), `stale`, `warnings`;
- `sketches`: per sketch `object`, `label`, `outcome`, `feature`,
  `component`, `plane`, FreeCAD's `geometry` and `constraints` counts,
  MitCad's `entities`, `mitcad_constraints`, `dimensions`, `error` of the
  solved points, `dropped`, `notes`, `dimension_sources`, `expressions`,
  `shape` against the stored shape, and the profile curves' `edges`,
  `length` and world `center`;
- `features`: the history in timeline order, per object `object`,
  `label`, `type`, `body` (its PartDesign Body), `outcome`, `features`
  (the MitCad features made), `mitcad` (their type), `check` against the
  stored shape (`volume`, `area`, `center`, `solids` and FreeCAD's,
  `distance`, `pass`), `notes` (which reading was kept, or why it fell
  back) and a fallback's `fallback_group` (mitcad#539): `missing` (a
  translation MitCad does not have yet: the reason says "not
  translated"), `no_counterpart` (a scripted object, a plain shape, or
  one FreeCAD failed itself), `other` (translated, but it did not build or
  give FreeCAD's shape); the readable report counts them (`fallbacks by
  group: …`);
- `parameters`: per parameter `name`, `source`, `object` and its `cell`,
  `property` or `constraint`, `describe`, FreeCAD's expression
  `freecad`, MitCad's `expression`, `value`, `freecad_value`, `outcome`
  (`parameter`, `value`, `mismatched`, `skipped`) and `note`;
- `expressions`: every expression FreeCAD binds to a property: `object`,
  `path`, `expression`, `mitcad`, `outcome` (`parameter`, `expression`,
  `value`, `mismatched`, `unused`) and `note`;
- with `reference`, `reference`: `checked`, `differences`, `pass`
  (volumes of solids and areas within 1e-9 relative, world centres of
  mass within 1e-6 mm, places with bodies of the history
  (`placed[].replayed`) within the replay's 1e-6; sketches' edge counts,
  lengths and centres within 1e-6 relative; parameters' values against
  FreeCAD's values of the cells, properties and constraints within 1e-9
  relative). A place of stored shapes also has `placed[].fixed`: their
  `volume`, `area` and `center` with the kernel's plain fixed-point
  integration, as FreeCAD measures; where FreeCAD's measures are those,
  a difference is listed as not compared (MitCad integrates faces bounded
  by B-splines of many spans more exactly, mitcad#139).

Tests: `core/freecad/tests/parse.rs`, `core/freecad/tests/sketch_corpus.rs`,
`core/import-fcstd/src/tests.rs` (mock kernel), `cli.import_fcstd`
(`tools/cli/fcstd-test.cmake`), `freecad.corpus` (`MITCAD_FCSTD_CORPUS`;
[core/import-fcstd/docs/freecad.md](../../import-fcstd/docs/freecad.md#tests)) and
`tools/ui-import-test.sh`.

### .ipt import

`{"cmd": "import_ipt", "path": "part.ipt", …}` (C++ `Document::command`,
or `Document::import_ipt(path, json)` for the report alone) imports an
`.ipt` part file (mitcad#60; `core/ffi/src/ipt_import.rs`, the reader is
[core/ipt](../../ipt/README.md)):

- **With its history** (the default when the file's definitions segment
  has features or parameters; stages 2 and 3): the part's parameters with
  their expressions, its sketches, work planes and features, decoded into
  the import's dump IR (`mitcad_ipt::design`) and replayed by the same
  importer as the `.f3d` import ([.f3d import with the
  timeline](#f3d-import-with-the-timeline)): each feature is checked
  against the state of the ASM history stored in the B-rep record that its
  operation made, and comes in as the bodies of that state where it
  cannot be replayed (`fallback`); the final bodies are compared with the
  stored ones. The report adds `history` (true), `parameters` (the
  definitions segment's parameter records: `records`, `model`, `user`,
  `outside` (not the part's: annotations, reference dimensions, features'
  own tables), `internal` (`RDxVar<n>`), `unread`), `expressions`
  (`translated`, `agree`: evaluated to the stored value, `differ`,
  `not_translated`, `computed` (parameters whose value the model computes,
  not their expression: the stored value comes in), each `name: why`),
  `features` (items with a history
  state), `features_with_states` (of them, those whose state the history
  has), `counts` (items per outcome), `design` (the importer's report:
  `items`, `parameters`, `history`, `bodies`, `warnings`, as for
  `import_f3d`), `design_text` (its text), `replayed` (false when the
  hang watchdog gave up on the replay outside its items, so that the stored
  bodies came in without the timeline; mitcad#507) and `seconds` {`read`,
  `import`}; `imported` lists the document's bodies after the replay
  (`feature` is the feature that made the body). Sheet-metal faces,
  flanges on one edge and cuts through the sheet replay as `sheet_rules`
  (named `Sheet rules <style>`, before the first face), `sheet_face`,
  `sheet_flange` and `sheet_cut` (mitcad#211; the `.f3d` import's base and
  edge flanges likewise; `core/import/docs/f3d-sheet-metal.md`, *Sheet metal*).
- **Bodies only** (`bodies_only`, and files without definitions; stage
  1): one base feature per body (solids and sheet bodies), built from the
  file's B-rep record with OCCT.

Either way the triangles of the part's mesh features come in as mesh
bodies (`source` `PmGraphicsSegment#<record>`, `mesh` true, `closed`,
`triangles`; after the replay with the history), and a part without
bodies and meshes opens empty with a warning (bodies that cannot be built
are still an error).

Either way the document's length unit becomes the part's when the
document has no features yet (else a warning says so), and the bodies get
the part's material when MitCad's library has one of that name or id (case
does not matter). One undo step (`Import part.ipt`). A job does not cancel
it.

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `text` | `import_ipt` returns a readable report |
| `report_path` | also write the JSON report to this file |
| `reference` | a STEP file of the same part: each of its solids is matched with the imported solid of the closest volume and their volumes and areas compared |
| `max_relative` | the largest relative difference of a volume or area that passes (default 1e-6) |
| `deviation` | with `reference`, also the sampled surface deviation (as `compare_step`) |
| `bodies_only` | the bodies only, as base features (stage 1) |
| `no_verify`, `no_fallback`, `no_compare` | as for `import_f3d`: do not check the replay against the history; leave out features that cannot be replayed; compare the final bodies by volume only |
| `time_limit` | seconds after which the remaining features take the file's bodies |
| `hang_limit` | seconds without progress after which a geometry kernel call counts as hung (an empty document only): as for `import_f3d`, the replay runs again on its own thread with the item it hung on taking the file's bodies, a warning saying so |
| `dump_path` | also write the decoded design (the dump IR, `core/import/SCHEMA.md`) to this file |
| `design_path` | replay this dump (as `dump_path` writes it) instead of the decoded design |

The command's result: `file`, `design` (the part number), `bodies` (the
number imported) and `report`: `format` (`ipt`), `part_number`,
`material`, `mitcad_material` (the material set, or null), `release` (the
release that saved the file, as it says), `units` (the document's new
length unit, or null) and `unit_code`; `records` (each B-rep record:
`source`, `asm_version`, `bodies`, `history_states` (the states of the
ASM history the record carries), `truncated`); `imported`
(each body: `source` `<segment>#<record>/<body>`, `solid`, `valid`
(OCCT's checker), `volume`, `raw_volume` (before the solids were
oriented), `area`, `faces`, `issues`, `messages` (the builder's, with what
the checker finds wrong), `feature`,
`bodies` with `uid`, `name`, `kind`); `skipped` (bodies not built:
`source`, `error`); `warnings`; `seconds` {`read`, `build`}; and with
`reference`, `reference`: `file`, `step_solids`, `solids` (pairs:
`step_body`, `step_volume`, `step_area`, `body`, `name`, `volume`,
`area`, `volume_difference`, `area_difference`), `unmatched_step`,
`unmatched_bodies`, `max_difference`, `max_relative`, `valid`, with
`deviation` `max_deviation`, and `pass` (every STEP solid and every
imported solid matched, all within `max_relative`, every imported solid
valid).

Tests: `core/ipt` (`core.ipt`, no OCCT), the design replayed on the
mock kernel (`core.model.imports`, `core/model-tests/imports/src/ipt_design_tests.rs`), `core.exchange`
(`core/tests/test_exchange.cpp`), `cli.import_ipt*`, `cli.ipt_design_file`,
`ipt.corpus`
(`MITCAD_IPT_CORPUS`, [core/import/docs/ipt.md](../../import/docs/ipt.md#ipt-import))
and `tools/ui-import-test.sh`.

### .iam import

`{"cmd": "import_iam", "path": "assembly.iam", …}` (also `import_ipt` with
an `.iam` file; C++ `Document::command`, or `Document::import_iam(path,
json)` for the report alone) imports an `.iam` assembly (mitcad#60, stage
4; `core/ffi/src/iam_import.rs`, the reader is
[core/ipt](../../ipt/README.md#assemblies)):

- Every distinct part file is imported once with the `.ipt` import, in a
  document of its own: its stored bodies, which become one base feature
  of a component of this document (the shapes shared, not copied), or
  with `history` its parameters and features replayed, that design copied
  into a component (`Document::add_component_copy`); each of its
  occurrences is an
  occurrence of that component, named after the file and the instance
  number (`part:2`) or the label the file stores.
- A sub-assembly is a component whose occurrences are placed in it the
  same way; each sub-assembly file comes in once, however often it is
  placed.
- Placements are the file's (cm become mm); hidden occurrences are hidden,
  grounded ones grounded, suppressed ones left out (counted).
- Referenced files are found as saved, else relative to the assembly as it
  was when saved (the saved paths of both), else by the saved path's tail
  under the assembly's folder and the folders above it, else by name in
  the assembly's folder tree and `search` folders. A part found there is
  checked to be the referenced document: its own file list names the
  version id the occurrence stores (`identity`). A file not found is an
  empty component with the occurrences placed, and the report names it.
- Checks against the file: each occurrence's placement in the document
  against the transform the file displays it with (where the file keeps
  one), and each placed part's bodies (their bounding box in the
  component) against the range box the file stores for the document:
  they must lie within it, to 1 % of its diagonal (at least 0.05 mm); the
  stored box is not tight (curved faces make it larger), so how much
  larger it is (`box_slack`) is information only. The stored centre of the
  placed range box is compared too, for information only: the file does
  not always keep it up to date.

- With `history` (mitcad#507): a part whose replay fails (the `.ipt`
  import's error, also a replay the hang watchdog gave up on in every try)
  comes in as its stored bodies instead, as without `history` (not with
  `no_fallback`, where it fails); a part without a design history (no
  features or parameters) and one whose replay came in without its
  timeline (`replayed` false) come in as their stored bodies too. An item
  the watchdog gave up on takes the file's bodies within the part's
  replay, as in the `.ipt` import (`hangs`). Each part's outcome is in
  its file's `part`.
- Progress: every referenced file is resolved before the first part is
  imported, so that the parts are counted. With `MITCAD_IMPORT_TRACE` set
  each part file is traced on standard error, `import: [<s>] part <n> of
  <m>: <file>` when its import starts and `import: [<s>] part <n> of <m>:
  <file>: replayed in <s> s` (or `bodies`) when it is done; `<m>` counts
  the part files found. A part's replay traces its items as the `.ipt`
  import does, between those lines.

The document's length unit becomes the assembly's when the document has no
features yet. One undo step (`Import assembly.iam`); a job does not cancel
it.

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `text` | `import_iam` returns a readable report |
| `report_path` | also write the JSON report to this file |
| `search` | more folders searched for referenced files by name (with their subfolders) |
| `history` | each part with its design replayed (as `import_ipt` without `bodies_only`), not only its stored bodies: much longer and much more memory |
| `no_verify`, `no_fallback`, `no_compare`, `time_limit`, `hang_limit` | with `history`, each part's import, as for `import_ipt` |

The command's result: `file`, `occurrences` (placed) and `report`:
`format` (`iam`), `release`, `units`, `unit_code`; `occurrences` (counts:
`placed`, `suppressed`, `hidden`, `of_missing_files`, `not_placed`,
`without_file`, `without_placement`, `not_rigid`); `parts` (part files:
`files`, `imported`, `missing`, `failed`, `identity_confirmed`,
`identity_differs`, `replayed`, `as_bodies`); `history` (the option);
`assemblies` (sub-assembly files); `resolution`
(files per way they were found); `files` (each: `saved`, `path`, `found`,
`kind`, `status`, `identity`, `occurrences`, `component`, and for parts
`part`: the part import's `bodies`, `solids`, `valid`, `not_built`,
`history` (the part's design was read), `outcome` (`replayed`: its
design replayed and copied into the component; `bodies`: its stored
bodies), `reason` (why `bodies`: `the stored bodies chosen` without
`history`, `the part has no design history`, `the replay failed: <error>`,
`the replay hung: <notes>`; null when replayed), `items` (the replay's
timeline items), `verified` (of them, those checked against the part's
history), `parameters` (made), `counts` (items per outcome), `features`,
`hangs` (the watchdog's notes), `warnings` (how many), `units`,
`material`, `seconds`);
`display`, `boxes`, `centers` (each `compared`, `agree`, `worst` in mm,
`failures`); `pass` (every display and range box check agrees);
`occurrence_list` (each placed or suppressed occurrence with its path
name, `file` index, `occurrence` uid, `grounded`, `hidden`, `checks`);
`warnings`; `seconds`.

Tests: `core/ipt` (`core.ipt`: the reader on assemblies made by
`mitcad_ipt::testassembly`), `core.model` (`add_component_copy`),
`cli.iam_files`, `cli.import_iam`, `cli.info_iam`, `cli.import_ipt_iam`
(a test project of those assemblies: a sub-assembly, parts found relative
to the assembly and by name, a missing one; hidden, grounded and
suppressed occurrences), `cli.import_iam_history_parts` and
`cli.import_iam_history_fallback` (with `history`: the parts' outcomes
and progress lines; `MITCAD_TEST_IAM_REPLAY_FAIL=<file name>` makes that
part's replay fail, for tests), and `iam.corpus`
([tools/cli/iam-corpus.cmake](../../../tools/cli/iam-corpus.cmake),
every `.iam` under `MITCAD_IPT_CORPUS`).

### IFC import

`{"cmd": "import_ifc", "path": "building.ifc", …}` (C++
`Document::command`, or `Document::import_ifc(path, json)` for the report
alone) imports an IFC building model (mitcad#273): IFC2X3, IFC4 or IFC4X3,
`.ifc` text or an `.ifczip` archive. The reader is
[core/ifc](../../ifc/README.md); the import `core/import-ifc/`
(generic over the kernel, tested on the mock kernel) and
`core/ffi/src/ifc_import.rs`.

- **Structure.** Each site, building, storey and facility (IFC4X3's
  bridges, roads, railways and their parts) is a component in its
  parent's, named after it and placed where the file places it; a
  storey's elevation is a fixed construction plane in its component
  (`<storey> level`), each grid axis a fixed construction axis in its
  grid's component (`<grid> <tag>`). Spaces, annotations, ports, the
  structural analysis model and virtual elements are not imported.
- **Elements.** Each element's `Body` representation (else `Facetation`,
  else another 3D one, else `Box`) comes into the component of the
  spatial element it is in (its container, its assembly's, its opening's
  element's), in one command of its own (`Document::add_features_with`):
  - swept solids and CSG as features: a sketch of the profile (in a frame
    of its own; parameterised profiles with their fillet radii as arcs)
    and an extrusion, a sweep along a fixed line for a slanted one
    (`orientation: parallel`), a revolve, ruled lofts for a tapered
    extrusion, a sketch of the directrix and a sweep for a profile swept
    along a planar curve, a pipe for a swept disk along a planar curve;
    blocks and cylinders are extruded rectangles and circles, cones and
    spheres revolutions;
  - booleans: the second operand cuts, joins or intersects the first's
    bodies as its feature's operation, or is built on its own and
    combined (`combine`); a half space is a rectangle on its plane
    extruded through all on the material's side (`cut`), a polygonally
    bounded one its polygon extruded from the plane on;
  - breps (faceted breps and surface models, advanced breps with their
    B-spline and elementary surfaces) as base features of the bodies the
    kernel builds from their faces (`Kernel::boundary_body`), solids where
    the shells close; face sets (triangulated and polygonal) as mesh
    bodies (`Kernel::triangle_body`); swept disks along a curve that is
    not planar as the kernel's pipe, a base feature;
  - its openings (IfcRelVoidsElement) are cut from its solid bodies with
    their own shapes (as tools of the same kinds); mesh bodies are not
    cut.
- **Types.** A representation map that an element uses with a rigid
  transform, when the element has no openings, is one component (named
  after its type), built once; each such use is an occurrence of it.
  Other uses copy the map's items into the element, moved by the
  transform: a scale or a mirror is applied to the items themselves (a
  profile's curves under a non-uniform scale become ellipses or rational
  B-splines; revolutions and curved faces of breps take uniform ones only).
- **Names and appearances.** An element's bodies are named `<name>
  <GlobalId>` (then ` (2)`, …); a surface style's colour (the item's, else
  the element's material's) is a document appearance, made once per
  colour and transparency.
- **Units.** Lengths become millimetres and angles radians; an empty
  document takes the file's length unit (`mm`, `cm`, `m`, `ft`, `in`).
- **The report** has a line for every product of the file: `parametric`
  (every item as features), `stored` (breps), `mesh`, `mixed`,
  `occurrence`, `partial` (some items did not build), `component`,
  `axes`, `cut` (an opening), `not_imported` (with why) or `failed`. Each
  element's bodies' volume (closed meshes' measured from their triangles)
  is compared with the file's element quantities (`NetVolume` where
  openings were cut, else `GrossVolume`; within 1e-3 relative they
  agree). What did not build stays on the timeline as an import note on
  the element's first feature, or a suppressed placeholder when nothing
  of it was built ([The import's outcomes on the
  timeline](#the-imports-outcomes-on-the-timeline)).
- **Memory.** The import process's memory guard (mitcad#80) stops the
  import before the next element when the process is low on memory; the
  remaining elements are reported as not imported (`low_memory`).

One undo step (`Import building.ifc`); a job does not cancel it.

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `text` | `import_ifc` returns a readable report |
| `report_path` | also write the JSON report to this file |
| `openings` | cut the elements' openings (default true) |
| `occurrences` | rigid uses of a type's shape as occurrences of one component (default true; false copies the items into each element) |
| `memory_limit` | the most memory (MiB) the import may use before it stops; the process's limits otherwise |

The command's result: `file`, `products`, `bodies` and `report`:
`format` (`ifc`), `file`, `schema` (`IFC2X3`, `IFC4`, `IFC4X3`),
`schema_name`, `view_definition`, `originating_system`, `project`,
`length_unit`, `angle_unit`, `units` (the document's units when set),
`products` (each: `id`, `global_id`, `kind`, `class`, `name`,
`outcome`, `component`, `bodies`, `occurrences`, `features`,
`parametric` and `stored` (item kinds), `volume`, `quantity`,
`quantity_difference`, `notes`), `outcomes` (products per outcome),
`maps` (each: `map`, `name`, `component`, `occurrences`, `bodies`,
`volume`, `notes`), `components`, `storey_planes`, `grid_axes`,
`appearances`, `features`, `bodies`, `quantities` (`compared`, `agree`,
`worst`, `differ`), `total_volume` (mm³, each map's bodies counted once
per occurrence), `warnings`, `low_memory`, `seconds`, `read_seconds`,
`instances`, `left_out_instances`, `text_report`.

Tests: `core.ifc` (the reader), `core.import` (`ifc::`: the test building
on the mock kernel, every product's outcome), `core.model`
(`add_features_with`), `cli.ifc_file`, `cli.import_ifc`, `cli.info_ifc`
(the test building with OCCT: volumes, the opening cut, the window type's
occurrences), and `ifc.corpus`
([tools/cli/ifc-corpus.cmake](../../../tools/cli/ifc-corpus.cmake),
every `.ifc` of `MITCAD_IFC_CORPUS`; faceted twins compared by volume).

### .rvt import

`{"cmd": "import_rvt", "path": "project.rvt", …}` (C++ `Document::command`,
or `Document::import_rvt(path, json)` for the report alone) imports an
`.rvt` project's building elements (mitcad#274, mitcad#275, mitcad#333;
`core/ffi/src/rvt_import.rs` and `mitcad_import_rvt`, the reader is
[core/rvt](../../rvt/README.md)). `.rte` templates likewise; an `.rfa`
family (or `.rft` template) opens with its metadata and report only (its
forms are a later ticket).

- One component per level (named as the level, lowest first; a component
  `Elements` for elements of a file without levels), each with a
  construction plane `<level> level` at the level's elevation. The grids
  are construction axes of the root component (`Grid <name>`); an arc
  grid is a sketch of its arc.
- **Walls, floors (and pads), roofs, columns, beams and monolithic stair
  runs** are rebuilt from their parameters as features of their level's
  component, one command per element (`mitcad_import_rvt::plan`): a
  sketch and an extrusion (a wall's footprint with its ends where its
  joins put them; a floor's boundary loops down from its top; a roof's
  footprint or extrusion profile under its slopes' planes; a column's or
  beam's section, rectangular, round, I, L, U or hollow, along its axis; a
  run's steps down to its support), with the cuts of the inserts it hosts
  (doors and windows: their type's cut loops) and of the elements whose
  geometry cuts it. Their bodies are named `Family:Type:Id` and take the
  appearance of their material (a layered type's exterior layer's, a
  family type's first).
- **Attached walls** (mitcad#348): a wall whose top (or base) is attached
  to a roof, floor, ceiling or reference plane follows that element's
  lower (or upper) surface, below or above its own top (or base): its
  prism runs from its base to above the surface, and the half spaces above
  the surface's planes are cut away (a roof's slopes: above each slope's
  lower plane; a base below its one plane), its line noting `its top
  follows roof 44's lower surface (2 slopes)`. The cut is fixed: the
  features do not follow the roof when it is changed later. An attachment
  the import cannot apply (a face roof's surface, several elements of
  different heights, a sloped roof whose footprint does not cover the
  wall, a base on several slopes) leaves the wall at its own height and
  its line names it (`its top's attachment to … is not applied: …`). An
  attached wall checked against its stored box is checked both ways
  there in height (its top must reach the box's, not only lie within it).
- **Openings** (mitcad#345): every insert that opens a wall (the inserts
  whose cut the wall takes, the doors and windows it hosts, the other
  elements it hosts whose types have cut loops or void geometry) cuts it
  by its type's cut loops, else by its type's void geometry (its family's
  void forms as faceted bodies at the instance's transform), else by the
  IFC export's opening its GlobalId fills when the export is the
  reference (`reference_ifc`, or found next to the project;
  `mitcad_import_rvt::reference_openings`); a
  rectangular wall opening cuts its rectangle through the wall. An
  opening without a tool is named on the wall's line (`insert 47 is not
  cut: …`); a wall that comes in as the geometry the file keeps or the
  reference's body holds its openings, as a saved mesh or a box it does
  not. The report counts them (and its text summary: `walls'
  openings: N cut, M missing (…)`): `openings_cut`, `openings_missing` (by
  reason) and `openings_missing_lines` (`insert 47 in wall 31: …`), and
  the insert's own line says it (`its opening in wall 31 is not cut: …`).
  Elements a wall hosts that cut nothing (trims) are counted on its line.
- Each element built is checked: against the IFC export given as
  `reference_ifc`, or found next to the project as `<name>.ifc` (unless
  `no_reference_ifc`), by its GlobalId (which the import derives from the
  element's creation episode): its volume within 1 % and its box within
  5 mm of the export's solid; else against its stored box (its body
  within 5 mm of it). An element whose features fail or disagree is
  undone and comes in as below, the reason on its report line.
- **Every other element** (family instances: doors, windows, furniture,
  curtain panels and mullions, …; curtain walls, railings, stairs of
  parts, wall sweeps, slab edges, sections of no known kind, …) is a body
  of its level's base feature `<level> elements`, from the first of these
  that gives one (mitcad#333):
  1. a mesh of the geometry the file keeps of it (the B-reps of its
     partition's geometry chain: its own bodies and the types it places
     at their transforms, [core/rvt](../../rvt/README.md#the-geometry-mitcad333)),
     when it agrees with the reference's solid of its GlobalId (its box
     within 5 mm, a closed mesh's volume within 1 %) or else lies within
     its stored box (but for a tenth of the box's largest extent);
  2. the reference's bodies of its GlobalId (the IFC export's);
  3. the triangle mesh its record saves;
  4. its box: a family type's box at the instance's transform (when it
     agrees with the element's own box within 0.01 ft), else the
     element's box in model coordinates. A box is **hidden** (its body's
     visibility off; showing it shows it) unless the element is
     structural: of a kind built as features but curtain panels and
     mullions (walls, floors, roofs, ceilings, stair runs, landings,
     columns, beams, sweeps, slab edges, rails; by class or category).

  Its report line says which, and a box's line why the others gave
  nothing. Lengths in feet become millimetres.
- **Groups**: the members of a placed group (`ElementGroup`) that it
  places where they are come in as any element; members of a group's
  definition placed nowhere stay out, and a member placed elsewhere comes
  in there too, as the mesh of its geometry moved by the group's
  transform (`group_copies`), on the group's level.
- **Built as features too** (mitcad#333; [core/rvt](../../rvt/README.md#curtain-walls-railings-stairs-sweeps-mitcad333)):
  ceilings like floors (their boundary loops between their two horizontal
  reference faces, else down by their type's width); curtain panels (a
  system panel's cell extruded by its thickness) and mullions (a
  rectangular, corner or custom profile along the mullion's path; a
  trimmed mullion's ends cut along its symbol's stored end faces,
  mitcad#385); stair runs of treads and risers (spiral ones about their
  centre, mitcad#385) and landings; wall sweeps, slab edges, fascias,
  gutters and rails (their profile family's profile along their path, a
  body per line; a spiral rail along a fixed helix; a wall sweep's ends
  mitred where its returns turn and where it meets another sweep, and cut
  by the sweeps joined to cut it, mitcad#385). A curtain wall and a railing whose geometry is
  their parts' have no body of their own (`outcome` `parts`;
  `curtain_walls`, `railings`); the balusters and posts come in as family
  instances. The batch of elements built in one command is 64 elements;
  one whose features fail or disagree is left out of it and comes in as
  below.
- An element's level is the one its records name (its associated level,
  a level field, a level its records hold, a level parameter, its host's);
  one that names none goes on the highest level at or below its box
  (counted as `by_elevation`).
- **Links**: each linked model (an `RvtLinkInstance`) is a component of
  the root, `<file> : <instance>`, placed by the instance's transform; the
  linked file (found by its name in `link_files`, else next to the
  project, at the relative path the project stores, or in `link_folder`)
  comes in there the same way (its own links are not followed). The name
  and path come from the project, so only a bare file name is looked for
  and a stored path only below the project's folder (no root, drive or
  `..`; mitcad#924). A link
  not found leaves its component empty, the report naming it. A linked
  IFC model (a link whose file is an `.ifc`) comes in from its cached
  model (`<name>.ifc.RVT`) when found, else from the IFC file by the IFC
  import into its component. The
  application asks for the missing files (`list_links`); the command line
  never does.
- Left out, counted by reason (`left_out`): types, view-specific elements
  (annotations), members of groups' definitions that no placed group
  places where they are, placed groups themselves, elements without a box
  or mesh, elements of categories that are no building elements (levels,
  grids, rooms, lines, views, materials, …), elements without records.
- The memory guard (mitcad#80) watches the reading and the building: when
  the process runs low on memory the remaining elements are left out
  (`memory_low`) and a warning says so.
- Each base feature gets an import note (the timeline's yellow badge,
  [The import's outcomes on the timeline](#the-imports-outcomes-on-the-timeline)):
  how many meshes and boxes (and how many boxes hidden), and that the
  report says why each one is not built.

One undo step (`Import project.rvt`). A job does not cancel it.

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `text` | `import_rvt` returns a readable report |
| `report_path` | also write the JSON report to this file |
| `report_only` | read and report; import no elements |
| `reference_ifc` | the IFC export of the same project to check the features (and meshes) against, whose bodies stand in for elements without geometry, and whose openings cut the inserts without a cut tool of their own |
| `no_reference_ifc` | do not take an IFC export next to the project as the reference |
| `link_files` | linked models' files by the links' file names (`{"linked.rvt": "C:/…/linked.rvt"}`; the application's file dialogs) |
| `link_folder` | a folder to look for linked models in, besides the project's |
| `list_links` | only list the links and where their files are: `{"links": [{"id", "file", "stored_path", "found"}]}` (the project's elements are read without the geometry the file keeps; the application lists them once, mitcad#413) |
| `mesh_only` | every element as its mesh or box, no features |
| `elements` | only these elements (ids; mitcad#385: checking a few elements of a large project), the others left out |

The command's result: `file`, `design` (the family's name, else the
file's), `bodies` and `report`: `format` (`rvt` or `rfa`), `kind`
(`project`, `family`), `release` and `build` (from `BasicFileInfo`),
`family` and `family_categories` (a family's `PartAtom`),
`external_files` (linked models and other files by name: `name`, `kind`,
`element`), `preview` (`bytes`, `size`), `schema` (`classes`,
`id_width`, `unknown_encodings`), `elements` (`declared`,
`with_records`, `walked`, `read_in_part`, `not_read`), `levels` (`id`,
`name`, `elevation` mm), `materials` (count), `import` (projects:
`levels` with `id`, `name`, `elevation`, `component`, `feature`, `link`,
`features`, `bodies`, `meshes`, `boxes`; `features` and `built` (elements
built as features, by kind), `fallbacks` (elements of those kinds that
came in as meshes or boxes), `reference`, `reference_agree` (the
reference's solids agreed with, by IFC class) and `reference_unmatched`
(its walls, slabs, roofs, columns, beams and members no feature agrees
with, and why), `bodies`, `meshes`, `oriented_boxes`, `boxes`,
`level_planes`, `grid_axes`, `grid_arcs`, `appearances`, `links` (`id`,
`file`, `found`, `component`, `elements`, `note`), `categories`,
`left_out`, `by_elevation`, `not_built`, `memory_low`, `warnings`, and
`geometry_meshes` and `geometry_triangles` (meshes of the geometry the
file keeps), `reference_bodies`, `hidden_boxes`, `curtain_walls`,
`railings`, `group_copies`, `openings_cut`, `openings_missing`,
`openings_missing_lines`, and `elements`: a line
per element (`id`, `link`, `global_id`, `kind`, `category`, `name`,
`level`, `outcome` (`features`, `mesh`, `reference body`, `box`,
`parts`, `not built`), `features`, `bodies`, `volume`, `checked_against`,
`reference_volume`, `volume_difference`, `box_difference`, `hidden`,
`notes`)), `warnings` and
`seconds`.

Tests: `core/rvt` (`core.rvt`, no OCCT; its corpus test reads

### .solidcraft import

`{"cmd": "import_solidcraft", "path": "design.solidcraft"}` (a document
command of the bridge, like `import_fcstd`; `mitcad-cli import-solidcraft`,
File › Open and Import, the headless MCP server's `document_open`) brings a
SolidCraft design in with its history (mitcad#450; `core/solidcraft` reads
it, `mitcad_import::solidcraft` maps it, `core/ffi/src/solidcraft_import.rs`).
Options:

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `text` | the report as text (the bridge's `import_solidcraft`) |
| `report_path` | also write the JSON report there |
| `expected` | a JSON file of values to check against: `body_count`, `total.volume_mm3`, `bbox`, `bodies[]` (by name: `volume_mm3`, `area_mm2` (a surface body's, mitcad#455), `bbox`), `timeline[].name`, `params[].name`, `sketches[]` (`curves`, `constraints`, `dimensions`), `parametric` (at least so many), `links` (the motion links that came in, exactly); SolidCraft's own `solidcraft-cli eval` output is such a file. Volumes within `volume_tolerance` (relative, 1e-3), boxes within `bbox_tolerance` (0.01 mm); every placed body counts unless `"scope": "root"` |
| `set_parameters` | `{"name": "expression"}`: parameters (the design's names) changed after the import, before the report measures the bodies |

The result has `file`, `design`, `format` (`solidcraft`), `items`,
`bodies`, `counts` (features `parametric`, `partial`, `unmapped`,
`failed`, `skipped`) and `report`: per feature its id, name, kind,
outcome, the MitCad features it became and notes; the parameters (the
design's expression and MitCad's, a renamed one's MitCad name); the
sketches with their points, curves and constraint and dimension counts
(the file's and those that came in) and what was left out; the joints;
the motion links (`links`: per link its number, name, coupling, outcome,
feature and notes); the bodies measured (volume, area, world box per placed body); the kinds
without a MitCad counterpart with their counts; notes; and `check` with
`expected`.

- Formats: any `solidcraft/N` (or the legacy `solvecraft/N`) up to 27 and
  the changes pending after it (28 with `format_pending`), upgraded first
  by SolidCraft's own steps (`third_party/solidcraft/format.rs`); a newer
  one is refused. The container (`solidcraft-container/1`: a zip of
  `container.json`, `document.json` and `blobs/`) is read with its STEP and
  mesh blobs.
- Parameters: user parameters, the model parameters of sketch dimensions
  and each feature input's parameter keep their names (a name MitCad
  reserves gets `_` appended) and their expressions in MitCad's language
  (`mitcad_solidcraft::expr`: SolidCraft's juxtaposed products, units as
  values, mixed numbers and decimal commas, `pi`, `log10`, `hypot`, `mod`,
  `trunc` and its signum `sign` translated). A dimension's or input's
  parameter is its slot's (`d3 = height`), owned by the MitCad feature;
  where MitCad's slot is a function of the file's value (a cylinder's
  diameter of its radius, a symmetric revolve's half angle) the file's
  parameter is a user parameter and the slot that function of it. Slots
  the file does not name get names of the import's own (`d<n>` past the
  file's), so that MitCad's names never collide with the file's.
- References: a face or edge is found by SolidCraft's persistent name
  where the import translates it (extrusion caps by their height over the
  sketch, sides by their sketch curve, box and cylinder faces, roundings
  and bevels, shell insides, pattern copies, a removed face's rim), the
  pick choosing among the faces the name means; else at the pick point
  (within 0.05 mm). Bodies by the file's names: a feature's new bodies are
  named as SolidCraft names them, the pieces a cut or split leaves
  `<name> (k)`, ordered so that the picks later features make on them by
  name lie on them.
- What maps to what: [core/import-solidcraft/docs/solidcraft.md](../../import-solidcraft/docs/solidcraft.md#solidcraft-import).
  Unmapped kinds and failed features become suppressed `placeholder`
  features with the reason as their import note ([The import's outcomes
  on the timeline](#the-imports-outcomes-on-the-timeline)).

Tests: `core.solidcraft` (the reader, formats and upgrades, the container),
`core.import` (`solidcraft::tests`, mock kernel), `cli.import_solidcraft`
(`tools/cli/solidcraft-test.cmake`: the hand-written test designs of
`core/solidcraft/tests/designs` against their worked-out values, a
parameter change, the container, the MCP open), `solidcraft.corpus`
(`MITCAD_SOLIDCRAFT_CORPUS`) and `tools/ui-import-test.sh`.

### .dwg import

`{"cmd": "import_dwg", "path": "drawing.dwg", …}` (C++ `Document::command`,
or `Document::import_dwg(path, json)` for the report alone) imports a
`.dwg` drawing's 3D content (mitcad#453; `core/ffi/src/dwg_import.rs`, the
reader is [core/dwg](../../dwg/README.md)), R13 to R2018. Bodies only:
a drawing keeps no history.

- **Bodies:** 3D solids, bodies, regions and surfaces with B-rep data,
  each converted by the `.f3d` reader's ASM code and built by the B-rep
  builder of the imports (one body per body of the record); 3D faces as
  one mesh body per block, layer and colour; polyface, polygon and
  subdivision meshes (the control mesh) as a mesh body each. Coordinates
  are drawing units scaled to millimetres (`$INSUNITS`; none: millimetres
  assumed, with a warning).
- **Components:** each named block with 3D content (in itself or its
  inserts) is a component named as the block, placed by an occurrence
  per insert (`MINSERT`: per cell), nested blocks in their blocks.
  Anonymous blocks, and inserts whose transform is not rigid (a scale or
  a mirror), are copied into the inserting component, the bodies moved by
  the transform (`Kernel::transform_shape`). A block that inserts itself
  is left out there with a warning.
- **Features:** the bodies of a component on one layer are one base
  feature named `Layer <name>` (in a component `<component> layer
  <name>`; feature names are unique), source `<file>, layer <name>`; bodies are
  named `Solid n`, `Mesh n` (the block's name when a component has one
  body) and coloured by the entity, its layer or the inserting entity
  (`BYBLOCK`; a block placed more than once takes its first insert's).
  The drawing's units become the document's when it was empty. One undo
  step.
- **Options:** `text` (the report as text), `report_path`, `expect` (data
  sheet values checked: `length_mm` the side of the bodies' box nearest
  to it, `chord_distance_mm` with `tube_diameter_mm` the nearest of the
  other sides, `tube_diameter_mm` and `tube_wall_mm` cylindrical faces of
  the outer and inner diameter, `mass_kg` the solids' volume times
  `density_kg_m3` (2700), `volume_mm3` the solids' volume, `solids`,
  `components`). Besides these, the checks are that every body built and
  is valid, every 3D entity was taken, a drawing with 3D entities gave
  bodies, and the bodies lie within the drawing's extents (when it has
  them: extents never computed are stored empty).
- **Report** (`report`): `version`, `units`, `drawing_units`, `unit_mm`,
  `units_assumed`, `extents` (`$EXTMIN`/`$EXTMAX`, mm), `bounds` (every
  placed body's box), `entities` and `taken` (by type), `left_out` (`type`,
  `count`, `why`: 2D entities, wires, entities without B-rep data, ...),
  `paper_space`, `objects`, `objects_failed`, `components` (`name`,
  `bodies`, `occurrences`, `placed` in all), `copied_inserts`, `bodies`,
  `solids`, `meshes`, `valid`, `solid_volume` (mm³, every placement),
  `cylinder_diameters`, `not_built`, `records` (each B-rep record's form:
  text, binary or binary from the data storage, and ASM version),
  `checks` (every body built and valid, the bounds within the extents,
  the `expect` values) and `pass`, `warnings`. The command's result:
  `file`, `bodies`, `components`, `report`.

Tests: `core.dwg` (the reader on drawings its tests write in every
version: header variables, classes, objects, data storage, both forms of
the B-rep record, the plan of components), `cli.import_dwg_<version>`
(the test drawing through OCCT) and `dwg.corpus` (`MITCAD_DWG_CORPUS`).

### The import's outcomes on the timeline

The importers that replay a history (the `.f3d` and `.ipt` imports,
FreeCAD documents) leave on the features they make what their report
says of them (mitcad#170): an **import note**, in the definition state
and the design file (a feature's `import_note`), so that a saved import
shows it when it is opened again.

- A fallback's base feature (`base` with `replaces`; one per component
  that changed) says which items it stands in for, each with the report's
  note as the reason: `Stands in for Extrude5 (its result is not in the
  file's history)`; items in a row with the same reason share it
  (`Stands in for Fillet2, Fillet3 (the import was stopped)`), and after
  eight the rest are counted (`and 37 more items (see the import
  report)`). A base feature the import added for another reason (the
  bodies brought to a history state exactly, the stored bodies at the
  end) has the report's warning about it.
- An item that came in partly (`partial`) has `Partly imported: ` and the
  report's note (`left out: 3 constraints ...`).
- An item skipped because it was suppressed or failed in the file (the
  `.f3d` import's `suppressed in the file`, `the file keeps no result for
  it ...`, `failed in the file: ...`; FreeCAD's `suppressed in FreeCAD`)
  becomes a **placeholder** at its place: `{"type": "placeholder",
  "item_type": "ExtrudeFeature"}`, suppressed, named after the item (when
  the name is free, else `Placeholder<n>`), its note the report's note.
  It builds nothing; unsuppressed, it warns that it builds nothing. Items
  skipped for having no geometry (occurrences, groups, relationships the
  import does not translate) get none.
- An `.f3d` item suppressed in the file whose definition translates
  (mitcad#180) comes in as that feature, suppressed, with the note
  `suppressed in the file; not checked against the file's history`;
  unsuppressed, it builds (status `warning` with the note until it is
  edited). Only where its definition does not come in is it a
  placeholder (`suppressed in the file; its definition did not come in:
  ...`). Suppressed sketches come in suppressed, their note ending
  `suppressed in the file`. A placeholder of an item the file suppressed
  only through an item it depends on ends `(suppressed through an item it
  depends on)`.
- An `.f3d` modelling item after the file's timeline marker (rolled back
  in the file) whose definition translates comes in as that
  feature after the marker (status `rolled_back`), with the note `rolled
  back in the file (after its timeline marker); not checked against the
  file's history`; the timeline marker is before the first such item.
  Where its definition does not come in it is a placeholder (`rolled back
  in the file (after its timeline marker); its definition did not come
  in: ...`).

A feature with a note has the status `warning` while it builds (the
note first in `error`, before its evaluation's warnings); a placeholder
stays `suppressed` with the note as its `error`; a failed feature shows
its error. The `timeline` and `feature` queries give the note as
`import`. A command that changes the feature's definition or one of its
dimensions (the parameters it owns) clears the note when the feature then
does not fail; renaming, suppressing and moving it do not, and undo
brings the note back. The report's texts are the source: the timeline's
notes are made from the report at the end of the import.

| Command (Rust, `Document`) | Fields | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `set_import_notes` | `[(uid, note)]` (an empty note removes it) | one undo step `Import notes`, no recompute |
| `add_import_placeholder` | `name`, `item_type`, `note`, `component` | the placeholder, suppressed with the note (`Add <name>`) |
| `import_note`, `import_notes` | `uid` | the note of a feature; every feature's |

Tests: `core.model` (`document::import_notes`: status, message, save
and reopen, an edit clearing the note), `core.import`
(`timeline_note_tests`: fallbacks, partial sketches and placeholders of an
`.f3d` design; `a_suppressed_feature_becomes_a_placeholder` and the
fallback's note of a FreeCAD Body), and
[tools/ui-import-status-test.sh](../../../tools/ui-import-status-test.sh).

### Mesh refinement

`export`'s `refinement` (STL, OBJ, 3MF, USDZ) is a preset or the
tolerances themselves (mitcad#398):

| Preset | Surface deviation | Angle between facet normals | Triangles a face at most (about) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `low` | 0.1 mm | 30° | 5 000 |
| `medium` (default) | 0.03 mm | 15° | 20 000 |
| `high` | 0.01 mm | 8° | 50 000 |

- A doubly curved face (a sphere's, a torus's, most freeform faces) that
  would get more triangles at the deviation meshes with a larger
  deviation instead, which grows with the face's size: about
  `0.8 × ∫√|K| dA / triangles` (K the Gaussian curvature; 1.1 mm for a
  sphere face of 4.5 m radius at `medium`). A dome of metres so exports
  in about as many triangles as one of centimetres; at an absolute
  0.03 mm, a 9 m dome took 1.5 million triangles and over a minute.
  Faces smaller than about 15 cm (the box's diagonal; a sphere up to
  about 50 mm radius), and planes and extrusions, whose triangle count
  does not grow with their size, mesh at the preset's deviation as
  before. Edges keep the deviation, so neighbouring faces still meet
  without gaps.
- A cylinder or a cone meshes at most as finely as a turn in
  `triangles / 40` straight pieces (mitcad#438: 125, 500 and 1 250 for
  the presets, 500 in the view; BRepMesh cuts an edge at half its
  deviation, so a circle gets about 1.4 times as many points):
  where the preset's deviation would cut a turn finer (radii over about
  0.3 m at `low`, 1.5 m at `medium`, 3 m at `high`, 0.5 m in the view),
  the face and the
  edges that bound it mesh with the deviation of such a piece, `R (1 −
  cos(π / pieces))` (2e-5 of the radius for 500), as their triangles are
  mostly their edges' points; an edge takes the smallest such floor of the
  faces it bounds (planes having no say, a doubly curved face its own
  floor, none when a face needs none) and no more than its own curve's,
  so it is shared by both faces as before and a small face beside a large
  cylinder (a bore's wall) meshes as without the bound.
- `{"deviation": mm, "angle": radians}` holds the deviation on every
  face, however large: the explicit absolute tolerance. `face_triangles`
  added to it bounds the faces as the presets do (`0`, the default when
  numbers are given: no bound). `max_edge` (mm; `0`, the default and the
  presets': none) is the longest edge a triangle of an STL, OBJ or 3MF
  file may have ([Mesh files](#mesh-files-in-a-unit-with-a-longest-edge)).
- `mitcad-cli export --refinement low|medium|high` takes a preset,
  `--deviation MM --angle DEG` the absolute tolerance.
- The 3D view meshes with the same algorithm: 0.01 mm and 5°, about
  20 000 triangles a face at most (`app/view/ViewTessellation.hpp`), on
  the model's worker thread after each job, all the bodies of the job
  together so that their faces are meshed in parallel on every core
  (`mesh_all_in_place`, mitcad#438; [architecture](../../../docs/architecture.md),
  Application).

Tests: `geometry.io` (`test_building_scale_sphere`: a 9 m dome's sphere
faces within the bound, its STL a few megabytes, a 9 cm dome meshed as
without the bound, meshing in place kept; `test_mesh_all_in_place`:
bodies meshed together as one by one, shared faces, kept meshes, cancel;
`test_building_scale_round_faces`: a tank's and a cone's floors and
counts with and without the bound, a small bore through the tank meshed
as without it, meshing in place kept),
`core.model` (`exchange_tests`: the presets' tolerances),
`app.view_tessellation` (the view's meshes of the dome, also meshed with
another body; `checkTank`: a tank's turn in the view, kept) and
[tools/ui-large-mesh-test.sh](../../../tools/ui-large-mesh-test.sh).

### Mesh files in a unit with a longest edge

The application's Save As Mesh (mitcad#734; a body's or a component's
context menu, [user guide](../../../docs/user-guide.md#save-as-mesh))
writes STL, OBJ and 3MF files with `export`; these are its options:

```json
{"cmd": "export", "path": "Bracket.3mf", "bodies": ["F2.b0"], "unit": "in",
 "refinement": {"deviation": 0.03, "angle": 0.26, "max_edge": 2}, "on_bed": true}
```

- **`unit`**: the numbers of the file in that unit, the bodies keeping
  their size: STL's vertices; a 3MF model's `unit` attribute (`inch`,
  `centimeter`, …) with its meshes and the placements' moves in it (the
  result's `meshes` volumes stay in mm³); OBJ by the kernel's writer
  (`geometry/io` `ObjWriteOptions::unit`). BRep and USDZ ignore it.
- **`max_edge`**: the model splits every edge longer than it at its
  middle after the kernel's meshing, round by round until none is longer
  (`core/model/src/exchange/edges.rs`): a triangle with one long edge
  becomes two, with two three, with three four, an edge split alike in both
  of its triangles. The new points lie on the triangles, so the mesh keeps
  its shape, deviation and volume, stays closed and faces outwards; only
  triangles are added. A body that would get more than 20 000 000
  triangles is refused (`Body1: the maximum edge length 0.001 mm would make
  more than 20000000 triangles`), and so is a negative length. OBJ with a
  longest edge (or on the bed) writes the model's meshes as mesh bodies
  (`Kernel::triangle_body`); without, the kernel meshes it as before.
- **`on_bed`** takes OBJ too: the bodies' placements turned and moved as
  for STL ([Print bed faces](#print-bed-faces)).
- **A file per body** is an `export` of each body alone (its `bodies` one
  uid, with the `occurrence` it was chosen in): each file one piece, so each
  body lies on its own print bed face.

Tests: `api::mesh_export_tests` (STL, 3MF and OBJ in a unit; a longest
edge in STL, 3MF and OBJ, kept shape and volume, refused; OBJ on the bed;
a file per body each on its own face), `exchange::edges` (splitting a box
and a sliver, too many triangles), `core.3mf` (a model in inches read back
in millimetres), `geometry.io` (`test_obj`: an OBJ file in centimetres),
`app.unit` (`save_as_mesh.cpp`), `tools/ui-save-as-mesh-test.sh` and
`tools/ui-windows-save-as-mesh-test.ps1`.

## Files and version history

### Design files

A design is one `.mitcad` file. The file format (version 2, a
single-file design; version 3, a design in a project; the B-rep store,
the per-user display state) is in
[docs/architecture.md](../../../docs/architecture.md#design-file).
What callers see:

- In a project (a folder with `.mitcad/project.json`, the nearest one
  above the file) a base feature body's `brep` refers to its data in the
  project's store: `{"format": "occt", "compression": "zlib", "size":
  6146, "sha256": "3fa9…e1"}`, the data in `.mitcad/brep/3f/3fa9…e1.brep.zlib`.
  A `brep` with `sha256` in a command is such a reference too.
- A reference whose data is missing or damaged stays a reference: its
  base feature fails (`body 0: its B-rep data … is missing from the
  project store (.mitcad/brep)`) and the `document` query's `warnings`
  say so. Saving a document with an unresolved reference keeps it, so
  even a single-file design is then version 3.
- Sizes are checked before data is inflated (mitcad#928): a `brep`
  whose `size` is above 512 MiB, or more than 64 times its zlib data
  plus 1 MiB, does not load (`B-rep size … is too large …`), nor does a
  file whose B-rep data adds up to more than 2 GiB; a store file of
