nothing yet (a session that left, or whose presence has not come: it
waits). A closing is given only for an entry that was given. When the
broker refuses the subscription to a session's presence, or the limit of
followed sessions is reached, its entries are given as they come.

`mitcad-cli live test <broker> [--prefix P] [--user U] [--ca FILE]
[--timeout S] [--json]` runs `test`, the password from
`MITCAD_MQTT_PASSWORD`. Tests: `core.vcs` (`remote::mqtt`: packets,
limits, payloads, the cleaning of text, a seeded random run of mutated
input, and scenarios against a broker in the test and against mosquitto
when it is installed: TLS with a certificate authority made with openssl,
the will (seen by a follower and by a newcomer), retained messages,
reconnecting, one connection for two
projects, a flood, a password refused over plain text), `core.bridge`,
`cli.live_*`; fuzz targets in `core/vcs/fuzz`.

### The project's id

| Command | Fields | Answer |
|---|---|---|
| `project_id` (a `Project` command) | | `project`: the first commit of HEAD's first-parent chain (hex), the same in every clone; null before the first version |

The application subscribes a Cloud project under it
(`app/files/LiveController.cpp`, [app/COMMANDS.md](../../../app/COMMANDS.md#live-updates)).
Test: `core/vcs/src/tests.rs`
(`the_project_id_is_the_first_commit_of_the_history`).

## Component libraries

Component libraries and the community library (mitcad#64, mitcad#63) are
git repositories of MitCad designs with a manifest; their format is in
[docs/libraries.md](../../../docs/libraries.md). The model knows no
git: it reads a library's component at a version through a
`LinkResolver` (`core/model/src/library.rs`), which `mitcad-vcs`
implements over the cache of fetched libraries
(`core/vcs/src/library/`). The bridge's `configure_libraries(json)` sets
the cache (`{"root"}`, default `MITCAD_LIBRARIES_DIR`, else the user's
data folder) and installs the resolver for every document; Rust code can
give a document its own (`Document::set_link_resolver`).

### Configuration tables

A design's table of sizes and options (`configurations` in the design
file, left out when empty) is described in
[Configurations](#configurations-options-rows-and-rules) (mitcad#797):
its options, open and closed tables, rows, rules, the cascade, the
`configure` command and query and `check_rules`. A library's design is
inserted in one of its rows (`config` below). A design written before
mitcad#798, whose table has `selectors`, opens as a closed table whose
options are text parameters made from the selectors.

### Library parts

`insert_component` with `library` instead of `path` inserts a library's
component: `{"id": "<library id>", "url": "<where it was fetched
from>", "rev": "<commit or tag>", "component": "<component id>",
"config": "<row>"}` (`config` left out: the table's default), with
`link`, `transform` and `name` as for files. The design is read at that
version, the row applied to a copy of its parameters, and:

- linked (default): its visible bodies in a base feature of a new,
  read-only component (one body is named after the designation), its link
  `path` the design's path in the library;
- a copy (`"link": false`): the design with its history in the row (the
  table is not copied), editable.

Either way the component records `library` (in the design file too):
`library` (id), `url`, `rev` (the commit, also for a tag), `label` (the
commit's tag), `component`, `path`, `config`, `license`, `authors` and
`designation` (`ISO 4762 M5x16`). The component is named after the
designation unless `name` is given; the undo step is `Insert <name>`.

- **Versions stay.** `update_links` (when a design opens) reads every
  linked library part at its recorded commit and takes new bodies only
  when that design or row differs from what was saved; a library or
  version that is not on this computer keeps the saved bodies with a
  message (`... library mitcad-fasteners v1.0.0 (3f9a2c1) (url) cannot
  be read (...); it keeps the bodies saved with the design`). Nothing
  follows a library's newest version on its own.
- **Updates are explicit.** `update_library_parts` with `changes`:
  [{`component` (uid or name), `rev` (another version), `config`
  (another row)}] changes linked parts as one undo step (`Update <name>
  to v1.1.0, M5x20` or `Update Library Parts`) and returns `changes`
  (`ISO 4762 M5x16: version v1.0.0 (3f9a2c1) -> v1.1.0 (7d0e5b2)`, `...
  size M5x16 -> M6x20`). A part named after its designation, and its
  body, take the new designation. A copied part is refused (it does not
  follow its library).
- The comparison of versions (`diff`) shows a part's changes field by
  field (`library.rev`, `library.config`, ...) and a table's changes row
  by row (`configuration M5x16: dk 8.5 mm -> 8.7 mm`).

| Query | Result |
|---|---|
| `library_parts` | `parts`: `component`, `name`, `linked`, `occurrences`, `library` (as recorded), `version` (`v1.0.0 (3f9a2c1)`) |
| `parts_list` | `rows`, one per component other than the root in the order they were made: `component`, `name`, `designation` (a library part's, else the name), `quantity` (how many times the design places it, through every occurrence of the components it is in), `linked`, `library`, `version`, `config`, `license`, `authors`, `url` (with `properties`, a list of keys `Key` or `Set/Key`: each row's `properties`, the text of each key's value or null; [Properties](#properties)) |

### Library commands

Commands of the cache of libraries, not of a document: the bridge's
`library_command(json, control)` (a fetch reports its progress to the
`SyncControl` and stops when it is cancelled) and `describe_library` (the
answer as text); `mitcad-cli library`. A fetch's failure is an answer
with `error` (`class`, `message`, `detail`, as the remote commands') and
`log`; other failures are errors.

| Command | Fields | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `library_fetch` | `url` (https, ssh, a file:// URL or a folder; never with credentials) | `kind` (`library`, `index`), `id`, `name`, `url`, `dir`, `cloned`, `head`, `versions`, `problems` (`errors`, `warnings`), `error`, `log`: a bare clone into the cache (`git clone --bare`), or new branches and tags fetched into it; a repository that is neither, or larger than 200 MB, is refused and leaves nothing. An update that would make the clone larger than 200 MB is `too_large` and is not taken: its references (fetched to `refs/incoming/` first) and new object files are removed, the versions fetched before stay (mitcad#938) |
| `library_list` | | `root`, `libraries`: `dir`, `url`, `kind`, `versions`, and a library's `id`, `name`, `description`, `license`, `authors`, `components` (count), `problems`, an index's `name`, `entries` |
| `library_show` | `url` or `id`, `rev` (default: the newest version) | `dir`, `url`, `rev`, `labels`, `versions`; a library's `manifest`, `problems` and `components` (`id`, `name`, `path`, `category` (its home category), `categories` (every one, the home first), `groups` (per category `{"category", "path", "order"}`: the group's names from the top and each name's place in the manifest's list, [Groups](../../../docs/libraries.md#groups), mitcad#527), `standard`, `description`, `keywords`, `license`, `license_note`, `preview`, `designation`, `supplier`, `part_number`, `supplier_url`, `build` (as the manifest has it, or null), `mounts` (likewise, mitcad#525), `configurations`: `selectors`, `selector_values`, `default`, `rows` with `name`, `select` and, when the row has them, its own `part_number`, `supplier_url` and `designation`); an index's `name`, `description`, `entries` |

| `library_diff` | `id`, `url`, `from`, `to`, `parts` ([{`component`, `config`}]) | `from`, `to` (commits), `from_labels`, `to_labels`, `library` (licence and version changes), `parts`: `changed`, `missing` (the component or row is not in `to`), `lines` (the row's value changes), `text`, `design` (the comparison of the design without its table) |
| `library_check` | `dir` (a library folder) | `id`, `components`, `ok`, `errors`, `warnings`: the manifest, the files it names (there, no symbolic links, designs that open and link no other files, PNG previews of at most 512 KB), a licence file; for BUILD parts the block's rules ([BUILD parts](../../../docs/libraries.md#build-parts)), the design's parameters and `mount:<name>` joint origins, a profile's layout, and library references that resolve (in the folder, else in the fetched libraries; one not fetched is a warning); a component's `mounts` against its rules and the design's mount frames ([Mount frames](../../../docs/libraries.md#mount-frames)) |

### Standards and suppliers of library rows

A library's manifest may name each configuration row's standards and the
suppliers' articles of it (mitcad#949; the format is in
[docs/libraries.md](../../../docs/libraries.md#standards-and-suppliers-of-rows)):
the component's `rows` (`{"M6x8": {"standards": ["DIN 912"],
"supplier_parts": [{"supplier", "part_number", "material", "finish",
"checked"}]}}`) and the library's `suppliers` (`[{"id", "name", "url"}]`).
A library without them answers as before.

- **`library_show`**: each row of a component's `configurations.rows`
  has its `standards` and `supplier_parts` (each with `supplier_name`, the
  supplier's name from `suppliers`) when the manifest gives them; a
  component has `standards` (the standards its rows name, those of its
  `standard` first in that order, `non-standard` last) and `suppliers`
  (`[{"id", "name", "url"}]` with articles on its rows). The `manifest`
  has `suppliers` and `replaces`.
- **`library_configure`** takes `standard` (the Standard filter's: `DIN
  912`): the `designation` of a row that names it is `DIN 912 M6x10`;
  without it, or for a row without that standard, the row's first; a row
  tagged `non-standard` is `M6x6 (non-standard)`. The answer adds
  `rows` (each row's `name`, `select`, `standards`, `supplier_parts`),
  `standard` (the standard the combination's row is named by, or null)
  and `supplier_parts` (that row's).
- **`library_search`**: a component's `standards` and `suppliers` as
  above; `supplier` also finds a component whose rows a supplier sells
  (its id or name), `part_number` a supplier's article number. With
  `sources` (the enabled sources' URLs), a library an index offers, or a
  fetched clone of one, is left out when an enabled source has its
  repository under another id (the same URL, or the source's clone has
  its newest commit or a version the index reviewed) or when a fetched
  library's `replaces` names its id; `left_out` lists them (`id`, `url`,
  `reason`, `text`: `mitcad-fasteners left out: same repository as
  https://github.com/mitcad/parts.git`). Without `sources` every fetched
  library counts as a source.
- **`library_check`** refuses an article whose `supplier` is not one of
  the library's `suppliers`, a `checked` that is no date (`YYYY-MM-DD`),
  an article without a part number, a supplier without an id or a name,
  and a row name the design's table lacks.
- **`insert_component`** takes the library's `standard` (`{"id", "url",
  "rev", "component", "config", "standard": "DIN 912"}`): the part is
  named by it when its row has it. The component's `library` records
  `standard` (the standard it is named by) and `supplier_parts` (its
  row's articles, with the suppliers' names); `update_library_parts`
  keeps the standard where the new row has it.
- **`parts_list`**: each row adds `supplier_parts` and
  `supplier_parts_text` (`Würth 0084 6 8 (8.8 zinc-plated); …`, the
  parts lists' "Supplier part numbers" column).

A part with options (inserted with `parameters`) is named by its
component's `standard` as before.

Tests: `core/vcs/src/tests/library_rows.rs` (the manifest read and
checked, `library_show`, `library_configure` with `standard`,
`library_search` by supplier, the index's library left out),
`core/model-tests/links/src/library_tests.rs`
(`library_parts_follow_the_rows_standards_and_list_supplier_parts`,
`library_parts_without_row_blocks_read_as_before`) and
`core/model/src/library.rs` (the designation).

## Configurations: options, rows and rules

A configurable design stands for a family of products (mitcad#797; the
design note is [docs/configurations.md](../../../docs/configurations.md)).
The user picks a value for each **option** (Color, Length, Size), **rules**
remove the values and combinations that are not allowed, and named
**rows** are presets of option values. A configuration only ever sets
parameters. The model is `core/model-base/src/configurations.rs` (the
table, the rules and the cascade, without a kernel) and
`core/model/src/document/configurations.rs` (the commands); the api is
`core/model-api/src/configurations.rs`.

### The table

`configurations` in the design file and in `set_configurations`:

| Field | |
|---|---|
| `options` | names of user parameters, in choice order: the order in which the cascade repairs them and the choosers show them |
| `closed` | default false. An **open** table allows every combination the rules allow; a **closed** table allows only its rows' combinations |
| `parameters` | other parameters the rows set (a closed table only, as tables did before mitcad#798) |
| `default` | a row's name; the first row when left out |
| `rows` | presets: `name` (unique; what `apply_configuration`, `library.config`, BUILD's `build.rows` and `derived_part.config` name), `values` ({parameter: expression}: the options' constants and a closed table's `parameters`), and optional `designation`, `part_number`, `supplier_url` |
| `rules` | see [Rules](#rules) (mitcad#799) |

- **Options.** An option is a user parameter. Its expression is a
  constant (`'Black'`, `1200 mm`, `1`); choosing a value writes that
  constant. An option whose expression is a formula is **driven**: it is
  shown as driven, it is never moved, and a rule it breaks refuses the
  change that made it so.
- **Domain.** What an option can be before rules: a **list** (its
  parameter's `values` limit, [Allowed values](#allowed-values)), else a
  **range** (its `min`, `max` and `step`, [Parameter
  limits](#parameter-limits)), else **free**.
- **Rows.** In an open table a row sets options only; an option a row
  leaves out keeps its value. In a closed table each row gives every
  option a value, and no two rows the same combination. A row's option
  values are constants.
- **The row of a combination.** The row whose option values the
  parameters have (all its values in a table without options) is the
  combination's row; it gives the designation, the part
  number and the supplier URL. Any other combination of an open table
  takes the library's designation pattern with the option values in
  braces (`ISO 4762 M{Size}x{Length}`: a text option's text, a number
  option's number in its unit without the unit, `16`), as BUILD writes
  `{L}`. A closed table refuses a combination that is no row, and a
  command that chooses its options (`configure`, `set_parameter` of an
  option, the cascade) also sets the row's other `parameters`, except
  those the command sets itself.
- **Problems** (`problems` of the queries; `set_configurations` and
  opening a file refuse the table with the first): an option or parameter
  that does not exist, is not a user parameter, or is listed twice; a
  parameter that is both; an option of an open table among `parameters`
  of rows (an open table's rows set options only); a row without a name,
  two rows with the same name, a value for a parameter not in the table, a
  row option value that is not a constant, a closed table's row without a
  value for an option (`A: no value for Size`), two rows of a closed table
  with the same combination (`B: another row has the same Size and
  Length`), a value its parameter refuses (unit, cycle, syntax, a strict
  limit: `A: d = 1 deg: …`), a default that is no row, and the rules'
  problems ([Rules](#rules)).
- **Old tables.** A table with `selectors` (before mitcad#798) opens as a
  closed table: each selector becomes a text parameter of its name (the
  next free name, `Size2`, when a parameter already has it, with a
  warning), each row's `select` becomes its values of those options (as
  texts: `"Size": "'M5'"`), and the new options take the values of the
  row the parameters have (else of the default row). Row names, the
  default, `parameters` and their values stay. An old table without
  selectors (its rows chosen by name) is closed too: a table with
  `parameters` and no `options` is always read as closed. The file is written in the
  new form from then on; `set_configurations` reads the old form the same
  way (the new parameters and the table are one undo step).

### Allowed values

`values` is a parameter limit next to `min`, `max` and `step`
(mitcad#798), on any parameter: a list of expressions in the parameter's
unit (`["'Black'", "'White'"]`, `["300 mm", "500 mm", "800 mm"]`; they may
use other parameters, which then take part in the dependency order like
the other limits).

- A **number** whose result is not in the list snaps to the nearest
  listed value (the lower one of two as near), and `limited` is `values`
  (`Length is limited to its allowed value 500 mm (its expression gives
  520 mm)`); a **strict** parameter refuses it instead (`parameter
  'Length': 520 mm is not one of its allowed values 300 mm, 500 mm, 800
  mm`). With `min`, `max` or `step` as well, the result is clamped and
  snapped first, then snapped to the list.
- A **text** whose result is not in the list is always refused (`parameter
  'Color': 'Green' is not one of its allowed values 'Black', 'White'`): a
  text has no nearest value. `values` is the only limit a text parameter
  can have.
- `add_parameter` and `set_parameter` take `values` as a list of
  expression texts or numbers (in the parameter's unit); `null` or `[]`
  removes it in `set_parameter`. The `parameters` query's `limits` has
  `values` (as written, or null), `values_value` (evaluated: mm or rad for
  a number, the texts for a text) and `values_text` (`["300 mm", …]`).
  The design file stores `values` with the parameter; undo, copies and
  renames treat it as the other limits; the parameters CSV has a `values`
  column (the list as a JSON array of expression texts, `["300
  mm","500 mm"]`; empty for none).

### Rules

`rules` of the table (mitcad#799): each rule has `name` (unique),
`enabled` (default true), an optional `comment`, an optional `when` (a
condition in the expression language, true when left out), `then` and an
optional `else` (lists of actions).

```json
"rules": [
  {"name": "Black is short", "when": "Color == 'Black'",
   "then": [{"option": "Length", "max": "1000 mm"}]},
  {"name": "Power needs tables", "when": "Tables == 0",
   "then": [{"option": "Power", "values": ["0"]}]},
  {"name": "No red XL", "when": "and(Color == 'Red'; Size == 'XL')",
   "then": [{"forbid": "Red is not made in XL"}]},
  {"name": "Deep enough", "then": [{"require": "Depth >= Length / 4",
   "message": "the shelf is too shallow for its length"}]}
]
```

- **Conditions** (`when`, `require`) are expressions of the language of
  [Values](#values) that give a number: zero is false, anything else
  true (`==`, `<>`, `<`, `and`, `or`, `not`, `if`, text comparison; a
  condition is read in parentheses, so a single `=` compares too:
  `Color = 'Black'`). They may use any parameter. A condition that does not evaluate is a problem
  of the table.
- **Actions**:
  - `{"option": "Length", "values": [...]}` allows only these values, and
    `{"option": "Color", "exclude": [...]}` not these (expressions in the
    option's unit; a text option's are texts);
  - `{"option": "Length", "min": "…", "max": "…", "step": "…"}` restricts
    a number option's range (any of the three; expressions in its unit;
    they may be given with `values` or `exclude` in one action);
  - `{"require": "<condition>", "message": "…"}` and `{"forbid":
    "<message>"}` reject the combination.
  - `{"in_table": "Made", "columns": {"Color": "Color"}}` requires
    the combination to be a row of a table: [Configurations and
    tables](#configurations-and-tables) (mitcad#806).
- **Rules only narrow.** An option's allowed values are its domain
  intersected with every active restriction (the actions of the `then` of
  each enabled rule whose `when` holds, and of the `else` of each whose
  `when` does not). Their order does not matter, and a rule never sets a
  computed parameter. When an intersection is empty, the problem names the
  rules (`Black is short and Long only leave Length no value`).
- **Rules do not take part in evaluation.** They check the evaluated
  parameters and change only the constants of options. They add no
  dependency edges, so they cannot form a cycle: two rules may point in
  opposite directions (Color restricts Length, and Length restricts
  Color).
- **Renames and deletes.** Renaming a parameter rewrites the rules'
  conditions and action expressions and `option` names; a parameter that
  a rule uses cannot be deleted (`parameter 'Wall' is used by the rule
  Thick walls`), nor an option or a row's parameter (`configurations:
  option Color of the table does not exist`, as before mitcad#799). The
  rules are checked first: an option that a rule uses is refused with the
  rule's name. The
  `parameters` query gives each parameter `option` (true for an option of
  the table) and `rules` (the names of the rules that use it).

**Rule problems:** a rule without a name, two rules of one name, an
action of no kind or of two (`values` with `require`), an option that is
not an option of the table, a range action on a text option, a step
that is not positive, an expression that does not parse or evaluate. An
empty intersection depends on the values: it is a broken rule (the
`configure` query's `problems`, a refusal), not a problem of the table.

### The cascade

After every change of parameters (`set_parameter`, `apply_configuration`,
`configure`, the parameters CSV import, `set_configurations`, and so MCP
and the CLI, which send those commands), the model goes through the
options in order:

1. An option keeps its value when it is allowed.
2. Otherwise it **moves**: a number with a range to the nearest allowed
   value by the step rule of [Parameter limits](#parameter-limits); a list
   to the nearest listed value (a number), else to the default row's value
   when it is allowed, else to the first allowed value; a single allowed
   value is chosen by itself.
3. An option the change itself set, an option before the first of those
   (only the later options move; all may when the change set no option),
   and a driven option, is never moved.

When every rule then holds, the change and the moves are **one undo
step**, and the answer lists the moves: `moves`, a list of `option`,
`from` and `to` (the values as text, `1500 mm`, `Black`),
`from_expression`, `to_expression` and `rule` (the rule that moved it),
and `text` (`Length 1500 mm → 1000 mm: Black is short`). When a rule that
held before the change is broken after it (a `require`, a `forbid`, a
restriction of an option the change set or of a driven one, a closed
table's combination that is no row), the change is **refused** with the
rule's name and message (`the rule Black is short: does not allow Length
= 1500 mm`, `the rule No red XL: Red is not made in XL`, `the
configuration table is closed: Size M6 and Length 99 is no row`), and
nothing changes. A rule already broken before the change (a file opened
so, a table just edited) does not refuse it: the `configure` query
reports it.

`set_parameter`, `apply_configuration` and `import_parameters_csv` add
`moves` to their answers (left out when empty for the first and the
last). Rust: `Document::configuration_moves()` gives the moves of the
last command.

### Commands and queries

| Command | Fields | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `set_configurations` | `configurations` (the table, new or old form; null or an empty table removes it) | `rows` (count), `options` (names, after any migration), `added` (parameters the migration made), `warnings`; refused with the first problem; undo step `Edit Configurations` |
| `apply_configuration` | `name` (a row) | `changed` (parameters whose values changed), `moves`; undo step `Apply M5x16` |
| `configure` | `values` ({option: value}, any of the options) | `changed`, `moves`, `row` (the combination's row or null), `refused` (null, or `{"rule", "message", "text"}` when the cascade cannot repair the change: then nothing changed); undo step `Configure Color = Black` (`Configure Color = Black, Length = 800 mm` for more) |

A **value** in `configure` and in the `configure` query is a text
option's text (`"Black"`), or for a number option a number in mm or rad
(as `set_parameter`'s `value`) or a constant expression (`"800 mm"`);
`configure` writes the constant (`'Black'`, `800 mm`). An expression with
parameter references, a driven option and a parameter that is no option
are refused.

| Query | Fields | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `configurations` | | `configurations` (the table or null), `selector_values` ({option: the rows' values as texts in natural order: `M2.5`, `M3`, `M10`}), `current` (the row the parameters have, or null), `problems` |
| `configure` | `values` (optional: values to try, as `configure`'s; nothing changes) | `options` (each option in order, after the cascade of `values`: `name`, `kind` (`number` or `text`), `unit`, `value` (mm or rad, or the text), `text`, `expression`, `driven`, `domain`, `allowed`, `restricted_by` (the rules that narrow it now)), `row` (the combination's row, or null), `designation_values` ({option: text} as a designation pattern takes them), `moves`, `refused` (as `configure`'s), `problems` |
| `check_rules` | `limit` (optional, default 100000) | the report below |

`domain` and `allowed` are `{"kind": "list", "values": [{"value",
"text", "expression"}, …]}`, `{"kind": "range", "min", "max", "step"}`
(mm or rad, or null, with `min_text`, `max_text`, `step_text`) or
`{"kind": "free"}`. For a list each value is tested through the cascade
from it: it is allowed when the cascade from it, given the options before
it, ends with no broken rule. A range is the intersection of the active
`min`, `max` and `step`. A closed table's allowed values are those of its
rows that match the options before. Every chooser uses this query (the
Configurations window, the active configuration bar, the part pickers,
MCP); the final check of a whole combination is always exact.

**Check Rules** (`check_rules`) goes through every combination of the
options' finite domains (lists, and ranges with a step, a minimum and a
maximum) up to `limit` combinations; above it, it samples `limit` of them
evenly and says so. The report: `combinations` (how many there are, or
null when a domain is not finite), `checked`, `sampled`, `never_allowed`
([{`option`, `text`}]: values the cascade never keeps), `never_applies`
(rules whose `when` never holds), `empty` ([{`option`, `rules`,
`values`}]: combinations of earlier options that leave an option no
value), `rows` ([{`row`, `rule`, `message`}]: rows that break a rule),
`unrepairable` ([{`values`, `rule`, `message`}], at most 20: combinations
the cascade cannot repair), `problems` and `lines` (the report in words).

Rust (for the application's and the inserted components' use,
mitcad#801, #807): `mitcad_model::configurations::{Configurations,
ConfigurationRow, ConfigurationRule, RuleAction, OptionValue,
ConfigurationMove, RuleViolation, Cascade, Domain, DomainValue,
OptionReport, RulesReport, cascade}`; `Document::{configurations,
set_configurations, apply_configuration, configure, configure_report,
check_rules, configuration_moves}`.

Tests: `core/model-tests/api/src/configurations_tests.rs` (`values` on
numbers and texts with save, load, undo, renames and the CSV; the
`configure` query on list, range and driven options; `configure`; open
and closed tables; an old table opened and written new; the design
note's rules and moves, opposite rules, an empty intersection, refusals
of `set_parameter`, driven options and the CSV, renames and deletes,
Check Rules), `expr::limits::tests` (snapping to the allowed values),
`library::tests` (the designation of a combination that is no row),
`core/model-tests/links/src/library_tests.rs` (old tables through
`set_configurations` and library parts).

## Options of inserted components

A library part, a linked design and a BUILD part have options of their
own (mitcad#801; [docs/configurations.md](../../../docs/configurations.md),
"Inserted components", decisions 8 and 11): `parameters`, values of the
source's options (and other user parameters), each an expression of
**this** design's parameters. The model is
`core/model/src/part_options.rs` (the source's rules, the combination,
the choosers' JSON) and `core/model/src/document/component_options.rs`
(the commands).

```json
{"cmd": "insert_component",
 "library": {"id": "shelves", "url": "...", "rev": "v1.0.0", "component": "shelf-board", "config": "Standard"},
 "parameters": {"Length": "Shelf_W - 2 * Wall", "Color": "Color"}}
```

- **How it is made.** A component inserted with `parameters` (with
  `library` or with `path`, linked; a copy has the design's own
  parameters and is refused) is made by a `derived_part` feature, the
  feature BUILD's parts have: the design keeps the source's design in
  `library_sources` (a linked file's as a source with an empty `library`
  and its `path`), and the part evaluates it in the row `config` (else the
  default row) with the `parameters` at recompute. A change of a parameter
  the values use recomputes that part only; the design needs no library to
  open. The component is linked (read only, `link.feature` is the derived
  part) and has the source's mount frames as joint origins on the part's
  frames (`F7:mount(name)`), so that they follow its options;
  `insert_component` with `parameters: {}` gives a component that can take
  options later. `derived_part.parameters` is the same field: a value may
  be a number (mm or rad), a text (a text option's, `'Black'`) or any
  expression, in the source's parameter's unit.
- **Options belong to the component.** All of its occurrences share them;
  a second configuration is a second component (both use one source).
- **The source's rules hold.** A **bound** value (its expression names
  this design's parameters, or it is one) is never moved; a **constant**
  is. The cascade runs when the options are set (insert,
  `set_component_parameters`, `update_library_parts`, `update_links`):
  the constants it moves are written into the part and listed in `moves`
  (`option`, `from`, `to`, `from_expression`, `to_expression`, `rule`,
  `text`: `Length 1500 mm → 1000 mm: Black is short`). When a bound value
  breaks a rule, the part fails with the rule (`the rule Black is short:
  …`): the component has the error status of a failed feature, the answers
  give it as `refused` (`rule`, `message`, `text`), and the design's own
  change (`set_parameter` of the bound parameter) goes through. A constant
  that a later change of a bound value no longer allows is moved in the
  evaluation, with a warning on the part.
- **Parts list and designation.** A library part's record (`library`:
  `config`, `designation`, `part_number`, `supplier_url`) follows its
  combination: the row whose option values it has (the row it starts from
  first) gives its own designation, part number and page; any other
  combination takes the library's pattern with the option values in
  braces (`Board {Color} {Length}` → `Board Black 800`), else the name and
  standard followed by the option values. A component whose name was its
  designation is renamed with it. A BUILD part's designation is BUILD's,
  with its options and `{L}`.

| Command | Fields | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `insert_component` | `parameters` ({option: expression or number}) beside `path` or `library` | as without, plus `moves` and `refused` |
| `set_component_parameters` | `component`, `parameters` ({option: expression or number; null removes the component's own value, so the row's holds}), `config` (another row to start from; not for a BUILD part, whose row is `build_edit`'s) | `component`, `name`, `part`, `moves`, `refused` and the component's options as `library_parts` gives them; undo step `Change Options of Shelf board` |
| `update_library_parts` | a part with options: its `rev` and `config` as for other parts (parts with and without options are changed apart) | `changes` |
| `build_place` | `part.parameters` ({option: expression}) beside `part.config`; the command's own `parameters` win for a name in both, and the cut length is `length`'s | as without |

| Query | Fields | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `configure` | `component` (an inserted component or a BUILD part) and optional `parameters` (values to try, by option, as `set_component_parameters` takes them) | the `configure` answer (`options`, `row`, `designation_values`, `moves`, `refused`, `problems`) for that component's source with its values, and `designation`; its bound options are `driven` and have `bound` true and `parameter` (the expression). The tried constants may move; nothing changes |
| `library_parts`, `parts_list` | | a component with options has `options`: `part`, `source`, `config`, `parameters` (its values as written: the part's own expression, or the name of the design's parameter), `row`, `designation`, `error` (the rule a bound value breaks, or why the source cannot be made; null) and `options` (as the `configure` query's) |

Library commands (`core/vcs/src/library/api.rs`, [Library
commands](#library-commands)):

| Command | Fields | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `library_show`, `library_build_candidates` | | a component whose design has options also has `options` (as the `configure` query's, in its default row): a chooser per option for the pickers |
| `library_configure` | `url` or `id`, `rev` (default the newest version), `component`, `config` (default the default row), `values` ({option: a text option's text, a number in mm or rad, or a constant expression}) | the `configure` answer on the component's design with the values tried, and `designation`, `component`, `library`, `rev`: what Insert from Library and the BUILD pickers show before inserting. A value tried is not moved; one that breaks a rule is `refused`, and the later options move |

Rust: `mitcad_model::part_options::{PartValue, OptionMove, BrokenRule,
ConfiguredSource, Naming, Combination, configure, configure_state,
combination, options_json, configure_json, command_value, is_bound,
part_values}`; `Document::{set_component_parameters, component_options,
component_configure_json}` with `OptionsChange`, `OptionsChanged` and
`ComponentOptions`; `InsertOptions::parameters`.

Tests: `core/model-tests/links/src/component_options_tests.rs` (library
parts bound and constant, the cascade's moves, a bound value that breaks
a rule, two components of one source, the parts list's designation, the
`configure` query, a linked design with options) and
`core/model-tests/build-frames/src/options_tests.rs` (a BUILD part's cut
length through `parameters`).
## Configurations and tables

The design's tables ([Tables](#tables), mitcad#803) meet its
configurations in three places (mitcad#806; the design note is
[docs/configurations.md](../../../docs/configurations.md), "Tables and
configurations"). Otherwise they stay separate: a row sets a key, and
lookups (`XLOOKUP(Size; Screws.Size; Screws.dk)`) do the rest.

**Option values from a column.** A parameter's `values` limit
([Allowed values](#allowed-values)) can be a table column instead of a
list: `"values": "Screws.Size"` in `add_parameter`, `set_parameter`, the
`parameters` query and the design file (which also reads the list of that
one entry, `["Screws.Size"]`; a column is a whole list, never mixed with
listed values).

- The domain is the column's distinct non-empty cells, in the table's
  order (`values_value`, `values_text` and the `configure` query's
  `domain` list them). A text option takes a text column; a number option
  a number column of its dimension (an `in` column gives `0.25 in`, the
  cell kept exact) or a unitless one, whose numbers are in the option's
  unit (`16` in an option in mm is `16 mm`). Another kind is a problem
  (`Screws.Size is a text column, and option Length is a number`).
- **A table edit** (`set_table`, a CSV import) that takes an option's
  value out of its column moves the option before the parameters are
  evaluated with the new table: to the nearest value for a number (the
  lower of two as near), else to the default row's value when the column
  still has it, else to the column's first value. The cascade then runs as
  after any change, and `set_table`'s answer lists every move in `moves`
  (`Size M7 → M6: its allowed values Screws.Size`), and so does
  `import_table_csv`'s (mitcad#849; Rust:
  `Document::configuration_moves`). A driven
  option is not moved: the edit is refused when its value would fail, as
  for any parameter. The edit and the moves are one undo step.
- A column as allowed values makes its parameter a user of the table
  (`used_by` of the `tables` query): a table or column rename rewrites
  the reference, and deleting the table is refused while an option's
  values or a rule (`in_table`, a list of its column) uses it (`table
  Made is used by the rule Made sizes`).

**Combinations in a table.** The rule action `in_table` requires the
values of some options to be a row of a table:

```json
{"name": "Made sizes",
 "then": [{"in_table": "Made", "columns": {"Color": "Color", "Length": "Length"}}]}
```

- `columns` maps options (keys) to columns of the table (values); each
  option's column is of its kind, as above. An action with `in_table` has
  no other kind of action.
- For the choosers and the cascade, each mapped option is narrowed to its
  column's cells in the rows that match the mapped options before it in
  option order (the first is narrowed by none): with `Color = 'Black'`,
  `Length` may be only the lengths of the Black rows. A row with an empty
  cell in a mapped column takes part in nothing.
- The final check is exact: the combination of every mapped option must
  be a row. A change that leaves it none is refused with the rule's name
  (`the rule Made sizes: Color Black and Length 1200 mm is no row of
  Made`), as a `forbid` is.
- Renaming an option renames its key; renaming the table or a column
  rewrites the action. `rules` of the `parameters` query names the rule
  for each mapped option.

**Rows generated from a table.**

| Command | Fields | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `generate_configuration_rows` | `table`, `column`, `option` (a user parameter) | `rows` (the rows of the column's keys, in the table's order), `added`, `updated` (row names), `moves`; undo step `Generate Rows from Screws`, nothing recomputed |

One row per distinct non-empty key of the column, named by the key (a
text's text, `M5`; a number in its column's unit without the unit, `16`),
whose `values` set the option to it (`'M5'`, `16 mm`). A row of the same
name is updated, not duplicated: it keeps its other values, designation,
part number and supplier URL, and is listed in `updated` only when its
value changed. The option becomes an option of the table when it is not
one. Refused when the option is not a user parameter or is one of a
closed table's other `parameters`, when the column cannot give it values,
when the column has none, and with the table's first problem afterwards
(a closed table's new row without a value for another option).

Rust: `mitcad_model::configurations::{TableColumns, TableColumn, Cell,
InTable, GeneratedRows, ColumnMove, column_domain, column_reference,
values_column, tables_of, columns_of}` (`tables_of` reads the tables the
parameters evaluate with), `Configurations::{generate_rows, in_table_allowed,
in_table_violation, in_table_problems, column_moves, table_users,
rename_table, rename_table_column}`; `Document::generate_configuration_rows`.

Tests: `core/model-base/src/configurations/from_tables.rs` (column
domains, `in_table`, generated rows, moves) and
`core/model-tests/api/src/configuration_tables_tests.rs` (the commands
with tables; `import_table_csv`'s moves).

## Progress and cancellation

A document can be given a `RecomputeMonitor` (`Document::set_monitor`,
`core/model-base/src/monitor.rs`), shared with another thread that shows the
progress and may cancel. Every recompute then reports to it and checks
for a cancel before each feature before the marker. The bridge gives it
to C++ as a `JobControl` (`core/ffi/src/jobs.rs`). Threading and the
application's worker:
[docs/architecture.md](../../../docs/architecture.md#application).

| Rust | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `RecomputeMonitor::cancel()`, `is_cancelled()` | ask the computation to stop; it stops before the next feature, or when the evaluation running now returns, which the kernel's long operations cut short. A monitor stays cancelled: a new job takes a new one |
| `progress()` | `position` (the features before the one computed, shown as `position + 1` of `total`; `total` when done), `total` (features before the marker), `evaluated` (evaluations kept in the cache so far, in all recomputes of the job), `feature` (the name of the feature evaluated last; a cache hit leaves it), `cancelled` |
| `set_test_delay(ms)` | for tests: each evaluation takes `ms` longer, in 10 ms steps that end on a cancel |
| `cancel_after(n)` | for tests: cancel once `n` evaluations were kept, as between two features |
| `ask(question)`, `question()`, `answer(answer)`, `take_answer()` | a question the job puts to its user (one line; the `.f3d` import's `retry_bodies` `ask`, mitcad#283): the thread that shows the progress finds it with `question()` until it answers; the job takes the answer once. A new question drops an answer not taken |
| `Document::try_recompute`, `try_undo`, `try_redo` | fail with `ModelError::Cancelled`; `recompute`, `undo` and `redo` stay for callers without a monitor (a cancelled `undo` gives None, a cancelled `recompute` keeps the last results) |

| C++ (`mitcad_bridge/lib.h`) | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `new_job_control()` | a `rust::Box<JobControl>`, one per job |
| `JobControl::cancel()`, `is_cancelled()`, `set_test_delay(ms)` | as the monitor's; both threads may call them at once |
| `JobControl::progress()` | a `JobProgress {position, total, evaluated, feature, cancelled}` |
| `JobControl::question()`, `answer(text)` | the job's question waiting for an answer (empty when none) and the answer (`keep` or `replace` for the `.f3d` import's) |
| `Document::attach_job(control)`, `detach_job()` | the document's recomputes report to the control until detached |

- A cancelled computation rejects what ran it with `the computation was
  cancelled` (`Cancelled::MESSAGE`, `ModelError::Cancelled`): a command
  (`recompute`, `undo` and `redo` too), a `preview`, the `update_links`
  of an opened design. The document stays as it was: the definition
  state, the undo and redo steps, the revision, the results of the last
  recompute and `recompute_count`. The exception is `import_f3d` with the
  timeline, which a cancel stops early with what it imported ([.f3d
  import with the timeline](#f3d-import-with-the-timeline)).
- A cancelled preview leaves no preview (`preview_body_shape` is null).
- An array of commands stops at the cancelled one as at any error
  (`commands[2]: the computation was cancelled`); the commands before it
  stay done.
- Results evaluated before the cancel stay in the cache, so trying again
  continues where it stopped. An evaluation that returns after the
  cancel request is not cached.
- Inside an evaluation: a recompute with a monitor runs each evaluation
  through `Kernel::interruptible(monitor, ...)`. The OCCT kernel
  (`core/ffi/src/kernel/cancel.rs`) gives the geometry the monitor as its
  `CancelSource` (`geometry/include/mitcad/geometry/cancel.hpp`) for the
  evaluation's thread; booleans, fillets and chamfers, sweeps, lofts,
  shells and offsets, drafts, splits and sewing run with a progress range
  whose user break asks it, and the geometry also asks between its own
  steps (`throw_if_cancelled`); a stopped operation throws `Cancelled`
  ("the operation was cancelled"). OCCT's checker (`BRepCheck_Analyzer`)
  cannot be stopped. Without a monitor nothing stops early.
- Commands that compute nothing (renames of parameters, comments, named
  views) are not cancelled.
- A document is used by one thread at a time; the other thread may hold
  shapes of earlier results meanwhile but must not read them (OCCT's
  algorithms set flags on the sub-shapes of their inputs, which earlier
  results share).
- The .f3d imports (`import_f3d` with or without the timeline) run
  without the control: they build the document in several steps and are
  not undone as a whole.
- Tests: `core/model-tests/api/src/monitor_tests.rs`; `core/tests/test_bridge.cpp`
  (a cancel from another thread, jobs handed between two threads, a
  modelled thread cancelled inside OCCT); `geometry/tests/test_cancel.cpp`.
  A ThreadSanitizer build of `test_bridge` (by hand, not in ctest)
  reports the progress read of the feature name: the Rust mutex is not
  instrumented.

## Caches

How the recompute cache and the result store work:
[docs/architecture.md](../../../docs/architecture.md#the-model).

### Result store

Results of costly evaluations can be kept on disk, so that opening a
design again (or a copy, or an older version of it) does not evaluate
them again. A result's version is a fingerprint of the feature's uid, its
definition and what it read (`core/model-base/src/fingerprint.rs`), the same
in every document and process. Store code and file format:
`core/model/src/store.rs` (module comment).

| Rust | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ResultStore::new(dir, build_id).with_label(name)` | a store folder; results stored by another `build_id` are not used. The label (the design's file name) is kept with the results written |
| `Document::set_result_store(Some(store))` | recomputes take results from it when the memory cache has none; None (the default) for none |
| `ResultStore::with_quick_results(memory_per_ms)` | quick results (below): stored when their shapes take at most `memory_per_ms` bytes per millisecond of evaluation; None for none. Default `store::QUICK_MEMORY_PER_MS` (128 KiB), None with `MITCAD_STORE_QUICK=0`; `worth_storing(time, memory)` tells |
| `Document::persist_results(min_time)` | writes the results of the last recompute that are not in the store yet: features that succeeded, took at least `min_time` or are quick results worth storing, and whose results the store takes; returns `PersistReport {results, shapes, bytes, quick, failed, errors, time}` (`quick`: of the results, those quicker than `min_time`). A preview's results are not written |
| `store::gc(dir, budget)`, `store::clear(dir)` | `gc` removes the files used longest ago until 80 % of `budget` bytes are used (when more is), and temporary files more than an hour old; `clear` removes all. `GcReport {files, bytes, removed, removed_bytes}` |
| `RecomputeStats::restored`, `restore_times` | the features whose results came from the store in the last recompute, and how long reading each took |

| C++ (`mitcad_bridge/lib.h`; `core/ffi/src/result_store.rs`) | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `Document::set_result_store(dir, build_id, label)` | as above; an empty `dir` for none. `build_id`: `mitcad::geometry::kernel_build_id()` (the shape format, OCCT's and MitCad's versions, the size and time of the running program's file) |
| `Document::persist_results(min_ms)` | JSON `{"results", "shapes", "bytes", "quick", "failed", "errors", "ms"}` |
| `result_store_gc(dir, budget_mb)`, `result_store_clear(dir)` | JSON `{"files", "bytes", "removed", "removed_bytes"}`; any thread may call them |

- Not stored: sketches and construction features, features that move
  occurrences, failed features, results evaluated with a parameter
  renamed since (their versions hold the old name). A result read from
  the store is in the memory cache afterwards and is not written again.
- Base features are stored too, also those that only bring in bodies
  (mitcad#887): bringing a body in reads its B-rep data and derives its
  edges' and vertices' names, which a stored body keeps (a body of
  23 000 faces: 1.4 s to bring in, 0.45 s to restore). Restored results
  whose shapes a recompute unpacks together are unpacked on the
  machine's threads, a result's several bodies too.
- Quick results (mitcad#882): a result that took less than `min_time` is
  stored too when its shapes (the bodies it sets and its tool, as
  `Kernel::shape_memory` estimates them) take at most 128 KiB per
  millisecond of its evaluation. Restoring it reads its file and leaves
  the state before it packed, so a run of restored features unpacks only
  its last state, where evaluating the quick feature unpacks the state it
  reads; quick results with large shapes (a move of a large body) are left
  out. On three large designs the quick modelling features were within
  the limit, and their warm recomputes evaluated 107, 75 and 288
  features before and 68, 53 and 143 after (store.rs's module comment
  has the times).
- The store keeps up to four variants per feature uid and definition,
  for different inputs. A file that cannot be read (damaged, cut short, a
  shape the kernel cannot read) is removed and the feature evaluated; a
  file of another build is passed over and replaced when the feature is
  stored again. A hit touches the file's time, for `gc`. Files are
  written to a temporary file and renamed, so programs sharing the folder
  see whole files.
- Kernel: `Kernel::shape_bytes` and `Kernel::shape_from_bytes` (the shape
  with its face names, notes and measured properties; OCCT:
  `geometry::serialize_shape`).
- `mitcad-cli info <file> --result-store DIR [--persist-min-ms MS]` (also
  `run --open`) opens the design with the store, writes the results
  that took at least `MS` (default 100) and the quick ones worth storing,
  and prints `Result store: restored from store: N, evaluated: M; stored:
  K (B bytes, Q quick); recompute T ms` (T: the recompute's wall time).
- `Document::hand_off_results(&store)` (the bridge's
  `hand_off_results(dir, build_id, label)`) writes every result of the
  last recompute that a store takes to `store`, however quick, and marks
  none written to the document's own store: the import worker hands the
  import's evaluation over to the application this way, which reads the
  imported design with that store instead of evaluating every feature
  again (mitcad#413, app/COMMANDS.md *The `.f3d` worker*).
- Tests: `core/model-tests/api/src/store_tests.rs`, `version_tests.rs`;
  `geometry/tests/test_persist.cpp`; ctest `cli.store_fill`,
  `cli.store_hit`, `cli.store_edit` (the perf model with a store).

### Warm opens: lazy restore and display meshes

Opening a design whose results the store holds (mitcad#858).

**Lazy restore.** With a kernel that can make stored shapes later
(`Kernel::shape_unpacker`; the OCCT kernel can), a result found in the
store keeps the shapes of the bodies it sets packed (`Output::changes`,
`Changes::heads` without them) and the body states hold a stand-in under
the stored version; its tool is read at once. The shapes are unpacked
when something reads them: an evaluation unpacks the results that set
the bodies it reads as it reads them (mitcad#886: a sketch on a face the
face's body, a join or a fillet its bodies; reading all of a component's
bodies unpacks them all), and the other bodies stay packed (the time it
takes is not the evaluation's); before a joint is applied every body;
at the end the bodies left; and whenever
anything reads the result's changes later (the timeline's history,
`body_before`, a pattern of features). A state the next restored result
replaces before that is never unpacked. Not with recompute workers nor
for a preview. `MITCAD_LAZY_RESTORE=0` reads every result whole.

- A command's answer with `"restored"` also has `"restored_packed"`: of
  those results, the ones whose shapes were never unpacked.
- The `cache` query's `store` adds `deferred` (hits kept packed),
  `unpacked` (of them, unpacked since) and `unpack_ms`, and
  `display_meshes`: `lookups`, `hits`, `faces`, `read_bytes`, `read_ms`,
  `writes`, `write_bytes`, `write_ms`; its `disk` adds `display_meshes`
  {`files`, `bytes`}; `last_recompute` adds `restored_packed`.

**Display meshes.** The application keeps each shown body's display
triangulations (the final tier's, `app/framework/DisplayMeshes`) in the
store beside the results, under the body's version and the meshing
options (`.mms` files, `store.rs`). `gc`, `clear` and the store's size
count them.

| Rust / C++ | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ResultStore::write_display_mesh(kernel, version, options, shape)` | writes `Kernel::display_mesh_bytes` of a shape meshed for display to the end; the file's bytes |
| `ResultStore::restore_display_mesh(kernel, version, options, shape)` | `Kernel::restore_display_mesh` of what is stored for that version and those options: the faces given a triangulation, None when there is none (another build, other options, another shape: nothing written) |
| `Document::restore_display_meshes(request)` (bridge) | `{"bodies": [uids], "options": "…"}`: each body at the marker takes what the store keeps for its version; JSON `{"restored": [uids], "faces", "bytes", "ms"}` |
| `Document::persist_display_meshes(request)` (bridge) | the same request: writes the bodies' display meshes; JSON `{"stored", "bytes", "failed", "errors", "ms"}` |

OCCT: `io::triangulation_bytes` and `io::restore_triangulations`
(`geometry/io/include/mitcad/io/mesh_store.hpp`): each face's nodes,
parameters, triangles, deviation and meshing parameters and its edges'
polygons, checked against the face (its surface's kind, its edges and
their end points) before anything is written. Tests:
`store_tests.rs` (`a_state_replaced_before_anything_reads_it_is_not_unpacked`,
`an_evaluation_reads_the_restored_shapes_unpacked`,
`display_meshes_are_kept_for_the_body_s_shape`), ctest `geometry.io`
(`test_display_mesh_bytes`), `app.preview_meshing` (`testWarmOpen`).

### Memory cache and diagnostics

`Document::set_memory_budget(Some(bytes))` (the bridge's
`set_memory_cache_budget(megabytes)`, 0 for none) limits the estimated
size of the memory cache's results: `Kernel::shape_memory` of each
result's shapes (OCCT: `geometry::memory_estimate`; parts shared with
other results are counted with each), a sketch's regions and what it
read. Beyond it the results used longest ago go, except those the
document's results and its preview hold; with a result store they come
back from there. Each feature keeps at most eight results whatever the
budget; without a budget (the default) nothing else goes.

| Command / query | Fields | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `clear_cache` | | drops the cached results the document's results and preview do not hold: `results`, `bytes`. No undo step, the revision stays |
| `cache` query | `disk` (default false: also read what the store's files hold) | `memory`: `bytes`, `budget` (null for none), `used` (bytes / budget), `results`, `features`, `lookups`, `hits`, `misses`, `restored` (from the store), `evicted`, `evicted_bytes`, `by_feature` (`uid`, `name`, `type`, `results`, `bytes`; the largest first), `by_type` (`type`, `features`, `results`, `bytes`); `store` (null without one): `dir`, `build_id` and what the stores of this process did: `lookups`, `hits`, `misses`, `damaged`, `other_build`, `read_bytes`, `read_ms`, `writes`, `write_bytes`, `write_ms`, `write_errors`, and with `disk` its `disk`: `files`, `bytes`, `other_builds` {`files`, `bytes`}, `damaged`, `by_document` (`document`, `features`, `results`, `bytes`), `by_feature` (`document`, `uid`, `name`, `type`, `results`, `bytes`), `by_type`, the largest first; `last_recompute`: `evaluated`, `restored`, `cached`, `evaluate_ms`, `restore_ms`, `features` in timeline order (`uid`, `name`, `type`, `source`: `evaluated`, `store`, `cache`, `suppressed` or `rolled_back`; `ms`: how long it took now; `evaluated_ms`: how long its evaluation took) |

The bridge's `query` adds to the `cache` answer `process`: `resident`,
`peak_resident` and `heap` bytes (`geometry::process_memory`, OCCT's
`OSD_MemInfo`). `mitcad-cli info <file> --diagnostics` prints it
(`Cache: {...}`, with `disk`). Tests: `core/model-tests/api/src/cache_tests.rs`,
ctest `cli.store_diagnostics`.

## Geometry of other components

A sketch belongs to its component and lies in that component's
coordinates, but its plane and its projections may be geometry of
another component (mitcad#100, `core/model/src/links.rs`): a planar face,
a construction plane or an origin plane, and edges, faces and vertices to
project. Such geometry is named with where it was picked: `occurrence`,
the occurrence path from the root to its component (`"O1"`, `"O1/O4"`,
`""` for the root), and optionally `context`, the path the sketch's own
component is seen at (default: the first path to it). The model keeps
both as an `OccurrenceLink` (`{"source": "O1", "target": "O2"}`):

- `sketch.create` with `occurrence` stores the plane's link as the
  sketch's `plane_link`; `sketch.project` with `occurrence` moves the
  picked geometry into the sketch, and a linked projection keeps the link
  in its record (`projections[i].link`). Geometry in the sketch's own
  component needs no link, and none is stored for it.
- Evaluation finds the geometry in its component at the sketch's point of
  the timeline and moves it by `placement(target)⁻¹ ·
  placement(source)`, the occurrences' placements there. The sketch
  follows when the geometry changes or either occurrence moves; the
  cache keys on those placements and on the other component's bodies the
  evaluation read. A face's frame is the frame of every planar face,
  taken in the sketch's coordinates; a construction or origin plane keeps
  its own axes.
- A target that no longer leads to the sketch's component (a copy, an
  occurrence deleted) is replaced by the first path to it; a source path
  that leads nowhere fails the sketch with the reason. The sketch must
  come after the features that make the geometry, as with any reference.
- Without `occurrence`, another component's body fails the sketch as
  before (`body F3.b0 (from Extrude2) belongs to A; …`), a construction
  plane of another component is refused, and `sketch.project` refuses a
  body of another component (`… is a body of A, not of B; pick it where
  an occurrence of A shows it`).

The `sketch` query shows `plane_link`. A combine's tools may be bodies of
another component the same way (tools in occurrences or `tool_links`,
[combine](#combine), mitcad#104, mitcad#544), an extrusion's and a
revolution's objects (`object_links`, [extrude](#extrude),
[revolve](#revolve), mitcad#762) and a sweep's path and guide
surfaces (`body_links`, [sweep](#sweep), mitcad#161), and a pulley's or
gear's shaft (a seat's `link`, [Seats on shafts](#seats-on-shafts),
mitcad#578). Tests: `core/model-tests/links/src/link_tests.rs`,
`core/model/src/links.rs`.

### derive

```json
{"type": "derive", "bodies": ["F12.b0"], "links": {"F12.b0": {"source": "O3/O5"}}}
```

Copies of bodies of other components as new bodies of the feature's
component (`Derive<n>`, mitcad#324): each body is read in its own component
at the derive's point of the timeline and moved into the derive's
coordinates by the placements there (`links`: one occurrence link per body
of another component, as a combine's `tool_links`; a body without one is
the derive's own component's), so a copy follows when its source changes
or its occurrence moves. The sources stay where they are. The copies are
the bodies `<derive>.b<j>` in the order listed, their faces named
`<derive>:inst1(<name>)`. A body is listed once; a link for a body that is
not listed, and an empty list, are refused. Paste New and moves of
occurrences carry the links like a combine's (Paste New of a component that
holds the source's occurrence links the copy to its own copy of it).

The `.f3d` import brings a design's derived bodies in so: each body's
document is imported from its own file like the other documents the design
refers to ([Components of other documents](#components-of-other-documents)),
placed as a hidden occurrence of a component filled with its copy, where
the derive puts the body (the source design's placement of the body's
occurrence seen from the deriving design's placement there), and the
derive copies the body from it; `report.designs[0].components` then lists
the documents among `references` as for occurrences.

## Moving features into components

A design often starts in the root: sketches, extrudes and fillets made
there, and components only later. The root then holds modelled bodies
and components (a hybrid assembly), and Create Components from Bodies
moves a body into a component without the features that made it.
`move_to_component` (mitcad#171, `document/move_features.rs`) moves the
features themselves into new components placed where they were, as if
they had been made there:

- **Everything** (no `bodies`, `features` or `groups`): every modelled
  feature of `component` (default the root) goes into one new component,
  placed in it at the identity and grounded; the component keeps only
  components and the features that place or relate them (Move and
  Position of occurrences, joints, rigid groups, assembly constraints).
  A feature that makes a component (a new-component operation, Component
  from Bodies) goes too when it uses what goes; the component it made
  stays placed where it is.
- **Bodies, features, groups:** `bodies` and `features` go into one new
  component with the features that made those bodies; `groups` (lists of
  bodies) into a component each, named after the body when it is one
  (otherwise `Component<n>`; `name` or `names` choose). Which features go
  follows the last recompute (the bodies each feature set, removed or
  read) and the references (for features after the marker, suppressed or
  failed): a feature goes with the features it refers to, those that
  refer to it and those that work on the same bodies.
- **Conflicts:** a feature that would belong to two components, or
  works on a body that stays (a combine or a cut through bodies of two
  groups, a sketch on a face of a body that stays, a sketch two groups
  use), refuses the move with the reason (`Combine1 ties Body1, Body2,
  which would go into different components; …`), unless `"together":
  true` keeps such bodies in one component (a body that would stay goes
  along). A feature that stays and uses what would go, which no
  occurrence path can follow (a Move of occurrences about an edge of a
  moving body), refuses it in every case.
- **Nothing moves:** features keep their uids, timeline order,
  parameters and the topological names of what they make. References
  from elsewhere take the new occurrence into their paths: sketch planes
  and projections of other components and combines' tools
  ([Geometry of other components](#geometry-of-other-components)),
  joint and constraint origins, Isolate; a moved feature's own links are
  seen from the new occurrence. The move is refused when a feature that
  worked fails after it, or a definition that checked no longer does.
- **Cut scopes follow** (mitcad#859): a moved extrusion's `cut_scope`
  (also a saved one of an extrusion that does not cut) takes the
  destination as its `context` (the component and its occurrence path)
  and so do its targets in the component it left; any scope's
  `excluded_bodies` of the bodies that went name their new place. What
  the component keeps stays named where it is: an automatic scope's
  exclusion of it, and another component's cut into it, then name both
  places. The same holds for an explicit `destination` and for
  `move_history_into_component`.
- `move_history_into_component` with `feature`, a `component_from_bodies`:
  the features that made its bodies go into the component it made, which
  then has their history (Paste New copies it), and the feature goes.
  Refused when one of them also works on a body that stays.
- Each command is one undo step (`Move Features of Root into Component1`,
  `Move History into Body1`).

| Command | Fields | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `move_to_component` | `component` (default the root), `bodies`, `features`, or `groups`; `name` or `names`; `together` (default false); optional `source_occurrence` and `destination` below | `components`: `component`, `occurrence`, `name`, `bodies`, `features`; explicit destinations also return `created` |
| `move_history_into_component` | `feature` | `component`, `name`, `features` |
| `set_hybrid_assembly` | `allowed` (default true) | |

| Query | Fields | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `move_to_component` | as the command, without the top-level `name` and `names` | `component`, `name`, `everything`, `bodies` (the component's at the marker: `uid`, `name`), `hybrid_assembly`, `groups` (`bodies` with names, `features` with `uid`, `name`, `type`), `conflicts` (`feature`, `name`, `groups` (indices), `staying` bodies, `message`), `together` (the expanded groups, or null), `problems`, `destinations`, `keep_together` (the requested boolean) |
| `feature_references` | `def` (a definition as `add_feature` takes it) | `features` it refers to, `components` they are in |

The application asks before it makes a component in a root with
modelled bodies (`app/framework/HybridAssembly.cpp`): Move into a New
Component, Continue as Is or Cancel. "Don't ask again for this design"
runs `set_hybrid_assembly` (undo step `Allow Hybrid Assembly`); the
`document` query has `"hybrid_assembly": true` then, and the design file keeps
`"hybrid_assembly": true`. Tests: `core/model-tests/assembly/src/move_features_tests.rs`,
`tools/ui-hybrid-test.sh`.

### Choosing an existing or new destination

The explicit Move to Component action (mitcad#201) asks for the destination
before executing a command. The query is read-only and lists the dependency
group that will move. Conflicts still require `together: true`: selecting a
destination never implies permission to take additional bodies.

An existing component is identified by its UID and its full occurrence
path from the root:

```json
{"cmd":"move_to_component","component":"C1","features":["F5"],
 "source_occurrence":"O1",
 "destination":{"kind":"existing","component":"C3","occurrence":"O2/O4"}}
```

To create the component in the same atomic move, specify its parent and
optionally its name:

```json
{"cmd":"move_to_component","features":["F1"],
 "destination":{"kind":"new","parent":"C0","parent_occurrence":"","name":"Housing"}}
```

The empty occurrence path is the root. `source_occurrence` may be omitted
when there is exactly one placement of the source. Both source and target
(or a new component's parent) must have one placement in the whole design;
this includes repetitions through an ancestor. A repeated or unplaced
component is refused rather than selecting an arbitrary instance of its
shared definition. Source and destination paths are checked again when the
command executes.

For the picker, `destinations` contains one row for every placed component
context, including the root:

```json
{"component":"C3","name":"Bracket","occurrence":"O2/O4",
 "path":"Root/Assembly:1/Bracket:1","parent_occurrence":"O2",
 "eligible":true,"reason":"","can_create":true,"create_reason":""}
```

`eligible` and `reason` describe a move into that existing component;
`can_create` and `create_reason` describe creation below it. Full UID paths
remain the selection keys even if display names repeat. Supplying a
`destination` in the query also adds its refusal reason to `problems`.
The expanded `together` group is considered when checking destinations;
`conflicts` remain separate until the caller explicitly consents. An
explicit destination accepts one resulting group. Top-level `name` and
`names` cannot be combined with `destination`; a new name goes inside it.

An existing destination creates no component or occurrence. To preserve
world placement, the model maps source coordinates by
`inverse(destination_world) * source_world`. Origin-plane sketches keep
their entities, constraints and parameters, with their stored frame
rebased into the target coordinates. Numeric-distance extrudes, fillets,
chamfers and combines can accompany them. Definitions requiring other
coordinate transformations (for example, a face-supported sketch or an
origin-axis revolve) are refused for differing placements with the
feature's name and a reason. At equal placements no frame change is
needed. A new component instead receives the source's world placement
relative to its chosen parent, retaining the features' local coordinates.

Sketch plane/projection links, combine/sweep body links and isolated-body
paths follow the geometry to the destination. Explicit moves refuse
read-only linked components, the current owner, components created by a
modelling feature, moved component-creating features, affected assembly
constraint references, and contexts positioned by timeline features.
Moving into an existing component is also refused when an affected
feature automatically reads all local bodies: the added bodies must not
silently become participants of an existing operation. These cases report
a reason instead of changing geometry or dropping references.

Validation, optional creation, ownership and reference updates, and the
successful recompute are one undo step. Cancelled or rejected commands
leave the design, component counters and history unchanged. Explicit
results use the full occurrence path in `components[].occurrence` (empty
for the root) and include `created`. Calls without `destination` retain
the original automatic child-creation behaviour and result format, used
by the hybrid-assembly prompt and grouped automatic moves.

`core.model` covers destination validation, dependency consent and atomic
moves; `app.unit` exercises the destination dialog. The OCCT checks
`cli.move_destination` and `cli.move_destination_reopened` preserve the
world-space bounds, volumes and external face support of three bodies
when moving a nested source into a differently rotated existing component,
including Undo/Redo and save/reopen.

## Moving an occurrence to another parent

`reparent_occurrence` (mitcad#219, `document/reparent.rs`) moves one
occurrence, with its component and everything placed in it, under another
parent: the root or a placed component. It is a hierarchy move, not a copy:
the occurrence keeps its uid, number, name, light bulb and grounding, its
component keeps its uid, features, bodies, parameters and history. Only its
parent changes, and its own placement, to
`inverse(new_parent_world) * old_parent_world * placement` so that it stays
where it is in the design at the timeline marker (through the parents the
old and the new way do not share; translated and rotated parents alike).

```json
{"cmd":"reparent_occurrence","occurrence":"O1/O2","parent":""}
```

`occurrence` is the occurrence's path from the root and `parent` the path
of the new parent's occurrence (empty: the root), by uids (`O1/O4`) or
names (`Assembly:1/Part:1`). The result has `occurrence`, `component`,
`path` (the new uid path), `path_name`, `parent` (the component),
`updated` (the references that followed it) and `features` (the features
that place it and went with it, below). One undo step, `Move Part:1 to
Root`; undo and redo restore or reapply the hierarchy, the placement, the
references and the carried features together.

Occurrence paths that lead through the moved occurrence follow it in the
same step: sketch planes and projections linked to other components,
combine, sweep, split and extrude body links, construction plane links,
cut scopes, joints and assembly constraints (their paths are relative to
their component), section analyses, Isolate, the model's annotations, and
the drawings (mitcad#743): their views' occurrence subjects, chosen
bodies' occurrences and the picks of their dimensions, notes, symbols and
balloons. A root drawing's paths go the new way; a component's drawing
keeps paths from its component, which follow while the old and the new
parent both lie inside that component, and the move is refused, naming
the drawing, when the occurrence would leave it. The changed drawings are
listed in `updated`. Everything is validated
before anything changes, in one place (`Document::plan_reparent`, which
design policies extend), and refused with the blocker named.

**The features that place it go with it** (mitcad#301): its joints and
as-built joints (it is the first occurrence of a side's path), the rows of
assembly constraint sets with it, rigid groups with it, and its Moves
(`move_occurrence`) and Capture Positions, wherever they are in the
timeline (also after the marker and suppressed). Each becomes a feature of
the new parent and keeps its place in the timeline; its occurrence paths
are rewritten relative to the new parent. The new parent is the one
component where such a feature can still place the occurrence: a joint,
constraint or rigid group moves only occurrences placed directly in its
component, and a Move or Capture Position places only those, so the
lowest component that holds everything the feature refers to after the
move must be the new parent itself. Typical: `Joint1` of `Box` joins
`Part:1` to `Box`'s own block; moving `Part:1` from `Box:1` to the root
makes `Joint1` a root joint from `Part:1` to `Box:1` (its side `b` was the
empty path, now `O1`). Moving `Part:1` into a component that holds the
geometry it is joined to (a joint to `Sub:1`'s block, `Part:1` into
`Box:1/Sub:1`) makes it a joint of `Sub` to `Sub`'s own block.

- A Move turns into the new parent's coordinates: a free move (`free`
  matrix) by `relative * move * inverse(relative)`, where `relative`
  takes the old parent's coordinates into the new parent's; a move along
  the axes (`translate_xyz`) stays as it is when the axes agree.
- A Capture Position's placement becomes `relative * captured`.
- A rigid group of the old parent holds the moved occurrence, in the new
  parent (an ancestor of the old one), to the occurrence that places the
  old parent there (`Box:1`), which stands for the members that stay.
- A feature that also places other occurrences is split: the occurrence's
  rows of a constraint set (with their parameters), its position of a
  Capture Position, its place in a rigid group of three or more, or (for
  a free move) its place in a Move go into a new feature of the new
  parent right after it (`Constraint2`, `Position2`, `RigidGroup2`,
  `Move2`, in the same timeline group), the rest stays.

The query's plan and the command list them in `features`: `name`, `from`
and `from_name` (its component), `to` and `to_name` (the new parent) and
`split` (the new feature's name, null when the feature goes whole):

```json
{"name":"Joint1","from":"C1","from_name":"Box","to":"C0","to_name":"Root","split":null}
```

The refusals:

- the root and an occurrence made by Pattern at Points;
- a placing feature that could not keep its meaning in the new parent
  (`Joint1: it joins Part:1 to Box:1, which is not in Lid; it places only
  occurrences placed directly in its component, so it could not place
  Part:1 there`; in `Root`, which holds both, it would move `Lid:1`
  instead); a Move along the old parent's axes when they are turned in
  the new parent (`Move1: it moves Part:1 along the x, y and z axes of
  Assembly, which are turned in Root; …`) or by geometry of the old
  parent (an axis or points, which a feature of another component cannot
  use); a Move by values that also moves other occurrences (its
  parameters belong to it, so it cannot be split);
- what a carried feature depends on moving later in the timeline in a way
  the moved occurrence would no longer follow: an occurrence below the
  new parent on the way to geometry it is joined to, or a member of its
  rigid group, placed by a later feature (`Joint1: Pin:1 is placed by
  Move1 later in the timeline, which Part:1 in Root would no longer
  follow`); a parent on the way between the old and the new parent placed
  by a later Move, Capture Position or Pattern at Points (later joints of
  the new parent are solved together with the carried ones); for a Move or
  Capture Position, a parent on the way placed by any later feature (it
  works in the parent's coordinates at its point of the timeline);
- an occurrence whose solved placement differs from its own without a
  timeline feature that places it (`Part:1 is placed by the joints`);
- a source parent placed more than once (the occurrence is in each of
  them, `Assembly is placed 2 times and Part:1 is in each of them; …`) and
  a destination placed more than once (it would appear in each): a single
  occurrence move never edits other instances of a shared component;
  other occurrences of the moved component itself stay as they are;
- linked (read-only) source parents and destinations;
- the current parent (`Part:1 is already in Assembly`), the occurrence's
  own component and anything placed in it (a cycle);
- a joint or constraint whose moved occurrence would change, or whose
  component the occurrence would leave (`Joint1: Part:1 would no longer be
  in Asm:1, the occurrence it moves`);
- Pattern at Points features and instances that refer to it;
- references across the occurrence (one side through it, the other not)
  while an occurrence on the way from the old parent or to the new one is
  placed by a timeline feature (anywhere in the timeline): the relative
  placement could differ where the reference is evaluated
  (`Sketch2: Assembly:1 is placed by Move1 in the timeline, …`).

A component made by a feature (a new-component operation, Component from
Bodies) can move: the feature keeps making its bodies, in that component's
coordinates. The command recomputes the new state before taking it and
refuses it (`the move would make features fail: …`) when a feature that
built before fails after the move, and when any occurrence would be
somewhere else in the design at the marker (`the move would change where
Box:1 is in the design: Joint1 would place the occurrences differently in
Root`; e.g. a joint whose side `a` was the old parent's own geometry,
which cannot move there, while in the new parent `a` is the old parent's
occurrence, which moves first unless grounded). Carried features are also
checked where they stand in the timeline, after the marker too. A refused
command changes nothing.

The query takes `occurrence` and optionally `parent`:

```json
{"query":"reparent_occurrence","occurrence":"O1/O2","parent":""}
```

It answers `occurrence`, `name`, `path`, `path_name` (`Root/Assembly:1/
Part:1`), `component`, `component_name`, `parent`, `parent_path`,
`grounded`, `contents` (`occurrences`: the paths placed in it below it,
`components`, `bodies`, `features`), `problems` (why the occurrence cannot
move at all) and `destinations`: every placement of the root and of each
component, as Move to Component lists them, with `current` (the current
parent), `eligible` and `reason`:

```json
{"component":"C3","name":"Bracket","occurrence":"O4","path":"Root/Bracket:1",
 "parent_occurrence":"","current":false,"eligible":true,"reason":""}
```

With `parent`, `plan` is `eligible`, `problems` (the blockers), and for an
eligible move `parent`, `parent_path`, `from`, `from_path`, `path` (the new
uid path), `transform` (the new placement's rows), `updates` and
