  record keeps the link and the geometry is moved by the occurrence's
  placement. Without the occurrence such a sketch is refused (`Sketch1 is
  a sketch of A, not of …; pick it where an occurrence of A shows it`).
- In the design file the source of a projection of model geometry is the
  name's text, as in every earlier version, so earlier files open
  unchanged; a sketch entity's source is the object above. A copied
  sketch's projection of a copied sketch names the copy.

Tests: `core/model-tests/sketch-refs/src/sketch_projection_tests.rs`
(the same, a parallel and an oblique plane; a dimension change followed;
an unlinked copy; a removed source curve; a later sketch and the sketch
itself refused; a whole sketch; save and reopen; another component's
sketch through its occurrence).

## Failed features in command results

A feature that fails does not reject a command (mitcad#401): the command
is applied and the feature is skipped. So that a client can tell "the
feature this command made fails" from "a feature elsewhere fails", a
command's result has, when any feature is in error after it,
`"failed_features"`: every failed feature in timeline order, each

- `uid`, `name`, `error` (the feature's error);
- `edited`: the command added the feature or edited it: its definition,
  suppression or component changed, or it is the `uid` of
  `edit_feature`, `suppress_feature` or `reorder_feature` or the `sketch`
  of a sketch command (an edit of a dimension's value changes no
  definition);
- `new`: it did not fail before the command (also a later feature this
  command broke, for example through a parameter, with `edited` false).

```json
{"changed": ["d4"], "recomputed": 1, "error": "Fillet1: fillet failed",
 "failed_features": [{"uid": "F3", "name": "Fillet1", "error": "fillet failed",
                      "edited": false, "new": true}]}
```

Without failed features the field is left out. `error` stays the first
failed feature, as before. The MCP server's `model_command` is an error
only when one of these is `edited` and lists them at the top level
([docs/mcp.md](../../../docs/mcp.md)).

Tests: `core/model-tests/api/src/failed_features_tests.rs` (mock kernel),
`core/mcp/src/tests.rs`, `tools/cli/mcp-results-test.cmake`.

## Adding a feature in the middle of the timeline

`add_feature` with `"after": "F12"` (a feature's uid) or `"index": 3`
(the number of features before the new one) inserts the feature there
instead of at the marker (mitcad#403):

```json
{"cmd": "add_feature", "after": "F1", "def": {"type": "extrude",
 "profiles": [{"sketch": "F1", "region": "r{c1}"}],
 "extent": {"type": "distance", "distance": 5}, "operation": "new_body"}}
```

- One undo step (`Add Extrude2`) and one recompute: the features before
  the place come from the cache, the new one and those after it are
  evaluated.
- The marker stays after the feature it was after (it counts one more);
  features after it stay rolled back. The place must be at or before the
  marker: `index` past it, `after` a rolled-back feature are refused.
- The new feature may refer only to features before it, as
  `reorder_feature` requires; a refused insert (that, an unknown `after`,
  both `after` and `index`) leaves the document as it was. A feature that
  is added but fails is in the result's `failed_features` with `edited`.
- Not with a Face's inline rules (`sheet_face` with a `rules`
  definition); the preview takes neither field.

Tests: `core/model-tests/api/src/insert_feature_tests.rs` (mock kernel),
`tools/cli/mcp-results-test.cmake` (through MCP).

## Signed point dimensions

A `horizontal_distance` or `vertical_distance` with `"signed": true`
(mitcad#404) is the coordinate offset `b.x - a.x` (`b.y - a.y`) in sketch
axes, which may be negative, instead of its size. Its sign says on which
side of `a` the point `b` lies, so a point `p3` dimensioned from a centre
`p1` with

```json
{"cmd": "sketch.add_dimension", "sketch": "F1", "value": "r * cos(angle)",
 "dimension": {"type": "horizontal_distance", "a": "p1", "b": "p3", "signed": true}}
{"cmd": "sketch.add_dimension", "sketch": "F1", "value": "r * sin(angle)",
 "dimension": {"type": "vertical_distance", "a": "p1", "b": "p3", "signed": true}}
```

follows the parameter `angle` through all four quadrants: a value that
changes sign moves `p3` to the other side of `p1`, where an unsigned
dimension would refuse it. To dimension a point from the sketch origin,
use a fixed point at [0, 0] (`sketch.add_point` with `"fixed": true`) as
`a`.

- Without `signed` (default false; sketches stored before, every import),
  the dimensions are as before: the size `|b.x - a.x|`, never negative (a
  negative value is an error of the sketch, `d4 must not be negative`), on
  the side where `b` is when the sketch is solved.
- Its value may be any finite number; a driven one measures the signed
  offset (its reference parameter and the `measured` field in the `sketch`
  query), as does a driving one added without a value.
- The `sketch` query and saved files give `"signed": true` only on a
  signed dimension, so files without signed dimensions are unchanged.
- Solver: `HorizontalDistance { signed: true }` keeps side 1 and holds
  `dx - d` (`core/solver/README.md`).

`sketch.set_signed` switches an existing horizontal or vertical distance
between signed and unsigned (mitcad#409), one undo step `Change Dimension
in Sketch1`, keeping the point where it is:

```json
{"cmd": "sketch.set_signed", "sketch": "F1", "dimension": "k4", "signed": true}
```

- Where `b` lies on the positive side of `a` (or level with it), the
  value stays as it is. Where it lies on the negative side, a driving
  value is negated: a value without parameters as a number (30 becomes
  -30), an expression as `-(…)` (`r * 0.6` becomes `-(r * 0.6)`; one
  that is `-(…)` already loses it instead, so switching back and forth
  does not nest), and a dimension that uses another parameter by name
  gets an expression of its own (`w` becomes `-w`).
- A driven dimension only measures the other way.
- Other dimension types are refused (`dimension k3 is a length, not a
  horizontal or vertical distance`); switching to what it is already
  changes nothing.

Tests: `core/model-tests/sketch/src/sketch_tests.rs` (`a_signed_point_dimension_*`,
`an_unsigned_point_dimension_*`, `signed_point_dimensions_round_trip_*`,
`switching_a_distance_signed_*`, `unsigned_point_dimensions_switched_*`),
`core/solver/tests/constraints.rs`
(`signed_distances_follow_through_all_quadrants`).

## The library parts a design uses

The part picker's **In this design** group (mitcad#418, `app/COMMANDS.md`)
lists the library parts the open design already uses, with how many times
each is placed:

| Query | Result |
|---|---|
| `library_usage` | `parts`: one per library component, `{"library", "url", "component", "count", "rows"}` |

- `library` is the library's id and `component` the component's id in
  it, as `library_search` gives them; `url` is where the library was
  fetched from, without credentials.
- Both kinds of library parts count: BUILD's derived parts by their
  [source](#sources) and components inserted from a library
  ([Library parts](#library-parts)), linked or copied.
- A component's versions and configuration rows are one entry: an M4x16
  and an M4x20 of the same screw count together in `count`.
- `rows` (mitcad#518) gives the same count per configuration row, so the
  part picker can show each size's own use count: `[{"config": "M4x16",
  "count": 35}, {"config": "M4x20", "count": 2}]`, in the order the rows
  first appear in the parts list; a row the design does not use is not
  listed. It is each use's row as the part was placed (a BUILD part's
  `config`, an insert's `config`). A use placed without a row is in
  `count` only (it is the component's default row), so `count` is at
  least the sum of the rows' counts; `rows` is empty for a part without
  rows.
- `count` is the parts list's quantity summed: how many times the design
  places the part, through every occurrence of the components it is in.
  A part placed nowhere (its last occurrence deleted) is left out.
- The entries come in the order of the parts list (the order the
  components were made).

Tests: `core/model-tests/links/src/library_tests.rs`
(`the_library_usage_counts_each_library_component_once`,
`the_library_usage_counts_each_configuration_row_of_a_component`),
`core/model-tests/build-timber/src/source_tests.rs`
(`the_library_usage_counts_build_parts_by_their_source`),
`core/model-tests/build-timber/src/timber_tests.rs`
(`the_library_usage_counts_build_parts_per_row`).

## Motion studies and contact sets

Assemblies' motion studies and contact sets (mitcad#454; `core/model/src/motion.rs`
the data, `contact.rs` the contact checks, `document/motion.rs` and
`api/motion.rs` the commands). Both are definition state, not timeline
features: saved in the design file (`motion_studies`, `contact_sets`, left
out when there are none), changed by undoable commands that recompute
nothing, deleted with what they name (a study's keys of a joint that is
deleted or no longer has the motion; a set's occurrences that are gone),
and moved with an occurrence that moves to another parent. Tests:
`core/model-tests/joints/src/motion_tests.rs`, `tools/cli/tests/motion_contact.json`,
`tools/ui-motion-study-test.sh`, `tools/ui-contact-test.sh`.

```json
{"motion_studies": [{"name": "Open", "steps": 40, "keys": [
   {"joint": "F7", "motion": "tz", "points": [[0, 0], [40, 12.5]]},
   {"joint": "F8", "motion": "rz", "points": [[10, 0], [40, 1.5708]]}]}],
 "contact_sets": [{"name": "Contact1", "occurrences": ["O2", "O3/O5"]},
                  {"name": "Stops", "occurrences": ["O1", "O2"], "suppressed": true}]}
```

- **Motion study:** a name, `steps` (1 to 100 000) and keys: per joint
  (or as-built joint) and one of its free motions (a cylindrical joint's
  `tz` and `rz` each), `points` `[step, value]` sorted by step, values in
  millimetres or radians. A motion's value at a step is linear between
  the points around it, the first point's before the first, the last's
  after the last. Steps outside `0..steps` are allowed.
- **Contact set:** a name, two or more occurrence paths from the root,
  `suppressed`. Its bodies are the visible bodies placed in the design
  whose instance paths start with one of the paths (a body belongs to the
  innermost one); the pairs checked are bodies of different occurrences
  of one set, once each however many sets hold them.
- **Contact:** two bodies pass through each other when the kernel finds
  more than 0.001 mm³ in common (`Kernel::overlap_volumes`, OCCT's boolean
  common with a fuzzy value of 0.01 mm, so that faces within 0.01 mm of
  each other only touch); pairs whose boxes, moved by their placements,
  are more than 0.01 mm apart cost no boolean. Pairs that already pass
  through each other where a motion starts are left out (parts can move
  apart). Shapes are those at the marker: a feature whose body depends on
  placements is not built again while the joints move.
- **Motions that stop at contact:** `drive_joint`, `drag_occurrence` and
  the `joint_drag` query, `play_study`, and the previews below. A motion
  is sampled from where it starts (Drive Joint and a study's straight
  path: every 5° of a turn and 1 mm of a slide, at most 64 samples; a
  drag: every 2 mm of the grabbed point, at most 16; a study's playback:
  every step), each sample the document's state with the joints driven
  there and recomputed (the joints solved as Drive Joint solves them, so
  constraints and other joints follow), and at the first sample with a
  contact the step before it is bisected 14 times: the motion stops at the
  last state without one. Values are held within the joints' limits.
  Without contact sets nothing is sampled.
- A stopped motion's answer has `contact`: `set`, `bodies` (each `body`,
  `name`, `occurrence` (path name), `path`), `fraction` (how far it went,
  0 to 1; not for drags) and `message` (`stopped at contact: Body2
  (Pin:1) and Body3 (Wall:1) in Contact1`). `drive_joint` also gives the
  message in `warnings` (a panel shows it) and keeps the value where it
  stopped as the joint's position (a number, not the expression given).

| Command | Fields | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `add_motion_study` | `name` (`Study<n>` when left out), `steps` (default 100), `keys` (each `joint` (uid or name), `motion`, `points` `[[step, value], …]`, a value a number in mm or radians or an expression in the motion's unit, `"90 deg"`) | `name`; undo step `Add Study1` |
| `edit_motion_study` | `name`, `new_name`, `steps`, `keys` (all of them) | `name` |
| `delete_motion_study` | `name` | |
| `set_study_key` | `study`, `joint`, `motion`, `step`, `value` (where the joint is at the marker when left out: Add Key) | `joint`, `motion`, `step`, `value`; a point at the same step is replaced; undo step `Key Joint1 in Study1` |
| `remove_study_key` | `study`, `joint`, `motion`, `step` (without it the whole key) | |
| `play_study` | `study`, `step` | `values` (per joint uid, per motion), `fraction`, `contact`; the keyed joints driven from where they are straight to their values at the step, stopping at the first contact, and kept: one undo step `Play Study1` |
| `add_contact_set` | `name` (`Contact<n>`), `occurrences` (paths from the root by uids or names, or one occurrence placed once), `suppressed` | `name` |
| `edit_contact_set` | `name`, `new_name`, `occurrences`, `suppressed` | `name`; undo steps `Suppress Contact1`, `Unsuppress Contact1`, `Edit Contact1` |
| `delete_contact_set` | `name` | |

| Query | Fields | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `motion_studies` | | each study's `name`, `steps`, `keys` (`joint`, `joint_name`, `motion`, `points`) |
| `study_values` | `study`, `step` | `values` per joint uid and motion at the step |
| `contact_sets` | | each set's `name`, `occurrences` (`path`, `name`), `suppressed` |
| `contact_check` | | `overlaps`: the pairs of the active sets that pass through each other at the marker (`set`, `volume`, `bodies`) |

Previews (`preview`, changing nothing but the preview; the report has the
preview's `placements` and `values`, `fraction`, `contact`):

- `{"cmd": "play_study", "study", "step", "from"}`: the study at `step`,
  along the study from step `from` (the application's playback, frame by
  frame), else from where the joints are.
- `{"cmd": "drive_joint", "joint", "values": {"tx": 12}, "from": {"tx":
  8}}`: the joint driven to the values from `from` (Animate Joint's
  frames), else from where it is.

The `.solidcraft` import maps the file's contact sets and motion studies
onto these ([.solidcraft import](#solidcraft-import), `core/import-solidcraft/docs/solidcraft.md`).

## Contour Flange, Convert to Sheet Metal and Perforate

Three sheet features of mitcad#461, with `add_feature` and `edit_feature`,
ordinary parameters, preview, Undo and persistence. Contour Flange and
Convert to Sheet Metal take their rules as a Face does: a `sheet_rules`
uid, or the rules' definition inline (a `sheet_rules` feature is added just
before them in the same undo step). The geometry and its conventions are in
[docs/sheet-metal.md](../../../docs/sheet-metal.md#implementation-notes-mitcad461).

### Contour Flange

```json
{"type":"sheet_contour","rules":"F1","sketch":"F2","curves":["c1","c4","c6"],
 "width":50,"side":"right","reverse":false,"radius":3}
```

`curves` are sketch lines joined end to end, in the order the chain runs
(the first line runs away from the second; one line runs from its start).
The chain is the sheet's surface on the rules' reference side, the material
on `side` of it (`right`, the default, or `left` of travel, seen from the
sketch's front), `width` along the sketch's normal (against it with
`reverse`). Every corner is the virtual sharp of a bend of `radius`
(default: the rules'). The new body is `<feature>.b0`; panel `i` is the
straight part of line `i` (slot `i`, its curves `g<50+100i>` to
`g<53+100i>`, `51` at its far end), bend `i` (slot `i`) joins panels `i`
and `i+1`. Refused: curves that are not lines or do not join, lines in one
line, and a line not longer than the setbacks of its bends.

### Convert to Sheet Metal

```json
{"type":"sheet_convert","rules":"F1","body":"F5.b0","face":"F5:side(c1[c12,c4])",
 "bends":["E{F5:side(c1[c12,c4])|F5:side(c12[c10,c1])}"],"radius":3}
```

The body becomes a sheet of the rules, keeping its uid. `face` (planar) is
the first panel's front, the material behind it. Without `bends` the body
must be a plate of the rules' thickness behind the face: the sheet built
from the face must have the body's volume and centre of mass. With `bends`
(edges between two planar faces), the faces reached from `face` across them
are panels with the rules' thickness behind them, each bend edge the
virtual sharp of a bend of `radius` (default: the rules'). Panel `k` is the
k-th face reached (slot 0 the picked face), bend `k` the bend that reached
panel `k+1`. Refused: a face that is not planar, a bend edge that is not
straight, does not join the picked face through the others or closes a loop,
two panels meeting at an edge that is no bend, a face that does not run the
whole bend edge after its setback.

### Perforate

```json
{"type":"sheet_perforate","body":"F3.b0","diameter":5,"pitch":10,"margin":5,
 "pattern":"square","stationary":{"feature":"F3","slot":0}}
```

Round holes of `diameter`, `pitch` apart on a `staggered` (default) or
`square` grid, cut through the sheet as a developed cut with every bend
open. The grid lies in the chart of `stationary` (default: the sheet's
lowest panel) developed with all bends, from the developed material's lower
left corner; a hole is kept where it lies on a panel, on no bend, and
`margin` (default: the diameter) or more from every edge, cut-out and bend.
The holes are generated curves `g<k>` of the feature. Refused: a pitch not
larger than the diameter, a negative margin, a sheet with overlays (no
developed form), more than 100000 holes.

Tests: `core/model-tests/sheet/src/sheet_more_tests.rs`,
`core/model/src/sheet/folded/perforate.rs` (the grid), the CLI fixtures
`sheet_contour`, `sheet_convert`, `sheet_perforate` with their reopen passes,
and the `.solidcraft` test designs `sheet-contour-perforate` and
`sheet-convert` (`cli.import_solidcraft`).

## Motion links

A `motion_link` feature (mitcad#466; `features/motion_link.rs` the
definition, `core/model/src/motion_links.rs` what recompute does with it,
`document/motion_links.rs` and `api/joints.rs` the commands; the cam's
geometry adapted from SolidCraft in `third_party/solidcraft/cam.rs`)
makes one joint's free motion (`b`, the follower) follow another's (`a`,
the driver) in the link's component. Tests:
`core/model-tests/joints/src/motion_link_tests.rs`, `core/solver/tests/rigid_couplings.rs`,
`tools/cli/tests/motion_links.json`, `tools/ui-motion-link-test.sh`.

```json
{"type": "motion_link", "a": {"joint": "F7", "motion": "rz"}, "b": {"joint": "F8", "motion": "tx"},
 "coupling": {"type": "rack_pinion",
              "radius": {"occurrence": "O2", "geometry": {"body": "F4.b0", "face": "F4:side(c1)"}}},
 "offset": "d12"}
```

| `coupling` | Fields | `b` follows `a` |
|---|---|---|
| `ratio` | `ratio` (unitless, not zero) | `b = ratio · a + offset` (mm or radians each) |
| `gear` | `ra`, `rb` (sizes), `internal` | two turns: `b = −(ra / rb) · a + offset` (`+` for an internal, ring gear) |
| `rack_pinion` | `radius` (a size) | a turn and a slide, either way round: the slide travels `radius` per radian |
| `screw` | `lead` (a size) | a turn and a slide (a cylindrical joint's own two, or a revolute joint and a slider): `lead` per turn |
| `cam` | `profile`, `follower`, `tip` | the follower rides the cam's profile (below) |

- **Sizes** (`ra`, `rb`, `radius`, `lead`, a roller's `radius`) are a value
  (a parameter, an expression or a number, mm; tooth counts work as sizes
  in proportion) or round geometry picked on an occurrence, a joint origin
  (`occurrence`, `geometry`): the radius of a cylindrical, conical or
  spherical face, a circular edge or a sketch circle or arc, found again
  on every recompute.
- `reverse` turns the follower the other way (a cam's follower rides it
  from the other side). `offset` (mm or an angle, as `b`'s motion) is added
  to the follower's value.
- **Joints:** `a` and `b` name joints (or as-built joints) of the link's
  component and one of their free motions each; the two must differ (a
  screw may name one cylindrical joint's `rz` and `tz`). Gears couple two
  turns; a rack and pinion and a screw a turn and a slide.
- **Solving:** at its point of the timeline the link works out its
  relation and solves its two joints together with every joint, constraint
  and link sharing moving occurrences with them (`mitcad_solver::RigidCoupling`:
  one row `b − relation(a)`). A follower whose driver is driven (a
  position or a rest value, or followed from a driven motion) lets go of
  its own position; a driven follower whose driver is free drives the
  driver. `drive_joint` (and a study's keys) take away the positions of the
  motions linked to the ones they drive (through links), so the last
  driven motion drives; a cam's follower is not driven (refused: drive the
  cam). Drags move linked joints together; the degrees of freedom count
  the link (two gears on revolute joints: one). A contact of a contact
  set stops the whole linked motion (the linked joints move in each
  sample of Drive Joint, a drag, Animate Joint or a study). A free driving
  turn is known from the placements only within a turn: the solve takes
  the turn its follower says (a gear past half a turn keeps its mate).
- **Cam:** `a` is a revolute joint (the cam), `b` a slider (a translating
  follower) or a revolute joint (an oscillating one). `profile` is a joint
  origin on the side of `a` that turns: a planar face (its outer boundary)
  or curves of a sketch (`{"sketch": "F3", "curves": [...]}`: the profile
  they bound, the one sharing most of them, the largest with none). In the
  cam's fixed frame (the other side's frame) the profile lies square to
  the axis and turns by a's value. The follower's guide is the side of
  `b` on the part the cam turns against (else `b`'s own side `b`); a
  translating follower comes along its slide axis through its tip, from
  the side of the cam's axis its tip is on now; an oscillating one swings
  about its axis (along the cam's) from its arm pointing away from the
  cam's axis, toward the cam the way its arm is turned now. `follower`:
  `{"type": "knife"}` (default), `{"type": "roller", "radius": <size>}`
  or `{"type": "flat"}` (a sliding follower only). `tip`: the knife's
  point or the roller's centre on the follower (a joint origin; a roller
  picked by its round face is its own tip); without it a sliding follower's
  tip is its joint frame's origin; a swinging one needs it. Over one turn
  of the cam the follower stands where it first touches the profile (360
  samples, followed sample by sample for a swinging one; a jump off the
  profile is refused), its value there with its tip where it is now along
  its line (or arm): it touches the cam, `offset` added. Between samples a
  monotone cubic.
- Failures name the link and the cause: a joint not in effect, a coupling
  that does not fit its motions, a size that is not positive, a profile
  not on the turning part, not flat or square to the axis, a follower that
  misses the cam.

| Command | Fields | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `add_motion_link` | `a`, `b` (`joint` by uid or name, `motion`), `coupling` (occurrences of picked geometry by uids or names), `reverse`, `offset`, `as_built` (default: true but for a cam), `name`, `component` | `uid`, `name`, `parameters`, `state`, `solved`; without `offset` and with `as_built`, the offset that keeps the joints where they are at the marker (b's value less what the relation gives for a's); undo step `Add MotionLink1` |

`add_feature` and `edit_feature` take the definition as it is (its
offset as given, zero without one).

| Query | Fields | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `joints` | | also `links`: per link `uid`, `name`, `component`, `coupling`, `a` and `b` (`joint`, `name`, `motion`), `reverse`, `status`, `error`, `state` (`placed`, `satisfied`, `failed`, `suppressed`), `solved` (b follows a at the marker), `ratio` (a linear coupling's b per a), `offset`, `values` (`a`, `b` at the marker), `moved` |
| `motion_link_offset` | `a`, `b`, `coupling`, `reverse`, `component` (as `add_motion_link`) | `offset`: what `as_built` would give (Motion Link's panel) |

The `.solidcraft` import maps the file's motion links onto these
([.solidcraft import](#solidcraft-import), `core/import-solidcraft/docs/solidcraft.md`).

## Boundary Fill

A `boundary_fill` feature (mitcad#457; `features/boundary_fill.rs`,
`Kernel::boundary_cells`, `geometry/src/boundary_fill.cpp`) makes solids
of the cells that tool bodies enclose, with `add_feature` and
`edit_feature`, preview, Undo and persistence:

```json
{"type": "boundary_fill", "tools": ["F2.b0", "F4.b0"], "cells": [[15, 15, 15], [5, 5, 5]],
 "operation": "new_body", "remove_tools": false}
```

- The tools' faces divide space into cells; a cell is all of the space
  inside every tool that holds its point and outside every other tool
  (several solids where that space falls apart). `cells` gives a point
  inside each cell to fill, in the coordinates of the feature's
  component. Two points in one cell fill it once, with a warning.
- `operation`: `new_body` (a body per cell, in the order of the points,
  `<feature>.b<i>`), `new_component` (the same in a new component), or
  `join`, `cut` and `intersect`: the cells together are one tool that
  works on `participants` as an extrusion's tool does (none: all bodies
  of the component, the tools that stay among them; a cut that splits a
  body makes bodies of the pieces, [Body ids of a split's
  pieces](#body-ids-of-a-splits-pieces)).
- `remove_tools` takes the tools out of the design before the operation;
  a removed tool cannot be a participant. Without it the tools stay as
  they are.
- Names: a cell's faces are pieces of the tools' faces and keep their
  names (`F2:top`, pieces of one face side by side merged again, others
  numbered `#k`), as a boolean keeps them; the fill gives no names of
  its own.
- Refused: no tools, a tool listed twice, no points, participants of a
  new body. Failures: a point inside no tool (`the point (50, 50, 50) is
  inside no tool body: no enclosed cell there`) or on a tool's boundary,
  a mesh body as a tool, a join, cut or intersection that reaches no
  participant.

Tests: `core/model/src/boundary_fill_tests.rs` (mock kernel),
`geometry.boundary_fill` (`geometry/tests/test_boundary_fill.cpp`, OCCT),
`cli.boundary_fill` (`tools/cli/tests/boundary_fill.json`, saved and
opened again by `cli.boundary_fill_info`), and the `.solidcraft` test
design `boundary-fill` (`cli.import_solidcraft`).

## Convert Mesh

A `mesh_convert` feature (mitcad#462; `features/mesh_convert.rs`, the
conversion adapted from SolidCraft in
`third_party/solidcraft/mesh_convert.rs`) rebuilds a mesh body of one
profile extruded straight (a constant-section part from an STL or OBJ
file) as a solid of planar and cylindrical faces, with `add_feature` and
`edit_feature`, ordinary parameters, preview, Undo and persistence.

```json
{"type": "mesh_convert", "body": "F3.b0", "tolerance": 0.05}
```

`body` is a mesh body ([Mesh bodies in surface
operations](#mesh-bodies-in-surface-operations)); `tolerance` (mm,
0.000001 to 1; slot `tolerance`) is how far the rebuilt faces may lie
from the triangles. The body keeps its uid, name and appearance; the mesh
it was stays as the features before this one left it (suppressed or
deleted, the mesh body is back). Default name `ConvertMesh<n>`.

- The mesh: its vertices within a ten-millionth of its size (at most a
  hundredth of the tolerance) are one; it must be closed and consistently
  oriented (two triangles at every edge), enclose a volume, and have at
  most 50000 triangles.
- The direction: the triangles' normals, those covering most area first
  (at most 16 are tried). Along a direction the triangles at the lowest and
  the highest level are the caps; every other triangle must stand upright,
  the two caps' boundaries projected across the direction must be the same
  loops (at most 50, 8192 corners), and every vertex between the caps must
  lie on them. So a twisted, tapered or stepped mesh is no prism.
- The section: a loop of 12 or more corners on one circle, each chord at
  most 30 degrees and within the tolerance of its arc, is that circle (a
  cylindrical face); other loops are polygons without their corners in a
  line (planar faces). A fitted circle may not reach across another loop,
  and the section's volume must agree with the mesh's within the tolerance
  times the boundary's length and the height.
- The solid is the kernel's extrusion of the section, so its faces are
  named as an extrusion's after the feature: `<feature>:side(<segment>)`,
  `start(<region>)` at the low cap and `end(<region>)` at the high one. The
  section's edges are curves `c1`, `c2`, … loop by loop: an outer loop
  counter-clockwise from its lowest corner (smallest x, then y, in a frame
  whose x axis is the model axis least along the direction), its holes
  clockwise, a circle one curve (`F4:side(c1[c4,c2])`, `F4:side(c5)`).
- Refused, with nothing converted: a body that is no mesh body (`body
  F2.b0 (from Extrude1) is not a mesh body; …`), a tolerance out of range
  (also when adding or editing the feature), an open or inside-out mesh, a
  mesh over the budgets, and a mesh that is no prism (`the mesh is not a
  supported constant-section prism (one profile extruded straight); no
  geometry was converted`).

The `.solidcraft` import maps the file's mesh conversions onto it
([.solidcraft import](#solidcraft-import)). Tests:
`core/model/src/features/mesh_convert/tests.rs` (`core.model`: the
conversion on meshes built there, the feature on the mock kernel),
`cli.mesh_convert` and `cli.mesh_convert_reopen`
(`tools/cli/tests/mesh_convert.json`: an STL file's plate through the OCCT
kernel), the `.solidcraft` test design `mesh-convert`
(`cli.import_solidcraft`) and `solidcraft::tests` (`core.import`).

## Patch, Stitch and Thicken

Three features of surface (sheet) bodies (mitcad#456), with `add_feature`
and `edit_feature`, ordinary parameters, preview, Undo and persistence:
a patch fills sketch regions or a closed loop of a body's edges with new
surface bodies, a stitch sews bodies' faces into one body, a thicken makes
surface bodies solid. Their inputs are any surface bodies: patches, a
loft's `surface`, a `delete_face` that leaves the gap open, imported
surfaces; mesh bodies are refused ([Mesh bodies in surface
operations](#mesh-bodies-in-surface-operations)). None changes the bodies
it reads but those a stitch sews or a thicken joins, cuts or intersects.
The definitions are `features/patch.rs`, `stitch.rs` and `thicken.rs`,
the kernel's inputs `crate::surfaces`, the OCCT side
`geometry/src/surfaces.cpp`.

### patch

```json
{"type": "patch", "profiles": [{"sketch": "F1", "region": "r{c1[c4,c2],c2[c1,c3],c3[c2,c4],c4[c3,c1]}"}]}
{"type": "patch", "boundary": {"body": "F5.b0", "edges": ["E{F5:end(r{c1})|F5:side(c1)}", "..."],
 "continuity": "g1", "edge_continuity": [{"edge": "E{…}", "continuity": "g0"}],
 "points": [[10, 10, 24]]}}
{"type": "patch", "boundary": {"body": "F5.b0", "opening": {"faces": ["F3:patch(r{c1})", "F4:side(c2)"], "index": 0}}}
```

- `profiles`: regions of one sketch, as an extrusion's (a set); each is a
  new surface body of one planar face `<feature>:patch(<region>)`, its
  normal the sketch's.
- `boundary`: a closed loop of a body's edges, one new surface body of one
  face `<feature>:patch`. The loop is `edges` (named edges; every edge a
  name without `#k` resolves to) or `opening`: a loop of the body's free
  edges (edges of one face only, the open boundary of a surface body,
  which have no names of their own), the `index`-th (default 0) in the
  kernel's geometric order of those whose edges bound exactly the faces
  named in `faces`. The `open_boundaries` of a body are the kernel's
  (`Kernel::open_boundaries`: each loop's faces and points along it).
- How the patch meets the face beside each edge: `continuity` `g0` (the
  default: through the edge), `g1` (tangent to the face) or `g2` (tangent
  and of the same curvature); `edge_continuity` sets single named edges
  of the loop otherwise. `g1` and `g2` need the one face beside the edge:
  an edge between two faces is refused with them (`unsupported: …`).
  `points` (mm, the component's coordinates) are points the patch passes
  through.
- A loop in a plane that the patch only passes through (`g0` everywhere,
  no points) is filled by the plane; otherwise by a surface fitted to the
  edges (OCCT's `BRepFill_Filling`).
- Both may be given: the regions' bodies first (`<feature>.b0`, …), then
  the loop's. The body of the loop is not changed.
- Refused: neither regions nor a loop; both `edges` and `opening`; a
  continuity of an edge not in `edges`; an opening that is not there
  (`body F5.b0 (from Stitch1) has no opening along the faces …`, or fewer
  of them than `index`); edges that do not close up into one loop.

### stitch

```json
{"type": "stitch", "bodies": ["F2.b0", "F4.b0", "F6.b0"], "tolerance": 0.01}
```

The bodies' faces sewn together where their edges meet within
`tolerance` (mm; 0 for the kernel's own precision, 1e-6 mm). The first
body keeps its uid and becomes the sewn body: a solid where the faces
close up (a closed shell), else a surface body; the others are consumed.
The faces keep their names. Faces that meet nothing stay as they are, in
the same body. Refused: no bodies, a body twice, a negative tolerance.

### thicken

```json
{"type": "thicken", "bodies": ["F3.b0"], "thickness": 2, "symmetric": false,
 "operation": "new_body", "participants": []}
```

Each surface body (a solid is refused: `body F2.b0 (from Extrude1) is a
solid; Thicken makes surface bodies solid`) becomes solids by a wall
`thickness` thick along its faces' normals (their orientations applied),
against them when negative, or half of it to each side with `symmetric`.
The surface bodies stay. `operation` and `participants` are an
extrusion's; a join, cut or intersection without `participants` works on
every body but the thickened ones (and mesh bodies). New faces:
`<feature>:front(<face>)` on the side the face's normal points to,
`<feature>:back(<face>)` on the other, `<feature>:wall(<face>)` along
the face's free edges (`#k` several). Refused: a thickness of 0, a body
twice, a thickened body among the participants; the kernel fails where the
wall does not close up into a solid (a face curved more tightly than the
thickness, faces meeting at an inside corner the wall crosses).

Tests: `core/model/src/surface_tests.rs` (mock kernel: bodies, names,
refusals), `geometry/tests/test_surfaces.cpp` (`geometry.surfaces`: an
open box of five patches stitched, its opening patched and closed into a
solid, a fill through a point, the stitch tolerance, thickening to either
side and both, the input check on), the `.solidcraft` test design
`patch-stitch-thicken` (`cli.import_solidcraft`) and
`core/import-solidcraft/src/tests.rs`. The `.solidcraft` import maps
SolidCraft's patches, stitches and thickens onto these
([.solidcraft import](#solidcraft-import), `core/import-solidcraft/docs/solidcraft.md`).

## Surface modelling

Features that make and change surface (sheet) bodies (mitcad#455),
beside [Patch, Stitch and Thicken](#patch-stitch-and-thicken), with
`add_feature` and `edit_feature`, ordinary parameters, preview, Undo and
persistence. Their inputs are any surface bodies (and the faces of
solids where a family says so); mesh bodies are refused ([Mesh bodies in
surface operations](#mesh-bodies-in-surface-operations)). The kernel's
methods are grouped under "Surface modelling" in `Kernel`
(`core/model-base/src/kernel.rs`), the OCCT side is
`geometry/src/surface_*.cpp`. The application has them in the SURFACE tab
([app/COMMANDS.md](../../../app/COMMANDS.md), "Surface modelling").

### Surface extrude, revolve, sweep and loft

The solid features with `"surface": true` (`features/surface_sweeps.rs`):
walls without caps, new surface bodies, never joined or cut (the
operation is `new_body` or `new_component`, without participants).

```json
{"type": "extrude", "surface": true, "operation": "new_body",
 "profiles": [{"sketch": "F1", "region": "r{…}"}],
 "curves": {"sketch": "F1", "curves": ["c5", "c6"]},
 "extent": {"type": "distance", "distance": 15}}
{"type": "revolve", "surface": true, "operation": "new_body",
 "curves": {"sketch": "F3", "curves": ["c1"]}, "axis": "z", "extent": {"type": "full"}}
{"type": "sweep", "surface": true, "operation": "new_body",
 "curves": {"sketch": "F5", "curves": ["c1"]}, "path": {"sketch": "F6", "curves": ["c1"]}}
{"type": "loft", "surface": true, "operation": "new_body", "ruled": true, "sections": [
   {"type": "curves", "sketch": "F8", "curves": ["c1"]},
   {"type": "curves", "sketch": "F9", "curves": ["c1"]}]}
```

- `profiles`: the walls the regions' boundaries sweep: the solid
  feature's faces without its caps (`Kernel::open_faces` drops the faces
  `<feature>:start`, `end` and `mid`), so every option of the solid
  feature applies (two sides, tapers, up to an object, partial paths,
  guide rails and surfaces) and the walls keep its names,
  `<feature>:side(<segment>)`. A full revolution is a closed surface
  without caps.
- `curves`: sketch curves (of the profiles' sketch; `chain` adds the
  curves joined to them) in chains of curves that meet end to end, open
  or closed; each curve's wall is `<feature>:side(<curve>)` (`#k` pieces,
  e.g. along the curves of a sweep's path). An extrusion of curves takes
  distances (one side, two sides, symmetric, through all) and a start
  offset, not a taper, a start object or an end at an object; a
  revolution of curves angles, not an object; a sweep of curves its path,
  extent, orientation and flip, not a twist, taper, end scale, guide rail
  or guide surfaces (`Kernel::extrude_sheet`, `revolve_sheet`,
  `sweep_sheet`).
- With both, the profiles' walls are the first new body
  (`<feature>.b0`), the curves' walls the second.
- A loft's `curves` sections (`Kernel::loft_sheet`): every section a
  chain of one sketch's curves, all open or all closed, through which the
  surface runs in order, ruled or smooth, `closed` back to the first; no
  end conditions, centre line or rails. Its faces are
  `<feature>:side(<curve>)` after the first section's curves. A surface
  loft of profiles and faces is the loft's own `surface`.
- Refused: a join, cut or intersect; `curves` without `surface` (`only a
  surface extrusion sweeps sketch curves`); neither profiles nor curves;
  a thin surface extrusion; curves of another sketch than the profiles';
  a curve section beside sections of another kind.

The `.f3d` import brings surface extrusions, revolutions and sweeps
(`isSolid` false) in as these; the `.solidcraft` import SolidCraft's
SurfaceExtrude, SurfaceRevolve, SurfaceSweep and SurfaceLoft.

### Free edges

A surface body's open boundary is made of free edges (edges of one face
only), which have no names of their own (`E{a|b}` needs two faces). The
features that take free edges take them as `openings`
(`features/sheet_edges.rs`):

```json
"openings": [{"opening": {"faces": ["F3:side(c1)", "F3:side(c2)"], "index": 1},
              "faces": ["F3:side(c1)"], "at": [[10, 0, 5]]}]
```

- `opening`: a loop of free edges as [patch](#patch)'s `opening` names
  it: the `index`-th, in the kernel's geometric order
  (`Kernel::open_boundaries`), of those whose edges bound exactly
  `faces`. Left out: every opening of the body.
- `faces`: only the free edges that bound these faces; left out: all of
  the opening's.
- `at`: of those, only the edge nearest each point (mm, the component's
  coordinates; with an `opening` only); left out: all. A surface of one
  face has one loop of free edges, all bounding that face: the points
  pick some of them, as an import's picks do.

### offset_surface

```json
{"type": "offset_surface", "body": "F2.b0", "faces": ["F2:end(r{…})"], "distance": 2, "chain": false}
```

A new surface body of the faces (every face of the body when `faces` is
left out; with `chain` also the faces joined to them through smooth
edges) moved `distance` along their normals (the faces' orientations
applied; against them when negative; 0 copies them). Faces
`<feature>:offset(<face>)`. The body is not changed. OCCT offsets the
faces as one sheet (`BRepOffset_MakeOffset`, intersecting where
neighbours meet); a face curved more tightly than the distance fails.

### ruled_surface

```json
{"type": "ruled_surface", "body": "F2.b0", "edges": ["E{…|…}"], "openings": [],
 "face": "F2:end(r{…})", "distance": 3, "mode": "tangent", "angle": 0.5,
 "direction": [0, 0, 1], "flip": false, "corners": "mitre"}
```

A new surface body: strips `distance` wide (more than 0) off chains of
the body's edges (`edges` and the free edges of `openings` together, each
run of them joined end to end a chain, open or closed; none branches).
Each edge leaves the
face beside it (`face` where an edge lies between two faces), and the
strip goes
- `normal` (the default): along that face's normal;
- `tangent`: continuing the face, square to the edge, away from it;
- `angle`: at `angle` (radians) from the face's normal (or from
  `direction` when given), turned towards the tangent mode's direction;
- `direction`: along the fixed `direction`;

and the other way with `flip`. At a sharp corner of the chain the
neighbouring strips are `mitre`d (their ends lean to meet along the
corner's bisector) or joined by a `round` sector turned about the corner.
Faces `<feature>:ruled(<edge>)`, for a free edge `<feature>:ruled(<face>)`
after the face it leaves (`#k` pieces), and `<feature>:corner(<vertex>)`;
the strips are sewn into one body. Refused: no edges, a distance of 0 or
less, the direction mode without `direction`, the angle mode without
`angle`, a direction of no length; the kernel fails edges that branch
(three at a vertex) and an edge between two faces without `face`.

### extend_surface

```json
{"type": "extend_surface", "body": "F3.b0", "openings": [{"faces": ["F3:side(c1)"]}],
 "distance": 2, "mode": "natural"}
```

The surface body's faces extended `distance` (more than 0, along the
surface) past free edges (`edges` by name, or `openings`): `natural`
continues the surface (an analytic surface its parameter range, a
B-spline its polynomials), `tangent` leaves the edge tangent to it (G1),
`curvature` also with its curvature (G2; both by OCCT's
`GeomLib::ExtendSurfByLength`). The body keeps its id and its faces their
names: each extended face stays one face; the faces are sewn again where
they meet. A face is extended where it is bounded by its surface's
parameter range only (four sides, no holes), and each edge must run along
a side of that range (`unsupported: …` otherwise); a solid is refused.
Extending a whole periodic surface onto itself fails.

### trim_surface

```json
{"type": "trim_surface", "body": "F3.b0", "tool": "F4", "offset": 2, "extend": true,
 "keep": [[50, -1, 4]]}
{"type": "trim_surface", "body": "F3.b0", "tool": {"sketch": "F5", "curves": ["c1", "c4"]},
 "direction": [0, 0, 1], "keep": [[10, 5, 0]]}
```

A surface body cut by `tool` and only the pieces kept that the `keep`
points (mm, the component's coordinates; at least one) pick, the piece
nearest each. The tool is `split_face`'s
([Face features](#face-features-shell-draft-offset_face-delete_face-replace_face-split_body-split_face)):
a plane (moved `offset` along its normal), a face of any body (continued along its
surface with `extend`, the default), a body, or sketch curves, open or
closed, swept both ways along `direction` (the sketch's normal when left
out). Pieces are the faces cut apart and joined again where their edges
meet away from the tool. The body keeps its id and its faces their names
(`#k` for the pieces of one face). Refused: a solid (`Split Body divides
solids`), the body as its own tool, no keep point; the kernel fails a
tool that does not cut the surface apart.

### untrim_surface

```json
{"type": "untrim_surface", "body": "F8.b0", "face": "F8:end(r{…})", "holes": true,
 "outer": false, "in_place": false}
```

A face restored towards its surface: `holes` (the default) takes its
holes away, `outer` puts its outer boundary back at the surface's own
bounds (a surface without bounds, such as a plane or a cylinder, at the
face's span); at least one of them. The face may be of a solid or a
surface body; the result is a new surface body of one face,
`<feature>:untrim(<face>)`. With `in_place` the face of a surface body is
untrimmed where it is: the body and the face keep their names (a solid is
refused).

### unstitch

```json
{"type": "unstitch", "body": "F1.b0", "faces": ["F1:end(r{…})"]}
```

A body taken apart into surface bodies: each face in `faces` its own new
body (`<feature>.b0`, `.b1`, … in the order named) and the faces left one
surface body that keeps the body's id. Without `faces` every face comes
apart: the first stays the body, each other one a new body. A solid comes
apart into surfaces; the faces keep their names.

### reverse_normal

```json
{"type": "reverse_normal", "body": "F3.b0", "faces": []}
```

The surface body's faces in `faces` (every face when left out) turned
over: their normals point the other way, which decides the side
[thicken](#thicken), [offset_surface](#offset_surface) and the ruled
surface's normal mode go to. The body and the faces keep their names. A
solid is refused (its normals point out of its material).

### Chains of edges

Blend Surface, Boundary Surface and Match Surface take chains of a
body's edges: `body`, named `edges` and free edges of `openings` ([Free
edges](#free-edges)) that join end to end into one chain (open or
closed), and `face` (`target_face` for a match), the face beside the
chain where an edge lies between two faces (else each edge's one face;
needed for G1 and G2 only). The body may be a surface body or a solid;
it is not changed unless the feature says so.

### blend_surface

```json
{"type": "blend_surface",
 "from": {"body": "F2.b0", "openings": [{"opening": {"faces": ["F2:side(c1)"]}, "at": [[10, 0, 5]]}],
          "continuity": "g1", "bulge": 0},
 "to": {"body": "F4.b0", "edges": ["E{F4:bottom|F4:side0}"], "face": "F4:side0", "continuity": "g2"},
 "stitch": false}
```

A new surface body of one face `<feature>:blend` bridging the chains
`from` and `to` (both open or both closed; a closed pair starts the
second where it is nearest the first's start). Each end leaves its chain
through the edges (`g0`: straight towards the other end), tangent to the
face beside it (`g1`, the default) or also curved as it (`g2`), with a
speed of the chord between the chains times `1 + bulge` (`bulge` 0 the
plain bridge, more fuller, down to -0.9 flatter). The chains are sampled
by length (about a station a millimetre, 16 to 200) and the surface,
cubic across (quintic with a `g2` end), is fitted through the stations:
its edges lie within a few micrometres of the chains. With `stitch` the
blend is sewn onto both bodies within 0.01 mm, into `from`'s body, which
keeps its id; `to`'s body (when another) is consumed and no new body is
made.

### boundary_surface

```json
{"type": "boundary_surface", "boundary": [
   {"sketch": "F1", "curves": ["c1", "c2"], "continuity": "g1"},
   {"body": "F3.b0", "openings": [{"opening": {"faces": ["F3:side(c1)"]}}], "continuity": "g1"}]}
{"type": "boundary_surface", "u": [{"sketch": "F1", "curves": ["c1"]}, {"point": [5, 5, 10]}]}
{"type": "boundary_surface", "u": [{"sketch": "F1", "curves": ["c1"]}, {"sketch": "F1", "curves": ["c3"]}],
 "v": [{"sketch": "F1", "curves": ["c2"]}, {"sketch": "F1", "curves": ["c4"]}]}
```

A new surface body of one face `<feature>:boundary`. Each curve is a
chain of sketch curves (`sketch`, `curves`, `chain`), a chain of edges
([Chains of edges](#chains-of-edges)) or a `point`, one of them.

- `boundary`: a closed loop of curves in order (one closed chain, or
  chains end to end), filled (`BRepOffsetAPI_MakeFilling`). Each meets
  the face beside its edges, or along sketch curves the sketch's plane,
  with its `continuity` (`g0`, the default, `g1`, `g2`). No points.
- `u` (two or more) and `v` (none, or two or more): a network. Without
  `v` the surface is lofted through `u` in order, the first or the last
  of which may be a point (a cone-like patch); with `v` it runs through
  every curve each way (`GeomFill_Gordon`: a Coons patch of two each
  way), every `u` crossing every `v`. No continuity, no points.
- Refused: both forms, a curve of none or several kinds, a point in a
  loop or among crossing curves, one crossing curve.

### match_surface

```json
{"type": "match_surface", "body": "F5.b0", "face": "F5:side(c1)", "target": "F7.b0",
 "edges": ["E{F7:bottom|F7:side2}"], "target_face": "F7:side2", "continuity": "g2"}
```

A face of a surface body (`face`; left out: the body's only face) rebuilt
against a chain of `target`'s edges (another body): the side of the face
nearest the chain moves onto it, meeting the face beside the chain
through it (`g0`), tangent (`g1`) or also curved as it (`g2`, the
default), while the opposite side stays where it was. The face is
resampled with the changes fading across it (quintic blends, no change
at the opposite side) and fitted again, its slopes across held at both
sides. The face must be bounded by its surface's parameter range alone
(four sides, no holes; `unsupported: …` otherwise); a closed chain is not
supported. The body keeps its id and the face its name; its faces are
sewn again within 0.001 mm (neighbours along the moved sides come
apart). A solid is refused.

### fair_surface

```json
{"type": "fair_surface", "body": "F6.b0", "faces": ["F6:boundary"], "strength": 1, "iterations": 1,
 "keep_edges": true, "tolerance": 0.1}
```

The B-spline faces among `faces` (every face when left out) smoothed:
each step moves the inner control points `strength` (more than 0, at
most 1) of a damped bi-Laplacian step towards a net of less bending, for
`iterations` steps (1 to 1000), none farther than `tolerance` (a
parameter, mm, more than 0) from where it was. The boundary row of
control points stays, so the faces keep meeting their neighbours; with
`keep_edges` (the default) the row next to it stays too, so they keep
their tangents there. Faces of other surface types are fair already and
stay as they are; a faired face must be bounded by its surface's
parameter range alone. The body keeps its id and the faces their names.
A solid is refused.

The `.solidcraft` import maps SolidCraft's surface blend, boundary patch,
network, match and fair to these ([core/import-solidcraft/docs/solidcraft.md](../../import-solidcraft/docs/solidcraft.md)).

Tests (surface modelling): `core/model-tests/features-solid/src/surface_modelling_tests.rs`
(mock kernel), `geometry/tests/test_surface_modelling.cpp`
(`geometry.surface_modelling`, the input check on), the `.solidcraft`
test designs `surface-*` (`cli.import_solidcraft`, areas and boxes
through the OCCT kernel), `core/import-solidcraft/src/tests.rs`,
`tools/ui-surface-test.sh` and `tools/ui-surface-fill-test.sh` (the
SURFACE group on a hidden display).

## Plastic part features

Molded plastic parts' features (mitcad#459, `core/model/src/features/plastic.rs`):
a Boss, a Lip, a Groove, a Snap Fit and a Rest, each on a face of one body
which it joins (a groove cuts it), and the plastic rules they take their
defaults from. The application's Plastic Feature panel makes them all
([app/COMMANDS.md](../../../app/COMMANDS.md#notes-on-particular-commands)).

A boss, a snap fit and a rest stand on `point` of `face` of `body`: put on
the face's plane for a planar face, else the face's point nearest to it.
They grow along `direction` ([x, y, z]; default: out of the face). The
tools start a little inside the material (5 % of their height, 0.001 to
0.5 mm) so that they overlap the body; sizes are measured at the face,
and a draft (`draft_angle`, radians or an angle expression) narrows the
walls from there. Values left out take the defaults below.

### plastic_rule

```json
{"type": "plastic_rule", "rule_name": "ABS (1.5mm)", "material": "ABS Plastic",
 "thickness": 1.5, "draft_angle": "2 deg", "clearance": 0.1, "min_thickness": 1.2,
 "max_thickness": 3.5}
```

A molded part's design values; it changes no body. `thickness` is the
nominal wall; `nominal_radius` (default half the thickness), `clearance`
(0.1 mm), `knife_edge` (1 mm), `reveal_height` (0.5 mm),
`thickness_variation` (0.15 times the thickness), `draft_angle` (2
degrees), `min_draft_angle` (0.5 degrees), `min_thickness` and
`max_thickness` (no limit without). A boss, rest or groove names one by
its uid in `rule`: a left-out `draft_angle` of a boss or rest and a
left-out `gap` of a groove are the rule's draft and clearance, and the
feature warns when its draft is below the rule's `min_draft_angle`, or a
wall (a boss's around its hole, a hollow rest's) is outside the rule's
thicknesses. A suppressed rule is not used (a warning says so); a failed
one fails the features that name it. Refused: a thickness not above 0,
negative values, drafts of 85 degrees or more, a smallest thickness above
the largest.

### boss

```json
{"type": "boss", "body": "F1.b0", "face": "F1:top", "point": [30, 30, 3],
 "diameter": 10, "height": 12, "hole_diameter": 4, "hole_depth": 10,
 "draft_angle": "1 deg", "fillet": 1, "ribs": 4, "rib_thickness": 1.5,
 "rib_length": 6, "rib_offset": 2, "rule": "F2"}
```

A round post `diameter` across at the face, `height` high, narrowing by
its draft (default the rule's, else none). `ribs` (0 to 64, rounded; a
count in a length slot, as pattern quantities) stand round it from half
its radius out to `rib_length` past its wall (default its radius),
`rib_thickness` thick (default 0.3 times its radius), their tops
`rib_offset` below its top; the first along the direction × X (× Y for
a direction near X: +Y on a face facing up). `fillet` rounds the root
where the post meets the face (the post's wall only). The hole of
`hole_diameter` runs `hole_depth` down from the top (default: to the
face), straight. Faces: the post `side(c1)` and its top `end(r{c1})`, rib
k's sides `side(c<10+4k>…)`, the hole's wall `side(c2)` and its bottom
`start(r{c2})`, the root's rounds `fillet(<edge>)`. Refused: a draft that
closes the post before its top, a hole not inside the top. A boss cannot
be patterned or mirrored (its hole cuts after its post joins).

### lip, groove

```json
{"type": "lip", "body": "F17.b0", "face": "F18:offset_cap(F17:top)", "width": 1, "height": 2}
{"type": "groove", "body": "F20.b0", "face": "F21:offset_cap(F20:top)", "width": 1,
 "depth": 2, "gap": 0.1, "outside": true, "rule": "F2"}
```

A band along a planar rim face: along its largest opening (an inner loop
with no material over the face just inside it: the open end of a shelled
body), or along its outer edge with `outside`. A lip raises the band
`width` into the face and `height` up. A groove cuts it `width + gap` into
the face and `depth + gap` down, `gap` defaulting to the rule's clearance
(else 0), the cutter reaching as far past the edge so that none of its
walls lies on the body's. Corners stay sharp; lines and arcs stay lines
and arcs. Faces (`Kernel::rim_band`): `band_side(<edge>)` along the
offset into the face and `band_edge(<edge>)` along the face's edge they
follow, `band_top` and `band_bottom`. Refused: a face that is not planar,
one with no inner loop, one whose inner loops are the feet of features
standing on it ("not an opening"), one with two openings alike in size
(the second more than half the first's area), a band that does not fit.

### snap_fit

```json
{"type": "snap_fit", "body": "F15.b0", "face": "F15:top", "point": [20, 20, 4],
 "hook": [1, 0, 0], "length": 15, "thickness": 1.5, "width": 6,
 "catch_depth": 1, "catch_length": 3}
```

A cantilever arm `thickness` across (away from `hook`), `width` wide
(centred on the point) and `length` up from the face, its face on the
hook's side on the point; the catch at its tip sticks out `catch_depth`
towards `hook` (across the direction) over `catch_length` (shorter than
the arm), a triangle from its foot out to the tip. Faces `side(c1)` …
`side(c6)` round its side profile (c1 the arm's foot, c2 its face on the
hook's side, c3 and c4 the catch, c5 the tip, c6 its back), its ends
`start(…)` and `end(…)`. It can be patterned and mirrored.

### rest

```json
{"type": "rest", "body": "F10.b0", "face": "F10:top", "point": [430, 30, 3],
 "along": [1, 0, 0], "width": 10, "length": 20, "height": 4,
 "draft_angle": "2 deg", "thickness": 1, "rule": "F2"}
```

A pad centred on the point: round (`width` the diameter) or, with
`length`, a rectangle `length` along `along` (default the direction × X,
as a boss's first rib) and `width` across; `height` high, narrowing
by its draft (default the rule's, else none), solid or with `thickness` a
wall (thinner than half its width). Faces: its walls `side(c1)` …
`side(c4)` (round: `side(c1)`), its hollow's `side(c5)` … (`side(c2)`),
its top `end(…)`. Refused: a draft that closes it (or its wall) before its
top. It can be patterned and mirrored.

Tests: `core/model-tests/parts/src/plastic_tests.rs` (mock kernel),
`cli.plastic` (`tools/cli/tests/plastic.json`: analytic volumes, round
rims, the rules' defaults and warnings, refusals), the `.solidcraft` test
design `plastic` (`cli.import_solidcraft`) and `tools/ui-plastic-test.sh`.

## Body transfers

A `body_transfer` feature (mitcad#465, `features/body_transfer.rs`) moves
bodies of another component into its own component, an existing one, at
its point of the timeline. [Moving features into
components](#moving-features-into-components) moves the features that made
the bodies, as if they had been made in the destination; Create Components
from Bodies makes a new component of each body. A body transfer moves only
the bodies, from where it is on the timeline:

```json
{"type": "body_transfer", "bodies": ["F2.b0"],
 "link": {"source": "", "target": "O1"}}
{"type": "body_transfer", "bodies": ["F5.b0"],
 "link": {"source": "O2", "target": ""},
 "transform": [[0, -1, 0, 0], [1, 0, 0, 30], [0, 0, 1, 0]]}
```

- The feature belongs to the destination. `bodies` are all of one other
  component at that point (the source), each named by its id.
- The bodies keep their ids, display names, attributes (appearance,
  material, visibility) and the topological names of their faces; their
  geometry is converted once from the source's coordinates into the
  destination's, so that they stay where they are in the design. From
  then on they are the destination's: its later features work on them
  (in its coordinates), the source's no longer see them (`body F2.b0
  (from Extrude1) belongs to Bracket; a feature works on the bodies of its
  own component`), and a later Move of the destination's occurrence takes
  them along. A sheet-metal body keeps its sheet state, moved with it.
- `link` says where both components are seen, as the links of
  [Geometry of other components](#geometry-of-other-components): the
  occurrence path to the source (`source`) and to the destination
  (`target`, the first path to it when it does not lead there); empty
  paths are the root. The conversion is `placement(target)⁻¹ ·
  placement(source)` at the feature's point, so the bodies stay in place
  when placements before it change. `transform` (optional; rows of a
  rotation and a translation) is a fixed conversion used instead, as an
  import keeps the one its file records.
- Fails (as features do, with the reason) when a body is not the
  source's at that point, the source is the feature's own component, or
  the conversion is not rigid. Moves of features, reparented components
  and copies follow the link like the other links; Paste New and Make
  Unique copy or refuse a component that takes bodies in as they do one
  made from bodies (its bodies, as a base feature, are copied).

| Command | Fields | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `transfer_bodies` | `bodies`, `source_occurrence` (optional: where they are seen, the first path to their component by default), `destination`: `{"component": "C2" or a name, "occurrence": "O2/O4"}` (the occurrence path optional, as `source_occurrence`), `name` (optional) | `uid`, `name`, `component`, `component_name`, `bodies` |

`transfer_bodies` adds the feature at the marker in the destination, one
undo step `Move Body1 into Bracket` (`Move 2 bodies into Bracket`).
Refused, changing nothing, when the bodies are not of one component at
the marker, the destination is their component, a linked component or a
library part, the policy refuses it, or the transfer (or a feature that
worked before) would fail. Features after the marker are not computed:
one of the source that works on a moved body later fails when the marker
passes it, with the reason above.

| Query | Fields | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `transfer_bodies` | `bodies`, `source_occurrence` | `component`, `name` (the bodies' component), `source_occurrence`, `bodies` (`uid`, `name`), `destinations`: every placed component by occurrence path, the root first, as `move_to_component`'s rows (`component`, `name`, `occurrence`, `path`, `parent_occurrence`, `eligible`, `reason`) |

The `.solidcraft` import maps SolidCraft's body transfers onto it (the
file's feature is in its destination already): the link from the
components' first placements, and the conversion the file records as
`transform` only where the placements give another
([.solidcraft import](#solidcraft-import)). The `.f3d` import translates a
cut and paste of bodies into another component as this feature where Move
to Component cannot take the features that made them
(`core/import/docs/f3d-undecoded.md`, *Copies and cut and paste of bodies*). Tests:
`core/model-tests/assembly/src/body_transfer_tests.rs`, `cli.import_solidcraft`
(`core/solidcraft/tests/designs/body-transfer.solidcraft.json`),
`mitcad-import`'s `a_cut_and_paste_whose_features_cannot_go_transfers_the_body`.

## Drawings

`export_drawing` (mitcad#471, `api/drawing.rs`, `crate::drawing`) writes
the bodies at the marker as a drawing on a sheet: orthographic views with
hidden lines removed, the overall sizes of the views, the diameters of round
holes, a hole table with their threads and a title block, as a PDF, SVG, DXF or
DWG file. The views come from the kernel (`Kernel::project_view`: OCCT's
hidden line removal, `geometry/include/mitcad/geometry/drawing.hpp`), the
holes from `Kernel::round_holes`, their threads from the `threads` query.

```json
{"cmd":"export_drawing","path":"plate.pdf","bodies":["F2.b0"],
 "sheet":"A3","orientation":"landscape","scale":"fit","projection":"third_angle",
 "views":["front","top","right","iso"],"hidden_lines":true,
 "section":{"analysis":"Section1"},"title":"Plate","date":"2026-10-20"}
```

| Field | Default | What |
|---|---|---|
| `path` | | the file; its extension (`.pdf`, `.svg`, `.dxf`, `.dwg`) gives the format |
| `format` | by the extension | `pdf`, `svg`, `dxf` or `dwg` |
| `bodies` | the shown bodies | uids or names; each where the design shows it (every placement of a component's body) |
| `sheet` | `A4` | `A4` … `A0` (ISO 216), `ANSI_A` … `ANSI_E` |
| `orientation` | `landscape` | or `portrait` |
| `scale` | `fit` | `fit`: the largest ISO 5455 scale (50:1 … 1:1000) at which the views fit; or `"1:2"`, `"2:1"`, a number (paper per model length) |
| `projection` | `third_angle` | or `first_angle` (ISO 5456-2) |
| `views` | `["front","top","right"]` | any of `front` (from -Y), `top` (from +Z), `right` (from +X), `iso` (from the front, right and above); Z is up |
| `section` | none | a section view: `{"analysis": "<Section Analysis>"}` (where it cuts) or `{"origin": [x,y,z], "normal": [x,y,z]}`; what lies on the normal's side goes, the view looks against the normal |
| `hidden_lines` | false | hidden edges dashed (not in the isometric and section views) |
| `tangent_edges` | false | edges between faces that meet smoothly, thin |
| `dimensions` | true | the width and height of each orthographic view, and one callout per hole size (`4x Ø6.6 THRU`, `CBORE Ø11 DEPTH 6.8`, a tapped hole by its thread) |
| `sketch_dimensions` | false | the distances, lengths, radii and diameters of the sketches whose plane faces a view square on, in that view |
| `hole_table` | true | the holes each view shows end on, tagged per view (`A1`, `A2`, … `B1`), with X and Y from the view's lower left corner, size, depth and thread |
| `units` | the design's length unit | the unit of the values (`mm`, `in`, …) |
| `title` | `Untitled` | the design's name in the title block |
| `date` | today (UTC) | the date in the title block |
| `per_body` | false | a sheet per body: pages of one PDF, or SVG, DXF and DWG files `<name>-2.svg`, … |
| `exact` | true | exact edges; false: from a triangulation (quicker on large bodies; also the fallback when the exact projection fails, and for mesh bodies). Views of bodies with free-form faces (not planes, cylinders, cones, spheres or tori) come from a triangulation within a 2000th of the bodies' size either way, their edges as lines and arcs where they follow them within 1.5 times that, polylines elsewhere (mitcad#962: exact edges took half a minute a view on modelled threads) |
| `drawing` | none | a drawing kept in the design (`D1` or its name, *Drawings in the design*), written as it is: its sheets, views and title blocks; the fields above are then its own and refused, except `title` (where its sheets have none) |
| `sheet` | all | with `drawing`: one sheet's index (0 the first) |

Without `drawing` the export lays out a temporary drawing from the fields
above (`api/drawing.rs`, `auto_drawing`: each view a base view in the
grid below, the section a section view without a parent) and draws it as
a kept one is drawn, so the two give the same file; `add_drawing` with
`layout` keeps such a drawing in the design (File › Export Drawing).

The sheet (ISO 5457): a frame 20 mm from the left edge and 10 mm from the
others, the title block (ISO 7200) at the bottom right with the title, the
bodies, the scale, the units, the date, the sheet, the projection method
and its symbol; the hole table at the top right. Views go into a grid by the
projection method (third angle: the top view above the front view, the right
view on its right, the isometric view top right, the section right of the
right view; first angle the other way), aligned with each other, each with
room for its dimensions; the views are centred in what the title block and
the table leave. Lines after ISO 128 (visible 0.5 mm, hidden 0.35 mm dashed,
dimensions, leaders and tangent edges 0.25 mm, hatching 0.18 mm, the cutting
plane long dash dotted with its arrows and letter); dimensions after ISO 129
(30° closed filled arrowheads, text 3.5 mm above the dimension line, reading
from below or from the right); text in Helvetica (sans serif, as ISO 3098).
A hole is coaxial cylindrical faces with the material all round outside
them: the narrowest is its drilled wall, a wider cylinder or a cone that
meets it on the side it opens to its counterbore or countersink; an end is
closed when material lies on the axis within twice its diameter beyond it.
A view shows a hole end on when it looks along the axis from the side it
opens to (a hole open at both ends from either side).

Files: SVG in millimetres (`width="420mm"`), a `<g class="…">` per group:
`view` (`id="view-front"`, `view-top`, `view-right`, `view-iso`,
`view-section`), `dimension`, `sketch-dimension`, `hole-tag`, `hole-table`,
`hole-row` (`id` the tag), `hole-datum`, `section-line`, `view-label`,
`frame`, `title-block`. PDF 1.4, a page per sheet, the standard Helvetica
font in WinAnsi encoding (`Ø`, `°`), uncompressed. DXF (R2000) in paper
millimetres, a layer per kind of line: `VISIBLE`, `HIDDEN`, `THIN`, `HATCH`,
`SECTION_LINE`, `FRAME`, and `TEXT` (the writer has no dashed line types:
hidden edges are told apart by their layer; arrowheads are outlines). DWG
(R2000, `AC1015`, mitcad#728; `core/model-drawing/src/dwg.rs`) holds what the DXF file
holds, on the same layers, written by MitCad's own writer
(`core/dwg/src/write.rs`, [README](../../dwg/README.md#writer)): lines,
arcs, circles and single-line texts (a text of several lines as a text
per line) in model space, the sheet as the layout's paper and limits;
texts in code page 1252, other characters as `\U+XXXX`.

The answer: `path`, `format`, `files`, `sheets`, `pages` (of a PDF; 1
otherwise), `sheet`, `orientation`, `scale` (`"1:1"`, of the first sheet)
and `scales`, `views` (per sheet), `bodies` and `body_names`, `dimensions`,
`holes`, `hole_table_rows`, `units`, `polygonal` (a view came from a
triangulation) and `warnings` (a view that shows nothing, views that do not
fit at the given scale, rows the table had no room for, holes that could not
be found). Refused: an unknown format, unit, view or sheet, no views, a
listed body that is not at the marker, an unknown Section Analysis, no
bodies to draw. File IO (`classes.rs`); MCP's `model_export` writes one
with `format: "pdf"` or `"svg"` (or `"dxf"` with `drawing`), the options in
`drawing` (`docs/mcp.md`); `mitcad-cli export-drawing` runs it. Tests:
`geometry.drawing` (the views, section and holes of a counterbored block),
`core/model-tests/drawing/src/drawing_tests.rs` and `core/model-tests/drawing/src/dwg_tests.rs`, `core.dwg` (the DWG writer), `cli.export_drawing`, `app.ui-windows-drawing`.

## Gears

A `gear` feature (mitcad#472; `core/model/src/features/gear.rs` the
definition and its placement, `gear_profile.rs` the teeth, the kernel's
`gear_sweep` and `gear_cone` (`geometry/include/mitcad/geometry/gear.hpp`)
the solids, `api/gears.rs` the query and the command) makes a gear with
involute teeth from parameters. The application's Gear panel makes them
([app/COMMANDS.md](../../../app/COMMANDS.md#notes-on-particular-commands)).
Tests: `features::gear_profile` and `features::gear_tests`,
`features::seat_tests` (seated on shafts), `tools/cli/tests/gears.json`,
`tools/cli/tests/gears_link.json`, `tools/ui-gear-test.sh`, `tools/ui-windows-gear-test.ps1`.

```json
{"type": "gear", "kind": "helical", "plane": "xy", "center": [0, 0], "module": 2, "teeth": 20,
 "face_width": 10, "helix_angle": "20 deg", "backlash": 0.1,
 "bore": {"type": "plain", "diameter": 8}, "keyway": true, "hub": {"diameter": 20, "length": 8},
 "operation": "new_component"}
```

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| `kind` | `spur`, `helical`, `herringbone`, `ring` (internal), `rack`, `bevel` (straight) |
| `plane`, `center` | where the gear's axis meets its plane (the plane's normal), in the plane's coordinates; a rack's start. Not with `mesh_with` |
| `angle` | turns the gear about its axis (tooth 1 centred on the plane's x axis without it; a rack about its start). Not with `mesh_with` |
| `module`, `teeth` | the normal module (mm) and the number of teeth (a whole number, at least 5; a rack's at least 1) |
| `pressure_angle` | the normal pressure angle, 20 degrees without it (10 to 35) |
| `face_width` | along the axis (a bevel gear's along its pitch cone, less than half its cone distance) |
| `helix_angle`, `left_handed` | helical and herringbone gears (needed), helical rings and racks (optional): up to 45 degrees, right-handed unless `left_handed` |
| `gap` | a herringbone gear's gap between its halves, a groove a quarter module below the roots |
| `rim` | a ring gear's rim outside its roots (needed) |
| `height`, `length` | a rack's height from its back to its tips (needed), its length (at least, and without it, teeth times the pitch) |
| `shaft_angle`, `mate_teeth`, `pair` | a bevel gear's shaft angle (90 degrees), its mate's teeth (its own) and whether it makes the mate too |
| `backlash` | mm at the pitch circle: a tooth is thinner (a ring's space wider) by half of it, so two gears with the same value mesh with it (at most a quarter of the pitch) |
| `profile_shift` | x in modules, away from the axis (-1 to 0.8; a ring's teeth outwards) |
| `bore` | `{"type": "plain", "diameter": d}` or `{"type": "thread", "thread": {"designation": "M8x1.25"}}` (the size's minor diameter, its tap drill; `standard` as a thread's): spur, helical, herringbone and bevel gears, through the gear and its hub |
| `keyway` | a DIN 6885-1 (form A) keyway in a plain bore of 6 to 230 mm: the hub's width and depth for the bore's diameter, at the gear's `angle` |
| `hub` | `diameter` (optional, mitcad#656: without it the bore plus a 2 mm wall all round, or half the root diameter without a bore, at least 4 mm), `length`: on the end face (a bevel gear's back) |
| `mesh_with` | `{"gear": "F3", "angle": <angle>, "position": <length>}`: in the plane of an earlier gear feature of the same component, at their mesh's centre distance in the direction `angle` from its centre (from its plane's x axis), or `position` along a rack from the middle of its teeth, turned so that the teeth engage |
| `seat` | on a shaft instead of `plane` and `center` ([Seats on shafts](#seats-on-shafts), mitcad#578): spur, helical, herringbone and single bevel gears, not with `mesh_with`; a gear meshing with a seated one lies in its plane. Without `bore` the bore is plain, the shaft's diameter plus `bore_clearance`, and follows the shaft; a `thread` bore stays the thread's; a plain `bore` of its own is refused |
| `bore_clearance` | mm added to the shaft's diameter for a seated gear's plain bore (0 without it; a printed fit 0.2, say); only with `seat` and without `bore` |
| `operation`, `participants` | as an extrusion's |

- **Teeth:** the ISO 53 basic rack (profile A): addendum 1 m, dedendum
  1.25 m, root fillet 0.38 m (smaller where it does not fit). An external
  tooth is what that rack leaves rolling on the pitch circle: the flank is
  the involute of the base circle (a cubic B-spline within 1e-7 mm), the
  root the envelope of the rack's tip fillet, which also cuts the undercut
  of small tooth counts (below 17 at 20 degrees) into the flank. Helical
  teeth have the transverse rack's section (heights in the normal module)
  turned along the axis by the helix (a screw motion of the section's
  curves within about 1e-7 mm; the volume is the section's area times the
  width). An internal gear's space is an external tooth's shape with a
  circular root fillet, its tips at the base circle at least. A rack has
  straight flanks. A straight bevel gear follows Tredgold's approximation
  (ISO 23509 nomenclature): the virtual spur gear of z / cos(delta) teeth
  on the back cone, wrapped onto it, the teeth ruled to the apex and
  trimmed by the back and front cones; its pitch angle delta from the
  teeth, the mate's teeth and the shaft angle.
- **Faces:** tooth k (from 1, counter-clockwise about the axis) has
  `tip(k)`, `flank_a(k)` and `fillet_a(k)` on its clockwise side,
  `flank_b(k)` and `fillet_b(k)` on the other, `root(k)` after it (a
  rack's `root(0)` before its first tooth); the caps `start`, `end`, a
  herringbone gear's halves `#k` pieces; `rim`, `back`, `end_a`, `end_b`
  (a rack's back and ends), `back`, `front`, `back_cone`, `front_cone`
  (a bevel gear's), `bore`, `keyway_a`, `keyway_top`, `keyway_b`, `hub`,
  `hub_end`, `groove`.
- **Meshes:** the gears must share the module, the pressure angle and the
  helix angle; external helical gears have opposite hands, a ring and its
  pinion or a rack and its pinion the same. The centre distance takes the
  profile shifts' working pressure angle; a rack's reference line lies
  r + x m from its pinion's axis. A bevel gear meshes only through `pair`;
  two rings or two racks do not mesh. A gear's result keeps its frame as
  the mount `gear` (x, y and the axis as columns).
- **Joints and links:** gears made as components (`new_component`) turn
  on joints of their occurrences; `link_gears` couples two meshed gears'
  joints.

| Query | Fields | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `gear_values` | `uid` (a gear feature) or `def` (a definition as `add_feature` takes it, without `type`) | `kind`, `module`, `teeth`, `transverse_module`, `pressure_angle`, `circular_pitch`; `bore_diameter` (given, or a seated gear's from its shaft at the timeline marker, with `shaft_diameter` and the `seat` as `seat_frame` gives it); `hub_diameter` (given or worked out) and `computed` (`["hub_diameter"]` when worked out); `pitch_diameter`, `base_diameter`, `outside_diameter`, `root_diameter`, `tooth_thickness` (at the pitch circle), `undercut`, `form_diameter` (where the involute starts), `helix_angle`, `lead` (external gears); a ring's `inside_diameter`, `space_width`; a rack's `pitch_line_length`, `length`; a bevel gear's `pitch_angle`, `cone_distance`, `virtual_teeth`, `mate_teeth`, `mate_pitch_angle`, `shaft_angle`; `section_area` (the transverse section's, without bore and hub); with `mesh_with` `centre_distance`, `mate`, `ratio`, `pitch_radii`; `error` when the values make no gear |
| `gear_link` | `gear` | `command`: the `add_motion_link` `link_gears` would run, or `reason` why it cannot |

| Command | Fields | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `link_gears` | `gear` (a gear with `mesh_with`), `name` (optional) | as `add_motion_link`: a motion link between the joints the two gears' components' occurrences turn on (a rack's slides on), the mate's joint driving: `gear` (`internal` with a ring) by their pitch radii, or `rack_pinion` by the pinion's; `reverse` when a joint's axis runs against its gear's. Refused when a gear has no such joint, a joint's axis is not along its gear's, or the two are linked already |

The `.f3d` and `.solidcraft` imports can map their files' gears onto the
definition later; it is kept in the design file as it is.

## Pulleys

A `pulley` feature (mitcad#562; `core/model/src/features/pulley.rs` the
definition, its placement and the belt, `pulley_profile.rs` the grooves,
the kernel's `gear_sweep` the solids, `api/pulleys.rs` the query) makes a
timing belt pulley, a smooth idler or a toothed idler from parameters.
The application's Pulley panel makes them
([app/COMMANDS.md](../../../app/COMMANDS.md#notes-on-particular-commands)).
Tests: `features::pulley_profile` and `features::pulley_tests`,
`features::seat_tests` (seated on shafts), `tools/cli/tests/pulleys.json`,
`tools/ui-pulley-test.sh`, `tools/ui-windows-pulley-test.ps1`.

```json
{"type": "pulley", "kind": "toothed", "profile": "gt2_2mm", "plane": "xy", "center": [0, 0],
 "angle": 0, "teeth": 20, "belt_width": 6, "clearance": 1, "pitch_correction": 0,
 "flanges": {"sides": "both", "diameter": 18, "thickness": 1},
 "hub": {"diameter": 16, "length": 7},
 "bore": {"type": "plain", "diameter": 5}, "keyway": false,
 "set_screws": {"count": 2, "thread": {"designation": "M3x0.5"}, "position": 3.5},
 "operation": "new_component"}
```

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| `kind` | `toothed` (a pulley), `idler` (smooth, for the belt's back or as a tensioner), `toothed_idler` (teeth on a bearing bore) |
| `profile` | `gt2_2mm`, `gt2_3mm`, `htd_3m`, `htd_5m`, `t5`, `xl`: needed with teeth; optional for an `idler` (the belt's pitch, and the check that two pulleys share a belt) |
| `plane`, `center` | where the axis meets its plane (the plane's normal), in the plane's coordinates. Not with `belt_with` |
