feature control frames and surface finish symbols on a drawing's views,
and text notes on its sheets (mitcad#707 phase 2;
`core/model/src/drawing/annotate_def.rs`, `core/model-drawing/src/annotate.rs`,
`api/drawing_annotations.rs`). One
engine with the annotations of the model (*Annotations*, mitcad#702): a
dimension's value is written by the same code, with its prefix (Ø, R),
decimals, own text (`format`: `decimals`, `prefix`, `before`, `after`,
`replace`), tolerance (`tolerance`: `symmetric`, `deviations`, `limits`
or an ISO 286 `fit` code) and the same checks; a datum label's letter and
a frame's `frame` are those of *Datums and feature control frames*.

**Picks are model topology seen through the view.** A pick is
`{"body", "occurrence", "edge" | "face", "point"}`: a body the view shows,
where an occurrence places it (a path from the drawing's component;
none for its own placement), and one of its edges or round faces by its
topological name, or a point of an edge (`"start"`, `"end"`, `"center"`:
a circle's centre, a straight edge's middle; a round face's `"center"`:
its axis). Commands take a pick, or a sheet point (`[x, y]`, mm) where
the view's nearest pick is found: the bodies' named edges
(`Kernel::edge_geometries`) and round faces (`Kernel::face_geometries`,
cylinders, their ends the body's circles on their axis), projected as
the view sees them (a circle end on as a circle, from the side as its
diameter; a round face from the side as its axis between its ends); an
edge's end or a circle's centre within 2 mm of paper first, else an edge
or face within 3 mm, of what the type wants (an ordinate a point, a
circle's rim or a round face giving its centre; an angle a straight
edge; a radius, a diameter and a centre mark a circle or a round face).
A view sees what it shows (mitcad#717): an edge's part nearest the click
must lie inside a detail's circle and outside a break's band (a long edge
across a band or into a detail is picked where it shows); a section sees
what lies behind its plane (an edge in front of it is no pick, one across
it is cut there) and picks a planar face where its plane cuts it (the
cut face's edge in the face's plane, `{"body", "face"}`, found again on
every draw among the projection's cut faces). Picks as near as one
another (within 0.25 mm of paper) are told apart by the view: the one
the projection draws as a visible line first, then the one nearest the
eye. An arc is where it is (seen end on its range of angles, from the
side its reach), and a whole circle has no start or end to pick. A round
face reaches between the circles of its own edges (not those of another
face on its axis). Whenever the
sheet is drawn each pick is found again by its name
(`Kernel::edge_geometry`, `Kernel::face_geometry`), so the annotation
follows the model; one that is gone (its body no longer shown by the
view, its edge or face not in the body, a face that is not round) makes
the annotation **broken**: it is not drawn or exported, the `drawing`
query says why and gives it a small box beside its view, and the sheet's
warnings say `annotation 2 on view 3: the face F4:side(c1) of Body1 is
gone`.

| Command | Fields | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `add_drawing_annotation` | `drawing`, `view`, `type` (below), `picks` (picks or sheet points), `along`, `at` (a sheet point: a dimension's line and text there, a leader's text, a symbol), `format`, `tolerance`, `text`, `letter`, `frame`, `finish`, `series`; a text note: `"type": "text"`, `sheet` (0), `at`, `text`, `height` (3.5 mm) | `annotation` (its id), `annotations` (all of a series); undo step `Add dimension 3 to Drawing1`, `Add note 4 to Drawing1`, `Add 2 dimensions to Drawing1` |
| `edit_drawing_annotation` | `drawing`, `annotation`, and what changes: `move` (`[dx, dy]`, a drag on the sheet), `at`, `picks` (drawn afresh), `along`, `format` (the fields that change; `null` back to the default), `tolerance` (`null`: none), `text`, `letter`, `frame`, `finish`, `line_offset`, `text_offset` (`null`: the default); a text note's `text`, `at`, `move`, `height` | undo step `Move dimension 3 of Drawing1` (a move alone) or `Edit dimension 3 of Drawing1` |
| `delete_drawing_annotation` | `drawing`, `annotation` or `annotations` | `deleted`; undo step `Delete annotation 3 of Drawing1` |

| `type` | Picks | Shows |
|---|---|---|
| `linear` | two | the distance of the picks along the view's x (`"along": "horizontal"`), its y (`"vertical"`; from the picks when left out: the axis they lie further apart along) or `"aligned"` (square to a straight edge picked, else along the line between them); a straight edge stands for its middle, its extension line starts at its end nearer the dimension line |
| `angle` | two straight edges | the angle between them as seen, an arc about their corner (refused for parallel ones) |
| `radius`, `diameter` | a circle or a round face | its true radius or diameter: end on, a line from the centre (across for a diameter) to the rim, run on to the text on a shoulder; from the side, a linear dimension across it |
| `ordinate` | an origin and a point | the point's coordinate from the origin along the view's x or y (`along`), on a leader to the origin's level |
| `center_mark` | a circle seen end on, or a round face from the side | crossed centre lines beyond the rim, or the face's centreline |
| `centerline` | a round face, two circles or points, or two parallel edges | the axis; the line through the centres; the line halfway between the edges, over both |
| `note` | one | `text` (lines split at `\n`) on a shoulder, a leader to the pick's point nearest where it was clicked |
| `datum` | one | the letter (`letter`; the first one neither the drawing's datum labels nor the model's have) in a square on a leader ending in a filled triangle |
| `frame` | one | `frame`'s cells (the characteristic's symbol drawn as lines, the zone, the datums) on a leader |
| `finish` | one | ISO 1302's symbol on the surface: `finish` `{"process": "any" \| "removal" \| "no_removal", "text": "Ra 1.6"}` |

Places are kept in millimetres of paper, relative to the picks, so an
annotation keeps its look at any scale and moves with its view and the
model: `line_offset` (a linear dimension's line across from the middle
of its picks, an ordinate's level from its origin, an angle's arc
radius; when left out, a linear dimension's line goes 10 mm beyond the
view's box on the side of its picks), `text_offset` (along and across a
dimension line; a leader's text, a datum's square, a frame, a symbol from
the arrow's point: 10, 8 by default; a circle's text from its centre),
`at` (where a leader's pick was clicked, in view millimetres). `series`:
`"baseline"` makes a linear dimension from the first pick to each other
one, their lines 7 mm apart; `"chain"` from each to the next, in a row.
An angle's arc keeps a radius of 2 mm at least, whether dragged, placed
or given as `line_offset`.

**Pictorial views** (an isometric view, a projected view from a
corner, any view that does not look along an axis of its component, and
their details; mitcad#717): lengths along the view's x or y, ordinates
and angles would be foreshortened, so a horizontal or vertical linear
dimension, an ordinate and an angle are refused there (and drawn broken
when a file has one); a linear dimension is aligned there unless told
otherwise and measures the true distance of its picks' points in 3D (a
straight edge's middle, a circle's centre); radii and diameters are true
anyway. A base view along a given direction (not a standard one) that
looks square at a planar face of a body it shows, and its details, are
orthographic for the annotations whose picks all lie on such bodies
(mitcad#718, mitcad#722); the isometric presets and the corner views stay
pictorial whatever face they look square at. An aligned dimension on any
view along no axis keeps measuring its picks' true distance in 3D (in
the face's plane the same as the projected one), so a file's aligned
dimensions keep their values.

**Datum letters** are one set for the model and its drawings: a datum
label of a drawing takes the first letter that neither the model's nor
any drawing's datum labels have and no frame refers to (the model's
`next_datum_letter`, which counts the drawings' too), and a letter in use
anywhere is refused (`datum A exists: DatumA`, `datum B exists: a datum
label of Drawing1`), in the model as on a drawing. An edit that keeps an
annotation's letter is no new claim (a file where two drawings share a
letter edits as before). A copy of a component (Paste New, Insert
Component as a copy) gives its drawings' datum labels the next free
letters where theirs are in use in the design, and their frames refer
to the new letters (mitcad#718). A datum's new letter reaches every frame
that refers to its old one, in the same undo step (mitcad#745): a model
datum's (`edit_annotation` with `letter`) the model's frames and every
drawing's, a drawing datum's (`edit_drawing_annotation` with `letter`)
its own drawing's frames, the other drawings' and the model's. A frame,
of the model or of a drawing, warns of a datum no label has only when
neither the model nor any drawing has that label.

**Views.** `add_drawing_view` and `edit_drawing_view` take
`center_marks` (on when a view is added: a centre mark on each circle
the view sees end on that turns half way round at least, a half hole's
too, concentric ones once, and a centreline on each round face it sees
from the side whose ends do; inside a detail's circle, outside breaks
and behind a section's plane only) and `retrieved_dimensions` (off: the
dimensions of the sketches that shape the bodies the view shows (those
of the features that made or name them, and of their components'
features that neither make nor name a body), seen square on, where the
view shows them (behind a section's plane, in a detail's circle, beside
breaks), written by #702's engine; the root's drawings; not on pictorial
views). A component's sketch dimensions are drawn where its occurrences
put them: once for each placement of its bodies the view shows, through
that occurrence's transform (mitcad#744; a sketch of the drawing's own
component that made a body of another component where it is), and the
square-on test and the section, detail and break filters take them
there; the sheet's `sketch_dimensions` place them the same way. A sketch
dimension a view retrieves is not drawn again by the sheet's
`sketch_dimensions`. A view's deletion takes its annotations along.

The `drawing` query's sheet asked for has `annotations`: each view
annotation in its file form with `view`, `broken`, `label` (its words on
one line: `40 ±0.1`, `Ø10 H7`, a note's lines joined by ` / `, a datum's
letter, a frame's cells joined by ` | `), `value` (a dimension's, mm or
radians), `warning` (a fit code out of range, a datum referred to that no
label has), `box` (on the sheet), or `error`; then the text notes
(`"type": "text"`, `text`, `at`, `box`). Views list `center_marks`,
`retrieved_dimensions` and their annotations' ids. Groups: `dimension`
(`id` `A3`), `center-mark`, `note`, `datum`, `feature-control-frame`,
`surface-finish`, `retrieved-dimension`. The export draws them and counts
the dimensions in its `dimensions`.

The `drawing_pick` query (`drawing`, `sheet` (0), `view` (the smallest
drawn view there when left out), `at`, `type` or `want`: `any`, `point`,
`line`, `circle`) gives the pick a click there makes: `view`, `pick`,
`seen` (`point`, `line`, `circle`, `axis`), `at` (its point on the
sheet) and `items` to show it (`{"point"}`, `{"line"}`, `{"circle":
{"center", "radius"}}`, `{"arc": {"center", "radius", "start", "end"}}`,
sheet mm), or `"pick": null`. The `drawing` query also gives
`datum_letters`: the letters of the model's and every drawing's datum
labels, what a frame can refer to.

Files: a view's `annotations` (`id`, `type`, `picks`, `along`,
`line_offset`, `text_offset`, `at`, `format`, `tolerance`, `text`,
`letter`, `frame`, `finish`), `center_marks`, `retrieved_dimensions`; a
sheet's `notes` (`id`, `text`, `at`, `height`); left out when empty or
off. Ids are unique among a drawing's annotations and notes; a drawing's
datum letters too. A component's copy maps its drawings' picks (bodies,
occurrences, the features in edge and face names).

Classes: the commands and `drawing_pick` are the model's. Tests:
the tests in `core/model-drawing/src/annotate.rs` (measures, layouts, checks, symbols),
`core/model-tests/drawing-views/src/drawing_annotation_tests.rs` (dimensions by names and by clicks with
tolerances and fit codes, the model changed under them, drags, broken
ones, a diameter end on and from the side, centre marks automatic and on
request, an ordinate, notes, datum labels, frames, finish symbols, text
notes, a baseline, the file, the export, refusals), `tests/drawing_tools.cpp`,
`tools/ui-drawings-test.sh`, `tools/ui-windows-drawings-test.ps1`, and
`core/model-tests/drawing-views/src/pick_tests.rs` (mitcad#717: a section's picks behind its plane and
of the faces it cuts, picks across breaks and into details, edges on one
another told apart by the eye, arcs and whole circles, a pictorial view's
refusals and aligned dimension in 3D, an angle's radius kept, a round
face's own ends and a half hole's centre mark, datum letters shared with
the model, a component's copied drawing's picks, retrieved dimensions of
the view's own bodies once), and `core/model-tests/drawing-views/src/model_follow_tests.rs` (a new
sheet without the last one's text notes, mitcad#742; views, dimensions
and balloons following an occurrence moved to another parent, and a
component's drawing refusing a move out of it, mitcad#743; retrieved
dimensions of a translated component and of one placed twice,
mitcad#744; datum letters changed in the model and on a drawing reaching
every frame, mitcad#745).

## Tables on drawing views

Hole tables, parts lists and balloons on a drawing's views (mitcad#707
phase 3; `core/model/src/drawing/tables_def.rs`,
`core/model-drawing/src/tables.rs`, `api/drawing_tables.rs`).
Each is an annotation of its view (*Annotations on drawing views*): it
takes the same commands, is kept, saved, undone, compared and copied
with a component as the others are, and a view's deletion takes it
along. Its rows are worked out from the model whenever the sheet is
drawn, so it follows the design.

| `type` | Picks | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `hole_table` | none, or one point: its origin | the round holes of the bodies the view shows that the view sees end on (`Kernel::round_holes`, with the threads of the `threads` query, as File › Export Drawing finds them), where it shows them (in a detail's circle, beside breaks, behind a section's plane), tagged in the view beside each hole and listed |
| `parts_list` | none | the components the view shows, each once with how many of its occurrences the view shows; numbered |
| `balloon` | one: an edge or a face of a component's body | that component's number in a parts list, in a circle on a leader to the pick |

`add_drawing_annotation` takes a table's place, `at` (its upper left
corner on the sheet, mm; needed), and `table`, its settings:

- `columns`: the columns shown, in order. A hole table's: `tag`, `x`,
  `y`, `size` (`Ø6.6`, with a counterbore or countersink), `depth`
  (`THRU` or the depth), `thread` (the designation, `-` without). A
  parts list's own: `item`, `quantity`, `name` (a library part's
  designation, else the component's name), `part_number`, `description`
  (the property `Description`), `material` (the computed `Material`);
  any other column is a property of the components, `Key` or
  `Set/Key`, as the `parts_list` query's `properties` give them (its
  header the key in capitals). Left out: all of a hole table's; `item`,
  `quantity`, `name`, `description`, `material` of a parts list's.
- `sort` (a column; a hole table's tags, a parts list's names when left
  out or `null`) and `descending` (false): numbers first, by value, then
  tags by their letters and numbers, then other text alphabetically
  (cells alike in that order by their texts as they are). A table sorts
  by a column it does not show too (mitcad#718). A parts list is
  numbered in that order; sorted by `item`, it is numbered by name and
  `descending` lists it from the last number up.
- A hole table's `tags`: `by_size` (default: a letter per size, depth
  and thread, A, B, … without I, O and Q, then AA, AB, …, and a number
  per hole of it along the view's x and then y: A1, A2, B1) or `numbers`
  (1, 2, … in that order); `origin` when it has no pick: `corner`
  (default: the view's lower left corner, marked with a cross) or `model`
  (the drawing's component's origin). Its X and Y are measured along the
  view's axes from its origin, in the sheet's unit; a picked origin is a
  point of the model, found again on every draw.
- A parts list's `levels`: `top` (default: the components of the
  occurrences right below the view's subject: a view of an occurrence
  lists what is in it, as do its balloons) or `parts` (the components
  whose bodies the view shows, at any depth); the bodies of the drawing's
  own component are rows of their own (their name and material). On a
  section, a detail or a broken view it lists only the bodies the view
  shows something of: those whose own projection keeps a line behind
  the plane, inside the circle or beside the breaks (mitcad#718).
- `title`: over the table; `HOLES (mm)` (the sheet's unit) and `PARTS
  LIST` when left out or `null`.

A parts list added with `"balloons": true` (false when left out;
mitcad#725) places a balloon on each of its rows in the same undo step
(`Add parts list 6 and 2 balloons to Drawing1`): on the first straight
edge, drawn as a visible line, of the row's bodies that the list counts
(on a section, a detail or a broken view those it shows something of);
their circles in one column 15 mm right of the view's box, 12 mm apart
from its top down, the highest arrow first, so that they cover neither
one another nor the view (`text_offset`). A row whose bodies show no
such edge gets none.
The result lists their ids, `balloons`; `balloons` on another type is
refused.

`edit_drawing_annotation` takes `table` with what changes, `picks` (a
hole table's origin; `[]`: none), and `move` or `at` (a table's place on
the sheet: whatever its picks); undo steps `Add hole table 5 to
Drawing1`, `Edit parts list 6 of Drawing1`, `Move balloon 7 of Drawing1`.
A balloon is dragged as a note is: its circle's place is kept from its
pick (`text_offset`, 12, 10 mm when left out), so it moves with its
component.

A balloon's number is its component's row (by the parts list's
`levels`): in a parts list of its own view first, else of another view
of its sheet. A balloon whose pick is gone (its occurrence deleted, its
body no longer shown) or that no parts list of its sheet lists is
**broken** (`no parts list on the sheet lists Pin`). Refused: a table
without its place, a hole table's unknown column, a sort column a table
does not have, a parts list's tags or origin, a hole table's levels,
`table` on another type, and a hole table on a pictorial view (it sees
no hole end on). A base view along a given direction that looks square
at a planar face of a body it shows counts as orthographic, as one along
an axis does: its lengths in that face's plane are true (mitcad#718;
for the annotations on such bodies, mitcad#722). On a section, a detail
or a broken view, which bodies a parts list counts and a body's own cut
faces (picks) come from each body's own projection there, kept in a
bounded cache of their own by the body's version and placement and the
view (mitcad#722), apart from the views' projections. A
placed body's holes are kept in the document's projection cache by its
shape version, placement and threads, so a sheet drawn again finds them
once; a search that fails is not kept, so it is tried again on the next
draw and its warning names the body as it is then (mitcad#722).

The `drawing` query's entry of a table has `columns` (shown), `available`
(`column` and `header`: its type's own and a parts list's property
columns shown), `sort`, `rows` (how many) and `label`: a hole table's
rows' cells (`A1 20 15 Ø6.6 THRU -; A2 60 5 Ø6.6 THRU -`, `no holes`),
a parts list's numbers, names and quantities (`1 Pin x1; 2 Plate x2`,
`no components`), a balloon's number. Groups: `hole-table` (its title,
cells, tags at their holes and its origin's cross), `parts-list`,
`balloon`, each `A<id>`; the export writes them (PDF, SVG, DXF). File ›
Export Drawing keeps its own sheet-wide hole table (`annotations`'
`hole_table`: every orthographic view's holes, tagged per view), which
is not one of these.

Files: an annotation's `table` (`place`, `columns`, `sort`,
`descending`, `tags`, `origin`, `levels`, `title`; each at its default
left out).

Classes: the model's. Tests: those in `core/model-drawing/src/tables.rs` (a table drawn,
its settings checked, cells sorted), `api::drawing_tables::tests`
(size letters), `core/model-tests/drawing/src/table_tests.rs` (a hole table's tags, rows,
origins, columns, sort and title, its origin following the model, moved,
saved, undone, holes gone; refusals; a parts list of an assembly's view
with balloons, sorted the other way and a property column, a placement
deleted and undone, a balloon without its list, the export, a parts list
that places its balloons, mitcad#725),
`core/model-tests/drawing-views/src/follow_up_tests.rs` (mitcad#718: hole tables on section, detail
and broken views; two parts lists on one sheet and their balloons; a
section's parts list; a hidden sort column and the item sort; a view
square to an inclined face; a copied component's drawing with tables,
balloons and re-lettered datum labels; an unchanged letter on a shared
file; the caches of geometry and holes; tables in PDF and DXF),
`tests/drawing_tools.cpp`, `tools/ui-drawings-test.sh` (a hole table on a
top view that empties when the hole is suppressed; a parts list with its
balloons, undone; a parts list and a balloon on an assembly, exported, the list following a deleted placement
and its balloon broken), `tools/ui-windows-drawings-test.ps1` (a parts
list and a balloon).

## Drawing templates and revisions

Sheet templates and revision tables of drawings (mitcad#707 phase 4;
`core/model/src/drawing/template_def.rs`, `core/model-drawing/src/template.rs`,
`api/drawing_templates.rs`). A
**template** is data: the frame's margins, the title block's size, lines
and fields, where the projection symbol goes, and a revision table above
the block. A sheet keeps a complete copy of the template it was given
(`template` in the file), so a drawing looks the same wherever its
design goes and a library change never changes it; a sheet without one
keeps the simple title block of File › Export Drawing.

Templates come from three places:

- **built-in**: `iso` (A sizes, A3 to start with; 20 mm filing margin,
  10 elsewhere; a 180 x 36 mm block) and `ansi` (ANSI sizes, B to start
  with; 12.7 mm margins; a 178 x 40 mm block), the JSON files in
  `core/model-drawing/src/templates/`;
- **user**: `drawing-templates/<id>.json` in the user's library folder,
  beside its materials and print profiles (`print_library::user_library`,
  `MITCAD_PRINT_LIBRARY_DIR`);
- **project**: `drawing-templates/<id>.json` in the project's library
  folder (`<project>/print-library`), versioned with the project.

A template file: `{"format": "mitcad-drawing-template", "id", "name",
"size" (the sheet a drawing made with it starts with), "projection" (its
projection method, `first_angle` or `third_angle`; ISO first, ANSI third;
mitcad#725), "margins": [left,
bottom, right, top], "title_block": {"width", "height", "lines": [[x0,
y0, x1, y1], …], "fields": [{"label", "text", "at": [x, y], "size": [w,
h], "height"}], "projection_symbol": [x, y]}, "revision_table": {"rows":
4}}`, lengths in mm from the block's lower left corner; the id is the
file's name. A field's label is written small in its cell's upper left
corner, its text at the bottom, made smaller down to 2 mm and then cut
when it is too wide. Names in braces in a text are filled in from the
design whenever the sheet is drawn, so the block follows the design:

| Name | Value |
|---|---|
| `title` | the sheet's title (`title_block.title`), else the component's or the design's name (the `drawing` query's `title`) |
| `name` | the component's or the design's name |
| `drawing` | the drawing's name |
| `number` | the sheet's drawing number, else the component's part number |
| `part_number`, `description` | the component's properties `Part number`, `Description` |
| `material` | the component's property `Material`, else the materials of the bodies it shows, each once: a body without its own takes the nearest default up its path from the component, then the component's and those above it where it is first placed, then the root's (mitcad#758) |
| `mass` | the component's property `Mass` (stored or its library's, not the one worked out; mitcad#722), else the bodies the component shows, each where it is placed: their volumes (kept by shape version) times their materials' densities, in the design's mass unit |
| `author` | the sheet's (`title_block.author`), else the property `Author` |
| `date` | the sheet's, else today's |
| `scale` | the sheet's first base view's |
| `sheet`, `sheet_number`, `sheets` | `1/2`, `1`, `2` |
| `size`, `units`, `projection` | `A3` (`ANSI B`), the length unit, `THIRD ANGLE` |
| `revision` | the latest revision's letter, `-` before the first |
| any other | a property of the drawing's component, `Key` or `Set/Key` (empty without one) |

Commands and the query:

| Command | Fields | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `add_drawing`, `add_drawing_sheet`, `edit_drawing_sheet` | `template`: a built-in one's id (`iso`, `ansi`), a template's data as `drawing_templates` lists it (a user's or a project's), or `""`/null for the simple title block; `add_drawing` takes the template's `size` and `projection` unless they are given (not a `layout`'s projection: its views are placed by it; mitcad#725); a new sheet takes the last sheet's template | as before |
| `add_drawing_revision` | `drawing`, `description` (needed), `letter` (the one after the latest: A, B, … without I, O, Q, then AA), `date` (today's), `author` | `revision`; undo step `Add revision A to Drawing1` |
| `edit_drawing_revision` | `drawing`, `revision` (its letter), and what changes: `letter`, `description`, `date` (`""`: today's, as for a new one, mitcad#722), `author` (`""` clears) | undo step `Edit revision A of Drawing1` |
| `delete_drawing_revision` | `drawing`, `revision` | undo step `Delete revision A of Drawing1` |
| `save_drawing_template` | `drawing`, `sheet` (0), `library` (`user` or `project`), `name`, `id` (from the name: `Company A3` → `company-a3`), `project` (the project's folder) | `path`, `id`, `choice` (`project:company-a3`); writes the sheet's template with its size and projection method, replacing one of the id; no undo step |

The `drawing_templates` query (`project`: the project's folder) lists
`templates`, each a template's data with its `library` (`builtin`,
`user`, `project`) and its `choice` (`iso`, `user:<id>`,
`project:<id>`), the built-in ones first, then the user's and the
project's by name; and `problems` (files that are no template).

The `drawing` query gives each sheet's `template` (`id`, `name`,
`library`, `choice`; null for the simple block), the drawn sheet's
`title_fields` (each `label` with its `text` as drawn; the simple
block's TITLE, DRAWING NO. or BODY, DATE and DRAWN BY), and the
drawing's `revisions` (`letter`, `description`, `date`, `author`) and
`next_revision`. A template's sheet draws `frame`, `title-block` (its
lines, labels, values and the projection symbol) and, once the drawing
has a revision, `revision-table` (REV, DESCRIPTION, DATE, BY: its
`rows` latest revisions above the block, the latest on top); the views'
area is the template's frame above its block and the revision table's
whole room (its `rows` and its header, 5 mm each), kept clear from the
start so that the first revision overlaps no view placed in the area
(mitcad#722; the export's hole table keeps clear of it too). Exports
(PDF, SVG, DXF) write them as drawn.

Refused: an unknown built-in template, a template that is not one (an
id of other than letters, digits, `-` and `_`, no name, a block of no
size, a field without a cell, a revision table of other than 1 to 50
rows, margins that leave no frame or a title block that with the
revision table's room does not fit in the frame of its own `size`), a
sheet whose template does not fit it so (its size or orientation changed,
or the template given; mitcad#722), a revision without a description or
with a letter the drawing has, saving the simple title block as a
template, and a library other than `user` or `project`.

Classes: the revision commands are the model's; `save_drawing_template`
and `drawing_templates` read and write library folders (file IO).
Saved, undone, compared and copied with a component's drawings as the
rest of a drawing. Tests: those in `core/model-drawing/src/template.rs` (the built-in
templates, fields filled, revision letters, a filled template drawn,
templates checked, saved and listed in folders of the test's own, a
template fitting its sheet), `core/model-tests/drawing/src/template_tests.rs` (a template's
projection method brought to a new drawing, mitcad#725; a
template's block following the design's material, mass, properties and
sheets; revisions added, shown, edited, deleted, undone and saved;
templates per sheet, a template's data with a property field, copied
with a component; saved to a project's library and chosen; exported),
`api::drawing_templates::tests`; `tools/ui-drawings-test.sh` (the ISO
template chosen in Create Drawing, the title block's material following
the body's, a revision added and exported).

## Drawing defaults, sketches, patterns and turned views

What a drawing adds to *Drawings in the design* and *Annotations on
drawing views* since mitcad#729 (`core/model/src/drawing/def.rs`,
`annotate_def.rs`, `core/model-drawing/src/annotate.rs`, `api/drawings.rs`, `api/drawing_annotations.rs`).

**The drawing's decimals and letters.** `add_drawing` and
`edit_drawing` take `decimals` (0 to 6) and `text_height` (paper mm,
more than 0 and at most 100); `edit_drawing` takes `null` for none (undo
step `Edit Drawing1`; `Rename Drawing1` for a name alone). They are what
every dimension and annotation of the drawing takes unless it has its
own: a dimension's value its `format`'s `decimals` (else the drawing's,
else as many as it needs, up to three), and the retrieved sketch
dimensions the drawing's; an annotation's letters (dimensions, leaders,
datum labels, frames, finish symbols, balloons, tables, whose cells and
rows grow with them) its own `height`, else the drawing's, else 3.5 mm;
a text note's and a text's likewise. `add_drawing_annotation` and
`edit_drawing_annotation` take `height` for every annotation now
(`null`: the drawing's again; before, a text note's only). The
`drawing` query gives the drawing's `decimals` and `text_height` (null
when none). File: the drawing's `defaults` (`decimals`, `text_height`),
an annotation's `height`; left out when none.

**Lines, arcs and texts outside the model.** `add_drawing_annotation`
takes `"type": "line"` (`points`: its two ends), `"arc"` (`points`: its
centre, its start and its end, counter-clockwise from the start; an end
the way the start lies makes a whole circle) and `"text"` with a `view`
(`at`, `text`, `height`), each with `pen` (`thin` (default), `thick`,
`hidden`, `chain`; not a text's) and, instead of a view, a `sheet` (0):
points are sheet millimetres. On the sheet they are kept in sheet
millimetres (a text on the sheet is a text note); in a view in its
coordinates (model millimetres in the view's plane), so that they move,
scale and turn with the view; they pick nothing of the model and follow
nothing else. Their ids are the drawing's annotation ids:
`edit_drawing_annotation` takes `points` (as when added), `pen`, `text`,
`height`, `at` (a text's place) and `move` (a drag on the sheet), undo
steps `Add line 4 to Drawing1`, `Move arc 5 of Drawing1`, `Edit text 6
of Drawing1`; `delete_drawing_annotation` deletes them, and a view's
deletion takes its own along. The `drawing` query lists them among the
sheet's `annotations` in their file form (`type`, `id`, `from` and `to`;
`center`, `radius`, `start`, `end` in radians; `text`, `at`, `height`;
`pen`) with `view` (null on the sheet), `label` (a text's lines joined by
` / `, else `line` or `arc`) and `box`; a view lists their ids under
`sketch`. Group: `sketch` (`A<id>`). Files: a sheet's and a view's
`sketch`, left out when empty. Refused: other annotations' fields on
them, a line of no length, an arc of no size or turning backwards, a
text without its text or place, a pen for a text, `points` or `pen` for
other annotations, a text in a sheet's `sketch` in a file.

**Centre patterns and edge extensions.** Two annotation types:

| `type` | Picks | Shows |
|---|---|---|
| `center_pattern` | one circle seen end on, or several | the circles of the pattern, found from one: those of its body (where the same occurrence places it) the view sees end on, as large and picked as it was (edges or round faces), where it shows them, each centre once, the one picked first (up to 256); kept by name, so the pattern follows the model. About one centre: the circle through their centres (long-dash dotted; an arc over them, a little beyond the outer ones, when a gap between two of them is wider than one and a half of their pitch), a radial line through each and a small cross at the centre; in a row: the line through them beyond the outer ones and a cross line on each; else a centre mark on each. Group `center-mark`. |
| `edge_extension` | two straight edges, or one | two: thin lines from each edge's nearer end, 1 mm off it, to 2 mm past where their lines meet (none where the corner lies on the edge); refused for parallel edges. One: thin lines beyond both its ends by `line_offset` (paper mm, 10 when left out). Group `edge-extension`. |

A centre pattern and an edge extension are refused when they cannot be
drawn when added (a straight edge for a pattern, parallel edges), and
broken when their picks are gone or no longer draw them. Undo steps
`Add centre pattern 7 to Drawing1`, `Add edge extension 8 to
Drawing1`. The `drawing_pick` query's `type` picks circles for the
first, straight edges for the second.

**A view turned on the sheet.** `edit_drawing_view` takes `rotation`:
how far the view is turned on the sheet, degrees counter-clockwise
(normalised to -180 to 180), about the middle of its box, which stays
where it is (refused for a detail, which turns with its parent: `a
detail turns with its parent`). Its x axis turns the other way about
its direction to the eye (`DrawingSheet::axes`); a view from it takes
its parent's axes as turned, so a projected view looks from its side of
the turned view, and a projected view turned on its own no longer keeps
in line with its parent. An isometric view stays pictorial however it
is turned. The `drawing` query gives each view's `rotation`; files its
`rotation` (left out when 0). The view's group keeps its direction's id
(`view-front`).

**Views that follow a turn.** Whenever a command changes the axes of
views (`rotation`, a base view's `direction`, a projected view's
`side`, a section's `flip`, the sheet's `projection`), what views keep
in their coordinates is carried over, parents first (`follow_turns`):

- a view turned in its own plane (its eye the same): its annotations
  turn with it (where a leader was clicked, a leader's or a circle's
  text from its point; a horizontal or vertical dimension keeps
  measuring along the same direction of the model: a quarter turn makes
  a horizontal one vertical or the other way, another angle keeps its
  `turn`, degrees, in the file), so do the lines, arcs and texts drawn
  in it, its breaks (by quarter turns only: `view 1 has breaks: it turns
  by quarter turns only while it has them`) and the circles of its
  details, which keep showing the same place of the model;
- a view that looks another way: a section drawn on it is turned with
  it, so that its line stays where it was drawn on it (its plane edge on
  to the view; it then cuts what the view shows there now), a detail
  keeps its circle; annotations follow their picks and are broken where
  the view no longer sees them.

Setting a dimension's `along` drops its `turn` (along the view's x or y
as it is). Undo steps `Edit view 1 of Drawing1`, `Edit Sheet1 of
Drawing1`.

The application: the sheet's panel (nothing selected) has the drawing's
*Decimals* and *Text Height*; an annotation's panel its *Text Height*
(empty: the drawing's), a line's or an arc's *Line* (its pen), an edge
extension's *Length*; a view's panel its *Rotation* and its menu *Rotate
90° Left* and *Rotate 90° Right*; the Geometry group *Line*, *Arc*,
*Center Pattern* and *Edge Extension*, and *Text*'s *Drawn* (on the
sheet or in the view clicked) (app/COMMANDS.md, *Drawings*).

Tests: those in `core/model-drawing/src/annotate.rs` (a centre pattern on a bolt circle, an
arc of one, a row and scattered holes; edge extensions to a corner and
of one edge; letters of a given height; a dimension turning with its
view; lines, arcs and texts drawn through a view's map, carried and
checked), `core/model-tests/drawing-views/src/feature_tests.rs` (the drawing's decimals and letters
with the items' own, saved and undone; lines, arcs and texts on a sheet
and in a view moving and scaling with it, edited, saved, refused and
deleted; a centre pattern from one hole by name and by a click, broken
when a hole goes; edge extensions; a view turned with its dimension and
line, saved and undone; a turned view's detail and breaks; a base view's
direction, a projected view's side, the projection method and a
section's flip with the sections and details on them following; files
without the new fields), `core/model-tests/drawing/src/stored_tests.rs` (a view with sections
or details turning), `tests/drawing_tools.cpp`,
`tools/ui-drawing-features-test.sh`.

## Inactive constraints and dimensions

(mitcad#721.) A sketch constraint or dimension can be inactive: kept in
the sketch and shown, but left out of the solve until it is activated. An
import makes the constraints and dimensions of a file's sketch that keep
it off the file's geometry inactive instead of leaving every constraint
out (core/import/docs/f3d.md, freecad.md); the user sees what was left
out and activates or deletes it.

In the definition, an inactive constraint or dimension has
`"active": false` and an optional `inactive_reason`, both written only
for an inactive one:

```json
{"id": "k7", "type": "coincident", "point": "p3", "entity": "c5",
 "active": false, "inactive_reason": "not met in the imported file"}
```

- The solve leaves inactive constraints out; an inactive driving
  dimension keeps its parameter and value but drives nothing (its value
  is not checked against its range). An inactive driven one constrains
  nothing either way, so it still measures: its reference parameter, and
  what uses it, never keep a stale value (mitcad#723). The spacing
  dimension of an inactive equal spacing is left out with it. Drawings
  leave inactive dimensions out.
- Edits keep what an inactive item asks for (mitcad#723): Extend and
  Trim keep an inactive length of the line, and Extend never re-measures
  an inactive dimension on the end it moves (an imported one keeps the
  file's value); a point merge (two curve ends made coincident) that
  makes an inactive constraint the same as an active one keeps the
  active one.
- `sketch.set_active` sets the flag: `{"cmd": "sketch.set_active",
  "sketch": "F1", "items": ["k7", "k9"], "active": true}`; `active` false
  with an optional `reason`. Activating is refused, the sketch left as it
  was, when the sketch then does not solve (`k7 cannot be activated: the
  sketch is over-constrained: k3 and k7 contradict each other`) or when an
  activated one is implied by the others (over-constraining, as
  `sketch.add_constraint` refuses it). One undo step, `Activate in Sketch1`
  or `Deactivate in Sketch1`. An equal spacing takes its spacing
  dimension with it either way, and activating the spacing dimension
  activates its equal spacing, since it applies only with it; deactivating
  the dimension alone leaves the equal spacing (mitcad#723). A copy
  (`sketch.move` with `copy`) of an inactive constraint is inactive too.
- The `sketch` query: each constraint and dimension with its `active` and
  `inactive_reason` as in the definition; an inactive driving dimension's
  `measured` is its value. A spacing dimension the solve does not apply
  (its equal spacing inactive) has `"active": false` and the equal
  spacing's `inactive_reason` there, so that it is drawn as it acts
  (mitcad#723). `unmet_inactive` (only when not empty) lists
  the inactive ones the solved geometry does not meet (1e-4 mm): those
  whose activation would move it.
- Model: `Constraint::active`, `Dimension::active` and their
  `inactive_reason` (`core/sketch/src/lib.rs`),
  `SketchDef::dimension_applied`, `SketchStatus::unmet_inactive` and
  `sketch::solve::unmet` (`solve.rs`), `SketchEdit::set_active`
  (`modify.rs`).

The sketch view draws inactive constraints and dimensions in pink, their
frames and lines dashed; the tooltip says `Not applied: <reason>`. The
context menu of selected inactive ones offers **Activate**, of active
ones **Deactivate**; Delete removes them as any other
(`app/COMMANDS.md`).

Classes: the model's. Tests: `api::sketch_inactive_tests` (the solve
leaves an inactive constraint out, a contradicting activation refused,
activation and undo, delete; an inactive dimension keeps its value and
drives nothing; the file round trip; mitcad#723: a point merge keeps the
active duplicate, an equal spacing and its dimension set aside and
activated together, Extend keeps inactive values, an inactive driven
dimension keeps its reference measured), the imports' (`sketch::inactive`,
`tests::constraint_tests`, `freecad::tests`),
`tools/ui-sketch-inactive-test.sh` and
`tools/ui-windows-sketch-inactive-test.ps1` (drawn inactive, its tooltip,
Activate refused and applied, undo, Delete). The sketch view logs where
each inactive constraint's symbol is (`Constraint k1 glyph at x,y`) when
the view or the sketch moves it (mitcad#723).

## Print bed faces

A body keeps the face that lies on the print bed (mitcad#731,
`core/model/src/document/print_bed.rs`): a planar face, stored with the
body's other attributes by its topological name as it was assigned, so
that it follows the body's edits as a face appearance does ([Appearances
of faces](#appearances-of-faces)) and applies to every occurrence of the
body. A body has one; setting another replaces it.

| Command | Fields | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `set_print_bed_face` | `uid` (body), `face` (a topological name of a planar face of the body at the marker; null or left out takes it away) | undo step `Set Print Bed Face of Body1` / `Clear Print Bed Face of Body1` unless nothing changes; it recomputes nothing. A body that is not there or is no solid or mesh body (a surface body is not printed), a name that is no face name or names no face of the body, and a face that is not planar are refused |

- The `bodies` query gives a body's `print_bed_face`: `{"face"` (as
  assigned), `"faces"` (a name of each face it finds at the marker),
  `"error"}` (only when it cannot lie on the bed: `the print bed face is
  gone`, `the print bed face is not planar` when its surface is no plane,
  `a surface body is not printed` for a body that is no solid or mesh
  body (one that became a surface body, or a file that stored one; it can
  still be cleared, mitcad#737), else why its plane is not found, such as
  a renamed face that two faces fit alike); left out without one. A face
  that is gone stays kept, for when it comes back (undo).
- The design file keeps it with the body: `"print_bed_face":
  "F2:end(r{c5})"` (left out without one; files without it have none).
  Copies rename the feature in the name; Paste New of a component copied
  as bodies names the face of the copy. The comparison of versions lists
  it with the body.
- **Export on the bed:** `export` with `"on_bed": true` (3MF, STL and OBJ, in
  the design's coordinates; other formats and `coordinates: component`
  are refused) puts the bodies written on the print bed. They are one
  piece, as the 3MF file's one object:
  - with one body's bed face among them (a body printed alone, or a
    component in which one body has one), placed once or placed several
    times turned alike (normals within 1e-9: a component placed again and
    moved only, as the face applies to every occurrence), the piece turns
    so that the
    face's outward normal points straight down (−Z; the smallest turn, half
    a turn about X for a face up), its lowest point goes onto the bed (z =
    0) and the middle of its box over the plate's centre: the centre of
    the design's printer's `bed_shape` ([Print profiles](#print-profiles)),
    else of a 256 × 256 mm plate, (128, 128);
  - with the bed faces of several bodies, or of a body placed turned
    differently, the bodies stay as they are assembled (a 3MF file whose
    `occurrences` picks them puts each on its face instead, [Export by
    occurrences](#export-by-occurrences); a face named in `bed_face`
    turns them onto it, [Print bed face chosen](#print-bed-face-chosen));
    with none, as the design has them;
  - a bed face that is gone or not planar is reported, and its body is
    written as the design has it (−Z down) unless another body's face
    turns the piece;
  - the bed faces of bodies that are not printed (surface bodies, which
    3MF leaves out) count for nothing.

  The design does not move: a 3MF part's placements (its components), an
  STL file's vertices or an OBJ file's placements are moved after the design's placements, and
  the meshes are the kernel's. The result adds `bed`: `body`, `name` and
  `face` (null when nothing turned), `transform` (three rows `[a, b, c,
  t]` of what moved the bodies after their placements, null when nothing
  moved), `plate` ([x, y]), `kept` (the bodies kept as assembled) and
  `problems` (`body`, `name`, `reason`); and `warnings`, one per problem
  (`Body1: the print bed face is gone; printed as in the design`).

```json
{"cmd": "set_print_bed_face", "uid": "F2.b0", "face": "F2:end(r{c1[c4,c2],c2[c1,c3],c3[c2,c4],c4[c3,c1]})"}
{"cmd": "export", "path": "print.3mf", "bodies": ["F2.b0"], "on_bed": true, "dialect": "bambu_studio"}
```

Print Analysis starts from the bed face as the export does: the
application's panel fills its Bed face with it when exactly one of the
analysed bodies has a usable one ([Print analysis](#print-analysis)); the
analysis keeps its own `bed_face`.

Classes: the model's. Tests: `api::print_bed_tests` (set, replaced,
cleared and refused, a surface body's face too; kept through an edit, a
sketch edit that renames the face, and in the design file; a box on its
top, on a tilted face, in a turned component and in a component placed
twice turned and centred on the default plate and the printer's; two bed
faces kept as assembled; a surface body's face counts for nothing; a face
that is not planar or gone reported; an STL file; the formats),
`tools/ui-print-bed-test.sh` and `tools/ui-windows-print-bed-test.ps1`.

## Export by occurrences

A 3MF file of the occurrences chosen (mitcad#856): 3D Print sends only the
placements picked, as its STL files do, and puts each one with a print
bed face on its face, also when the body is placed many times turned
differently (a nut in an assembly). `export` takes, for 3MF only and in
the design's coordinates:

- `occurrences`: per body (uid or name, among those written), the
  occurrences whose placements are written, each a path from the root
  (`O1/O4` or `Arm:1/Pin:2`; `""` the design itself, for a body of the
  root); an empty list writes the body's placements as the design shows
  them (the shown ones, all when none is). A body not listed is written
  as before. An occurrence that does not place the body is refused
  (`Body1 is not placed by Nuts:1`).
- `whole`: occurrences sent whole (a component selected), each a path;
  the placements in each are one object, as they are assembled.

With `on_bed` the file's objects are:

- each occurrence of `whole` (the outermost one a placement is in): one
  object of the placements in it, put on the bed by the rule of
  [Export on the bed](#print-bed-faces) (one bed face among them turns
  it, several keep it as assembled);
- the placements `occurrences` picks of bodies with a usable print bed
  face (printed, the face planar and there), outside those: **when there
  are two or more**, each is an object of its own, named `Body1
  (Nuts:1/Nut:2)`, turned onto its face, its lowest point on the bed and
  its middle over the plate's centre; one alone stays with the rest, so
  that bodies printed together (an inlay of another colour) turn with it
  as before;
- the rest: the file's own object (named after the file), as before.

The objects turned are set side by side along X, 5 mm apart, the row
centred on the plate; overlaps with an object kept as designed are left
to the slicer's arrange. Several objects are several build items of the
3MF file (`mitcad_3mf::Model::objects`), each a components object of the
parts' placements; the Bambu family's `model_settings.config` names each
object with its parts. One object is written as before.

The result's `bed` describes the file's own object as before (`body`,
`face`, `transform` and `kept` null or empty when it has none: every
placement went apart) and adds `objects`, the others, each `name`,
`body`, `face`, `transform` (rows as `bed`'s) and `kept`, and `on_faces`,
how many placements lie on their print bed faces in all objects (the
application's last line, `3 bodies on their print bed faces`).
`problems` lists each face once.

```json
{"cmd": "export", "path": "nut.3mf", "bodies": ["F2.b0"], "on_bed": true, "occurrences": {"F2.b0": ["O1/O3"]}}
{"cmd": "export", "path": "nuts.3mf", "bodies": ["F2.b0"], "on_bed": true, "occurrences": {"F2.b0": []}}
{"cmd": "export", "path": "assembly.3mf", "bodies": ["F2.b0"], "on_bed": true, "occurrences": {"F2.b0": []}, "whole": ["Nuts:1"]}
```

Tests: `api::print_bed_tests` (a block with its top as the bed face in a
component placed three times turned differently: one occurrence chosen
one object on its top at z = 0; all three three objects side by side; the
component sent whole, and no `occurrences`, keep the assembly; the
refusals), `core.3mf` (several build objects written and read back),
`tools/ui-print-test.sh` (one occurrence selected: one object).

## Print bed face chosen

A piece kept as assembled because two or more print bed faces apply to
it (mitcad#857) can be put on one of them: 3D Print asks the user which,
and the export turns the piece onto the face named. `export` with
`on_bed` (3MF, STL and OBJ) takes:

- `bed_face`: `{"body", "occurrence"}`, or a list of them, one per
  piece: the body (uid or name) and the occurrence of its placement
  (`O1/O4` or `Arm:1/Pin:2`; `""` or left out for the design itself).
  The piece that placement is in (the file's own object, or an object of
  [Export by occurrences](#export-by-occurrences)) turns so that the
  face's outward normal at that placement points straight down, its
  lowest point on the bed and its middle over the plate's centre, as for
  a single bed face, whatever the automatic rule says; the bodies keep
  their places to each other. `bed.body` and `bed.face` (or the object's)
  name it, `kept` is empty and `on_faces` counts the placements of that
  body turned alike. Refused: a body not written (`Body1 is not among the
  bodies written`), without a print bed face (`Body2 has no print bed
  face`) or with one that cannot lie on the bed (its reason), a placement
  not written (`Body1 is not written where Nuts:1 places it`), two faces
  in one piece (`the print bed faces of Body1 in Pair:1 and Body2 in
  Pair:1 are chosen for one piece; choose one`), and without `on_bed`.
- `plan`: true gives only how the bodies would lie, before anything is
  written: the result's `bed` as the export would give it (a 3MF piece's
  `transform` is its turn alone, without the move onto the bed), and no
  file is written or meshed. Without `on_bed` it is refused.

The result's `bed`, and each of its `objects`, has `choices`: the faces a
piece kept as assembled for several bed faces could lie on, one per
placement (a body placed twice turned differently has two), each
`body`, `name`, `face` (as assigned), `occurrence` (uids, as `bed_face`
takes it) and `occurrence_name`; empty when the piece turns onto a face
or has none or one.

```json
{"cmd": "export", "path": "pair.3mf", "bodies": ["F2.b0", "F3.b0"], "on_bed": true, "plan": true, "whole": ["Pair:1"]}
→ {"bed": {"kept": ["F2.b0", "F3.b0"], "choices": [
     {"body": "F2.b0", "name": "Body1", "face": "F2:end(…)", "occurrence": "O1", "occurrence_name": "Pair:1"},
     {"body": "F3.b0", "name": "Body2", "face": "F3:side(…)", "occurrence": "O1", "occurrence_name": "Pair:1"}], …}, …}
{"cmd": "export", "path": "pair.3mf", "bodies": ["F2.b0", "F3.b0"], "on_bed": true, "whole": ["Pair:1"],
 "bed_face": {"body": "F3.b0", "occurrence": "Pair:1"}}
```

Tests: `api::print_bed_tests` (a component of two bodies, each with a
bed face: the plan lists both, a body placed three times turned
differently three, one face none; either face chosen puts the piece on
it at z = 0 with the bodies together, whole or not; the refusals),
`tools/ui-print-test.sh` (3D Print asks, a click sends on that face, Esc
as assembled).

## Copy and paste of sketch geometry

Copy, Cut and Paste of sketch geometry (mitcad#788): a query copies
selected points, curves and texts of a sketch as a fragment, and
`sketch.paste` adds a fragment to a sketch, of this design or of another
(the fragment is plain JSON). Cut is a copy and then `sketch.remove` of
the same items.

```json
{"query": "sketch_fragment", "sketch": "F1", "items": ["c2", "t5"]}
→ {"sketch": "F1", "sketch_name": "Sketch1", "base": [10, 10],
   "outline": [[[10, 10], [40, 10]], ...], "points": [],
   "entities": 3, "texts": 1, "kept": 3, "left_out": 1, "held": [false, true],
   "fragment": {"version": 1, "base": [10, 10], "entities": [...], "texts": [...],
                "constraints": [...], "dimensions": [...],
                "references": [{"id": "p1", "is": "origin"}], "left_out": 1}}
{"cmd": "sketch.paste", "sketch": "F2", "fragment": {...}, "at": [30, 10]}
→ {"made": ["p2", "p3", "c4"], "kept": 3, "left_out": 1,
   "entities": [...], "constraints": [...], "dimensions": [...], "status": {...}}
```

- **What is copied.** The selected points, curves and texts (`p3`, `c4`,
  `t5`; constraints and dimensions listed are ignored: they come with
  their geometry), the points the curves use, and for a text the points of
  its frame and the curve it runs along. Projected and intersected
  geometry becomes ordinary geometry: free, not reference geometry and
  following nothing. Patterns and offsets come as the geometry they made.
  Construction and centre lines, splines of both kinds, arcs, conics,
  points and texts (with their fonts and stored outlines) keep what they
  are.
- **Constraints and dimensions** are kept when every entity they
  reference is copied or is the sketch's origin or one of its axes
  (mitcad#500); an equal spacing's common spacing goes with its equal
  spacing. Those that reference copied geometry and something else are
  left out and counted (`left_out`); the others are not about the copy.
  Inactive ones stay inactive (mitcad#721).
- **The origin and the axes** are not copied: the fragment's `references`
  name the ids that stood for them (`origin`, `x`, `y`, and `x_end`,
  `y_end` for an axis's far end), and a paste uses the target sketch's
  own, made when it has none (as `sketch.axis` makes them). A curve that
  starts at the origin point starts at the target's.
- **Values.** A driving dimension keeps its value (`value`, mm or
  radians) and, when its parameter uses other parameters (or it uses a
  parameter of the design as it is), its `expression` and the
  `parameters` it uses. A paste takes the expression where every one of
  those parameters exists in the target design, else the value, and lists
  the dimension in the answer's `values` with a warning. A text that
  follows a text parameter (mitcad#664) keeps it the same way, else its
  text.
- **The base point** (`base`) is the first selected item's first point
  (a line's or an arc's start, a circle's centre, a spline's first point,
  a text's anchor). `sketch.paste` moves the fragment by `at - base`;
  without `at` it goes where it was. The coordinates are the sketch's own,
  so a paste into a sketch on another plane keeps the 2D coordinates.
- **Held directions.** Constraints and dimensions kept to the origin and
  the axes hold the fragment where it was in the directions they fix, and
  the solve puts it back there whatever `at` says. The query's `held`
  (`[x, y]`) gives those directions: a point at the origin (or an axis's
  end) holds both; a point or line on the x axis, a vertical distance
  from the origin or a level alignment with it (`horizontal_points`)
  hold y (the y axis, a horizontal distance or `vertical_points`: x); a
  distance from the origin holds both; parallels,
  perpendiculars, angles and sizes hold none, nor inactive ones. The
  application places a paste only in the free directions.
- **Warnings** of a paste: the constraints and dimensions it dropped
  itself (of a fragment that names entities it lacks; what the copy left
  out is said at the copy, and `left_out` counts both), and dimensions
  that took their values.
- **One undo step** `Paste into Sketch2`; the new entities and texts get
  new ids, in `made` in the fragment's order. Refused: a fragment of a
  newer version (`version`), one whose curves use points it lacks, an
  empty one, a place that is not finite.
- `outline` (the curves and the texts' glyph contours as polylines) and
  `points` (lone points) are for a preview, in the source sketch's
  coordinates; `sketch.paste` takes only the `fragment`.

The application keeps the query's answer on the clipboard under the type
`application/x-mitcad-sketch-fragment+json` (`app/COMMANDS.md`, Sketch
mode, "Copy, Cut and Paste").

Classes: the model's. Code: `core/sketch/src/clipboard.rs`,
`core/model-api/src/sketch_clipboard.rs`. Tests:
`core/model-tests/sketch/src/sketch_clipboard_tests.rs`,
`tools/ui-sketch-clipboard-test.sh` and
`tools/ui-windows-sketch-clipboard-test.ps1`.

## Redefine Sketch Plane

(mitcad#787.) `sketch.redefine_plane` moves a sketch to another plane or
planar face and places it there: an offset along the plane's normal, a
move in the plane, a rotation about the normal and a flip. The sketch's
geometry keeps its own 2D coordinates; only its frame moves, and the
features built on it (extrudes, revolves, holes, sweeps, …) follow at the
recompute. One undo step, `Redefine Plane of Sketch1`.

```json
{"cmd": "sketch.redefine_plane", "sketch": "F1",
 "plane": {"face": "F2:end(r{c1})", "body": "F2.b0"}, "occurrence": "",
 "offset": "5 mm", "x": 10, "y": "Gap * 2", "angle": "30 deg", "flip": false,
 "upright": true}
```

- `plane`: as `sketch.create` takes it (an origin plane, a construction
  plane `"F5"`, a planar face); left out, the sketch keeps its plane and
  only its placement changes. `occurrence` and `context` are as in
  `sketch.create` (mitcad#100): a plane of another component is linked
  (`plane_link`), from the sketch's component.
- A plane made by a feature at or after the sketch in the timeline (a
  construction plane, a face of a later feature, of a feature built on the
  sketch itself) is refused with the reason: `Sketch1 cannot lie on a
  plane or face of Plane1: Plane1 comes after Sketch1 in the timeline, and
  a sketch's plane must be made before it`. A plane the sketch does not
  find where it is evaluated (a face that is not planar or is gone) is
  refused too (`Sketch1 cannot use this plane or face: …`, the
  evaluation's reason), unless the sketch failed before (it does not
  solve); so is a plane whose link or feature is not found (`Sketch1
  cannot use this plane: …`). The document is then unchanged.
- On another plane the own frame (`frame`) of the old plane is dropped.
  With `upright` the sketch gets the own frame that shows the design
  upright on the new plane, as Create Sketch's (see [An upright sketch
  frame](#an-upright-sketch-frame)), in the same undo step. The same plane
  again keeps the own frame.
- `offset`, `x`, `y` and `angle` are values (numbers or expressions with
  units, parameters by name): the sketch keeps them as its own parameters
  in `placement` (slots `placement.offset`, `placement.x`, `placement.y`,
  `placement.angle`), so a parameter moves the sketch and a later
  `sketch.redefine_plane` or the parameters table changes them. A value
  left out stays; a plain zero (`0`, `"0 mm"`, an expression without
  parameters that is zero) takes it away with its parameter. `flip` (left
  out: kept) turns the sketch over.
- The placement acts on the base frame (the plane's frame with the own
  frame): the origin moves by `x` and `y` along the base's x and y axes
  and by `offset` along its normal; the axes then turn by `angle`
  counter-clockwise about the normal; a flip then reverses the y axis, and
  with it the normal, keeping the x axis. A sketch without placement
  keeps none in the file; files without one read as before.
- Linked projections and section curves (Project, Intersect) follow their
  sources from the new plane at the recompute; those that cannot say so
  in the sketch's `warnings` (and in the result's). Projections that are
  not linked keep their geometry in the sketch's coordinates.
- The result: `uid`, `name`, `plane`, `plane_link`, `placement` (the
  parameters by name, null without one), `plane_changed`, `label`,
  `parameters` (those made), `warnings` (the sketch's) and `frame` (the
  sketch's frame now, when it evaluated); `failed_features` names the
  later features the move breaks.
- The `sketch` query's `frame` is the placed frame. Reorient Design turns
  the base frame and keeps the placement.

Classes: the model's. Tests: `core/model-tests/sketch`
(`sketch_plane_tests`: a plane change with the extrude following and one
undo step, the offset, move and rotation as expressions and parameters
changed again and taken away, a flip, a face and a construction plane, a
later plane and a face that cannot take it refused, upright, the design
file), `core/model` (`sketch::placement`, `document::sketch_plane`),
`tools/ui-sketch-redefine-plane-test.sh` and
`tools/ui-windows-sketch-redefine-plane-test.ps1`.

## Image references

Images placed in the design to model from, such as a photo of a part or a
scanned drawing (mitcad#782; `core/model/src/document/image_references.rs`,
`core/model-base/src/image_header.rs`, `api/image_references.rs`): the
browser's Images folder. An image reference keeps the image file's bytes
(PNG, JPEG, BMP, WebP or HEIF, at most 32 MB and 32768 pixels on a side)
embedded in the design, no path; it changes no geometry, and every command
below is an undo step that recomputes nothing.

**HEIF** (`.heic`, `.heif`; mitcad#850, `image_header/heif.rs`): the
file's primary image, a still image coded with HEVC (an `hvc1` item, or a
`grid` or `iden` of `hvc1` tiles), 8 to 10 bits per channel, with or
without an alpha plane. Its `pixels` are the image as it is shown: the
`ispe` size, then the transformations in the file's order (`irot` turns a
quarter or three swap the width and height, `clap` crops, rounded;
`imir` mirrors), which the application's decoder applies too. A HEIF
file states no pixel size (96 to the inch). Refused with the reason: AVIF
(AV1), other codecs (`coded as 'jpeg'`), an image sequence without a
still image, a protected item, more than 10 bits per channel, a file cut
short. The model keeps the file's bytes as they are; decoding the pixels
is the application's (builds with `MITCAD_HEIF`, libheif and libde265;
docs/development.md, "Licence policy").

- **Its plane** is a [plane reference](#references-to-geometry) (an origin
  plane, a construction plane, a planar face or a fixed plane) with an
  optional `occurrence` (the plane's UID path from the design root), as a
  section analysis' ([Analyses](#analyses)). It is resolved at the
  timeline marker each time it is asked for, so the image follows its
  plane or face when the model changes; one whose plane is gone says why
  (`error`).
- **Its place** in the plane's frame: `center` (mm, `[x, y]` along the
  plane's x and y axes), `angle` (degrees, about the plane's normal,
  counter-clockwise seen from the side the normal points to) and `flip`
  (mirrored left to right). Seen from the normal's side, an image that is
  not flipped reads as in a picture viewer.
- **Its size** is `scale`, the size of a pixel (mm). A new image takes the
  size its file states (PNG's `pHYs`, JPEG's JFIF density, BMP's pixels
  per metre), else 96 pixels to the inch; `width` (mm) sets the scale from
  the image's width instead.
- **Pixels** are counted from the image's top left corner, `u` to the
  right and `v` down, `[0, 0]` to `[width, height]`.
- **Calibration** scales the image about its first point so that two
  points are a typed distance apart: the first point stays where it is.
- **Display:** `opacity` (0 to 1, a new image 0.5), its light bulb
  (`visible`), and `through`: drawn through the bodies (over them) instead
  of hidden behind them. The view never picks an image.

| Command | Fields | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `insert_image_reference` | `path` (the image file) or `data` (its bytes, base64) and `file_name` (kept for the user; the path's own name with `path`); `plane`, `occurrence`; `at` (a design point the centre is put on, projected onto the plane; the plane's origin when left out) or `center`; `angle`, `flip`, `scale` or `width`, `opacity`, `through`; `name` (the next free `Image<n>` when left out) | `name`; undo step `Insert Image1`. Refused: a plane that is no plane at the marker, a file that is no image of those formats, `path` and `data` both, `scale` and `width` both, a size not greater than zero, an opacity outside 0 to 1, a name in use, other fields |
| `edit_image_reference` | `name`, and any of `plane` (a new plane without `occurrence` is in the root), `occurrence` (alone: the same plane in another occurrence), `center`, `angle`, `flip`, `scale` or `width`, `opacity`, `through`, `path` or `data` with `file_name` (another image in its place, at the same place and pixel size) | undo step `Edit Image1` unless nothing changes |
| `calibrate_image_reference` | `name`, `pixels` (two `[u, v]`) or `points` (two design points, projected onto the image's plane), `distance` (mm, greater than zero) | `scale`, the new size of a pixel; undo step `Calibrate Image1`. Refused: two points that are the same pixel |
| `set_image_reference_visible` | `name`, `visible` | undo step `Show Image1` / `Hide Image1` unless nothing changes |
| `rename_image_reference` | `name`, `new_name` | undo step `Rename Image1` |
| `delete_image_reference` | `name` | undo step `Delete Image1` |

| Query | Fields | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `image_references` | | per image, in the order they were inserted: `name`, `visible`, `plane`, `occurrence` (when it has one), `center`, `angle`, `flip`, `scale`, `opacity`, `through`, `file_name`, `format`, `pixels` (`[width, height]`), `size` (mm), `sha256` (of the file's bytes: the same image, the same digest), and `corners` (top left, top right, bottom right, bottom left, design coordinates) at the marker or `error` |
| `image_reference_image` | `name` | `name`, `format`, `pixels`, `sha256`, `data` (the file's bytes, base64) |
| `image_reference_outline` | `plane`, `occurrence`, `pixels`, and `at` or `center`, `angle`, `flip`, `scale` or `width` (96 to the inch when neither) | `corners`: where an image of that many pixels would lie (a panel's preview); `center`: its centre in the plane's frame (`at` projected onto the plane: a panel's X and Y) |
| `image_info` | `path` | `format`, `pixels`, `pixel_size` (mm: the file's, else 96 to the inch), `stated` (whether the file states it), `size` (mm) |

```json
{"cmd": "insert_image_reference", "path": "plan.png", "plane": "xy", "at": [0, 0, 0]}
{"cmd": "calibrate_image_reference", "name": "Image1", "pixels": [[112, 640], [1530, 640]], "distance": 450}
{"cmd": "edit_image_reference", "name": "Image1", "opacity": 0.35, "through": true}
```

The design file keeps them as `"image_references"`, each with its settings
(`visible` left out when shown, `center`, `angle` and `flip` when not
zero) and `image`: `{format, width, height, data}` (`data` base64); a
file whose bytes are not the image its fields say, or with a name twice,
is refused. They are left out when there are none.

Classes: `insert_image_reference` and `edit_image_reference` are the
model's own unless they name a `path`, then file IO
(`command_class_with`); `image_info` reads a file. Tests:
`image_header::tests` (the four formats' sizes and densities, files
refused), `image_header::heif::tests` (HEVC images turned, grids cropped
and mirrored, AVIF, other codecs, 12 bits, sequences, files cut short and
too large refused), `document::image_references::tests` (pixels and places, corners
turned and flipped), `analysis::image_reference_tests` (inserted,
calibrated by pixels and by points, edited, hidden, renamed, deleted and
undone; following a face; a file read by its path; what is refused; saved
and read back; a HEIF photo inserted upright, saved and read back, its
`image_info`, and HEIF files refused), `tools/ui-image-references-test.sh` and
`tools/ui-windows-image-references-test.ps1`.

Not yet: the `.f3d` import leaves canvases out (the stream decoder does not
read their records or the images they keep); a reference does not follow
an occurrence moved to another parent or Reorient Design.

## Bindings: values from expressions

A body's appearance and material, a face's appearance, a feature's
suppression and the visibility of a body or an occurrence can follow an
expression of parameters instead of a value set by hand (mitcad#800;
[docs/configurations.md](../../../docs/configurations.md), "Bindings"). A
configuration only sets parameters, and these follow; they work as well
in a design without configurations. Code:
`core/model/src/document/bindings.rs`.

| Command | `expression` | Undo step |
|---|---|---|
| `set_body_appearance` | a text: an appearance id, else the name of one appearance (`switch(Color; 'Black'; 'paint_black'; 'White'; 'Paint - White'; 'plastic_white')`) | `Set Appearance of Body1` |
| `set_face_appearance` | as above, for the faces given | `Set Appearance of Face of Body1` |
| `set_body_material` | a text: a material id, else the name of one material | `Set Material of Body1` |
| `suppress_feature` | a condition: suppressed while it holds (`Holes = 'No'`) | `Suppress Extrude2 When` |
| `set_body_visible` | a condition: shown while it holds | `Show Body1 When` |
| `set_occurrence_visible` | a condition: shown while it holds | `Show Board:1 When` |

- **The value and the expression are alternatives.** A command gives
  one of them; both are refused. Setting the value by hand removes the
  expression in the same undo step (`Hide Body1`, `Unsuppress Extrude2`).
  An empty `expression` removes the expression and keeps the value it
  gave (`Clear Appearance Expression of Body1`, `Clear Show When of
  Board:1`, `Clear Suppress When of Extrude2`). The same expression again
  is no undo step.
- **Checked when set.** The expression must evaluate with the design's
  parameters: an appearance's or a material's must give a text, a
  condition a number (true when it is not 0: `Color = 'Black'`,
  `Length > 1 m`, `and(Tables = 1; Power = 1)`). A text that names no
  appearance or material is accepted and gives the warning below.
- **Values follow.** Every command settles the bound values after its
  edit, in the same undo step: changing `Color` in Change Parameters, a
  configuration row, a CSV import or undo all switch the look. The value
  is stored next to the expression, so readers that ignore bindings (the
  exports, older versions) see the value as if it were set by hand.
  - A changed suppression recomputes from that feature on, as
    `suppress_feature` does; the features before it keep their results.
  - Appearance, material and visibility recompute nothing.
  - A material that follows an expression gives the body the new
    material's appearance by the rule of [Materials](#materials): unless
    the body's appearance was set by hand or follows an expression of its
    own.
- **Warnings.** A text that names no appearance or material, or names
  two, gives the body a warning, and the body has the default look: no
  appearance of its own (its material's) or no material of its own (its
  component's). A face shows the body's look. A condition that cannot be
  evaluated (a text, a parameter that is gone) leaves the value as it
  was, with a warning.
- **Parameters.** Renames rewrite the expressions (in the rename's undo
  step). A parameter that a binding uses cannot be deleted: `parameter
  'Color' is used by the appearance of Body1`. A feature's own parameter
  that a binding uses stays as a user parameter when the feature is
  deleted.
- **Queries.**
  - `bodies`: `appearance_expr`, `material_expr`, `visible_when` and
    `face_appearance_exprs` (`{face name: expression}`) when bound, with
    `dependencies` (the parameters the body's bindings use) and
    `warnings` (one line each, `appearance: there is no appearance 'Gloss
    Purple'; the body has the default look`).
  - `timeline` and `feature`: `suppressed_when`, `dependencies` and,
    when the condition cannot be evaluated, `binding_warning`.
  - `components`: each occurrence of the tree has `visible_when`,
    `dependencies` and `warnings`.
- **Design file.** A body keeps `appearance_expr`, `material_expr`,
  `visible_when` and `face_appearance_exprs` beside its values, a feature
  `suppressed_when` beside `suppressed`, an occurrence `visible_when`
  beside `visible`. Opening the file settles the values with the file's
  parameters.
## Tables

A design keeps named tables of data (screw sizes, standard dimensions)
that parameter expressions look values up in with `Table.Column` and the
lookup functions `XLOOKUP`, `MATCH` and `INDEX` (mitcad#667; the design is
[docs/table-lookups.md](../../../docs/table-lookups.md); `tables.rs`,
`document/tables.rs`, `api/tables.rs`):

```text
Size    = 'M5'
HeadDia = XLOOKUP(Size; Screws.Size; Screws.dk)   → 8.5 mm
```

| | Fields | Result |
|---|---|---|
| command `set_table` | `name`, `table`: `comment`, `columns` [{`name`, `unit`}], `rows` (arrays of cells: numbers in the column's unit, texts, null) | `changed`: the parameters whose values changed; `moves`: the configuration options it moved ([Configurations and tables](#configurations-and-tables), mitcad#806); creates the table or replaces it; one undo step `Edit Table <name>`, none for the same table |
| command `rename_table` | `name`, `new_name` | `{}`; the expressions, limits and configuration values that use it follow; undo step `Rename Table <name> to <new_name>` |
| command `rename_table_column` | `table`, `name`, `new_name` | `{}`; the same; undo step `Rename Column <table>.<name> to <new_name>` |
| command `delete_table` | `name` | `{}`; refused while a parameter or a configuration row uses it, naming them; undo step `Delete Table <name>` |
| query `tables` | `name` (optional: only that table) | `tables`: each with `name`, `comment`, `columns`, `rows`, `used_by` (the parameters that use it), `problems` (first cells more than one row has: lookups find the first) |

- **Names.** A table's name follows the parameter name rules
  (case-sensitive, not a unit, function or constant) and the tables share
  the parameters' namespace: a table cannot take a parameter's name, nor a
  parameter (added, renamed, copied) a table's. Column names use the same
  characters, are unique in their table and may be reserved words (`in`,
  `Max`): a column is only ever written after `Table.`.
- **Cells** are constants. A column's `unit` is any unit a parameter
  takes (`mm`, `in`, `deg`, `mm^2`), `""` for unitless, or `Text`; a
  number cell is in the column's unit (`5.5` in an `mm` column is 5.5 mm),
  a text cell a string, an empty cell `null`. A row has a cell per column;
  a text in a number column, a number in a `Text` column, a number that is
  not finite or a text over the text limit is refused with its row and
  column. At most 10 000 rows and 100 columns.
- **Edits re-evaluate.** `set_table` re-evaluates every parameter that
  uses the table, and the parameters that depend on them, in one step.
  When one of them would fail (a key no longer found, a column of another
  kind) the command is refused with that parameter and its error, and
  nothing changes; a column a parameter uses cannot be left out
  (`column Screws.dk is used by HeadDia`). The features then recompute by
  the usual rule: only those whose parameters changed value, so an edit
  that changes no used value recomputes nothing.
- **Renames** rewrite every expression and limit that uses the table or
  the column, keeping the rest of their text, and the configuration rows'
  values; values do not change.
- **Copies.** Copying parameters into another design (Paste New, inserting
  a design's copy) brings the tables they use: the same table there is
  used as it is, a different one of the same name gets a free name
  (`Screws_1`), and the copied expressions follow.
- **Configurations** stay separate: a row can set only the key
  (`Size = 'M5'`), and the lookups follow when it is applied.

The other queries:

- `parameters`: each parameter's `table_dependencies`, the columns it
  looks values up in (`["Screws.Size", "Screws.dk"]`).
- `evaluate`: `table_references`, the same for the expression, beside
  `references`.
- `formula_help`: `tables`, each table's `name` and `columns` (`name`,
  `unit`), for completion.
- `diff`: a `tables` section (the "Tables" lines of the text), by name:
  tables added, deleted, renamed (the same content under another name),
  and changed ones by their comment, columns (`column Pitch added`,
  `column dk mm -> in`) and rows (`table Screws row 3 (M5): dk 8.5 mm ->
  8.7 mm`); rows are matched by their first cell when it tells them apart.

The design file keeps them as `"tables"`, left out when there are none,
each `{name, comment, columns, rows}` (`comment` left out when empty); a
table with a problem, a name twice or a parameter's name is refused.

Classes: all of them are the model's own. Tests: `tables::tests` (the
file form, refused tables), `tables_tests` in the model (recompute only
what a changed value reaches, refused edits, renames, deletes, undo,
copies, configurations), `api::tables_tests` in `core.model.api` (the
commands and queries) and `files::tables_tests` in `core.model.files`
(saved and read back, the diff's rows).

## Tables as CSV

A table of the design (mitcad#667, `docs/table-lookups.md`) is exported to
and imported from CSV, one file per table (mitcad#804; `tables_csv.rs`,
